Yes, I have his hat; I found it after the Butcher's Masquerade, and he can have it back when he stops being disgusting and changes the name of our alliance. Then Carl pulls out a bowler hat I have never been given.

beats.headline: The garbage truck people cancel
beats.text: I get a notification that a sponsorship has been cancelled. The garbage truck people, for a conflict of interest, whatever that means, and Carl says huh. At least I opened their box already. There is going to be an auction for a new one. I do hope it lines up properly with my brand this time. Veriluxx was a dud, Empress D'nadia sold my sponsorship, and it would be nice to have something to complement the Apothecary, even if she does sponsor half the dungeon.

beats.headline: A name she cannot change
beats.text: Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority. It is a terrible name, and it will not let me change it, because the Sledge and the changelings kept changing it back and forth until the AI told them to shove it. Carl reads out the initials and laughs. I am absolutely not calling my castle that. It's obscene, and the bad guys are going to laugh at us. I give Florin a direct order not to spread it. He has already put it in the chat.

beats.headline: Skanked, and a hat
beats.text: The skunks' leader is a little battle wizard called Fancy Boy, in a starry hat, and I shout that nobody touch him because he's mine, and knock him out with a Magic Missile. That, apparently, is what was stopping the rest of them spraying. Now I am Skanked. Three hours, Charisma down seventy per cent, and nothing in my inventory takes it off. Mongo is sick. I got the hat, and it smells worse than I do. And I was supposed to be moral support for Katia's treatment.

beats.headline: None of my spells work
beats.text: The periscope screens have amazing resolution, much better than the stolen television in Carl's living room. Everything from a pawn shop is stolen, Carl. Then the pets come out of the fog, rot sticker behemoths as big as cars, full of the Gurgles, and I am feeling very useless all of a sudden. None of my spells work. Wait, Love Vampire works! It doesn't work on pets.

beats.headline: A prize for the most
beats.text: Warlord Donut, to everyone. The moment the first bomb drops, take the ear potion or put your earplugs in. Drink your invisibility, and go up and over, and don't stop running until you're in their trenches. The soldier who brings me the most dead cheese sticks gets a prize. The veterans say their old officers always threatened them. My army is different. Positive reinforcement worked with Mongo. Carl asks if I'm scared. Of course I am. It's more numb than anything. Nowadays it hits me more when it's done.

beats.headline: I got this
beats.text: The Empress has shield after shield, and my clockwork Mongos go through every one of them and her dress. She tells me she was my sponsor. She got me my glasses. Don't I like my glasses? Then Carl says he has changed his mind, he wants to do it himself. No, Carl. Please. I need you to step back and calm down. I've got this. When he does, I sit, lick my paw, and tell the Empress, darling, that Mongo would like to express his utmost disappointment at how she judged him during the pet show.

beats.headline: Carl is the party leader now
beats.text: Carl's base stats make him the strongest member of the party, so the system has made him Party Leader of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Of my Royal Court. If he changes the name of the party I will leave, and then Mongo will come from a broken home. He says we'll keep the names and the titles. For now. Then I tell him the thing that is not for show. Throw that ring away, Carl. It's doing something to you. You're scaring me. He says not yet. It won't matter if it kills you first.

beats.headline: A spellbook called War Crime
beats.text: My 1914 box has given me a spellbook called War Crime, and I am not sure if I should read it. The spellbook itself is bleeding and crying and it's disgusting. Then the castle starts blowing up, and Bomo notices an extra door in the situational whatever it's called space: a door for the Reaver team's saferoom. They are doing what we were going to do. They are sneak attacking us through the saferoom door. The Bamboozle! Carl tells Bomo and Sledge to guard it.

beats.headline: Comrades, from the castle roof
beats.text: These people really need to follow orders faster. We need more team-building exercises. So my headset goes on, I jump on Mongo, and we land on the castle roof right above the door, where everyone can hear me, even the bad guys. Comrades! There are over a hundred of them behind that building, and some of them are wormheads who killed our friends. Are we going to let that stand? Alpha squad card reserves, to the roof! Everyone else, save your cards for the main force. Tina! Sic 'em! For the Posse!

beats.headline: The banners have to be wavy
beats.text: Rosetta insists we spend the last of our money defending the base, so I am spending it: a standalone hangar for five million gold, and another anti-air gun for five million, which is simply unfair when the other guys blew up the last one. And banners. Carl says we need to make the king angry enough to attack before his backup arrives, and nothing will do that like banners. I am the general and she is the colonel, so it's final. They need to be wavy. The bopca can't control the wind. Elle can.

beats.headline: From a Maserati to a dump truck
beats.text: The plan requires a mount the same size as the bad guy's, so I am riding Simoom, Ferdinand's albino rhinoceros, in a covered howdah with curtains I can barely see through. Mongo is whining. It's only for show, Mongo. Pretend mommy is acting in a movie and pretending someone else is her child. Push the horn to go, Kibben says, and if she gets to trotting, pat her behind. I will certainly not be smacking a rhinoceros's behind like some racetrack jockey. A gentle rub, he says. It's like moving from a Maserati to a dump truck, and she smells like one.

beats.headline: Mongo is all alone
beats.text: I had a whole plan to upset him, including banners making fun of the Maestro, and he spoils it by crying and talking about his daughter blowing up the sun. Most inconvenient. When it's over I ask Carl if he was telling the truth. Does that mean we're all about to die? That all of this was for nothing? We have to go back. Mongo is all alone! Then Carl tells me in private that the failsafe won't work, and calls it a hunch. That's a pretty big hunch, Carl.

beats.headline: Spill the tea
beats.text: I land in Carl's lap in Orren's office, and Growler Gary is alive! Carl gives me three quick taps. Gary needs relationship advice, and obviously Carl and Orren are no use. When Orren says the girl looks like Agatha I make one small remark about hygiene, and Gary cracks the desk with his hand. I do not flinch. Then I give him my advice. If a bunch of people want someone dead, that person is really good or really bad. Find out which. Even then, stay out of it unless you have no choice.

beats.headline: Much too poor
beats.text: While Carl was busy I had a little chat with Stalwart. He demanded his father's ring, his body and the credits. I told him his father's skin is now a powder room rug, which it is not, and that his father called him a disappointment before he died, which is the one thing I am not lying about. He says he will boil the fur off my skin. I told him he is much too poor to be talking to me like this. I do feel a little bad about the poor line.

beats.headline: Filth, clutter, squalor
beats.text: Carl's new tattoo is a little crooked. The system calls it expert quality, but I should have been there. Closing off the saferoom from the base is causing all sorts of problems. We have been separated, Tipid has to build more bathrooms, the whole base smells like Carl's friend Sam, and nobody can take a shower. I will not have a filthy army. With filth comes clutter, and with clutter comes squalor. Carl says to tell Tipid I want showers. I think Carl should tell him. I don't like being separated like this.

beats.headline: Princess TV, and a word for Vinata
beats.text: Carl asked me to stall, so I stall. Everyone at this table has their own channel and the Princess Posse does not, which is quite unfair, so I propose Princess TV: reruns of the Earth classics, Golden Girls, an exposé on Mongo's greatest kills. Imagine the ratings. Then Odette says the Sultanate made Blood Hunter, and I realise which show that is. The one with the pterodactyl and the vampire hunter. I look the naga princess up and down and address her directly for the first time. Oh, honey. And I thought I was going to be the one who killed you.

beats.headline: It should be purple
beats.text: The Nest should be purple. Gray is clinical. Boring. And it needs flags, and its own unit patch, with Mongo on it. Toyotomi says it is the colour of granite because it is made of granite. My tiara has thirty-five of its ninety-nine skills and upgrades now; the newest is Perfect Night Vision, drained out of a hat, so I can see the builders at the very top in the dark. Carl keeps asking Toyotomi the same questions over and over. I'll be fine, Carl. Especially if the tower is painted purple.

beats.headline: I do not ask permission
beats.text: They installed the wireless PA speakers in time, the deluxe package, with more speakers than towers, and it hooks into my headset with one of those recording studio boards with all the slidy dials. Distortion. Reverb. Something called a phaser. Carl says to get Li Na's permission before I use it. I am a warlord. I do not ask permission, I give orders. I will warn them, though. Carl says to aim my shots, breathe, and make each one count. I know I can do this. I am a warlord.

beats.headline: A ball of everyone
beats.text: Everyone Eris summoned is in one pile beside the Dream castle, friends and enemies all mixed in, and if the invulnerability goes they will be crushed. Carl wants to go. I tell him to finish his mission and let me deal with the pile. Rolling Battle Formation, from that skunk's stinky wizard hat. It is an Atrocity spell, and the tower makes it really, really big. I can drive it like a remote control. Unfortunately Meatus got pulled in too, still wrapped around Eris. In my defence, I did not know the dink would be included.

beats.headline: A song for Harpocrates
beats.text: Harpocrates is chasing my ball, trying to get his stolen wiener back, and guys are single-minded about that. So I tell Li Na's people to cover their ears and I get on the PA, with reverb and a little delay. Hey, dickless. It's gone. You should accept your body how it is. My friend Lil Wayne wrote you a song. It's Lollipop, and it's bass-heavy, and the ground shakes, and he stops and covers his ears. It's working. I'm starting a battle playlist. Message me your songs.

beats.headline: A second atrocity
beats.text: The ball reaches the field of corpses and I cast You're Not Done Yet, tower-enhanced, on all of them at once. The system calls it another Atrocity and me a naughty kitty. Thousands of skins come up and go looking for the Dream and the Reaver soldiers inside the ball. Then I start hitting it with Magic Missile to break it open, and Carl and Li Na both tell me to stop. Our friends are in there, Carl, with fleshers crawling all over them. He wants it kept whole and rolled toward the city. So I set it rolling toward Larracos.

beats.headline: Donkey Kong
beats.text: Lucia is in the tower, coming up the stairs, shouting for Mongo, and Bomo and the others are dead. I cannot leave; there is a net. I tell Carl to get the war mages, because the castle is more important than me. He says he is coming and to do Donkey Kong. So I hit the switch, and the stairs turn into a ramp, and I roll barrels. The sleep barrel does not work. She crawls on the ceiling and blocks explosions. Mute does not work on her. I have a better idea. I summon Raul.

beats.headline: Level seventy-four
beats.text: I am in my ghillie suit at the parapet, sniping. The war mage atop that death ray tower is not so tough with his head blown off. Carl says to focus on the towers hitting the Nest, and then he holds out his arms, and I blink and jump into them and go round his neck like I used to when he came home from work. I went up this tower at level 65. I am 74 now. My Magic Missile is level fifteen, and it tripled in power. And Rend saved my boy.

beats.headline: A tattoo on the right flank
beats.text: Rosetta says it has to be a tattoo, with Milk etching words of power over it, and Edgar wants a spot on my backside shaved as big as his foot. I never agreed to a tattoo! Carl says I don't have to, and nobody will fault me. I tell him about the scars. I hoped none of them would be on the outside. He says if I choose it, it is a badge of honour. Fine. Only if he gets a matching one. And not a tramp stamp. Then I ask Edgar what he is drawing. A dog.

beats.headline: A dog that licks itself
beats.text: It's done, and I have received two very rude achievements, one calling me a traitor. But I did get the spell, at level two. It came from a god called Wepwawet, in the Court of Nekhebit, and I can worship Odette now too! Cover it up. It is getting lasered off on the next floor. Not yet, says Milk, and writes words of power over it, which stings. Apparently the dog underneath lifts its leg and starts licking itself. I am not looking. The spell has gone up to level fifteen.

beats.headline: Three baps, and again
beats.text: Carl says anything but fire, so it is Bijanbi and Astral Paw. The messages call me the Oak Fell, and a champion, and then I can't move and my health is draining. Outside, the paw hangs over the hole with thousands of soldiers and a god floating up under it. Carl gets the healing scroll on me. I shouldn't have picked Astral Paw. I have to do it myself. I can feel them under my paw. Li Na builds a lattice of chains and says it is all she can build. I close my eyes and swipe down. Three quick baps. Then again, until the screaming stops.

beats.headline: Level one hundred and thirty-five
beats.text: I sit up and compose myself. I still have my Former Child Actor benefits, with the Oak Fell class and the champion title on top. I don't have to worship Nekhebit, only nobody outside her court. For strength I pick Muscle Mommy, so Mongo gets a quarter of mine. Brain Trust for intelligence. Wholesale Discount, for my charisma topping two hundred. Level one hundred and thirty-five! I am once again the strongest crawler in the dungeon. Mongo stays caged. If he eats any of that Meatus, I could never look at him the same again.

beats.headline: Druid spells and a vermin call
beats.text: My Oak Fell spells are enormous. Raise Forest sprouts trees and plants over a kilometre per level of the spell. Another turns water into salt water. Gather Ye, Vermin draws every mammal under a certain size within ten kilometres, which is clearly the pervert AI's doing so Carl can summon squishables. Map the All Tree costs one mana and only works on the twelfth floor and deeper. And Carl can play his bagpipes now! We can play at Louis's second wedding. He says the bagpipes are staying in the folder.

beats.headline: Epitome Tagg's Sexy Mother
beats.text: I didn't get to say goodbye to Katia. Then Mordecai needs Tagg distracted while they have Louis open, so I ask him how he will look his mother in the eye, knowing Louis had sex with her. He insists it was a changeling. So I change my name to Epitome Tagg's Sexy Mother and ask Louis to come help with my hand stuck in the washing machine. He screams at me to change it back. I can't. No more name changes until tomorrow. Carl says stall, not provoke. We're playing good cop, bad cop.

beats.headline: We just need to kill you
beats.text: Huanxin wants Katia to choose so they can go. Darling, I have a better idea. Laundry Day, level sixteen now, and she is ripped out of the goddess onto a circle of words of power where she can't teleport. My Claw, nearly fifteen, takes her shields. I have Katia's knee pads on, the goddess's boon gives me 500 percent, and Carl's party bonus another 500. The Apothecary's box was a weapon mount, and Katia's crossbow is on my back. Mordecai loads one bolt. We don't need to kill the gods and goddesses to win. The crossbow fires. We just need to kill you.

beats.headline: They are not going to break me
beats.text: Katia left two things on the table. Her card from the last floor, with Annie the skull-headed bird on it, which I take, and a bra with Carl's face on one cup, which Elle takes. I feel really bad now about having pooped in Mordecai's mother's ashes. It was supposed to be a grand gesture. Carl says don't you dare tell Mordecai. At the stairwell he asks if I'm doing okay. I'm going to miss her. But they are not going to break me. No matter how hard they try.

beats.headline: Her new attorney
beats.text: A Naga called Princess Chandra, Esquire, informs me that she is my attorney now, not Quasar, and that I have been put under a conservatorship with Carl as my guardian. She has married him, too, through some widow's law, and she has seized the Posse's accounts. I refuse every deal, since Carl is refusing his. Then I read every one of her papers and tell her what they say about her. And, for any reporters watching, I am most definitely not offering fifty million credits to anyone who turns her inside out on my behalf.

beats.headline: Assassin of Sekhmet
beats.text: Four minutes to pick a new class, which is simply not enough time for a decision of this importance. The Las Vegas Showgirl comes with a feathered hat for Mongo. Mordecai suggests Zoo Warden, which I will not dignify. Then there is a whole new tab tied to my deity titles, and even Mordecai says it is new to him. I take Assassin of Sekhmet: a healing aura, a hat, and accessories for every pet in the party. And straight away, a very nasty message from Khepri, the bug god, saying he is forming a death cult in my name.

beats.headline: Two missiles for a manatee
beats.text: The manatee is called Miss Talulah, she is level ninety, and she smells simply awful. Two magic missiles and she collapses into the water with holes in her you could put a soccer ball through. I am the number one crawler at level 135, so this is hardly surprising. Then a notification: I must choose the fate of my kill. Keep it dead for regular experience, or let the audience vote. It says the second choice will be more fun. Naturally, I pick the second choice. Results pending.

beats.headline: Fatty
beats.text: A unicorn in a tumbleweed calls me fatty, and the bug-eyed rat in a racing helmet on his head calls me a corpulent swine. Fatty! I stand in the road and explain that I am practically twice their levels and that their mount is very likely flammable, and Carl tells me to let them go around, which I do not, and then Mongo leans on the horn and they run over everything anyway. As soon as the next race starts, I am setting them on fire. Also, my vote came back: the people have chosen Otto the slime guy to be the manatee's stand-in in the arena. That is all it says.

beats.headline: A godslayer box
beats.text: Forty boxes, and the achievements are mostly rude. Emergency Gremlin scrolls by the dozen, apparently for when the truck breaks down mid-race. Crossbow bolts that pin whatever they hit in place. A crupper that matches my champion cloak. And then the celestial godslayer box, which is only smoke: it becomes Meatus, and a smoky paw comes down on him, and Rosetta says she can still taste it. No prize falls out. My right front paw, the one I used for the War Crime, starts to glow, and it hurts, and I stretch my claws, and the kitchen table rips in half.

beats.headline: Blue claws, and caps
beats.text: The claws glow blue. Blue! Like cheap LED lights, and they will not turn off. Mordecai calls it a boon. They cut through anything, which is lovely until one considers my litter box, and Carl's shoulder, and biscuits. Rosetta finds claw caps on the shop wall and buys red ones, so the glow comes out purple, which I suppose will have to do. Then the crupper's description, which is about a gnoll I killed and his children, and I do not wish to discuss it. It made me choose a spell. Puddle Jumper is now level sixteen.

beats.headline: Rule number one
beats.text: Prepotente has a biscuit that makes whoever eats it fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them, and he came to me for advice, which was the correct instinct. My advice is absolutely not. She would be level one and stuck with us, and it is a crime against nature besides. So I am compiling him a list of rules to live by. Rule number one: do not use magic to make someone fall in love with you. It is creepy. Rule number two is to stop arguing with me.

beats.headline: Is Katia okay?
beats.text: A greenroom at the bottom of the ocean and no snacks, which is not how Prepotente described this show. And Lexis is here! She has a minute, she says, so I ask the only thing that matters: is Katia okay? Something strange happened at the kinder facility after Faction Wars. A third party has appeared and is protecting it, and it is confused. She believes Katia is okay. Then her tablet beeps and all the colour goes out of her face, and I do not get to ask anything else.

beats.headline: The War Crime question
beats.text: A goat judges me worthy and asks which three spells I would combine if I cast War Crime a second time. I stiffen. Then I compose myself, because we are live and I am a professional. It will depend on the circumstances. Nothing is off the table. But I cannot cast it until the twelfth floor, and Carl and I must first get through these next two. The goat nods. I ask whether it is my turn to ask. It says yes, and the table turns to the next goat anyway.

beats.headline: A throne called Dorota
beats.text: The audience voted me a throne, which shows some of them have taste. It is a Smart Companion Royal Pet Throne, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition, and the moment I sit on it a little fluffy bed appears, it holds me steady like a gyro, and it feeds me snacks on demand. It came with a creepy man's voice, so I had it changed to a woman with a Polish accent, and I have named her Dorota. She agrees with everything I say. Dr. Metcalf is jealous.

beats.headline: A letter from Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in my Banquet Fit for a Princess, from a crawler I do not remember: Luca Di, a Pastamancer, who gave me his train hat on the fourth floor. His mother had dementia. On the third floor she took a race that mended her mind, and they talked, properly, before she fell on the bubble level. He says I saved that for him. He says it is all right to forgive myself for War Crime. The spell he left me is Temporary Macaroni.

beats.headline: A tunnel of cannelloni
beats.text: I killed more than ten thousand of them and did not go up a level. That is an outrage. Then the skulls come up out of the road and down out of the sky, and I cast Temporary Macaroni, which I have had for about a minute, and I chain it: uncooked cannelloni, a foot thick, a tunnel of it. When Gluteus passes out on the wheel I rip myself free of Dorota's belt and hold the accelerator down with both paws. We win.

beats.headline: Easier not to like him
beats.text: The gauge at the Lollipop was clearly broken. I sang Journey and it did not move, and Finley says I did fine, and I thank him. Then Osvaldo is in our heat and tells Carl something extremely vulgar, so I tell him he is only alive because of me and Carl, and he is a straight-to-video leprechaun. Carl says he is not an enemy. He is not going to help us. It is us or him. It will be easier if we stay not liking each other.

beats.headline: The Astral Paw, and a bite
beats.text: Cannibals, hundreds of them, dropping out of the trees and bursting on our shield. I swipe my Astral Paw and sweep the arch clear like pieces off a chessboard. Elle calls me terrifying, which is fair. It is a lot stronger than it was, but it does not last, and now I cannot cast it for eight hours, and I killed about eighty and did not go up a level, which is ridiculous. Then something bites my bottom. I believe it was the dog tattoo.

beats.headline: What she tells the shark
beats.text: I Hover up to the ceiling and whisper to him, and he flips down and lands right by the truck. Carl asks what I said. I told him it is true, it could happen at any moment, but if we worry about things we cannot control, we ruin the things we can. And even if he is annoying, he is family now, and he should tell us when he is in trouble, because family helps. Mongo, mind Mommy and guard Hedy.

beats.headline: Relationship advice for a pig
beats.text: Carl wants a distraction, so I take the driveway with my headset microphone and address the fake tiger people. My charisma is high enough now that All Eyes on Me works with plain talking, no singing required. I explain to Penelope that throuples in which two members are at each other's throats end in heartbreak, and then Miss Piggy, and Piglet, and Wilbur, and Peppa. They cannot look away. By the time I wave goodbye they do not even know they were charmed.

beats.headline: Jezebel the hedgehog
beats.text: Satan is a hedgehog, a kaiju-sized one, and I would bet anything he talks with a fake British accent, and I do not care what Carl says, this has nothing to do with Tacoma. Yes, there was a Cutest in Show, and yes, I was a kitten, and yes, the winner was a baby hedgehog from a rescue named Jezebel, and Miss Beatrice sulked all day. It was fixed from the beginning. Who names a hedgehog Jezebel? It hardly matters now. I have raised the toad, head caved in and all, to drive us.

beats.headline: We are calling her Chachi
beats.text: WE'RE JUST GOING TO CALL HER CHACHI. I only have so much room on my cut-and-paste, and I am not filling it with a name that long. Anyway, it is concert day. Prepotente is coming, and he is singing as well, which is lovely for him. Mine is a surprise. It will be a duet with Carl, and he has to take a great many potions and scrolls first so that he does not mess it up. Then we go and collect the pig from the empty house.

beats.headline: She is not a weapon
beats.text: Carl says we need people like Li Na, because she is so strong. She is not a weapon, Carl. She is a person. I like her, of course I do, but we cannot let her keep hurting people, and we certainly cannot let Zhang kill himself to stop her. That is not right, and I told Zhang no, twice. We will find something to fix this. Somebody has to talk some sense into her. It is the only way.

beats.headline: Robbed of a perfect score
beats.text: My part was perfect, Auto-Tuned and in key, and in the middle of a chorus I shot the axe out of a Draconian's hand before he could put it in Dong's head. Then, on my very last line, a paralysed kappa fell backward right into me, and now there is a sign over my head that says FAILED. I was robbed of a perfect score. Carl has to go through the glowing door by himself. We are never going to mention this again. I do love that song, though.

beats.headline: A letter from a half-orc
beats.text: The newest entry in my Feast book is from Mees Koning, a half-orc mage, final level sixty-three. Before the battle at the southern border I stopped at his stinger unit and told him I liked his fangs, and we talked for maybe a minute, and he says it was the first time anyone had been nice to him just to be nice. He was inside the ball when I cast my Atrocity. He drew me a magnet, a very well-shaded one. It is called Big-Ass Magnet. I did not choose the name.

beats.headline: Twice now
beats.text: At the shop terminal, as the white bot sold, Mordecai's hood came down, his head was on fire, and he said something about the Oak Fell in a deep voice that was not his usual one. Then he blinked, patted the fire out and carried on as if nothing had happened. He said that would only happen once. That is twice now. Carl says he told us to ignore it. It is really scary, and I do not like it, and nobody is explaining it to me.

beats.headline: Not a kangaroo anymore
beats.text: The Dominators' car went through a hole in the floor, and I saw it, so I made Carl stop and reverse. It is a ten-metre drop, and horrible little dolls are tearing the car apart. Carl wants to jump down. And then what, Carl? You are not a kangaroo anymore. I got this. I land on the car and cast Puddle Jumper. I cannot teleport Corky into the truck, so I bring us both up to the road beside it, which is the next-best thing. My fur is smoking.

beats.headline: Laundry Day, and then a magnet
beats.text: Grull came crashing through a wall with that awful Maestro riding inside him, so I cast Laundry Day, and the orc dropped out of the god's chest into the molten metal. We do not have time to kill you now. Maybe next time! But Corcunda is still marked, and he and Dong decide to go and meet the god themselves, and I try to say no, and I cannot finish saying it. So I cast Big-Ass Magnet on Dong's lance, the spell that was meant for the Dominators' car. Every screw in the room goes with them.

beats.headline: Dong is dead
beats.text: We came in last place, and the stupid unicorn won by going over the factory instead of through it, which is cheating, and Osvaldo agrees with me. Dong is dead. He was my friend. Grigori says some people believe death is only a movement on to another plane, and that Dong did not think it was the end. Perhaps. It is still horrible for those of us who are still here. Grigori agrees.

beats.headline: Not speaking to Carl
beats.text: I am not speaking to Carl. His strategy has him leaving the party for the eleventh floor, so that I do not get hurt, as if I cannot look after myself. So I am sitting in the stables while Rosetta explains dungeon lore that will not matter because we will all be dead in a few hours. A child who can take the powers of gods and use them for herself, just like that Spock on the show with the cheerleader. Carl laughed. You are not allowed to laugh at my observations, Carl.

beats.headline: The message board caught him
beats.text: Let the record show it WAS NOT ME. It was the Princess Posse message board. Linus is the brother, which was the big theory, and WriggleInDew2023 of the Mongo Mommies Valtay chapter said all along he was no Valtay agent, and she will be thrilled. He leaned far too hard into the romantic material, which real admirers rarely say out loud, and one of his brother's friends noticed his tattoo was wrong. Honestly. He could at least have taken acting lessons. He is worse than Prepotente, and I mean that with love.

beats.headline: Plan Mach Schnell
beats.text: Carl is a dog now and cannot even say the name of the plan properly. It is Mach Schnell. Dorota rolls the window down for me, bless her. When the light goes green I am through the window as smoke and onto the roof before the vine has finished dying, and before Osvaldo's gnu has stopped staggering I take that tiresome unicorn's head off with one swipe and his horn goes into my inventory. The announcement is complimentary. I prefer decisive. Carl is wagging again.

beats.headline: Astral Paw on the Cadillac
beats.text: The Russian car throws itself up on end in the middle of the lobby to make a run for the exit, after all our planning and all Imani's pleading. The APV and Chris's truck fire into its shield, Prepotente throws something, and the shield flickers out. So I cast Astral Paw and the Cadillac simply ceases to exist, all in less than a second. Three new skulls over my head before Carl can even think a rude word.

beats.headline: She tells the giant Imani it is a dream
beats.text: The giant Imani is sitting in the lobby holding Gucci, and the building will not let her leave, and she says she should have left them all when she had the chance. So I switch on my headset microphone. Darling, this is a dream. Out in the real world you already left: Detroit, then Washington, and friends named Yolanda and Brandon and Elle, and a man named Chris, and happily ever after. Close your eyes. Before that I moved Onikuma and Old Shuck into our garage with Dwight's keys. We will need them. I am not discussing it.

beats.headline: The pickle class
beats.text: Mordecai, help me pick a class. Comeback Kid comes with a movie deal, which is obviously me, but CARL says my Glass Cannon ruins it, because you get all your old bad parts back too. So: Elite Gurkha Warrior. It sounds like a pickle. Extra skills for pets and mercenaries, a big claw upgrade for Mongo, Cockroach to fifteen. Carl says I am going to pick it, so I nearly didn't. I picked it. Also, his psychotic wife tried to accept a deal on my behalf, and then got scared and vanished.

beats.headline: An advance copy of a spell
beats.text: My new spell book is a paperback, which is common. Tome of Gatekeeper, an Advance Reader Copy: I may install it now, and it works on the twelfth floor. It takes away a target's class skills for a while, even a god's. The duration is nerd math. And I got a Legendary box for seeing the shadow mimic before he revealed himself, and a Legendary Steed upgrade so Mongo can pull a cart.

beats.headline: Her title goes with his
beats.text: I do not like this. Carl's royal bodyguard title has gone, and now his says nothing at all. Then he grins and tells me mine has gone too. MINE. I am not the one who left the stupid party, and I cannot even add a new one. This is so unfair. At least the float is beautiful: Requite Dahlias from my Sprout Forest, black and gold and magenta and white, which match the Gurkha blankets, on every square inch of everything.

beats.headline: I love you too
beats.text: At the arena door Carl lifts me off his shoulder and holds me much too tightly and tells me to get to Elle and Imani and stay away. I know the plan. I am scared, and I say so. Then he says he loves me, and then he starts on if this doesn't work, and I will not let him jinx it. People keep asking how he would react if something happened to me. Nobody asks me. I love him too.

beats.headline: Two bolts, and Puddle Jumper
beats.text: Now. One of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps swaps me into the room and the pig out to Taranis's feet. Scorpion's Bite on my back, Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus loaded, and it goes straight into Emberus's eye. The second, one of my Danforth bolts, goes into the other, and he cannot move. Toodles. Puddle Jumper, level seventeen, and Carl and I are outside the arena door. When he tells me to get off his motorcycle, I tell him exactly where he can go.

beats.headline: His inventory is a disgrace
beats.text: Eris swaps everybody's pockets and I get Carl's, and it is not organised. Rocks, CARL. Why are there rocks. Why is a chicken and goblin recipe book in his hotlist. He shouts at me to combine the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve, and my hotlist only has ten slots, so I search and combine and drop it into his xistera, very fast, while the centipede glows.

beats.headline: The wrong biscuit
beats.text: I am sitting in the dirt and not being sarcastic, which should tell everyone something. Carl sends me a party request and I accept it without a word. Then I have to tell him. Don't get mad. The inventory was happening so fast. The goo drains away and there is a centipede with lips and a red bow, and she is not a pet. She is Sexy Scolopendra, level one, crawler, in our party. I gave him the wrong biscuit.

relations.note: She considers him her son. He agrees.

entities.name: Mongo
entities.tagline: I am small, and pink, and in a cage. The cat gives me biscuits. I bite the cat.
entities.voiceNote: Does not talk. What the camera gets is the dinosaur: single words, capitals, appetite. MOTHER is Donut. Everything else is FOOD, NOT FOOD, or BAD. Never more than a few short lines.

beats.headline: Seven inches of pink feathers, in a cage
beats.text: CAGE. Small. Pink? Pink. TWO BIG THINGS. Bite them. Bite them. Bite. Biscuits. FOOD. Peck. Peck. Cat pats head. Bite cat.

beats.headline: MOTHER comes fast
beats.text: BUG. Big bug holds Mongo. Up. Mouth. MOTHER comes fast. Bug head OFF. Mongo down. Mongo MOTHER'S now. Jump. Jump. Bite MOTHER nose.

beats.headline: Bow tie, three seconds
beats.text: BOW on neck. BAD. Off. Lady hand. Bite. MOTHER's back. Hold fur. Quiet. Quiet. Wall. WALL. Wall. MOTHER's tail. Bite.

beats.headline: Clown ankle
beats.text: Clown DOWN. Ankle. Bite. Bite. BITE. Mongo is BIGGER. Carl picks Mongo up. NO. Clown is FOOD.

beats.headline: Two more Mongos
beats.text: Mongo BIGGER. Too big for Mother's back. Collar. BAD. Mother says no. Collar stays. Two more Mongos! FRIENDS! Friends fall apart. Mongo sad. Mother, AGAIN.

beats.headline: Lion belly
beats.text: LION. Big FOOD. Belly. Rip. Rip. Lion swipes. Lion dead. Mongo on lion. RIP. Mongo BIGGER. Bigger than Mother.

beats.headline: Guarding Mother
beats.text: Mother asleep. Mother does NOT wake. Carl builds pile around Mother. Carl says STAY. Protect. Mongo on top of pile. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: He stands over her
beats.text: Mother down. Mother NOT MOVING. Mongo on top of Mother. Spiky things. MANY spiky things. Bite. Bite. Bite. Hurts. Mongo stays on Mother. Carl says something. Mongo does not listen to Carl.

beats.headline: Brown drink, then big
beats.text: Carl back. Carl pours brown drink in Mongo mouth. Spikes fall out. Mongo BIG now. Mother wakes up. MOTHER. Jump on Mother. Jump on Mother again.

beats.headline: Sparks
beats.text: Carl puts shiny teeth in Mongo mouth. Bite. SPARKS. Mongo scared. Mongo wet. Mordecai LOUD. Bite again. Sparks do not hurt Mongo. Bite. Bite. Bite. GOOD.

beats.headline: The smell in the alley
beats.text: Out of box. Street. Carl throws biscuit. GOOD. Then SMELL. Burning meat. Mongo must go. Mongo goes. Carl yells. Mother yells. Tall one. Tall one falls down. Head. Mongo has head. Shake head.

beats.headline: Benjamin, twice
beats.text: FOOD. Small lizard on a stick. BAD. Lizard comes back up. Small dwarf hits me. Arm is FOOD, and lizard again. MOTHER says HOLD. Tummy BAD. Small dwarf wants arm back. Give.

beats.headline: Pony-sized
beats.text: Cold ghosts. Bite! Level thirteen. BIG now. MOTHER on my back! Jump! Jump! MOTHER falls off. MOTHER angry.

beats.headline: Hanging ladies
beats.text: Hanging ladies. Heads FOOD. Crunch. Crunch. Crunch. One head NOT THERE. Bite legs instead. MOTHER says RETURN. Ladies wake up. Screaming. More FOOD.

beats.headline: Rabbits make everybody sick but him
beats.text: RABBIT hums. Carl falls down. MOTHER is sick. Mongo is not sick. Rabbit is FOOD. Level fourteen. Bigger now.

beats.headline: Earthquake
beats.text: Armadillo is FOOD. Crunchy. Level fifteen. Big now, big as a pony. New trick: jump, land, EARTHQUAKE. Bad things fall down. MOTHER says good boy.

beats.headline: The saddle
beats.text: MOTHER on back. Strap holds MOTHER. BAD. Mongo bucks. MOTHER flies. MOTHER lands on the potion table. Carl laughs. Katia laughs. MOTHER says BAD MONGO. Mongo rolls over. Off, saddle. OFF.

beats.headline: Down the tracks
beats.text: MOTHER on back. Down the dark tracks. Mongo RUN. Really, really fast. Dead things on tracks. MOTHER finds map. MOTHER finds gold. MOTHER says Mongo FAST.

beats.headline: Floor is FOOD
beats.text: LOCKED UP. Too long. Mongo squawks at them. Then: blood. Blood on Carl. Blood on Mother. Lick Carl. Carl smacks beak. Blood on floor. Mongo cleans floor.

beats.headline: Face first, then the hands
beats.text: Bar dog asleep. Mother says GO. Face first. Arms off at the elbow, onto the counter. NOT FOOD. Back to bar. Again. Again. Bar dog in the corner with a stick. Mother says WAIT.

beats.headline: Blood rain
beats.text: Katia goes BOOM. Red. Red EVERYWHERE. Rain! Mongo spins. Mongo splashes. Tap, tap, splash. MOTHER jumps away. Mongo stays. Mongo dances.

beats.headline: Spiky lizard eats the copies
beats.text: Two Mongos, not Mongo. Big spiky lizard. Copies BITE. Lizard CRUNCH copy. Lizard CRUNCH other copy. Mongo HOWL. MOTHER says stay back. Mongo stays. Pieces on sand. Mongo sad.

beats.headline: Too much UP
beats.text: UP. Too much UP. Brothers jump off. Basket rocks. MOTHER says carrier. NO. Carl yells very loud. Fine. Carrier.

beats.headline: Small NOT MOTHER
beats.text: Small MOTHER. Smells wrong. NOT MOTHER. Says bad things about dogs. BITE. Head off. Fire. MOTHER says bad Mongo. Too late.

beats.headline: Goose NOT FOOD
beats.text: Brothers go POP. Hurts. Goose. BITE goose. Shake goose. Goose gets up. Goose has teeth. MOTHER pulls tail. Up the stairs. Rabbit. Mine.

beats.headline: Rabbit for small gnome
beats.text: Small gnome sad. Crying smell. Rabbit from her room. Rabbit NOT FOOD. Put rabbit down. Small gnome holds rabbit.

beats.headline: The glass lady falls
beats.text: Sniff the glass lady. She WOBBLES. BAD. Back away. CRASH. Glass everywhere. Only her head stays. Carl puts the head away.

beats.headline: He finishes Maggie My
beats.text: Thing on Chris. Thing OFF Chris. Thing goes for Carl. Thing is FOOD.

beats.headline: No dinosaurs
beats.text: Mushroom points stick at Mongo. Mongo SCREECH. Mushrooms GROWL. Paper says NO DINOSAURS. Bear falls down hill. River eats bear. Carl slaps. Mongo RUN.

beats.headline: Kiwi
beats.text: Smell. Out there. Mongo RUN. MOTHER on back. Many Mongos. Big one. Pink feathers. One eye. Mongo GROWL. Big one says UNK UNK UNK. Mongo says UNK. Not fight.

beats.headline: In one side, out the other
beats.text: BIG FROG. FIRE HOLE IN FROG. MOTHER JUMPS OFF. MONGO GOES IN. MONGO EATS THROUGH. MONGO COMES OUT THE BACK. FROG GOES BOOM. MORE GUTS. FOOD.

beats.headline: Small bears, hiding
beats.text: Big one outside. Roar. Mongo SCREECH. MOTHER say shush. Small bears behind counter. Scared. Mongo peep. Small bear say Mongo not bad one. MOTHER say Mongo nice.

beats.headline: Glass of Mongo
beats.text: Sleep. Wake. Big glass of red. Smells like Mongo. NOT FOOD. BAD. Carl BAD. Next town, box on wall. Dinosaurs in box! Mongo jump. Mongo SCREECH.

beats.headline: LADIES
beats.text: MOTHER lets me out. KIWI! BITE. So many LADIES.

beats.headline: Two in the trees
beats.text: Hunters run at Carl. JUMP. Kiwi jumps too. Two for two. FOOD. MOTHER says good boy!

beats.headline: Mongo moonwalks
beats.text: SMOKE. LOUD. MOTHER on back. EARTHQUAKE. Stomp. Three lady Mongos. MOTHER says taken. Mongo DANCES. Backwards. MOTHER bops.

beats.headline: Finish her
beats.text: BUG. Mongo and Kiwi. Bite. Rip. BUG has no legs. Carl says finish. Make it hurt. Kiwi touches heads with Mongo. Kiwi goes. Mongo finishes BUG. Happy.

beats.headline: Shiny man
beats.text: SHINY MAN. OTHER MONGO IN SHINY MAN. PUSH FACE. SHINY MAN FALL DOWN. LOUD! SHINY MAN LAUGH. GOOD SHINY MAN.

beats.headline: Purple thing
beats.text: BIG LOUD CROWD. PURPLE THING! MONGO JUMP. MONGO BITE. PURPLE THING GONE. NOTHING LEFT. MONGO ANGRY.

beats.headline: On slug duty, for now
beats.text: SLUGS COME OUT OF CARL. SLUGS ARE FOOD. MOTHER SAYS EAT THE NUN. CARL SAYS WAIT. MOTHER SAYS NOT YET. SLUG DUTY. FOR NOW.

beats.headline: Hairy lady under the leaves
beats.text: Samantha SMELLS something. Leaf pile, big tree. Hairy lady asleep inside. Feet on backward. POUNCE. BITE BITE. Gone before anyone can look at her. She drops two cards.

beats.headline: The man in the sailor suit
beats.text: MOTHER ALONE. MOTHER SCARED. BAD MAN WITH CARDS. SEAL FLIPPING. MONGO JUMPS. THROAT. BAD MAN GONE. FOOD.

beats.headline: Swordfish
beats.text: FISH FLIES AT CARL. MONGO JUMPS. CATCH. GROUND SHAKES. FISH FLOP. THEN BUGS. SHINY BUGS. BAD. BAD. MONGO BACKS AWAY.

beats.headline: Turkeys
beats.text: SO MUCH FOOD. MONGO EATS HEADS. MOTHER SAYS BAD. MOTHER SAYS COME HERE. MORE FOOD. ONE TURKEY NOT FOOD. BITE. BITE. NOTHING. DARK.

beats.headline: Fake Carl
beats.text: FAKE CARL. FOOT ON CARL. BAD. MONGO HITS. FAKE CARL GONE. RED FOOD EVERYWHERE. MONGO EATS.

beats.headline: All of the hydra
beats.text: Hydra breaks. Spaghetti. FOOD. ALL FOOD. Belly hurts now. Lie down by Mother.

beats.headline: A hole under his feet
beats.text: Mongo stands by Mother. Zombie is BAD. Rip. Fish opens a hole under Mongo. Fish is BAD. Rip in half.

beats.headline: Awake, and a wing gone
beats.text: WING GONE. Burns. MOTHER rides. Running. Fire. CARL AWAKE. CARL SAYS SORRY. Push head into CARL. GOOD.

beats.headline: A potion smashed on his rump
beats.text: WING GONE. Mongo looks. Wing GONE? Mother says sit. Carl smashes glass on Mongo's butt. Sparkly. Healing. Mongo does not mind.

beats.headline: Small thing, in and out
beats.text: Small thing. Jumps IN mouth. Mother yells. Mongo swallows. Hurk. Hurk. Out again. Small thing wants back in. Mongo runs. Then: bowl. Small thing pushes bowl. SOUP. Mongo licks it all.

beats.headline: Kiwi goes inside
beats.text: Big one says PA-PA. Bear comes out. Kiwi. KIWI. Sniff. Kiwi hugs Mongo. Mongo stays still. Kiwi goes inside. Big one goes inside. Mongo sniffs air. Peep.

beats.headline: STINK, and a branch
beats.text: Skunks. STINK. Mongo in tree. Mongo sick. Sick again. MOTHER jumps onto Mongo branch. Branch goes crack. MOTHER falls. Mongo falls. Cage. Mongo whimpers.

beats.headline: Credit for the Empress
beats.text: EMPRESS is down. Mongo gets the KILL. System says so. Blue goo on the WALL. Lick the wall. MOTHER says broken home. Mongo SQUAWKS. Yes.

beats.headline: The bacon is not his
beats.text: BACON. From Katia. In the air. Mine. Second bacon, for the new one. Also mine. MOTHER says BAD. Mongo does not steal. Mongo wants third bacon.

beats.headline: Dog is BAD
beats.text: MOTHER says NO. Mongo goes down slide. Dog. Dog is BAD. Bite dog. Dog is spikes. Spikes in mouth. HURTS. Dark. Girl pours drink on Mongo. Mongo not dead.

beats.headline: Going to be a daddy
beats.text: MOTHER says Mongo DADDY. I tilt my head. MOTHER says Kiwi. MOTHER says BABY. I back up. Screech. Screech. Rend giggles.

beats.headline: Two babies
beats.text: Kiwi says MONGO. MOTHER says go. I go. Kiwi screams. A baby cries. Another baby cries. Fur. Beaks. I wave my wings. Carl pats my back.

beats.headline: NOT FOOD
beats.text: Wet plastic heart on the ground. BAD. I bite. I chew. I chew more. NOT FOOD. Spit. The System gives Mongo the kill. For the baby shower.

beats.headline: Nearly lost, and then a father
beats.text: Mongo, dinosaur, registered pet of Crawler Princess Donut, has survived the ninth floor. This was not the expected outcome. The last of Lucia Mar's dogs very nearly ate him, and Sir Rendlegore saved him, and the dog died. Mongo is also, as of the stairs, a father. Nobody is going to explain that to you, least of all me.

beats.headline: HAT
beats.text: MOTHER has a HAT. Hat is NOT FOOD. Mongo backs UP. Dong puts hat on Mongo anyway. Floppy ears. Hat is fine. Rend gets red one. Fries are FOOD.

beats.headline: Beer is FOOD
beats.text: Bug-bear man pours BEER. Slug drinks it. Mongo WANTS. MOTHER says NO. Mongo does not stay back. Now floor moves. Tater tots. FOOD. Mongo waves both wings. HAPPY.

beats.headline: Friend is dead. Friend is not dead.
beats.text: Rend not moving. Mongo stands over Rend and cries. MOTHER says time-out. Then Rend is up. Rend is BIGGER. Mongo dances. Ghoul things at door. Mongo turns too fast. Falls over.

beats.headline: He guards the garage
beats.text: Big box. Sniff. Sniff bumper. BAD. Mongo backs up. Shark on ceiling. Shark comes down. Mongo lies down by shark. MOTHER says stay. Guard Hedy. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: Into the fight
beats.text: MOTHER singing. Loud. FIGHT. Tail. People fall over. Fairy throws fire at Imani. Fairy is FOOD. MOTHER has beer on her. Lick MOTHER. MOTHER is cross.

beats.headline: Three Mongos, one sat on
beats.text: Table bites MOTHER. Now THREE Mongo. Chandelier eats shiny Mongo. BAD. Shiny Mongo goes BOOM. Mongo ANGRY. Mongo bites chairs. Big mimic last. MOTHER kills it first. Mongo sits on it anyway.

beats.headline: Claw caps
beats.text: CLAW CAPS. On FEET. Sharp. MOTHER has hats for everyone. Mongo keeps the old head thing. Mongo is marching band. Rend is marching band. Flowers on EVERYTHING. Flowers are NOT FOOD.

entities.name: Mordecai

tagline.text: This is my tutorial guild, kid, and I can't open the door while there are mobs right outside it. Rules are rules. And nobody tells old Mordecai anything.
I crawled once myself. I took Changeling, it cost me everything I had, and now the dungeon hands me a new body every floor and I wear whatever I'm given.

entities.voiceNote: Tired professional, precise about rules, exasperated by clients who ignore them. Leads with the warning, follows with the reason, ends with a sigh you can hear. Kid, listen, you don't get it. Bitter about Borant in short sentences. Does not gush and does not comfort; drunk, he talks about the past and stops himself.

beats.headline: Tutorial Guild Hall, first floor
beats.text: Rule one: I don't open the door until you kill a goblin. The cat desecrates my mother. The man blows up a Murder Dozer. I open the door. My name is Mordecai. Borant holds my indenture, which means I guide for the first three floors and run a magic guild after that, where they mostly leave me alone to brew and look up old friends. Try to live long enough for that to matter.

beats.headline: The seventh or eighth human world
beats.text: When I signed on as a guildmaster they rebuilt my home for me, possessions and all. I had a few moments to grab what I wanted before they evaporated the rest. Every new world, they change my shape. Always some mob from the current floor. I don't know why. This is the seventh or eighth human-seeded world I've worked, kid, and it's always the same. You humans want to know why. My people last longer than yours. You know why? We roll with it.

beats.headline: This is my last tour
beats.text: I've been preparing for this world longer than you've been alive. Entered the prep phase in your 1964. Once got to wear a human shape and stole James Bond tapes from a Blockbuster. This is my last tour. When it's over I'm a full citizen with a moderate stipend. My home planet is not open to me. Ask about the ones who stayed up top and we get back to the tutorial. I made it to eleven, saw what guarded the stairs to twelve, and knew it wasn't worth it. Deepest anyone has gone is thirteen. One man. A human, from another human world. Dead within half an hour.

beats.headline: Not until floor twelve
beats.text: Now I'm their registered guide. Walk into any other training guild and it brings them back to this room; they lose me at the fourth floor. At the door I take the kid by the jacket, because this part matters. It's not worth it, no matter what they tell you. Not until floor 12, and even then, negotiate as much as you can. Remember that. Then I shut the door.

beats.headline: Bosses, explained with a hangover
beats.text: They wake me up. The photograph of my brother's on the cot with me, and the bottles are on the floor. Six main kinds of boss, kid: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, Floor. And elites, which are not your problem yet. The kid asks if they'll all be people from his world. No, not always. There's a lot of recycling from earlier iterations of the game. Some will be human stock. Most won't be, or they will be and it won't be as obvious. You can't run from most boss fights on the early floors. Be careful.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: I read the fight notes. The weight did what his fist would have: the bare knuckle skill is as good as any unenchanted weapon. Give scrolls to the highest intelligence; his fog lasted fifteen seconds, the cat's would have run two minutes. Her potion cooldown is her constitution, and her shred attack is useless until her health catches up. The borough boss? If I knew, I could not say. That is cheating. But the llama died at the throat and the Juicer at the vein. Look for the weakness. There will always be clues. Look for them.

beats.headline: Just those who pay for the privilege
beats.text: The kid gets a war gauntlet with a warning about striking a war god's worshippers, and asks how to spot them. Horses, centaurs, tikbalangs, blue face paint, a lot of talk about wenches and dying gloriously. Then I tell him the part I probably should not. That god isn't real. There are no real gods in this game. He has been saying some of these bosses are like him, down here against their will. Not always, I tell him. Especially further down. There are no gods here. Just those who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: He has done this before, and it cost him everything
beats.text: I crawled. I took Changeling, and I can't shift on my own any more, so the dungeon hands me a body at the start of every floor and I wear what I'm given. This one is a rat-kin. What I actually am is golden, and has wings. I don't talk about the family. When I've had enough to drink, I talk about the family.

beats.headline: A Bugaboo, and a hard no
beats.text: New floor, new body. A Bugaboo this time: seven feet, no neck, and the chairs are too small now. The kid tells me Odette wants me to seek her out. I'd rather spend another two thousand years in this room. Her show, though, you should go on; it's one of the few I'd recommend. And listen. Viewers can see you in here. They can't see me or hear me. Only those with press credentials can. Like Odette.

beats.headline: The Party, in a whisper
beats.text: While the fish and the cat talk Gossip Girl, I get the kid alone. Listen. The Party is the Bloom: ultra-nationalists, under fifteen percent of the vote when I signed my indenture, and now they run the whole kua-tin government. They've run it into the ground. Borant is being forced by its own government to end this game fast; it gets no money until the season's over. The committee has already warned them about the bugs. So the government is working extra hard to get you killed. Don't upset them.

beats.headline: Arcanist, and a brother
beats.text: Now I'm allowed to talk about the third floor, and I've cleaned the place up. Down the stairs, back in this room: race, then class, then stats. The AI will recommend, and its recommendations are good, and they don't care how you look on camera. Me? Arcanist. Changeling Fire Mage Arcanist. I almost picked a class called Storm Commander. Odette talked me out of it. My brother picked it instead, on her recommendation. The third floor itself we'll do when you get there.

beats.headline: Manoeuvred into managing a cat
beats.text: Odette says my memory is the most valuable thing a crawler could get hold of, so the two of them arrange for me to become the cat's manager during class selection, and they make it look like an accident. It was not an accident. I will forgive Donut. Carl, no.

beats.headline: An incubus, in a tuxedo
beats.text: Three hours I have been standing in this tuxedo waiting for them. The third floor has made me an incubus: grey skin, short horns, bat wings, a barbed tail, and a deeper voice. Guildmaster of this guildhall, the tooltip says. Carl tells me I look good. The cat says something about crackers. I welcome them properly, because the training levels are over. Then the door closes, the public cannot see in here, and the jacket and tie come off. I hate formal wear.

beats.headline: Money, and lots of it
beats.text: Compensated Anarchist is potentially the best of the three, and it requires a lot of work: grind, grind, and focus, on shortened timers. He picks it while I narrow my eyes at him. Only one thing is going to make this work, and it is not training. It is money, and lots of it. As a manager I cannot fight beside them, but I can still step outside now and then, especially on the urban levels, and I have to present them. So the tie goes back on.

beats.headline: Props who do not know it
beats.text: Most of the people in these villages were engineered by Borant, so Borant owns them. It is the only world they have known. Every time they are regenerated their minds are altered and planted with false memories, and anything inconvenient, like a crawler explaining that they are props, is erased. Those meth-addicted goblins were written for this world only. Carl asks how that is legal. You cannot alter the memories of naturals unless they sign their rights away. Using the printed ones outside sanctioned entertainment is basically a war crime.

beats.headline: He remembers none of it
beats.text: I am in my room, it is getting late, and Carl asks how my head is. The cat informs me, in capitals, that I molested someone's grandma. I let Carl explain everything, and then I tell them to back out of there and get to the safe room before dark, and that I will explain how stupid they are once they arrive. Then horns and a charm: break your own finger. Then the cat says it is no succubus but an elite. Get out of there. Do not get involved.

beats.headline: An incubus's weakness
beats.text: I apologize. I have not had a drink in an Over City pub in a very long time, and I did not take into account the incubus's weakness, which is alcohol. Sober, I would have told them that quests are great for experience and loot only when you are comfortably ahead of the curve, and with eight days and the two of them playing catch-up, skip it. And once I was cogent, I told them to stay away from the elite. They made a date with her for tomorrow night.

beats.headline: Never trust an elite
beats.text: Elites are never naturals. They are designed, printed and imprinted with the memories their drama needs, and they move freely between the urban floors. This circus is a storyline with its own show and a team of writers, and if the story drifts they hot patch new instructions right into the elite's head. The fairness rules are looser around them. One crawler's life against a drama that has been building for weeks: you know what happens. You are the red shirt. When this floor collapses, the important ones go down to the sixth. Forget the quest. Go to the city.

beats.headline: The rules he cannot break
beats.text: Most of what I know I'm not allowed to volunteer. Some of it I can only give you if you ask the exact question. Without press credentials nobody watching can see me or hear me, and as a manager I can't touch a mob. My advice is what it has always been: stay ahead of the curve, never trust an elite, stay away from gods. Carl has heard all three.

beats.headline: Managers have one rule
beats.text: The Bopca tells me he has not felt himself since those two arrived, so I mix him a draft from behind his own bar. It knocks him out, and I go into his kitchen for the newsletter; shopkeepers get a printed brief after each recap. I take a few herbs while I am there and pass them to Carl under the table. Managers have one rule: no direct battle with mobs. Everything else is fair game. The brief warns of a major battle event in this area today or tonight. Eat, and get to that town.

beats.headline: The cure is not in this town
beats.text: I visit my old friend Eklund, the only game guide in this town I know. He is too smart for his own good and will not look up the Water Lily cure, but he does tell me the name of Signet's programme, and Carl's hunch is correct. Then I have the recipe: Satch Toad extract mixed with a standard healing potion. It negates all naiad sleep effects and curses. Simple. I can buy it at the alchemical market in a medium or large town. Not in this one.

beats.headline: How to kill a Pestiferous Vine
beats.text: I explained it after the recap. A Pestiferous Vine is a trope, lazy writing. Really a fungus hybrid: its spores infect parasitic worms, and the worms infect the mobs. Plants are easy to kill if you know the trick, and this one's trick is poisoned blood. A few drops on the vine break its link with every symbiont, in fifteen to twenty minutes, and it will not know. If it suspects, the same blood with an antidote in it cures it, so it will try to get its monsters to bleed you. A city boss as well? The core should be the same size. I think.

beats.headline: A potion that works on a pet
beats.text: A Heal scroll does nothing for the dinosaur and neither does a potion. Listen. Take out a heal potion. There is a cinnamon stick in your inventory and I gave you a couple of branches of thistle rot. The whole cinnamon stick goes into the potion. Wait five seconds. Add the thistle rot. Cork it, shake it, pour it down the pet's throat, and try not to get your hand bitten off. The cinnamon and the thistle both came out of the Belly Rubbed Pug's kitchens, where I stole them.

beats.headline: The manager goes where Donut goes
beats.text: I pop into my own room with a drink in my hand, because nobody warned me. As a manager, my town now matches wherever Donut last entered; a plain guide can dial it anywhere. There is a guide-only town these two cannot reach, and I was looking forward to it. The drink works because I brewed a potion that lets alcohol affect demon spawn. On my world I was a mycologist. Odette made me learn plenty about vegetation when we made it to the sixth floor. The cat gives Carl a sharp look when I say that. Neither of them says anything.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: An orc woman at the pub, GumGum, says she needs our help. No. Not tonight. It is a quest, and we are doing no more quests on this floor. Then the kid wanders back out of his room, and she is already gone. So I tell him, and I want it to sink into that thick skull. You can't save them all. The people running this know who you are, and they will always be baiting you. If you truly want to help others, get as strong and as deep as possible.

beats.headline: Immortal, sort of
beats.text: Carl asks why I was so upset to be picked. It is not you. It's complicated. Then he asks whether that opossum was right that I am immortal. Sort of. From the fourth floor, managers get a protection package. Not you. We can still be hurt and still feel it, but dying there only kicks us out of the game. For the rest of this floor I am as unprotected as you. If I die as a manager I am done for the season. The rules pay me more the longer Donut survives, and past the ninth it is an obscene amount. Let's go look at the Silk Road.

beats.headline: City elves and a squiggly letter
beats.text: The shirt is from the 201st Security Group, the city elves' militia. Conspiracy nuts, too stupid for the high elves, who kick them out. Their cause is protecting the eagle folk, my own old people, whom they take for angels, all because of a few stories about their tree goddess. I have never known them to be violent. The cat declares she is doing the quest; I ain't your dad, I'm your manager. Then the letter off the dead orc. I can't read it, but I know these squiggles. Necroscript. You two might have a lich problem.

beats.headline: New rule: nothing outside the dungeon
beats.text: I distinctly remember saying subtle. The kid calls an orc king a pussy on air, the king's son lasers the wrong trailer from orbit, and the Valtay answer by blowing up the royal yacht. His wife is dead. So, new rule. We do not mention anyone outside this dungeon, not until after the sixth floor, if these two idiots make it that far. Odette asks, they have no opinion. I wanted his people aimed at the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor. I don't think that's going to be an issue now. What can he do to them in here? Nothing yet. That changes very soon.

beats.headline: What the newsletter does not say
beats.text: I talk Fitz into showing me his herb stash and steal his newsletter. Borant is warning shopkeepers and pub owners to be extra careful not to anger crawlers. It doesn't say why. I can read between the lines. Some of you are getting stronger than you should; the kid who trashed the Desperado Club is proof. Borant controls the mobs and most of the experience. The System AI controls most of the loot boxes, it is still the ultimate arbiter, and it is evening the odds against the shorter floors. These elaborate quests are the same symptom. Keep the new girl alive. If she dies, get those rings off her.

beats.headline: Liches never shut up
beats.text: Liches come in all shapes and power levels. But they all have one thing in common. They are just like Odette: they never, ever shut the hell up. Narcissists, and cowards, who will do anything not to let go of the life they have grabbed back, so they always have minions and grandiose plans. I said blow the building and take a chance on losing the quest. Then they killed most of his support, and I changed my mind: he'll be weak. One more wrinkle. The last one was a neighbourhood boss. I'd bet my left nipple this is a borough boss. Come prepared.

beats.headline: A bereft minion, then run
beats.text: Not a lich, he says. No. A bereft minion: one still alive after its controller is dead. You killed the head bad guy when you blew up Miss Quill. Quests sometimes look bigger than they are; I should have known, it was only a silver quest. Sorry about the dynamite. Get the story, put him down, get out before the swordsmen wake. Then the quest drops. Run for the Desperado Club; the second room is out of the blast. Protective Shell won't work, it's magical. Break the gem? Probably makes it blow early. It's called The Fools Who Broke the Glass for a reason.

beats.headline: The skill that stayed behind
beats.text: Kid, listen. Her Negotiation came at level five with the Artist Alley class, and she sold it up to seven. The class is gone and the five levels went with it, but she kept the two she earned, experience and all, so it bumped itself to four. So a skill she levels even once, she keeps. Stat points, no. Use Mongo as much as you can and Mascot stays. Watch for classes with rare spells. And it's probably a bug, so don't talk about it out loud. They won't notice until she carries a spell down a floor.

beats.headline: A toad, not a frog
beats.text: This floor they've made me Grulke Infantry. Toad warriors: leapers, a tongue that hits hard, and a people gone to mercenaries and vagrants. Tunnel trolls hunt them to lick them. Don't ever call a real Grulke a frog; they're mean bastards. Toads. And yes, I know about the quest. I get notices of court decisions that go against my client. You got screwed, but you're alive. The third floor is usually twenty days, and you had ten. Level 27 and 26 after that is lucky and a miracle. We can't rely on luck.

beats.headline: Two hours of sleep, then a schedule
beats.text: You only sleep two hours now, so I'll see you out here for the recap. Then the schedule. Wake, eat, buffs: shower, the cat's brushing, your feet. An hour in the training room on one skill, because you only get one a day. Carl, Smush. Katia, Catcher. Donut picked Dodge. Crafting after that, starting tomorrow. The recap freezes on REDACTED; get used to it, that's the part explaining the level. Where I woke up was station 317: the Yellow and Emerald lines, and a big one called the Misery. I wrote it all down.

beats.headline: A control sigil
beats.text: That's a control sigil. Only you can see it, because of your Escape Plan skill. Secondary programs like Vengeance of the Daughter use them, and so do the dungeon's makers sometimes, though it's considered sloppy programming because they're easy to break. They're mostly for controlled gating: stopping a specific type of mob passing. The showrunners turn them on and off, not the AI, which is why they use them. Blue means it's on. It'll have no effect on you. Can crawlers make one? No. There's a similar kind of magic you'll never have the mana for. Donut might.

beats.headline: Special Brew and potion balls
beats.text: Get back. You'll contaminate it. I put Donut's two table upgrades into the alchemy table, so it's level three. Two of my Special Brew: thirty seconds of healing and regeneration, near enough immortality, but not against decapitation or blowing yourself up. It adds about ten hours to your potion sickness, and two is the lifetime limit; I've never got past that. Two Superb Constitution potions for the cat. And fragmenting potion balls: pour a potion in, throw it at a bad guy. Potions work on mobs. It doesn't make sense. It's always been that way.

beats.headline: Naughty, for seven days
beats.text: The Prize Carousel materialises in the personal space, and its host is Chaco the Bard. Guide Mordecai throws a metal chair at him with his tongue. The chair stops a quarter of an inch from the host's head. Naughty. Mordecai blinks out, and the room marked Manager goes with him. Time out: seven days, for violating the rules, which returns him with a day and a half left on the floor. Chaco says it was a long time ago, that he was doing what Mordecai's manager told him, and asks that Mordecai be told he is sorry.

beats.headline: Seven days, in a blink
beats.text: Where is he? Where did that — oh. By his left tit. The notifications say seven days. For me no time has passed at all; I lost my temper at Chaco, blinked, and here I am. The cat has a player-killer skull over her head. So does Katia. The dinosaur is jumping circles around me. I see I have missed a few things. Carl starts to tell me, and then Katia erupts. Blood, gallons of it, in every direction, over the walls and the ceiling and me, and I go backward over the couch with my legs in the air.

beats.headline: The map is the Syndicate logo
beats.text: Look at the named lines from above: rings of different sizes, overlapping. That's the Syndicate logo, and the Nightmare's loop is the second ring. So a train has to loop to the front, and you already found it: the Escape Velocity line, named for the ship that found the wormhole that led to the Vog Generation Ship. The abyss is the centre of the galaxy; the tracks are the original worm paths. Six station mimics are the H'lene, who set six waystations near the centre as traps and ate the travellers. The Valtay and the orcs wiped them out. They really went all out.

beats.headline: No cooldown on a god
beats.text: Carl, if you've summoned Grull: run. Don't fight him. He's invulnerable. Take my special brew. You haven't? By the gods, don't scare me like that. The rules, then. An involuntary summoning lasts the vessel's level in seconds plus the god's. Grull is sanctum tier, level 250; from a level-forty vessel that's 290 seconds. Summoned, he grows until he fills the room. There's no cooldown, and a god held in one summoning breaks out and goes to the next if someone calls him. I learned that the hard way. The hardest way possible. Now don't you even dare think about —

beats.headline: Fifteen days is a warning
beats.text: I was expecting twelve days. They gave us fifteen, and three extra days are not a gift, they're a nasty surprise waiting to happen. I got here first and gathered what I could: two towns, a sandstorm an hour or two a day, a castle that's a speck against the top of the dome, and maybe three dozen crawlers in this quadrant, every one I've seen so underpowered it's a miracle they're alive. Then the announcement. Four quadrants, four castles, and the stairwell won't open until all four fall. So assume the other hundred and fifty are idiots. Eat. Open your boxes. Sleep.

beats.headline: Pawna's Tears, saved
beats.text: Every box on this floor is handing out water-breathing scrolls and antidotes. That's the floor telling you what's coming, kid. Then Carl opens his deity box and I have to ask to hold it. Pawna's Tears. Goddess of peace, Grull's sister and enemy. Plus five to any skill he picks, and unlike a Cheat Code it doesn't have to be drunk on the spot. Train something to fifteen, take it, and it's twenty. Single best piece of loot he's had since he came in. Not including the pet biscuit, the cat says. Fine. We decide after he picks his subclass.

beats.headline: Selling to the armies
beats.text: The marketplace interface is on Donut's account, because her Charisma goes into the prices. For now it's a virtual general store. Once the sixth floor opens, the tourists and the factions trade through it too, and anything magical you list gets snapped up, because this is how they outfit their armies. Yes, kid, you might be selling to people you'll fight. If you don't sell your gear, somebody else will, and they'll mostly be using it on each other. Once the ninth floor opens the factions can't buy new gear at all. I'll explain that when you get there.

beats.headline: Safe only with a crawler inside
beats.text: Kid, a saferoom protects whoever's in it, but a Borant-owned NPC alone in one isn't protected. If there are no crawlers or off-world NPCs in the room, the room's probably gone with the rest. The Toe isn't a real saferoom; if the proprietor isn't a Bopca, it's about fifty-fifty. Our personal space is. So if the gnomes do to this town what they just did to the Bactrian one, you come in here. There are other rules, and the manual on saferoom procedures is like a phonebook. The primary and secondary zones are different; they don't directly touch crawlers or NPCs at all.

beats.headline: Rapid Detox, and a wasted spell
beats.text: One of these two fuckwits has his boots on the table, so I land on it, and it breaks, and I tell them to shut up for five minutes while I brew. Rapid Detox, with sage beetle ichor so they can't read the label. Clears alcohol and most drugs, and for one floor, if they drink, they get violently ill. The good kind of poisoning. Then the part that matters: Louis carries an enhanced, legendary-tier Cloud of Exhaust, almost certainly the same spell the goat lady has, and he's been using it to run away. He should be level forty by now.

beats.headline: A sect after a full library
beats.text: Ah, shit. I should have known. Changeling Principals. It's an old story; I haven't seen it used in a long, long time. They're a sect of changeling culture, cultish, like those city elves, but less apocalyptic and more power hungry. They're obsessed with a full library, and since a changeling can only become something it has physically touched, they go after rare creatures. Get the brain, kid, the glowing part. If you kill one, take the head; I can make a potion from it. Only if it's untransformed when it dies. Knock them out first.

beats.headline: A timeout, not a glitch
beats.text: I felt it. It happens. That half-second freeze usually isn't a glitch; it's a gameplay timeout, so the dueling routines can reconcile a rule conflict. An artifact is a legendary or celestial-tier item you find lying around or drop as loot, and they start turning up around the eighth or ninth floor. The showrunners control the storylines, but the AI picks the specific loot, and it can and will adjust the story to keep the game fair. If you get what I'm saying. And remember what I said about the word feral.

beats.headline: This is not a daycare
beats.text: I don't have the materials for Feather Fall; the seed pods are scarce until the sixth floor. I can make him one kind of potion, two doses, and he won't like it. Then he walks in with forty children. This isn't a goddamned daycare, Carl. Do you see a jungle gym? So I stream a movie to the screen from the library I collected before we went live. Toy Story. It's a manager benefit, for strategizing on the screens. Now the cat knows. And that is why I never told her.

beats.headline: Sell the kit, use the stone
beats.text: Kid, keep the Half Splat in your hotlist until you find a real Featherfall; it stops the fall killing you and leaves you at five percent. And don't knock Dolores Doesn't Splat. Unpleasant, sure, but you landed at a hundred percent. The platinum stone is what I was talking about: items that enhance the items you already have. Use it now, it has a short shelf life. The author kit you'll never have the skills for; a simple Light scroll would take a week of practice. Sell it. One guy last season used the same scroll over two hundred times and learned the spell.

beats.headline: Infiltrators
beats.text: Oh, fuck. Shoot him again. I've told you about brain worms, kid. Intellect hunters take corpses, and the bodies rot. The Valtay keep their bodies alive. Their cousins, the Scree, are better known as the Infiltrators: they take living bodies, and after a few days the host is locked out and watches himself move like a puppet. She's in his brain. His body is her armor. Getting her out without killing him? Next to impossible. There's an antiparasitic that will kill her, and I won't have the materials until the next floor.

beats.headline: Veriluxx, and who owns it
beats.text: Kid, don't press your luck with that panel. It's a non-enhanced toy; set off the self-destruct and I honestly don't know what the AI does with it. Most toys need a licensed enhancement zone, and some need a license key in the kid to prove his parents paid their taxes. This one needs neither. As for Veriluxx: never heard of them, but the logo says Veritan Linkage, a mostly-Soother lending fund that advocates enslaving people who can't pay their taxes. Odds are it's a way to funnel money to Borant. Carl asks if the whole universe is assholes. Just the ones with the money.

beats.headline: A liaison hold
beats.text: I didn't think I'd see you again, kid. I got a notice there was a liaison hold on Donut, and then five days were gone. Only the fifth floor, and the liaisons are already involved. By his left tit. Next thing you know, the lawyers will be here, and everything gets complicated once the lawyers get here. A Syndicate liaison, and he let you walk right out? Then the kid pulls Loita's rebreather out of his waistband. He looted it off her body.

beats.headline: Do not let it touch you
beats.text: Do not let it touch you. Once a sand ooze gets ahold of you it's like quicksand, and Carl's already burned his Protective Shell. It won't just suffocate you, kid. It pours sand into every opening you've got until you burst, and he's wearing boxers. They hunt by vibration and sound, not heat, so clomping across a ceiling will still get noticed; he'll need one of the toys he was building. And I wouldn't trust a guy who married an ooze. Katia, watch him while Carl's in there.

beats.headline: Two potions he should not drink
beats.text: Carl's Pacifist box gives him two Potions of Bloodlust. Double strength, double speed, half dexterity, half constitution, and a debuff that means you don't remember where you are or why you're fighting. Don't use those. The last time I saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. And don't get ideas about the gate either, kid. Crawlers can't hop floors. If you ever get the last watch, stick it in your inventory until you're strong enough to deal with whatever comes out. Which will be never.

beats.headline: Keep her, as a trainer
beats.text: A withering spirit. Sometimes a soul gets split, and the two halves try to reunite in a proper vessel; when that goes wrong, you get this. Not alive, not dead, hard to kill, mostly harmless, haunting the object. They use them as quest-givers a lot. We avoid gods like we avoid outside factions. And then, knowing I'll regret it, I say we keep her. In the saferoom she can't summon anything, and a minor deity may know potions. Donut can hire her as a trainer. She'll live in a corner of the training room.

beats.headline: Drakea was a bune
beats.text: I remember Drakea. A bune: a slight, dragon-like people, peaceful by nature, some of the cleverest fighters there are. Class like Carl's, but more magic. A big trap guy. He died on the eleventh floor. Or was it the twelfth? He'd had a pretty good offer and spat in their faces, and then his setup backfired. Unnaturally backfired. Lawyers got involved, and the Syndicate, acting on his behalf, collected a big sum from the Sultanate.

beats.headline: Going primal
