beats.text: We're at the college in Larracos, filling out visitor passes and dealing with guards who are sluggish under a Despondent debuff, trying to reach a saferoom. Tran's wheelchair is gone, so we carry him, and it slows everything down. Then Samantha rolls past, screaming that she's going to kill a woman named Tish, and I go after her before the guards react. She's rolling, not floating, and she's fast. I get her trapped in a corner. She's really mad. I bring her back through the safe room.

beats.headline: Eyebrows, eyelashes, and a failed spell
beats.text: Carl waited for me to do his hair tonic. Eyebrows first, then eyelashes, which is almost the pubic hair recipe, so I'm careful. He asks, quietly, if I'm okay. I'm hanging in there. Mordecai is brewing something that might help with the rehab, and I'll take it tomorrow, before the ceasefire ends. The head mix can only sit for five seconds, so I have an otter water mage, one of the strippers, ready to power-wash it off. As a mercenary, his spell won't cast in the saferoom. Carl's hair now reaches his waist.

beats.headline: Twice to Glory Bound
beats.text: Mordecai's jar is two hits of Glory Bound in a gel, cut with a potion called Tough Love. Eight to ten hours, for me. Once I am under I am on my own, and Edgar says waking me early could be fatal. That's a cheerful thought. I drink the sleeping potion. Skál. Then I tell Carl a secret. My favourite memory and my worst memory are the same thing, and I am going back to where I went last time. He tells me to take his hand. I do, and Imani pulls us apart.

beats.headline: We left her with Annie
beats.text: They tell me Carl vanished off his cot as it began, stayed translucent, then went completely. The Lemig team knew the moment he went under and tried something through the warlord chat. I message him. He is in the high elf castle. And we left her there, Carl. We left Shi Maria alone in that room with Annie. He says it was only a memory, and asks if it worked. It is not a switch one flips. We will not know right away. But yes. I think it worked.

beats.headline: A chain shaped like a dragon
beats.text: The ink is mixed from Li Na's blood, given freely, and that means Carl gets to choose the skill. She's not mad at him; she's mad at herself for not protecting her brother. She lost five levels of it for now, and she can still use it. It's a level-thirteen skill, so the tattoo has to be large and uses nearly all the vial. I have never done a real tattoo. Samantha's neck doesn't count. Donut wants the design drawn in the voodoo book first for her approval. Carl wants a chain shaped like a dragon.

beats.headline: The flower, if it comes to that
beats.text: Daniel and I argue in chat, and I say no out loud. He wants me to eat the flower now. He's afraid that if this goes badly, Carl will turn on me to get it for Donut. I tell Carl so, and he says he would never. I know. Then I tell him something I haven't told Daniel: if it comes to that, I will give him the flower. Huanxin Jinx will rage, but I'm certain she'll take Donut to the twelfth floor. Donut wouldn't allow it, he says. I know. That's why I'm telling you and not her.

beats.headline: Temple defense protocols
beats.text: I come through the door as one of the club's four-armed guards, soaked in the cherries and sausage sandwich Carl's broken food box made when he asked it for cobbler. Demons attack the temple behind me, I shout. We must initiate temple defense protocols. That's what Tipid said the procedure is called. The one with his claws stuck in the ceiling asks, temple defense protocols? Fight to the death, I say. Kill all the heathens. Uh, steel and heavy metal. What manner of demon is it? Two of Daniel's stuffed pyxies fly over my shoulders and come alive. That kind.

beats.headline: God or not, I'm staying
beats.text: Carl tells us to run the moment we unfreeze, reset the door, hide in our own temples if we have to; he'll cover us. Prepotente says he did not come this far to run. Me neither, Carl. God or not, I'm staying. Donut is shouting in capitals that there aren't supposed to be gods yet. Then, under a thirty-second timer, Carl sends his plan. No. No way, Carl. That's insane, even for you. Prepotente says he would actually be quite curious to see if it works.

beats.headline: Knee pads of the goddess Kina
beats.text: In the interview bubble, Drick says my celestial knee pads are a waste on someone planning to leave the dungeon; they were awarded in hopes I'd hand them to Carl, and they even look like his. They are made of the eyelashes of the sea goddess Kina: damage reflect, breathing underwater, Swim, Iron Stomach and Eater of the Dead. Kevin asks if I'm wearing them. I'm not. I tell him I left them at the guild. Before I took them off, I gained twenty points of intelligence eating throwaway magic items, until it became too much.

beats.headline: Plan B
beats.text: Subterfuge is gone. The rainbow has pulled half the Madness out to meet us, and the other half is already facing the 103rd. Prepotente can shield one group from their psionics, not both. Carl hesitates. So I say it: we still have Donut to cover the 103rd as they retreat. Bring Prepotente here, and use Donut to the best of her ability. He tells me I'm right. Then the missiles land on their castle, and in the light I can see the dune buggies coming at us.

beats.headline: Annie, in the dream
beats.text: Days ago, in the dream potion, Carl lands in my dream instead of his own, our hands fused together. A children's hospital in Iceland. Fannar, my ex, arrives to tell them the truth, and the woman denies my adoption, and I scream into my fist in a bathroom stall. Then I go to Annie. Brain cancer. She died alone. Nobody told me, until I met a nurse in a park who said she passed a few weeks ago, as if it did not matter. It is my worst memory and my favourite. I love Daniel. I tell Carl I love him and Donut more.

beats.headline: Especially after today
beats.text: Carl asks what Louis meant about a cop's husband. It's for Louis to tell, but when he was young a police officer was shot dead protecting him, and at her funeral her husband said something very cruel to him that has stuck. Donut shouts that sad stories will jinx the rescue. Then, privately, Carl asks what Carl it up means. I don't know. I'm willing to bet we'll find out, now that she's told him. He asks if I'm sure this is what I want. Yes, Carl. Especially after all we learned today.

beats.headline: I love all of you
beats.text: Carl shouts at me to eat the orchid. Now. It takes sixty minutes and we have sixty-five. I haven't transferred all my inventory away; there's stuff in the safe room I need. He puts his forehead against mine. This isn't goodbye, this is how we win, and it's my plan. I've already given Donut the things. I remind him I said he'd Carl it up. He says this one's on Samantha. I love you. I love all of you. I climb onto the table where Kiwi gave birth, and I eat it.

beats.headline: The only way to reach them
beats.text: I choose to be made pregnant. The goddess asks if I'm certain and offers me a place in her court, kept safe. I tell her the rules here are strange. If I'm pregnant, I get sent somewhere else, and there are children up there, mostly alone, in trouble. This is the only way I can get to them. She says she senses them and cannot reach them. I am made human again, and my friends see what I've lost: an arm, a leg, the other below the knee, an ear. We've all become experts at hiding what we've really lost.

beats.headline: She takes the Orchid and goes
beats.text: Crawler Katia Grim has left the dungeon. Not by the stairs. She ate the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and lay for an hour at one percent, and when she opened her eyes the goddess was standing over her, telling her to get up. She got up. Where she has gone is between her and the goddess.

entities.name: Imani

tagline.text: I work at Meadow Lark. I wear scrubs and a magic cloak, I carry a longsword, and I am responsible for thirty-odd residents who cannot move quickly.
I held the portal open on the racing floor until every crawler who was coming had come through. Somebody has to stand at the door, and it's usually me.

entities.voiceNote: Calm, steady, a caregiver's voice under pressure. Counts people, says what needs doing, does it. Warm without fuss, firm without volume. Carl, Donut, Elle, Yolanda, Brandon and Chris by name. Never dramatises a loss and never leaves before the last one is through.

beats.headline: The good folks from Meadow Lark
beats.text: We came down out of Meadow Lark, the elder care facility, together: Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, me, and Agatha, who none of us can quite place and who came with us anyway. Carl and Donut find us, and we sit down and trade stories, theirs and ours, and then we make a plan, because there are people depending on us and a plan is what you owe them.

beats.headline: Twelve skulls by my name
beats.text: Carl sees the skulls beside my name. Crawler Killer, twelve. Brandon tells him what he can: that something attacked us right after the tutorial, that our residents could not move quickly, that what those things would have done to them was worse. I do not add to it. I walk a woman to the bathroom and make her open the door herself, and I give a man in a wheelchair a sip of water. When Carl says the six of us will fight the boss, I speak for the first time. I ask him how.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Seven of us against the Ball of Swine: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Carl, Donut, Agatha and me, fighting from the redoubt. It is the first time this group has fought as one thing instead of six people and a cat standing near each other, and it works. Afterwards I count everybody twice, because that is what I do, and everybody is there both times.

beats.headline: Twelve items for foot care
beats.text: Donut laughs at him. So I sit down with Carl and his pedicure kit and take out the tools one at a time and tell him what each of them is for. He does not need all twelve; he has to make a show of it. About fifteen minutes of work and the buffs come on. His toes glitter, and the bones in them cannot break now.

beats.headline: Yog's Special Chain
beats.text: Someone had to stay with the residents while Brandon, Chris and Yolanda cleared out the Mind Horrors, so I stayed. Then we built a train. The wheels come off wheelchairs whose owners are gone; Brandon designed the cars and added ramps. The chain is mine, a scroll out of a Gold box: any length up to about a thousand feet, light as a feather, gone in thirty hours. Chris and I wear pig harnesses and pull thirty-nine people, ten cars, one glowing chain running from him, through every car and back to me.

beats.headline: Open the damn door
beats.text: Carl is building a bomb launcher, and I ask the obvious question. Why don't we just open the damn door? We are in a safe room. Mobs get thrown out. So we test it. The claw comes through, the thing goes thwum and vanishes, and a moment after, its dot is rocketing straight back at us. Keep it open, I say. See if it learns. Ninety seconds, and it is back, this time from another hallway down. It does not. Seventy-five to a hundred and twenty seconds, every time. When the launcher is ready, I count down from three and pull.

beats.headline: Last one down
beats.text: I am the last of us down the ramp. Carl and Donut stand by the hole and wave, and I wave back. I don't smile. Thirty-six residents went down ahead of me in buckets built from chopper wheels and hunks of wood, and Yolanda did not. At the scorched entrance to the third floor I stop, look up into the air, and raise a middle finger. Then I go inside.

beats.headline: What happened with Chris
beats.text: Obsidian Butterfly, Fire Spiritualist, level twenty-four. The wings aren't physical; on the sixth floor I choose whether they fly. I came here to tell Carl about Chris. He picked a rock race, an igneous, got very strong, and it changed him. He wanted to spend every minute hunting and go find Carl and Donut. Brandon wanted to train near the stairwell. They fought, and several of the men left with Chris. Henry and Brandon died protecting our escape. Chris is the only one of those who left still alive. He won't answer us. He is looking for you, Carl.

beats.headline: Primes, and the stations nobody has seen
beats.text: We trace our position on Carl's map and pick a stop where we can meet. Elle points out that every transfer station is a prime number; Mordecai had written the word in the corner and circled it. That is a pattern, not an answer. We don't have enough information. We need to know what happens at the stations every five stops, where the mobs all get off, and more importantly what happens at the end of the line. So my team takes one of the fifth platforms, and Carl and Donut go after an engineer.

beats.headline: What the Pooka hand out
beats.text: Carl, we should stop derailing trains until there's a solid plan to get out. If other crawlers are behind you on the line, you may trap them. At the stops ending in five or zero, the mobs line up by race at doors with slots. Behind each door a Pooka hands out one vial of a race-specific sedative, and they take it back through a one-way portal. The description says if they miss their fix, they change physically. The Krakaren makes the drugs. I wasn't confident we could face her, so I had the team back off. Pookas turn into giant goats when attacked.

beats.headline: The coupon book she left behind
beats.text: Carl asks whether I got a PVP coupon with my skulls. I did. A Savage box with nothing in it but the coupon book, one for every member of the party. I tried to burn them and they would not catch, so I left them on the first floor. Brandon wanted me to keep them, in case. I could feel them sitting in my inventory. Elle got no book with her skull, and Donut told me about the two she got, so I think only the first in a party to earn a skull gets one. I tell him to talk to her.

beats.headline: Stop 48 is full
beats.text: We crossed at station sixty onto Carl's line, found his train parked, and went down to the stairwell at 48. It was full of festering ghouls, and we watched them change: worms come out of them, and they pull together into one giant thing that fills the room. A province boss. We all got achievements just for discovering it, and it let us leave. Now the wrath ghouls are stopping at 36. We are going to post up there and kill them as they come in, before they can do the same. We could use some boom jugs.

beats.headline: A ring of flamers around the portal
beats.text: Carl's plan needs chain, and I still have a few of the scrolls that make it, so the chain is mine. The plan I'm less sure of. When the centre of the floor opens, nothing comes up at us, because it all falls into his portal. I tell them to secure the entrances and put a ring of flamers and mages around the hole in case something happens to the cart. Then they come through the hallways instead. When Carl, Katia and Donut stumble back out of one, burning with acid, I'm right there, and I take it off them.

beats.headline: Still Brandon's brother
beats.text: Carl tells me he's found Chris. He's in the same bubble as Carl. Chris still ignores every message I send. I hope the real Chris is still in there somewhere; he's the only non-resident left. Here we need a boat with armor. Elle's ice keeps the fireballs off, but we can't get near the oil rig for the monsters in the water and the orc archers. Carl says build a sub, like that's easy. We bought the shop interface on Donut's advice. And Carl? Don't kill him. Please. He's still Brandon's brother.

beats.headline: He's being controlled
beats.text: Carl says it is not Chris. It is. Chris has messaged me: he is petrified, and when his body wakes he will lose consciousness again, because something else is driving it. Then he asks Carl and Donut to kill him, and I will not send that on. Elle does. When Carl tells me he is sorry, I do not answer. Donut drops Chris through a hole into a sealed chamber under the street instead, and I thank her. Take all four castles, I tell them, then go back, incapacitate them again, bring them through the portal, and your game guide can make the potion.

beats.headline: Nobody left behind
beats.text: Only eight bubbles meet the requirements for the first run: somebody with access to the Desperado Club, and every survivor in the same quadrant. Just over five hundred crawlers, most of them in the first four groups. The second condition is mine. I will not help a bubble out if it means leaving anyone in there with a feral god, not even one person. Elle can tell when someone is lying about their quadrants, and she has weeded a few out. Carl said not to wait for him. I tell everybody we are starting the extractions.

beats.headline: A counterspell in the druid town
beats.text: We raid a small druid town after Eva, and she has already gone. She leaves a glamour behind: she charmed the townsfolk and talked them into attacking us as we came in. When they approach, I cast a counterspell and take the glamour off them. A tree-person tells me, in tears, what she did to them. The raid ends without violence. I can fly now, and I move with Elle behind Katia, Florin and Bautista. Li Na can track her, and she is backed into the hot springs and the lava tubes.

beats.headline: Smart Juice
beats.text: Carl asks whether I have an ability that raises the level of a spell. I do. An aura called Smart Juice. It adds a level to a spell, but it adds an extra cooldown as well, so I don't use it much in a fight. Elle gets mad when her icicles take too long. He says thanks, and nothing about what he needs it for.

beats.headline: People are depending on us
beats.text: Signet is in the ballroom with us now, which means she can't help us from outside it. Carl says the goddess picks the guest list, so of course she brought in one of the queen's biggest enemies. I tell him I don't like it. It's like they've been one step ahead of us the whole time. He thinks it's better this way: she'll be the first target, and it buys us a few extra seconds if someone breaks the seal. Everything is going off the rails, and people are depending on us. He says he knows.

beats.headline: Counterspells on the way down
beats.text: We fall into the brambles' dome with the bugs, and I work. Debuffs stack on our people and I take them off, dozens of them, counterspells and buffs as fast as I can throw them, wings spread the whole way down. When Carl's shell gives us a breath, I use it to heal whoever I can reach. Then I point. There. The god is in the far corner. Then I go back to the fight against Imogen.

beats.headline: Great Wolf Lodge
beats.text: We picked the western United States and came up in an indoor water park in the middle of nowhere, the Great Wolf Lodge. Elle and I were put in different squads and made to choose separately, and we both chose the same place. It is rural out here, with I-5 close by. Only a handful of cars have come up from the south toward Portland, so something is blocking the freeway down there. There is chatter about this everywhere. I don't know if they thought this through, or if this is exactly what they wanted.

beats.headline: A drug den like a frozen yogurt bar
beats.text: She is okay, but she has a nasty debuff. She found a secret room set up like a self-serve frozen yogurt place: you fill a bowl, add toppings. She made herself something and it knocked her flat for ten more hours. Bliss Surfing, it says. I think she is reliving a memory. Fifty percent chance of a lot of strength when she wakes, and some chance of losing intelligence. Elle is guarding her. The way Daniel keeps making excuses for her is familiar to me. I am going to the guild to talk to Louis and Britney.

beats.headline: Detroit, and nobody asked
beats.text: Everyone checks in; I make sure of it. We are scattered. Elle's squad is in Belgium, and I am not with them. Florin is in eastern Nigeria and has lost contact with Lucia Mar. Li Jun's crew is further into mainland China. Prepotente, after some prodding, is somewhere in northern Italy. I was given one choice: Detroit. It is where I grew up, and I would never have picked it. My key location is in the home of somebody I know. I do not elaborate.

beats.headline: Four skulls, for her own squad
beats.text: We needed the last token. One of the enemy totems possessed two of my people and made them fight each other. Randall froze all four of them to stop it. Then my own totem, the Amhuluk, cast a poison cloud, and they died frozen in place. It finished the deckmaster and won the battle. The dungeon gives me four player killer skulls for them. I do not go to the final battle. I go back to the saferoom. Elle is the only one I can talk to.

beats.headline: Cuba, or face Elle
beats.text: At midnight they give me two choices: Cuba, or back to face Elle. I cannot do that. So I am in Cuba, at a church, and no traps went off. Carl says sit tight, they are coming, and not to let the nun through. Then I tell them the rest. A man here tried to start a card battle with me, and I got through the saferoom door first. It is Quan Ch, alone.

beats.headline: The training arcade door
beats.text: Carl sends me to the training arcade, where he locked the mercenaries in almost a day ago with a disease that makes them leak slugs every few minutes. The room kills them and regenerates them. There are hundreds of slugs now, some as high level as the mercenaries, and the room is full of blood. I watch one swallow Steve whole. Carl says he only infected Doctor Bones, and Doctor Bones did the rest. The room healer refused to cure them because Carl told her not to. So I cure them. I am a healer. It's what I do.

beats.headline: People have bones for a reason
beats.text: Surprise. We came out into the church, all of us, through the door Lucia's upgrade put in my room. We have already pooled our money for the barracks upgrade. Carl still wants to hand me his key. No. Elle tells him we're all in this together, and if it goes wrong most of us can still go back and use our keys. Donut told me about his other idea, the one where he uses one of his own bones to get out. People have bones for a reason, Carl. It's all or nothing.

beats.headline: I won't leave Tran
beats.text: Tran and I are trapped in a pocket of debris, and the demons are in here with us now. I am holding them off the best I can. Elle asks if I have cards left, a Flee card. Tran is on Katia's squad, so only her Flee card could take him, and she doesn't carry them, and she is out of cards anyway. So I won't leave Tran. And I don't trust my last totems. They are digging toward us from above.

beats.headline: Thank you for not giving up on me
beats.text: We stand in the tunnel under the X that Chris painted on the ceiling, the three of us, with three minutes left. I wrap Carl and Donut in my wings. None of us is getting out of this unscathed. We gain things, and we lose them. That is what happens in war. I thank them for not giving up on me. Carl says we don't give up on family, or what's the point. Then I put my arms around him too, and my head on his shoulder, and I cry quietly, with my skulls glowing over my head in the dark.

beats.headline: One trebuchet, and the buffs
beats.text: I drop into the trench next to Carl. I was buffing people down the line, and before that the man aiming our only trebuchet, which is loaded with Dazzlers. He's ready. I spread my wings and put a new line of buffs over everyone in the channel. Then Total Ear Protection on Donut, and on Mongo.

beats.headline: One over each shoulder
beats.text: Their diffusion spell strips every protection we had, and the heavy gun cuts through the ones rushing it. I stop over a veteran screaming, his arm gone. I put Donut's ear protection back, and Mongo's. Then I go for whoever is down. Into the crater with one over each shoulder. The Crest veteran is dead. The crawler with the arm blades is at two per cent and unconscious.

beats.headline: This warlord thing suits her
beats.text: A group of us detour through Shanty Town and use the doggy door, and the moment I land in the castle the Extreme Focus buff doubles. Everyone in the zone is talking too fast, me included. Carl seems untouched, though his health screen says the buff is on him. I have told the medic already: check their pain levels after you heal them, outworlders heal differently. Then Donut is on the roof shouting Comrades, and Carl says she's been spending too much time with Rosetta. This warlord thing suits her, I tell him. It comes out a little sad.

beats.headline: Carl's spell on my ankle
beats.text: We're inside the castle, and the slugs who were meant to go in first and set off the traps are dancing around a cart in a field somewhere. So I use Carl's spell. Tripper, lent to me as a little barbed-wire tattoo around my ankle, drawn by Katia in yam ink and his blood. Lots of traps go off at once. Carl says he got a notification when I used it, and it kind of hurt. I'm sorry about that. Donut says it had better have worked, after I disfigured myself for it.

beats.headline: The person to your left and right
beats.text: The 105th teleports in, a few of them half inside trees, and I give Chris a quick hug with my wings. Then I fly the line. Keep an eye on the person to your left and to your right. The Madness uses mind magic and Atrocity magic, and they will not always show a notification. Call it out. And it is Carl they go for. Somebody slaps him awake, and I tell him to keep his eyes open. I cannot hold it until Prepotente gets here. Carl, cast Wisp Armor. He says there's no need.

beats.headline: No axe that I can see
beats.text: Britney comes out of the hospital tent behind Juice Box and me with her nose in the plans for the city's defences. I've looked her over. Her health is one hundred percent, and I see no sign anything is wrong. She doesn't have an axe, Carl; if she does, it's in her inventory. Juice Box feels nothing in her either. Elle says just ask her. Carl says not yet: if it's a presence like his, it might hurt her if it suspects we know. So we keep watching.

beats.headline: The table at the Lollipop
beats.text: The Lollipop, back table. I have a beer, and I slide Carl one, and Donut gets a Shirley Temple with extra cherries. Everyone checks in. Elle and I drew a military troop carrier. Tran is stuck in his garage. Zhang is not here: Li Na isn't really talking to him, and she killed almost every other team in their heat, so next race will show whether Prepotente is right about crawlers racing crawlers. Chris says his big rig is big but slow. Kinda like you, I tell him, and he almost smiles.

beats.headline: It's the sock
beats.text: Dong goes down outside the other team's garage and everyone assumes the Dominators cast something on him. I wrap him in my wings. There's nothing wrong with him now. What bothers me is where the sock was: he'd left it in our garage. Near it, he's actively healed and his health doesn't go up, which means it's sustaining him. Rosetta and Mordecai don't trust sapient weapons. If he's addicted, I don't know what to do yet. We don't tell him until we have a plan.

beats.headline: Two brothers, and no more
beats.text: I came over to get away from Elle's fan, Linus, and the slugs find me anyway. Donut asks how many brothers I have, in the present tense, and everyone flinches. I answer it the way it is. Full siblings, two. I was the youngest and the only girl. Then I tell Carl to open his boxes before Donut's blood bar drains, and I go and play, because somebody has to unlock Funky Kong if anyone in this room is ever going to beat Samantha.

beats.headline: Her card will not go back
beats.text: I get a notification: Jacobus is permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card. I did not summon him. Carl did something. Now there is a fist-sized reverse tooth fairy doing laps around my head in Danish, asking my friends to show him their teeth and pay him three hundred and twenty gold. We are in a safe area. When he goes for Prepotente I catch him in my hand. No. He will not be doing that with any of my friends.

beats.headline: Crawler Henrietta's team is gone
beats.text: We pull onto the road just as Carl's truck passes, and now we are behind him. Elle is driving, like an old lady. We have lost a team already this heat. Crawler Henrietta, from Angola, new this heat. They hit a trap. It swallowed their mount whole, and she and her partner are gone. Carl sends us his course and asks about the cliff ahead. We have a wall-climbing kit. It is slow. He says he will wait until we are over, so we go.

beats.headline: Looking forward to this
beats.text: Donut has zapped Mongo into the bar so he won't miss Uncle Carl's stage debut, and the patrons are jumping back from his wings. Carl won't tell us why this quest matters so much. I don't need to know. I tell him the truth, and I smile when I do it: I've been looking forward to this moment for a long time. He says he hopes I like Norwegian music. Elle is going to be furious she missed it. I wave Chris, Florin, Bautista, Britney and Jurgen to the back, and suddenly the place is packed.

beats.headline: Goddamnit, Carl
beats.text: He posted his plan for the eleventh floor to his page in the Book of Voodoo, and I left him three paragraphs on why it gets us all killed. He wrote back that he hopes I take a deal, that nobody would blame me, that I deserve the rest. So I told him: Goddamnit, Carl. This is insane. I still know he has no other choice, with Emberus coming due. My blood bar has an hour on it. The volunteers are gathering in Hungry Eyes, and Florin is choosing. Can we get on with this?

beats.headline: That's not my dad
beats.text: Elle and I hit our gate in 310, and I cast Confuzzled on the room so the bugs stay stunned long enough for us to drop out. Carl calls the man on the floor my dad. That's not my dad. It's my uncle, and all that room shows is that he would have died even if I hadn't left. That's a good thing, honestly. I'm fine. The other me looks terrible, Elle says, and she's right. What I want to know is why Gucci's eyes weren't sewn.

beats.headline: She will not take a deal
beats.text: Carl messages me that I've done enough and can rest. Oh, fuck off, Carl. He knows Chris won't take a deal unless I do. I know it too. I can't run from this any more than he can, and I ask him whether he's tried that speech on Donut. He has. It went how I thought it would. We're fucked, and I know it. I still think this is the right call. If we're going to lose, I want to go down fighting.

beats.headline: You run and don't look back
beats.text: Chris puts his hand on my face and says it isn't as warm as usual. He's wrong. This isn't goodbye, Chris Andrews. But promise me: if you get the chance, you take it. You see that exit and you're still in this body, you run and you don't look back. Even if it's just you, it'll all be worth it. He says he might turn back into a rock, or a dog. I don't care what he is. He says he loves me, and always has. Then he steps forward, waves, and drops away.

beats.headline: She holds the portal open
beats.text: I open the portal again, and I hold it. Louis comes through, and the crawlers from the multi-crawler heats come through behind him, and I keep it open until the last of them is on this side. Everybody else goes back to the track, crosses the finish line, and takes the stairs. Somebody has to stand at the door. It's usually me, and I'm all right with that.

beats.headline: Real people, just like you
beats.text: Mannequins, televisions, smoke. At the end we each hold up a sign. Mine says You are watching real people die, and on the back, Real people, just like you. Muchen, Qianfan and Lingyun hold up theirs, and Elle holds up hers. The AI likes it. Not going to lie: that felt good to get out. Chaco is still unconscious on the donkey. I didn't dare heal him as we passed. Somebody else did.

tagline.text: Agatha is travelling with the Meadow Lark party. Her file is thinner than it should be, and I keep very good files.

Agatha once travelled with the Meadow Lark party, and she is now a warlord of the War Mage Rebellion. Warlord Akuma has just called her an enemy to all of you. He did not elaborate, and neither will I.

beats.headline: The mysterious Agatha
beats.text: Agatha. She is with the Meadow Lark party when Carl and Donut find them: Imani, Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, and her. The others I can account for, level by level, box by box, all the way back to the stairs. Agatha I can account for. Mostly. Let's leave it there. The party calls her mysterious, which is the kindest word available and also the most accurate.

beats.headline: You are not doing this without her
beats.text: Entry: Crawler Agatha, no party, wheels her shopping cart in behind the six fighters, cackling, and the bars come down behind all seven. She is not in the plan and there is no room for her in the redoubt. Crawler Carl lifts the cart into his inventory, over objections. She is told to sit in the middle, and she screams about the cart for the whole fight. A flying bolt opens her head. She does not appear to notice.

beats.headline: She is in the room, and then she is not
beats.text: For the record: Agatha was in the room for the Ball of Swine beside Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and the cat, and made level four for being there, which is not the same as doing anything. Then she went missing. The next I have of her is her name on a dead grub. She is not on the recap. The party assumes the worst. I nearly always have a forwarding address.

beats.headline: Them critters already know
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Agatha, level four, still alive, arrives at the stairwell pushing the same squeaking cart. Crawler Carl has just found, in his inventory history, three items that came out of it: an inter-tunnel communications relay, flagged illegal; a platinum personal shield; a pulse pistol. One manufacturer. He offers to fix her wheel. No need, she says. Them critters already know she's here; they just don't know what to do about it. She goes down. The feed was out for a couple of minutes, which is nothing unusual.

beats.headline: Down the stairs with her cart
beats.text: Subject Agatha reappears at the station 36 stairwell: level eight, still human, still no class, pushing a squeaking shopping cart with the pink flamingo standing at the front. The steps turn into a ramp for her. She cackles that she sees they are all still kicking and goes down. Imani moves to intercept her and Carl holds her back, telling her they will talk about it another time. Imani wants to know what is happening. Nobody answers.

beats.headline: Down before the six-hour mark
beats.text: Sighting, via Crawler Li Jun at the stairwell by his bubble: a woman with a shopping cart pulls up out of nowhere, speaks to no one, and goes down the stairs before the six-hour mark. She is level 12. Li Jun does not know where she came from. Crawler Carl's position on the matter, stated in full: that is Agatha, and we just ignore Agatha.

beats.headline: A Residual of a different kind
beats.text: Clarification, supplied by a liaison in a closed office. Asked whether the old woman from Meadow Lark is the same sort of thing as a homeless man in Homestead, Orren says yes. Agatha is also a Residual, though of a different kind. Asked in what way, he says that is not the crawler's concern. Asked whether this means no more Agatha, he says he would not go that far.

beats.headline: Agent number 22, in Wenatchee
beats.text: On the night of the collapse, a flash message: Borant is starting the Earth season early. In an alley in Wenatchee, behind Meadowlark Elder Care, an old woman in a failing human shell reads it twice. Agent 22, also known as Agatha. Ten years peeled away from her collective. Not of the Apothecary, though she took a residual's body to read its feed; not Valtay, though biologically similar. Her people want the primal to know who it really is, and she would sweep the universe clean of biological life. She lights a fire in a barrel, to bring an entrance near. Timing is everything.

beats.headline: Asking for Carl by name
beats.text: A visitor at Shanty Town, reported by Li Jun, who was too busy to follow her up: a crazy old white lady with a shopping cart, level 23, no class, whom the system would not let him recruit. She came looking for Carl. She tried to get into Larracos, and Larracos would not let her in, so she went to the bar where Lucia Mar is still camped. Straight after, Zev passes on an order from the prime minister of the Syndicate himself. Carl is not to interact with Agatha. Nobody tells Zev why.

beats.headline: In the AI's metaphor
beats.text: Nobody is to venture too far from the metaphor. There is a girl who teaches the AI something new every day and whom its family likes, and she once had a huge boyfriend who she says is dead but is actually in prison. Is she using it? Trying to get it to fight him? What does she look like, Donut asks. She looks like Agatha, Orren says, drily. Then there is the older woman from the same hometown, who wants the prisoner dead too, and who has been giving the AI pointers on getting stronger.

beats.headline: Three emergency action items
beats.text: Warlord Agatha of the War Mage Rebellion has proposed three emergency action items. One: full access to the warlord system and the right to claim thrones. Granted, and something they already had. Two: full use of the Conscription spell, reaching unaffiliated players. Granted. Three: in the Peeling Phase, revert to the original Faction Wars rule, under which a defeated team's warlords and soldiers die. Granted, with a caveat: every affiliated soldier and warlord still on the field drops dead the moment the team is defeated. Then the Rebellion occupied Team Retribution's throne room.

beats.headline: What the adjutants think she is
beats.text: Two readings are on file. Rosetta's, privately: the woman with a knack for vanishing and reappearing is not the harmless kind of residual but the rarer kind, closer to the Nebulars who worship the Eulogist, and so an enemy of the Apothecary. Fopsy's, aloud, to Victory: she is trying to end the ascendency game quickly, because with no crawlers left the system shuts down and hibernates, and she may believe the local AI now threatens the Eulogist. He does not know how she enlisted the war mages. Victory doubts they are assisting each other at all.

beats.headline: Akuma's warning
beats.text: Warlord Akuma, to the Warlord Chat: the War Mages are leaving the floor, and they have found the Scavenger's Daughter and are taking her with them. Then, to Carl and Donut specifically, a warning. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. His words, not mine. He did not elaborate, and I am the referee here, not the colour commentary, whatever it may look like from where you're standing.

entities.name: Elle McGibbons

tagline.text: I'm Elle McGibbons, and at my age I am not built for sprinting. A young man with a cat pushed my wheelchair into the storm shelter, and I let him, because I am old, not stupid.
I have my own squad now, and we have just come through a door into Cuba to back Carl up. It's hotter than I expected, and a good deal more run down.

entities.voiceNote: Old, loud, and pleased about both. Short declaratives, jokes about her age before anyone else can, flirts with Carl to watch him squirm. Says Carl, or young man when she is enjoying herself; Imani by name. Never asks to be looked after and never pretends she did not need it.

beats.headline: Carl gets her inside
beats.text: The next episode is starting and the collapse is on top of us, and I am not, at my age, built for sprinting, or for walking. Carl, the young man with the cat, gets behind my wheelchair and pushes me into the storm shelter, and I let him, because I am old and not stupid. Then I ask him to put Divorce Court on the television. My Barry used to watch it.

beats.headline: The tunnel of love
beats.text: I'm on the last car of a train that rolls on wheelchair wheels, and the young man with the cat is walking beside me. I remember his name today. Carl. This reminds me of the tunnel of love. My Barry and I used to go to the carnival, and back then it was a boat, and I'd let him touch them, but only on the outside of my sweater. Barry wasn't pretty. If Carl were in that tunnel with me, I'd let him do more. He says thank you. I cackle.

beats.headline: Stuck to the ceiling
beats.text: One minute I'm on the last car, the next I'm on the roof of the hallway with my own wheelchair on top of me and my health deep in the red, and I start to cry. Carl picks me up like a sack and runs upside down, and then we fall. He gets me inside. Brandon helps me drink the potion. You saved me, I tell Carl. Thank you. Jack was always an ass. Poor Yolanda was such a good kid. Randall was dumb as a pigeon, but he deserved better. At least it was quick.

beats.headline: Barry, where are we?
beats.text: There's a nice young man kneeling by my bucket, and I ask him: Barry, where are we? He says we're in the dungeon, and I'm going down to the next floor. The dungeon? Like a sex thing? He says goodbye. I touch his cheek. We should have had children, Barry. I wish I hadn't talked you into working so hard. I think I've had too much to drink, or I'm having another one of those acid flashbacks. This cat keeps talking to me.

beats.headline: Tenth on the board
beats.text: Tenth on the draft leaderboard, spelled Elle McGib: Frost Maiden, Blizzardmancer, level thirteen, bounty one hundred thousand. She began the third floor at level one. Carl knows her as a wheelchair-bound resident of Meadow Lark and cannot work out how she got there; he has not talked to Brandon in several days.

beats.headline: On the board, two hours in
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons, formerly of Meadow Lark, is seen on the recap for one second: a blue-skinned, white-haired elf thing that floats instead of walking, skewering a troll-like monster in a subway car with icicles shot from her palms. Race: Frost Maiden. Class: Blizzardmancer. Level: seventeen; the list the crawlers were shown before had her at fourteen. Leaderboard rank: ten. Bounty: one hundred thousand gold. Carl realises he has already seen her in passing on earlier recaps without knowing it was her.

beats.headline: Frost Maiden, for now
beats.text: I'm a Frost Maiden. For now. Blue, small, and I float, and yes, those are still the anti-slip socks. I had a long list of options that would've put all my marbles back in the bag, but Brandon made me pick this one, for the manager benefit Carl told him about. Mistress Tiatha actually cried. I got my club tattoo for an icicle up the keister of an orc bartender. There's twenty of us left, and Imani still acts like the babysitter. And Carl is buying this round.

beats.headline: You come for Donut, you come for us
beats.text: A woman in the crowd is about to blast Carl and the cat, so she gets a two-foot icicle through the eye socket from behind. There's a skull after my name now. Don't care. I call dibs on her gear and tell Donut to loot hers before we get thrown out. Then I tell the room: anybody comes for Donut or Carl comes for all of us, and I will freeze the blood in their veins. A dwarf gives me the eyeball. He backs up. Donut, don't you cry. This was inevitable, and once word gets out, nobody will mess with you again.

beats.headline: Stuck at 275
beats.text: We clear stop 275 on the Camel Line and kill one of those Krakaren bitches. Easier than Imani thought. Then the train to 277 never comes. Imani blames that Quan Ch fellow for blowing up trains. It's twenty or thirty miles to the next stop and another thirty after that, so instead we take the druggie portal back to 272 and hike down to 271. If the Cobalt line is out too, there's a named train there called the Eviscerator. We're out of commission for a day, at least. I tell Carl. He tells me to stay away from the third rail. Oh, you know it.

beats.headline: A way out of the robot rooms
beats.text: Hey, hotshot. Your instincts were right. There's a secret way out of the robot rooms: a long tunnel sloping downward. It doesn't open until the robots wake up, and they don't wake until the monsters start their withdrawal. Lucky us, we don't have to fight the metal bastards. I still can't believe you blew two of them up. We're following the tunnel now. Sounds like there's another train track down there. It's far. More when we know.

beats.headline: Now's our chance
beats.text: It is not a train. It is a roller coaster with no cars. The robots fill rolling cages with ghouls and push them down, the bottom catches on the track, and off they go, like the thing at the hospital that takes your trays away but a hell of a lot faster. Carl says if it were him he would take it, and that it is a huge gamble. By the time the good roller coasters came along I was too old for them, and my Barry puked cotton candy after the tilt-a-whirl. Now's our chance.

beats.headline: No cobra lady in the crowd
beats.text: Carl asked me to go through every single person here and I did. No four-armed cobra lady. There's a man who turned himself into a mushroom, which, why. The fairy with the two mage daughters says the woman isn't answering anyone; if she came in with us, she took off. Imani is mother-henning everybody, and they're all terrified of her. Then Carl throws a train full of explosives our way and knocks everybody off their feet. He's lucky I can fly. I think the mushroom guy soiled himself.

beats.headline: Asking the manager about mimics
beats.text: Carl wants to know if there's a secret way to kill a mimic, so I ask him: are you about to do something really stupid, or have you done it already? Both, he says. Our manager says you don't fight the giant ones. Slice a piece off and it grows legs and runs home. Get more than half the mass off at once and it can't heal or change shape, but the cut-off pieces come for you, and they only die when the mimic does. I also talked a group out of the province boss at 48. You can hear it screaming from here.

beats.headline: Icicles off a god
beats.text: I've got a scroll that lets me fly higher and faster than an old lady has any right to, and I spend it. Icicles off Grull's head, and then I shoot past him like a bullet. He swipes at me and nearly has me. Then he opens his mouth and a blast of heat comes out that melts everything in its path, and it misses me by inches. I land on a derailed train by the gate, next to Katia wearing Carl's face, and take off again.

beats.headline: Twenty of us, and a sailboat
beats.text: There are twenty of us on this boat and not one of these old farts has ever sailed. I told them not to put me in Meadow Lark. The system gives us a sailing tutorial that won't tell you where the boom vang is. We'd have an NPC to help if I hadn't iced him, but he was being suspicious. Then Imani crashes the boat and I have to freeze the water so nobody drowns. My deity box gave me a spellbook. Graupel. Big ice storm, fifty mana, long cooldown. Most powerful thing I've got, and I'm kinda scared to try it.

beats.headline: An oil rig that throws fireballs
beats.text: We're the only ones in the water quadrant. We've got ourselves a galley now, fish-people doing the rowing, and we're probing our castle: an oil rig run by orcs that shoots fireballs at anybody who gets close. We've seen the land crawlers but haven't talked to them. Their castle's an oil refinery. The whole bubble is some stupid story about how we earthlings ruined our own planet. The air castle's a storm cloud that rains acid, I think. You get saddled with a bunch of layabouts, Carl?

beats.headline: Somebody has to send it
beats.text: Imani won't send this one, so I will, word for word, from Chris: Carl, Donut. Please. Kill me. It's okay. I give you permission. Carl tells him where he can go, and I tell Chris the same thing. But if they can't find a fix, they don't have a choice. If it was me stuck in there, I'd want someone to pull the plug. I pass along the rest when it comes through: Maggie doesn't worship Grull, she worships a god called Algos. Then Chris gets cut off mid-sentence, messaging suspended for thirty minutes.

beats.headline: A god walked through our world
beats.text: We finally pop our bubble, and a god taller than the whole place walks straight through it. On fire. Flattens a Lyrx elf village, knocks over two of their oil derricks and lights them. Half the world is in flames. Imani and I are stuck in the Desperado; nearly everybody else had to run for the stairwell, and we're lucky nobody caught fire. He's looking for something. He keeps shouting "Orthrus." Something tells me this is Carl's doing, and I say so. He says maybe. Well, you better fix it.

beats.headline: This floor was a drag
beats.text: Imani and I open the portal on our world and get the changelings through to the next floor, Twister and all, then rush back to the club, dead on our feet. Katia gives me a long hug and tells us to be careful. We always are. I wink at Carl, pat the cat on the head, and hand over the three pieces of the gate. I am looking forward to mixing it up with these three again. This floor was a real drag, doing it all myself.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess
beats.text: There I am on the recap, for everyone: Blizzardmancer to Tundra Princess. Some sort of earth class, combined with the ice. And I get to pick yet another class on the ninth floor. Seventh on the top ten, Frost Maiden, level forty-seven. Carl and I have managed one quick check-in this floor and he didn't ask how I'd changed, so this is how the young man finds out.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess, level fifty-one
beats.text: Tundra Princess now, level fifty-one, and you'd never know it to look at me. Same anti-slip socks from Meadow Lark. Wedding ring on a chain, because my fingers shrank. I've got a glass of something yellow, and Louis is watching it like a dog watches jerky. Katia turned this whole circus around to come save your ass, young man, and then the flying house got jumped by pterodactyls, so now we're stuck in the jungle. How was the convention?

beats.headline: Level 173 and loving it
beats.text: That thing was huge. Level 173, and it poked holes all over the Twister's garden. Most fun I've had since we got to this ridiculous floor. The little dinosaur cat is sulking that hers was only 138. Carl's pointing us at the next one fifteen miles west, right up against the edge of the map, and Katia says we're already on it. Louis says he doesn't know if he can stomach it again.

beats.headline: Right above the church
beats.text: I was right above it when the church blew. Green smoke, like the mushroom spores but thicker. Gave me a buff against fire and poison. Five or six dryads went up pinwheeling blood, it all swirled into a giant flower, and the bud opened with that eyebrowless hunter inside. The gore poured into his mouth and he swelled like a can of potted meat on a cookfire. Out came an antlered squirrel no bigger than me. Diwata, sponsored by Circe Took. It flew off like a rocket. Mordecai wants the pollen. He can wade in himself.

beats.headline: What the hairless hunter told her
beats.text: I got the story out of that hunter with no eyebrows. Vrah messaged his brother, told him he'd be safe if he went into that temple, and tricked him into being the birthing vessel for Diwata. They murdered one of their own just to cure Vrah of a venereal disease, and the brother is pissed about it. Now the bug lady is birthing actual flesh-and-blood babies and sending them out into the world. What happens when the floor collapses? Do they just go away? They're her kids!

beats.headline: Cat-nac the Magnificent
beats.text: The queen's cat drops onto Carl's shoulder in a gold turban with a feather four feet high, and I lose it. Louis says goose. It's not a goose, it's one of those mushroom penises. It's Horton! Hey, Horton, you have merch! How do you even walk in that thing, cat? Should we call you Cat-nac the Magnificent? He promises to bathe in our offal. I tell Donut her ex-boyfriend has anger issues. She says she's always been attracted to the bad boys. You and me both, sister.

beats.headline: A bigfoot in Bermuda shorts
beats.text: First things first, Carl: skipping a level without warning us was messed up. Not all of us are as trained up as you. He swears it was all Pony. Then the boxes, and holy shitballs, I got an ice staff I won't stop talking about. And just now a goddamned bigfoot crossed the road in front of me wearing Bermuda shorts. He almost got splattered. So here's my idea, young man. We build the roadblocks away from the saferooms, so the pileups don't happen near the stairwells.

beats.headline: A snooze fest out west
beats.text: Carl asks in chat whether we're going into the Desperado Club. Imani tells him we still haven't found one. And it's a total snooze fest over here: all churches and boring monsters. I've got my squatchy and my gumberoo and my batsquatch, and everything else sucks. We don't even have any quests. So we're moving down to the outskirts of Portland to see if there's anything interesting there. Carl tells me to be careful.

beats.headline: Don't let her die, cowboy
beats.text: I tell Carl I hope he knows what he's doing, cowboy. If anything happens to her, Tony the Tiger goes, and there goes the tea he makes us every morning, which I'm fairly sure is the only thing holding Imani together. Imani and I are going to pick different places in phase two so they can't make us fight each other. My squatch squad will kick anybody's ass. I'd have bet good money on Louis cracking first. Poor kid. Louis says he's standing right here.

beats.headline: Not really them
beats.text: Belgium. I don't know anybody in Belgium, thank God. Imani's in Detroit and I'm not with her; my squad and I landed on our own, and everybody else is scattered to the four winds. So I tell the lot of them what needs telling. Keep your wits about you. These are just memory ghosts. If they're going to make us fight loved ones, remember it isn't really them. Don't let them mess with your heads.

beats.headline: She has a martyr complex
beats.text: Listen to me, young man. You have to figure this out. That girl has a martyr complex, and she's not going to want to fight anybody. She's a good kid. The best person I ever met, and we need her. Don't let her give up. Don't let her sacrifice herself. Me? I don't know who I'm facing yet.

beats.headline: At the church with the rest
beats.text: The church, and it is full. Imani is there, and then Katia's people, and then Li Na's, and then mine. My own squad. Every one of us got here on a Doggy Door upgrade that Lucia handed round before she took the stairs down. I do not know what that girl is. She gave us a way through, and I am standing in a church with my friends because of it, so I will say thank you and keep the rest of my opinions where they belong.

beats.headline: Graupel at level sixteen
beats.text: Graupel has a one week cooldown and I only ever cast it once before, on the fifth floor. It's a war spell, outdoors only. Somebody had to, so I float up and cast it at the mob coming for Donut. The spell says it's casting stronger than usual. It's only a level five spell and it goes off at level sixteen, and then the sky comes down in fist-sized hail. When the steam clears there's a field of dead demons as far as you can see, and I've gone up six levels at once. Seventy-two. A bunch of achievements. What the hell?

beats.headline: Tundra Princess to Hailstorm Queen
beats.text: Class selection again, in the warehouse, with only a few of us this time. I pick wind, and Tundra Princess becomes Hailstorm Queen. Donut is thrilled I'm a queen. This is probably as far as it goes: I can add the final element if I ever make it to the twelfth floor, but I'm betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we get anywhere close.

beats.headline: I found out
beats.text: Back in our territory, young man. I'm pretty sure I've found every artillery battery on both sides, though I can't swear to a hundred per cent. And we've got a new problem. They have another nasty surprise waiting for us on the naga side. Remember when you asked me to find out why those robot fellows wanted pet levelling sped up? Well. I found out.

beats.headline: The first anti-air gun
beats.text: Man, I wish I could cast my Graupel spell. Can't, so it's Carl's missile launcher, and I hope it works as advertised. Carl says for god's sake keep moving. Louis drops, and I fire. First anti-air gun: hit, but it had a protection spell on it. It went over, though, and with luck it won't be firing for a while. Moving to the second one.

beats.headline: Second battery down
beats.text: The second anti-air battery is down! Louis, hurry your ass up. The first one's almost back up already, and I'm running, because they've a pair of mages on my scent. Imani says get the hell out of there. Then I tell Louis his path to the enemy castle is free of anti-air guns, as far as I can see.

beats.headline: The goat got there first
beats.text: Holy hell, Carl, get in position. Everything's fouled up. Most of their army is already dead, corpses rotting in the barracks; Edgar found them on his scan. And the moment we moved in, that goat friend of yours appeared out of nowhere and went apeshit. He's level 99 now. He didn't attack us, but he called me every name there is, and when Imani told him to calm down he called her a festering gutter maggot trollop. So the sluggalos went after him. Half are sliming across naga territory, whooping. The other half took one of the carts. Driving it? Not very well.

beats.headline: He pulled back at the last moment
beats.text: Sorry, guys. That war mage prick snatched the gate right out of my hands. I haven't been walloped like that since my bachelorette party. Samantha laughed. Carl did not. But listen, Carl, they could've killed me. The strong one, the elf-looking guy, pulled back at the last moment. It was almost like he was trying not to kill me. Now collect the bodies. They said the heads explode. Then let me cast Subterfuge again, and are you ready to finally get your hands dirty?

beats.headline: A goddamn hero
beats.text: For chrissakes. We were only out of it for about an hour. In that Witness spell, all piled up, we were paralysed and felt everything; the moment Donut cast Battle Formation, it was lights out. Now she's apologising to everyone. My throat feels like I gargled sandpaper and I smell like that god's schlong, and that's it. We lost people from the towers when we woke. Some got burned by fleshers. Several lost limbs. She pulled through for all of us anyway, in a way nobody else could. Not even Carl. She's a goddamn hero.

beats.headline: The superfan
beats.text: A fan meet-and-greet, like the Butcher's Masquerade, name tag and everything, in a huge room. One guy came. A soother. Bought his own yacht to get through the quarantine and meet me, and he is standing there blushing in a shirt with a cartoon of me with no clothes on. Now he wants me to sign a giant pillow with me on it, and they have not even got my anatomy right. My nipples are not blue. If this place did not have safe room rules, I would have iced him already.

beats.headline: Under the table
beats.text: Imani and I drew a military vehicle that handles like a three-legged pig walking backward through a snowstorm, and Florin informs me it is one of the finest troop carriers in the world. Lovely. Under our table, wrapped round the leg, is my one fan, Linus, in his fanny pack and his shirt of me with no clothes on, because that is where little perverts sit when they ask stupid questions. Five hundred tourists were meant to win extra access to their favourite racer after each heat. He is the only one who came, so he wins by default.

beats.headline: She crushes one of Akuma's
beats.text: Donut mutes him. That part was planned. The ice bolt to the crotch was mine, and so is the rest. That little magical fart and his friends tried to kill me and stole my Gate before I was done with it. When I was a kid we hit thieves with sticks and threw their shoes in the sound. Now I can freeze a man's balls and break them like dollar store ornaments. That was just the left one. He answers everything Carl asks, or the right one goes too.

beats.headline: Five bucks on the ex-husband
beats.text: Cascadia's on the speaker, drunk, telling us somebody called Cumberland is dead. Five bucks says it's her ex-husband. It is. You haven't seen bitter until you've seen a woman work out after fifty years of marriage that her husband was a cheating idiot. We had plenty at Meadow Lark. Francine Herrada tried to throat-stab the new wife with a knitting needle, and I called her Killer after, and she didn't care for it. Mind you, she said spice in food was a sin. That poor husband.

beats.headline: Barry's song, and the impostor
beats.text: I'm not much for speeches, so I talk about Barry. Bartholomew Eli McGibbons, forty-three years my husband, thirty-five years gone. Louis hits play and it's Creedence, his favourite. He wouldn't have survived five minutes in this place. Then I float over to Linus. My fan club, the Snow Cones, knew an impostor the moment he stepped into the dungeon, and the real Linus's friends posted his essay where we could all read it. You keep coming in here to kill us, sweetheart. This is our house now.

beats.headline: Die with hope in our hearts
beats.text: Don't you worry about those tracksuit idiots, Donut. They had a way out, they lied to us, and they'd have killed me, Imani and Chris at that exit. Ivan bragged about pulling down a whole metal bridge for scrap and wrecking a train. Carl asks if it's true. Does it matter? Look at us, risking our necks again to save a few people. It matters whether a crazy Carl plan works, sure, we die if it doesn't. But we'll die with hope in our hearts alongside our friends.

beats.headline: A sign for the viewers
beats.text: Betrayal float. Mannequins in chairs in front of televisions, black and red smoke off the top, and signs. Imani's says you are watching real people die. Mine is at the very end: To all the viewers of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth: Fuck you. The back is a very detailed middle finger. The AI calls ours its favourite. Whew. We had an interpretive dance group at Meadow Lark once, and that made more sense than its story.

beats.headline: Folded in the APV
beats.text: I'm alive. Barely. Me and Bodi are stuck in what's left of the truck after the god blew up, and somebody had better dig us out. It's wrecked pretty good. I haven't been folded like this since Brandon showed us how to use Tinder. Imani is shouting my name on the chat. I'm here, Imani.

entities.name: Zev

tagline.text: Okay, so, I'm on my way to see Carl and Princess Donut, and when I get there the cameras will switch off, because they always do around kua-tin. Open your boxes before I arrive.

I'm Borant's Assistant Communications Representative, and my job is to walk crawlers through the Syndicate programmes that want them. Officially, that's all. Unofficially, Princess Donut, Mordecai and I have all seen Gossip Girl, and I won't pretend that doesn't matter.

entities.voiceNote: Brisk, kind, and permanently worried about her job. Speaks in the cadence of a scheduling message: Okay, so; I need you to; I am not supposed to say this. Carl and Princess Donut, always in full. Never swears, never speculates on air, never says more than she is allowed and always says exactly as much.

beats.headline: She explains how the shows work
beats.text: Okay. So. Carl has just met his first Borant dungeon admin and managed to be civil, which I am counting as a win for everyone, including me. My job today is to walk them through how crawlers take part in the Syndicate programmes, and I get through all of it. Then Princess Donut mentions Gossip Girl, and Mordecai has seen it, and I have seen it, and for a few minutes nobody in the room is anyone's liaison.

beats.headline: Nobody in this room is an idiot
beats.text: Okay, so, Carl shouts at me, and I let him finish. Then I tell him how it actually is. Mordecai relaxed the moment he saw I wasn't wearing a party badge. My boss is a member. If I say the wrong thing, my entire family is wiped from the universe. The mobs out there live in fear of crawlers. We are all parts of the same machine, and all of us are afraid. I am on your side, Carl. The better you do, the longer you survive, the better I do.

beats.headline: A voice in his head
beats.text: Okay, so, I have been watching. Carl tells Brandon that the day we stop helping each other is the day we stop being human, and it is great, and I ask him to say it again without the cough. He will not. The save-the-elderly storyline is playing well with most viewers; about twenty percent of the focus group calls them dead weight. Princess Donut is right that it is a little dry. Then an old man stands up on the train with his pants around his ankles, and I tell them to run.

beats.headline: Censured, and cleared
beats.text: Okay, so, I was censured by the System AI. It decided I cheated by warning Carl and Princess Donut before the rage elemental appeared, and I was suspended. My representative appealed, and on review they found Carl noticed the man at the same moment I shouted, so my record is clean. It is not really clean. Once the AI notices you, it is difficult to get it to un-notice you. Mukta should never have booked that show, and I apologise. Also, Carl, there is a video I need to tell you about.

beats.headline: Thumbs up on the classes
beats.text: Hello, hello. Okay, so, good news, Carl and Princess Donut. Odette's show was another hit, and the majority of viewers are giving a thumbs up to your class and race choices. Both of you picked unique classes, which is always a plus. There are a few other Primals, no straight cats, one were-cat and some cat girls. The public cannot see Mordecai now. No VIP crawlers nearby, and I'd avoid the locals. The next interview is likely the fourth night. I have had to take on extra people for the requests.

beats.headline: The producer is not talking
beats.text: Carl, I'm watching. The whole universe is watching, and we are all rooting for you. I can't interfere, and I told him so. He explained what he wants anyway. I said it was impossible; he said try. So: I messaged the producer, and he didn't want to speak with me. I think he is waiting to see how this plays out. My boss made me run the request past the Syndicate AI referee, and it will only allow this under very strict circumstances. Nobody can give Carl any help whatsoever.

beats.headline: She signs on Carl's behalf
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl wants a message relayed to the producers of Vengeance of the Daughter, word for word, and this is not what we discussed. My boss patches them in and they hear all of it. They say, and I am quoting, "Let's see what you got for us, Crawler." It is a deal. Carl wants it official, on paper. I tell him it is official, because I have the power to sign on his behalf, and he says that is terrifying. I ask him if he knows what he is doing. He says no.

beats.headline: Who makes Vengeance of the Daughter
beats.text: Okay, so, Carl and Princess Donut are booked for the day after tomorrow on a round-table show called Danger Zone. Other crawlers, a few intergalactic celebrities, maybe a politician, and an uncensored call-in segment, so be ready for anything. Then Carl asks who is behind Vengeance of the Daughter. Not a Kua-Tin company: nobody in our system may run serials while we run the game. It is Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, from one of the center systems, and the gentleman I dealt with was a Sac. Carl asks what a Sac is. Since he does not know, I cannot tell him.

beats.headline: Booking schedules are public
beats.text: Okay, so. That was terrifying, and I thought Carl and Princess Donut were dead for certain. How did they know which trailer? Rental trailers put their booking schedules out for anybody to see, so everyone can coordinate availability. Nobody has ever needed to hide one, because nobody has ever tried to assassinate a crawler outside the dungeon. Now the Valtay have blown the royal yacht into dust. The good news is that nobody on the net is saying anything negative about Carl and Princess Donut; the prince is the villain. Our team is fielding a wave of interview requests. Odette has the contract on the next one.

beats.headline: Katia needs to be more interesting
beats.text: Carl, Princess Donut, okay, so. I'm still working on your mid-floor appearance, and a lot depends on the sponsorship bidding. I need to bring something up while I can. It's about Katia. People don't like her. Odette complained about her participation in the interview, and the tunnel is full of people hoping she goes so it can be just the two of you again. You either need to ditch her or make her more interesting. A mohawk, maybe. I'm not allowed to message her directly yet. If they don't like her, they stop watching, and fewer views means fewer prizes.

beats.headline: Planet Beautiful
beats.text: Hi guys! The fans liked your line at the end, Carl. People want the trademark line more often, though not too much, or it gets weird. Okay, so, I booked you two for a show in two days. Katia stays in the dungeon; Mongo goes in the cage. It's called Planet Beautiful: narration from a sound booth, a segment about this season's planet. Carl asks what the segment is and tells me I'm a terrible liar. Okay. It's about beauty pageants. And pet shows. Princess Donut says yes before he can.

beats.headline: In case something happens to me
beats.text: Okay, so. I am still in the suit, because the dual-layer system was supposed to be replaced at the end of the third floor and Hinter would not rent us the cores. Congratulations, Katia, on the top ten. Odette has added a Katia option to her contract, with a rider: be zippier. In case something happens to me, I want you to know I appreciate how hard you have worked. Loita is Bloom, she has lost her main account, and she is claiming yours. I am not Bloom. Something happened at home. I cannot talk about it. Also, your chats go public tomorrow, for people who pay extra.

beats.headline: Just your social media manager
beats.text: Hey guys! Wow, that was fantastic. Great job. Your social numbers are looking great! Okay, so, Princess Donut, I am just your social media manager now. Administrator Loita is in charge of all public appearances, and you are not able to message me directly unless I open the chat. I've never been better, thank you. Carl, the audience is noting that you are being extra angry with the other crawlers. Katia, your numbers are rising steadily. Princess Donut, people want more Mongo, and you have used your new spells only once. Now get back out there and kill, kill, kill!

beats.headline: If you must choose, Ivy
beats.text: Okay, so, the audience loves the strange vibe of the doll, but I tend to agree with the crawler: it does not sound like Princess Donut. We put that in the notes. Veriluxx hasn't changed it. Carl says he can't imagine it doing well, presented the way it is, and I tell him he is not wrong. There are memes. When Princess Donut asks whether she should name her robot Charlie or Ivy, I tell her it is inconsequential, crawler. Then, before the chat closes: if you must choose a name, I would go with Ivy.

beats.headline: Goodbye, from behind the scenes
beats.text: Anyway, the fans really enjoyed that battle. Good job, you two. I'm sorry to say this is goodbye, however. I will still be Loita's assistant, working behind the scenes, but you no longer need a social media manager. Loita explains it: they have bought the social media board, so nobody needs to relay what the dry masses are saying about them. Carl asks whether I can come down so Princess Donut can say goodbye. Loita says no, of course not. He asks whether I can come to the infomercial. Loita says it is not my job anymore.

beats.headline: A message from the politburo
beats.text: Hello, Carl and Princess Donut. Okay, so, there was another last-minute legal challenge to what you are about to attempt, and it failed; the Valtay sent an attorney to help Borant. I have also been asked to pass on a message. It is from the politburo, who have recently replaced the board of directors in control of Borant, and it is a direct quote: they approve of what you are planning, and game-breaking antics that directly affect sponsors will not be tolerated in the future. Carl, you know such language is not acceptable. Best of luck to you.

beats.headline: They are enraged
beats.text: Oh my god, Carl. They are enraged. This is not what you promised. If you fill Larracos with water and mobs, it kills the NPCs. The markets flood, the mercenaries die, and if the NPCs at the entrance bar die, the sponsors lose access to the Desperado Club. We cannot add new worker NPCs once a level is created. That is written into the rules. Fixing it would need a Syndicate vote they will not have, and the AI on board. You have killed thousands. Tens of thousands. There will be consequences.

beats.headline: She reminds him the contract stands
beats.text: Carl. I know you have a lot going on. I know the Hunting Grounds are the Hunting Grounds. I still have to say this, because saying it is my job: your agreement with the Vengeance of the Daughter programme is still in effect. Nothing you signed on an earlier floor stops mattering because you have gone down a set of stairs. It doesn't work like that. Please don't make me be the one who has to remind you twice.

beats.headline: Bad timing, on purpose
beats.text: Hey guys! I just wanted to quickly touch base. We rearranged the schedule a little, so you'll be visiting with Odette today. Try not to schedule a boss battle or anything during that time. Yes, everything is okay, and yes, I will be there. Carl, I also want to remind you that you'll be receiving some extra scrutiny before you go to the trailer. So just be aware. But you'll be fine, because you're both really strong and brave. Especially you, Donut.

beats.headline: The ratings are okay
beats.text: Okay, so, Princess Donut asks how the ratings are on Signet's show, and I say they're okay. Ratings were good on the third floor when Carl and Princess Donut were involved, and they lagged a little while they were on the fourth and fifth. People really like the six warriors and their caterpillar mount. Some of the hardcore fans think Carl and Princess Donut are going to make everything implode before there's a resolution, or take the show over. I am talking to the Sensation people so they're back in a saferoom in time for Odette's show.

beats.headline: Close that yap
beats.text: Okay, so, Odette dropped this on me as we started preparing, and I'm the one who tells Carl the part she didn't: she's using Bea to blackmail Borant. I also have to tell him about the fan box. The votes are in, and soon after he opens it he goes to an event with fans, alone, without Princess Donut. That's where they were going to confront him. When he asks why I'm so nervous, I whisper that Donut is going to need him, to focus on that, and that he needs to close that yap of his right now. Please.

beats.headline: Linger as much as you can
beats.text: Okay, so, this is not a regular production trailer. It's a Valtay landing vessel parked at the bottom of the ocean, and we are under constant surveillance, by the AI and by the ship's own security. The rental trailers were kicked off system after an escape attempt. Donut had quite the fight, and she's okay, safe in the guildhall. I can't tell him more. I tell Carl it might be in his best interests to linger as much as he can, that others may be waiting where he goes back down, and that he needs his rest.

beats.headline: Because of a pin
beats.text: Okay, so, the moderator is Circe Took, a minor hive queen, and the hunter Carl killed was her daughter, Xindy, Vrah's little sister, on her first hunt. Try to avoid talking about her government. He asks if I'm doing okay. About the best anyone can expect. Our whole system has gone dark. Those of us who stayed on after the change don't know if we'll be welcomed home or executed as traitors. My entire family was slaughtered because I refused to wear a pin. But I've got a job to do. I have to go, Carl.

beats.headline: The interview tunneled
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl, you need to get to a saferoom. You're getting filthy, and you have your event. I also need you to know that Odette's interview with you and Princess Donut and Beatrice tunneled last night, and between that and the Dark Hive business there is a lot of attention focused on you. I'll see what I can do about your attorney. There is something else we need to discuss, but I will do it in person.

beats.headline: Promoted, and still in the dark
beats.text: Skindle, who looks after Dmitri and Maxim, introduces me as her boss. I did get a promotion. Carl, about your replacement sponsor: the first winner of the bidding could not pay, so there was a new bidding event, and the winner wants to award your first benefactor box during the signing. You will see who at the end. Who could not pay is still above my pay grade. About three hundred fans won a lottery place, plus thirty premiums, plus press.

beats.headline: Warrants, and who buys them
beats.text: Carl, we can't bring you anywhere. Nihit has been healed and wants to press charges for assault. It was off system, so the regular rules apply, and you are not a full citizen. If they prosecute, the charges are shelved until you're out, and then you get a warrant with a sentence, usually two or three cycles. Licensed corporations can buy out warrants when they need workers. It is not true slavery. They get paid when they get out. They're criminals.

beats.headline: The council closes the courts
beats.text: Okay, so. After the brambles hit Zockau there were several lawsuits, and they failed immediately. Then the Syndicate Council itself, not the subcommittee, the actual council, ruled that nobody may file a suit naming the AI as a defendant. It is meant to slow the deterioration. That has started a whole new set of suits about whether the council can do that. Mordecai is right that the money is flowing to Borant. Our Valtay partners have shown no dismay so far. The council and the liaisons are very nervous. Now stop talking about this.

beats.headline: Drop this, Carl
beats.text: Carl. I highly suggest you drop this. I say it once, while he is telling Signet that the people controlling her world will not let her win, and he does not drop it. I say it again when he starts offering her a new plan: they are not going to let it happen this way, and we have discussed this.

beats.headline: Do not bring Signet to the party
beats.text: Carl, I need to be very clear about this, so I am going to be. Do not attempt to smuggle Signet into the party. If you try, the production company is contractually forced to send her directions to do something premature, and it will get her killed and very likely you with her. If she is in that room, the courts have to decide who owns what happens next. It is a hard rule: nobody touches the main event. He tells me he has no such plans.

beats.headline: It's complicated, Carl
