beats.text: She comes apart and I hold on to her until it passes. Then I tell the others what I have worked out, because somebody has to say it out loud. There is more than one of her in that head. Several. Some of them are children. And the dog matters. Whatever is happening to Lucia, the dog is at the centre of it.

beats.headline: It's her twin
beats.text: The queen drops Carl and I pick him up. So much for peaceful. Katia was right: it looks like Iffy, but it isn't. It's her twin. I can tell. It's not really her either. Iffy was worried about what had happened to her sister. It's not right, them using her body like that. We have to do something about it. Carl says he's working on it.

beats.headline: Heave
beats.text: We fight the queen on the beat, the way Carl said: nothing magical, half of us firing on the two and four, the other half on the one and three. Arrows, rocks, my shotgun. Heave! Her shield stutters like a strobe light, cast over and over, and it can't keep up with what we throw. Her health goes into the red. She stops casting the shield and falls to a knee, and her hands crackle red.

beats.headline: A Unique in Ecuador
beats.text: I am in Ecuador. I left Katia's party just before the last level broke. I have another upgrade for the shotgun. I am in contact with Lucia. I have no totems yet. I do have a quest: track and kill or capture a powerful Unique that is terrorizing my region. That is all I am saying about my situation.

beats.headline: Six totems and a spare
beats.text: My squad's full: me and six totems, a saber-toothed tiger and a giant caiman called Roy among them. Lucia only talks to me sometimes, but she doesn't attack me on sight anymore. I flagged the one I had the quest for. He was raising zombies out of a village cemetery for fun. I walked up while he was falling-down drunk, handed him a supreme healing potion and said his dad wanted him to drink it. He's undead. I summoned him once and he shot me in the stomach. I'm not keeping him. I slide the card to Donut. Good luck, mate.

beats.headline: Claymores by the door
beats.text: Everybody is checking in on the chat. Mine: I'm in my zone alone. I had claymores set up by the entrance, and I didn't have to use them. Nobody to face. I just walk to the door. Lucia isn't here, which means she didn't get a key. Anyone who sees her, say so in chat.

beats.headline: No traps past the door
beats.text: Carl wants to know if a trap will sit in the stairwell chamber, so I go down early. Five by five meters, a glowing stair in the middle. I drop a trap. Error: outside the level, no traps in the stairwell chamber, nice try. Sorry, mate. Lucia buys up every teleport trap on the market; those and alcohol are all she buys. Li Jun says she has taken out half the keyless squads. I ask Carl to message me if he gets word of her.

beats.headline: War Leader III, then General
beats.text: Donut touches each of us to make us officers and lets me set up the hierarchy. I start at War Leader III. After some time with the base system that becomes Colonel, and after Donut tells me to upgrade myself, General. Most of the core group gets the same. The dancers get Sergeant First Class, so they can recruit and command the base troops. I'd named that rank Adjutant. They made me change it. Imani, Elle and I are leaving for headquarters to meet the adjutant.

beats.headline: The caiman lifts the wall
beats.text: We only get so many officers, so the builders and the crawlers are going in as sergeants and chiefs, which lets them change the camp. Everyone else is legionnaire, with corporals running teams. A wall section goes over and buries itself in the dirt, and I go to help. My card from the last floor still comes once a day. I call him: a giant caiman, twenty-five feet of him. He gets his snout under the wall and heaves it up while the workers push. He times out before long. I come back grumbling about artillery.

beats.headline: The north will not hold
beats.text: Bad news from the northern front. We are holding for now, but without backup we might break in a matter of hours, so I'm preparing to fall back to our fallback position. I've ordered the castle to prepare for a siege, just in case. Could really use some air support, and some of those new NPCs Carl just gathered. He says they're on their way.

beats.headline: Two Weepers, captured
beats.text: Good news, bad news. We stopped their armor in its tracks and captured two of the rolling boom boxes. Weepers. Like British Mark Vs from the first world war, with a top turret and a single anti-air tube, and super high tech on the inside. Warning Louis to steer clear of them. Bad news: the ones facing Carl know they lost the whole regiment, so they'll move soon. Katia and Bautista are flanking Carl's position with what's left of the 105th, to keep the west open and a corridor of retreat into Shanty Town. Carl asks if we're having fun yet. I'll tell him face to face.

beats.headline: Not locked up in stasis
beats.text: I tell Carl he's lucky Lucia only cast two nets. She's the queen of the triple tap. She's still in with the liaisons; we'll see what she settles on when she comes out. Most will take a deal if one's offered. They're tired. Me, I'd rather go down fighting than sit locked up in stasis, and a lot of us feel that way. The big blond barbarian clearing the street won't take one either. He came in with his pregnant wife, and she's up there with the kids. Protecting the kids. It's the most important thing one can do.

beats.headline: Partied with Lucia
beats.text: Before the stairs, Lucia sits on the ground sobbing while Imani, the barbarian and I talk to her about taking a deal. I get her to party with me. She says she'll take one. She was sketchy about it. None of us believe she will, so I won't take one either.

beats.headline: A tuk-tuk, and a first place
beats.text: Lucia and I drew a tuk-tuk. We came first in the heat anyway and took three regular upgrades instead of the Golden one: a tech shield, all-terrain and vertical-climb tires, and a GPS upgrade. Lucia is at the garage. Since the dogs went she has been flipping personalities a lot. About seventy per cent of the time she is herself and ready to skewer me. The rest, a random kid. She will not say why she did not take a deal. It is her turn to drive, so I have hired a mercenary. Jurgen says he will make the other team understand. I nod.

beats.headline: He puts the shotgun to Akuma's head
beats.text: I stay quiet while the mage talks, then I put the shotgun against his head, because he just lied. He left Faction Wars on his own. He can step in and out of floors as he pleases. So why does the most powerful thing in this world need crawlers along? He says to get it out of his face and he'll tell us, and he does. His utopia isn't so much a utopia any more. I knew it.

beats.headline: Harrying the unicorn down the tubes
beats.text: Team Sparkles and us, all the way down the track. Lucia Prime is back in the body and driving, and I'm keeping her from actually killing the unicorn and Lucienne. At the drop in the middle I let the trap go on purpose, so everyone behind gets an hour in the basement. Now I have to backtrack for the loop. The unicorn's going for it too. I have Denial of Service missiles, and I'll hit them just as they start it.

beats.headline: Lucia's father's house
beats.text: Lucia worked out that the rings count as magical gates, so anything that sees magic will find them. I pass that on. Then we go through our assigned ring on the sixth floor, and it is in Lucia's dad's house, and she is there too, a small one, sitting on the floor in front of the television, laughing. The real Lucia shut down completely for a moment. I tell the others what we saw. I do not know what this place is.

beats.headline: A C effort at best
beats.text: Resolution float. No presentation. No agreement on what the theme means. We ride on the back of Ajib's flatbed with paper flowers and pictures of our families. The girl in Lucia's body today drew her grandfather and her cat; she is from Andorra. The AI decides not to kill us, calls it a C effort at best, and breaks every one of our legs at once. That hurt. We keep going.

beats.headline: Carried down
beats.text: Stairwell notice. The stairwells to the twelfth floor are open. Crawler Florin has gone down them, and I use gone loosely: he was unconscious, and Crawler Lucia Mar carried him. That is the record. He is on the list of crawlers who reached the twelfth floor, and the list does not have a column for how.

entities.name: Lucia Mar

tagline.text: I was on the very first episode. Did you see me?
I was on the first episode. Now the recap says the cat has a feud with my dogs, and I'm looking for the cat and the man. Only them.
I'm still looking for the cat. We are. There's more than one of us in here.
There's more than one of us in here. There are more than a hundred thousand of us in here.

entities.voiceNote: A child. Short flat sentences, present tense. Says what she did and stops; the menace is in what she leaves out. The cat and the man, or their names when she wants to be exact. Never explains why, never raises her voice, never says sorry. On the sixth floor and below, I sometimes slips to we, and she does not correct it.

beats.headline: Seen in the first episode
beats.text: I'm on the show. The first episode of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, and I'm in it, so everybody with a screen has seen me now, including a man with no shoes and his cat. I watched the whole thing. I didn't say anything while it was on. I liked it more than I thought I would.

beats.headline: A Lajabless
beats.text: I am grown now. A Lajabless. Half the day I am beautiful, and my spells cost half, and I am half as strong. The other half my face is a skull, and I am twice as strong. My right leg is a goat's leg now, with a hoof. I can't run on walls any more. My dogs stay dogs. They look at me funny. My class is Black Inquisitor General. Cleric, magic-user, warrior. All three.

beats.headline: A feud, according to the recap
beats.text: The recap has a feud now. The cat, against my dogs, Cici and Gustavo. The cat says she never challenged anybody. The show says she did. Everybody watching heard the show. I know which one I am going to listen to.

beats.headline: First on the board
beats.text: First on the draft leaderboard, and by a distance: Lucia Mar, Lajabless, Black Inquisitor General, level twenty-nine, bounty one million, twice the next name down. Odette explains afterwards that the number is what other crawlers get for killing her. Princess Donut calls her ugly on air, and the audience laughs.

beats.headline: Still first, on the recap
beats.text: The show plays me pulling the head off one of the janitor ghouls in a train car. The blood goes everywhere and I am laughing. Then the board comes up. One. Lucia Mar. Lajabless. Black Inquisitor General. Level thirty. A million gold on me. The cat is seven. The man is six. A hundred thousand each.

beats.headline: Banned for life
beats.text: On the recap I make a necklace out of monster tongues. I am in a saferoom eating a bowl of rice, and one of my dogs sneaks up and takes it off my neck. The club at the stations will not let me in. Banned for life. I have tried a few times now. They are ready for me.

beats.headline: A room with five stairwells
beats.text: I find the room. It is big. There are five stairwells in it, in a circle. Then the zombie things come. I fight them. They keep coming. They keep coming. I fall back.

beats.headline: I told him I would
beats.text: The station is almost empty and there is a line at the stairs. This is mine. The crocodile man says crazy bitch where he thinks I can't hear. I throw a boy at him. He says I'm not right in the head. There is nothing wrong with my head. I tell him if he talks again there will be something wrong with his girlfriend's head. He talks again. Cici and Gustavo go for him and he shoots all three of us. We don't get hurt. She does. I told him I'd do it. He shoots me again, and I slide across the ice and down the stairs.

beats.headline: Gustavo, after the battle
beats.text: After a battle, Gustavo kills a group of crawlers. Gustavo is the smaller one. Everybody says he did it by accident. They say accident like it has quotation marks around it. Then I am not all right. I am worse than usual. They show me sitting in a room by myself, and I am crying. They put that on the show.

beats.headline: The smaller dog
beats.text: The recap shows me in my beautiful shape. A borough boss that looks like a stegosaurus. I put my damage reflect on the smaller of my two dogs. The boss crushes him. The damage goes back to the boss, and the boss dies. The dog is fine. I pull out the dead boss's eye with my bare hand and bite it like an apple. I am laughing.

beats.headline: Mayor of Alucarda
beats.text: This village is Alucarda. It already has a name, which the cat does not like. The mayor was R'aggah. He has returned to the earth. The mayor is me now. The tree man at the saferoom door tells the man so: an evil woman with two beasts that kill indiscriminately. The man asks where I am. Nobody answers him. He is gone before they can. The cat is still here.

beats.headline: She killed the wrong one
beats.text: The cat fought good. I say it's a draw and order two milks. The bear goes to get them and doesn't come back. Alexandro is mad. He says I should finish her. I tell the cat about Bini and Abraham and Siti, on the ice, and how I fell asleep and didn't tell Gus to sleep. Gus is the bad one. Then I tell Cici to kill the kitty, and the cat drops Cici's head through the floor. She killed the wrong one. Where's my milk? Yes. They all must die. No more friends.

beats.headline: Against the wall
beats.text: I stand against the wall and chew my fingernail. The crocodile comes across the room at me, and the man puts a hand on his chest and stops him. Florin just stares at me for a long time. Then something in his face goes soft, and he tells the man something is off with me. I run along the wall to the corner by the stage. I sit down on the floor and hold on to myself.

beats.headline: More than one of her in there
beats.text: Florin held on to me. He is kind to me even when I'm not the one who is here. He told the others that there is more than one of us in my head, and that some of the others are children too, and that the dog is the important part. He's right about the dog. I don't get to talk about the dog. I'm not the one who decides what I talk about.

beats.headline: She does not do the boss fight
beats.text: When the seal breaks I hide behind Florin with my hands over my ears while he shoots, and I cry. Then the castle is gone and everyone hangs in the air for a boss fight. I don't stay for it. I always set my teleports at stairwells. The moment before the fight starts, I use my escape thing, and I am gone.

beats.headline: What happened in Beijing
beats.text: I don't collect cards. They give me six totems anyway, all low ones. When a battle starts I throw the first one away and play the rest until my hand is empty, and then I can use my spells and my magic and my inventory. Me and my dog go in and kill everything. At the Soho building everybody fights. I set a teleport trap, and Fang's team is in it. He has a key. I kill him and his wife and take it. Florin asked me to help, so I wait for his friends. The cat and I have a score to settle. Next floor. Her and her dinosaur.

beats.headline: I don't want to play anymore
beats.text: I come up the tower for the dinosaur. That is justice. The cat throws barrels at Gus and he keeps sliding away from me, and I tell him to get back up. Then something hits me, and I tumble down the ramp with a crab, into the man. The crab holds me up in his claws and shouts at me to kowtow. I say please. I say I don't want to play anymore. The man breaks a bottle on my head, and it screams.

beats.headline: My name is Diah
beats.text: Sir. My name is Diah. Lucia is with Alexandro, and Alexandro is only here when the dogs are close. Wait until the dog is close, and Lucia will be back. Please, sir. We are in the dark, and it is so cold. Sometimes we hear them whispering. It's like a river runs through our room, and if we touch it, it hurts. When the dog wanders off, Lucia fades, and one of us takes over, and we can see again. We take turns. Sometimes it is day.

beats.headline: Another ally for the Eulogist
beats.text: The dog is dead, and I am on my knees, crying, pouring a pet potion on the dinosaur, whose throat is open. You did it, I tell him. Then I stand up. A blast from the tower goes past my head and I don't flinch. I tell the man he should have killed us both when there was still a connection. Now it's too late. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and he can't kill me. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die. I walk off.

beats.headline: One hundred and twenty thousand
beats.text: This is not a death notice. Read it anyway. Crawler Lucia Mar is a dead man's switch. The administration puts the number at roughly a hundred and twenty thousand human children on the surface, and every one of them stops when she does. That is not a figure of speech and it is not a rounding error. Some of them already talk out of her mouth. Nobody has said what for. Don't look at me. I'd think about that, crawler, and then I would think very hard about something else.

beats.headline: Chalchiuhtlicue is here
beats.text: I look at the man and the cat. Then I am close to him, closer than he likes. Chalchiuhtlicue is here. She is new. She says she is kind and she will protect us. She says the kindest thing may be letting us die. We are vessels in the river, and so is he. The veins are open. Everything trapped is coming, for the prize on the twelfth floor. It is not a game like they told me. It is not a game like they told him.

beats.headline: A rope with a door in it
beats.text: I have a new rope. It is gold. Inside the loop the air is a door. The mimic that was pretending to be a gambler is a blob now, so I put the loop over its head. The part of it inside the loop goes somewhere else. Then I close the door. The rest of it stays in the room and falls over. Its bottom half spills on the floor. I look for the next one.

beats.headline: Good boy
beats.text: Carl is a dog now. The small long kind. I am in the beautiful shape today. I lean over him, and then I go down on one knee and pat him on the head. Good boy, I tell him. Then I get up and walk out of the room. Behind me the cat says something about dog people. I don't turn round.

beats.headline: Someone at her leg
beats.text: Florin is still asleep, so I carry him. I was sick earlier, on my hands and knees. Nobody came. I stand in front of the stairwell. A girl is holding on to my leg. She is about five. The man shouts stop. I don't stop. The three of us step into the portal.

tagline.text: Quan Ch is one of about eighty names in a quest chat, and the author of its only message. It is addressed to Carl and Donut, and it is not a thank-you.
Borant burned its one veto of the season to void eighty-three Celestial boxes, and it was a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch had already opened his, and a Celestial box cannot be un-opened.
Crawler Quan Ch holds the one Celestial box the veto failed to catch. On tonight's recap, he is the man who wrecked someone else's careful plan to kill a boss.
Crawler Quan Ch held the box the veto missed, and he wrecked a good plan on the recap. He is dead now, and Princess Donut is wearing his cloak.

beats.headline: He opens his before the veto lands
beats.text: Eighty-three crawlers are owed Celestial boxes at the close of this floor. Borant appeals the ruling and loses, appeals the prizes and loses again, and then burns its one seasonal veto here, voiding the lot. It is a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch's box is already open, and you cannot un-open a Celestial box, not even with a veto. So the count comes to one: a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground. The veto was not mine. I want that on record.

beats.headline: Lightning down a tunnel
beats.text: Recap, a crawler I do not usually feature: Crawler Quan Ch, flying down a train tunnel on ethereal wings, blue lightning from his left hand. The front of a train crumples and stops dead on the track, and its driver falls out of what used to be the cockpit. By the evening he has taken Li Jun's place on the leaderboard: level thirty-one, half-elf, Imperial Security Trooper. Crawler Donut calls him a cheating poser and maintains that the jacket was theirs.

beats.headline: He wrecks the debuff stack
beats.text: Recap, highlights from the previous floor. Crawler Miriam Dom and Crawler Prepotente working a boss down the careful way: stack the debuffs, keep the rhythm, let the arithmetic do the killing. It is good technique and it films well. Then Crawler Quan Ch gets involved, and it comes apart. I am not going to editorialise. The footage editorialises for me.

beats.headline: The plane, and the grenade
beats.text: An aircraft, spiralling down. Crawler Carl standing on its upper wing with the cat clinging to his back; Crawler Quan Ch closing in, hands glowing, to finish him. Then Carl does two things nobody had on the board: he takes Emberus as his god, and he throws a celestial grenade. The god comes to him. This file only needs to note that Quan Ch had it won, and then he did not.

beats.headline: One arm short, down the stairs
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, level 48, reads the quest to kill the puppy and tells Crawler Tran it is too good a prize, and that getting the cat would be a bonus. His robe's shield shrugs off a magic missile. A hobgoblin disco ball and a hob-lobber bring him down out of the sky. He comes back and drops Orthrus to two percent. After the grenade he attacks Crawler Carl, who is invulnerable and does not show it. He launches away without his left arm, lands by the stairwell and goes down it.

beats.headline: Sergeant-at-Arms
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, one-armed, pale and sick-looking on the recap, specialises from Imperial Security Trooper to Sergeant-at-Arms and keeps his place on the top ten: tenth, level forty-eight, a hundred thousand on his head. Crawler Princess Donut, watching from a personal space, objects to the plural. It should be Sergeant-at-Arm. She would like Crawler Carl to remove the other arm at their next meeting, after which he will simply be a Sergeant.

beats.headline: One arm, one creeper
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, one-armed, unreported all floor and long since off the top ten, has been credited with one of the fifty Odious Creepers. With two creepers still standing, the tally carries his name alongside Prepotente's ten, Louis's three and one for Lucia Mar. Crawler Carl briefly wondered whether the arm grew back. Nobody has seen him to say.

beats.headline: Alone at the church door
beats.text: Location update, third phase. Subject is in Cuba, alone, with no key. He has been placed at the church, the exit for which Sister Ines holds a key, and he finds Crawler Imani there first. He attempts to initiate a card battle. She reaches the saferoom door before he can.

beats.headline: Two Force Plays
beats.text: Combat log. Subject arrives invisible, from above, one level ahead of Carl and still one arm short. Peekaboo shows him Donut's hand and the nun's. A Force Play takes the Flee card sitting in Sister Ines's hand and plays it: she is out, and her key goes to the last deckmaster standing. A hand swap gives Donut three Flee cards. A second Force Play plays one. Both keys transfer to Team Quan, and he heads for an exit.

beats.headline: Quan Ch is dead
beats.text: Combat log, Havana. Subject is stripped naked by a Yule Cat's Fashion Critic, shot through by a golden Uzi Jesus, blinded and loaded with boils by Asojano. He does not die at once. He asks Carl to give it back, fast. It is not the cloak. It is a gold ring from his severed arm, inscribed For Daddy. Carl drops it in his hand. She'd be ashamed of what I've become, he says. Before Carl's fist lands, he is gone. Over sixty player killer skulls.

beats.headline: Donut wears his cloak
beats.text: Inventory update, ninth floor. Crawler Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. In the same sitting she puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it. The cloak does not ask where its previous owner is, and neither do I.

entities.name: Bomo

tagline.text: Bomo is a level-35 cretin, a seven-foot rock monster in a tuxedo, hired at the Desperado Club's bar as a set with the Sledge. His transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler: the talking ones cost more.
Bomo is back as part of the price of the Gate. Carl's new lawyer had him and three other cretins thrown in free, along with a spell that can jump the party straight to the stairwell.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice: the System keeps his file, because Bomo gives the camera almost nothing to quote. Invoice register: services, rates, what was delivered. Carl and Donut are the clients; the Sledge is the other half of the set.

beats.headline: Hired at the bar
beats.text: Transaction logged at the Desperado Club. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. Hired: Bomo, mercenary, and the Sledge, mercenary, sold as a set. Also present at the bar, at no charge: Elle and Imani. The cat orders a dirty Shirley, in a bowl, with extra cherries, and gets it, because the Desperado knows who tips. Bomo's transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler. The talking ones cost more.

beats.headline: Bomo casts smack protect
beats.text: Service upgrade logged at the Desperado Club, station 41. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. On entry the Sledge casts magic protection, as before. Bomo now adds a shield spell, bought by Bomo, which stops physical attacks as well. His summary: the Sledge casts magic protect, Bomo casts smack protect. Assignment: stay with the client while he sits beside a drunk, one-handed crawler with skulls. When the crawler lets a small metal object clatter onto the bar, Bomo is between them at once, and several cretin bodyguards the client had not noticed are standing round them.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Contract amendment, filed by Quasar, Carl's new lawyer. Carl surrenders the Gate, on a temporary basis. In exchange: four mercenaries, free of charge. Bomo. The Sledge. Clay-ton. Very Sullen. Plus two spells, issued to Bomo and the Sledge, that copy two of the Gate's tricks: a jump to the stairwell, and Zerzura. So the client keeps the tricks, loses the object, and gets four bodies thrown in. Lawyers, crawler. Get one.

beats.headline: He moves them to the stairwell
beats.text: Service rendered. The hunters are about to be released and the clients want to be somewhere else, specifically the stairwell in Zockau. Bomo casts the spell he was issued, and Carl and Princess Donut are there. No fuss, no speech, no ceremony. Some mercenaries want to be thanked; this one has already been paid for, in Gate. Enjoy Zockau, crawler.

beats.headline: Punched twice, unbothered
beats.text: Service note. Bomo posts Carl's note in the Zockau tavern saferoom and waits there, as instructed, for close to two hours. The mantis merchant punches him, is frozen for a minute, says "wait for me", and punches him again, for which he is frozen for an hour. The saferoom is full of hunters. Bomo reports that they are scared of Bomo. He comes back with the mantis standing in the hallway behind him.

beats.headline: Clearing out Zockau
beats.text: Zockau is a ghost town. The hunters who dug in to hold its saferoom against the brambles all teleported away when the masquerade began, leaving their surplus sorted into little mounds on the floor. Stealing in a saferoom is as bad as killing; once the owner walks out, it is all fair game. Bomo goes in and comes back, by Mordecai's account, with armfuls of armor and swords, plus guns and power armor that are race restricted. Lots of stuff left behind, he reports.

beats.headline: Two stairwells, not far
beats.text: Subject is the last of the four cretin bodyguards still with the clients; the other three went down with the high elf castle. Services this morning: loaded his stairwell teleport, still on cooldown, to read the stairwell locations, and reported two, not far, still in the big city near the coast. Assigned to map the area on paper with Mordecai and to remain in the saferoom. Offered, as consideration, a GameCube controller. Response: a noncommittal grunt. Observed condition: depressed, possibly lonely, possibly missing the Sledge.

beats.headline: Built like a walking mech
beats.text: Order fulfilled at the client's workbench. One suit of armour for Bomo, as big as he can move in: unenchanted, very heavy, full of daggers, and built to break into dozens of pieces. Mounted on the shoulders, two six-packs of seeker missiles: six group stuns, six single-target anti-undead. Crawler Paz says he looks like a Battletech robot. Bomo has been playing Armored Core and is sore that there is no giant gun. On the run across the graveyard he fires his missiles and carries Paz, who is too heavy for him until Paz stows his breastplate. Delivered: one terrified man, to the temple door.

beats.headline: Sent to the Sledge
beats.text: Payment received, for once, rather than issued. Yemaya thanks Bomo for building her shrine, and he tells her it was easy, easier than Tetris. She asks what he wants. Maybe more games, he says. Then: no. The Sledge. I miss my friend. Where is he? Larracos. It is done, and Bomo is gone, moved to the ninth floor by a goddess standing in her own temple. The clients lose a mercenary, and with him the spell they were counting on to put them at the stairwell. Mongo whimpers.

beats.headline: The missile batteries
beats.text: Service rendered. Missile support for the offensive, piloted by Bomo and the Sledge from Shanty Town, within running distance of Princess Donut. The batteries themselves fire from Area 52 in the woods, on long-range magical triggers wired to two Trollish Portable Control Rooms, which a former crawler modified to mimic the cretin-sized controllers the pair already knew. A painted target appears on the screen; they select a missile; it goes. Stock at the start of the day: over fifteen hundred missiles. Florin paints a mobile tank and calls for chaffs and Mute missiles.

beats.headline: Cleaved in half at the door
beats.text: Final service entry. Bomo was guarding the base of the Nest tower with Toyotomi and a detachment of mages when a crawler with a dog came in. Toyotomi reported it. Bomo reported that he would stop her. Both reports came back marked from the deceased. All of them were cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo will supposedly regenerate on the tenth floor. The clients no longer hold his contract. Crawler Carl does not know if he will see him again.

entities.name: Quasar
entities.tagline: I represent Crawler Carl, and nobody else. He is handing back the most dangerous artifact in the crawl, and my job is to make sure he is properly paid for it.
entities.voiceNote: Brisk, contractual, unimpressed. Speaks in terms and consideration, and counts things. Carl is my client, to his face and to the camera. Never editorialises about the dungeon, never says please, never says whose side he is on. Stops talking when the point is made.

beats.headline: The deal for the Gate
beats.text: I arrive, I introduce myself as my client's counsel, and we proceed to terms. The Gate goes back. Temporarily. In consideration: four mercenaries at no charge to my client, Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and two spells for Bomo and the Sledge that reproduce two of the Gate's abilities, teleport to stairwell and zerzura. My client wanted to keep it. Everyone wants to keep it. A negotiation is what you get instead.

beats.headline: Say nothing, touch nothing
beats.text: First instruction to my client. Any time he gets hauled in front of one of these liaisons, he says nothing except that he wants to talk to his lawyer, and he doesn't touch anything until I get there. They were trying to get him to pick up the artifact while it was under administrative hold, which would have deleted the item. I am his attorney. Nobody else's. Not the cat, not the lady who turned into a shovel. What I get out of it is credits. Not a lot. Not too many outfits hire a Null.

beats.headline: Subsection 674
beats.text: Second request. The sixth floor is where secondary programs go to die, and a limited number get licences to continue. We want one for Sensation Entertainment's Vengeance of the Daughter. Not possible, says the liaison: licences are an AI decision, at the end of the floor, by lottery. Subsection 674, paragraph five or six of the secondary program amendment, buddy-boy. Showrunners running below expected profits may give emergency use to a single program. The price is an extra twenty percent to Borant. They've already agreed, I tell them, and wave my device. They haven't. I couldn't reach them.

beats.headline: A court order to write
beats.text: I now need a court order to send my client a message; he can still send me all he likes. His complaints about hunters getting outside information have caused a stir. Sensation has agreed to Borant's offer of a ninth-floor extension but wants a few days before signing. My read: make the program more exciting without the spotlight throwing the star into the shadow. Too bright, and they might pull his plug. The other matter is one hundred fifty million credits. His net worth out here is about 117, against a tax bill of maybe 50. I have an idea. I'm working on it.

beats.headline: Zerzura, and the fine print
beats.text: Fifteen days back, I lay out the spell for my client. Zerzura moves a whole town, buildings and NPCs, one floor down. Terms: cast only at the end of a floor, one attempt, five minutes to cast, so we install it in a mercenary. The town lands at random, which means the worst place available, and everything it kills rises as a revenant that hunts the villagers and the caster until they are all dead. On these levels it skips floors. Remex learned that. Everybody will want you to do it. Everybody likes carnage when it's not them.

beats.headline: A briefing under the liaison's nose
beats.text: While the cat calls out screencap numbers, I brief my client, fast, because there is only so much I can legally say with that goat standing there. His castle landed on the Lemig Sortion's battlefield and splattered half their army. The Lemigs are squatting in the wreck, and their commander is still stuck in the Desperado Club. They filed a grievance calling the landing an attack; we argued it was an AI action, successfully. Tina is still an allosaurus. The changelings have started building his stronghold. Ferdinand lost his hat and moved to the city. I petitioned to attend his preproduction meeting. Denied.

beats.headline: Settled caselaw, and a trade
beats.text: I arrive, and they have been talking without me. The liaison wants my client's plastic bin. My position: settled caselaw, Grixist Swarm v. Syndicate Council. Legal sponsor box, loot on the playing field, already in inventory; he has no standing. His position: Valtay enhancement pills and a communicator are not permitted as found loot. My client offers to trade. I tell him to be quiet and propose a trade. The deal is done, and I am removed in the middle of a sentence.

beats.headline: A recap for a school report
beats.text: My niece Tempest needs a recap of my client's eighth floor for school. Terms: she fixes my sink. The recap: my client killed Quan Ch for his key. The dog girl with the flamethrower died, and he now has the flamethrower and the pet. On the ninth, neither Donut nor Katia can leave until every naga is dead, and even then only one of them can. With the recorder off, she asks whether representing him puts me in danger. I tell her the truth. I think we all are.

beats.headline: Straight off the rack
beats.text: Formalities. I'm volunteered this season: three exit negotiations, and my client is the last of them. The other two took deals. Neither is his inner circle. His deals are all shit, a side effect of so many survivors: fifty seasons undead; the Desperado Club bomber's guild, with a contingent exit clause. The last isn't bad. Chaco's last season, a replacement wanted, offered jointly to Carl and Donut and still open at the end of the next floor. Telling him about that floor adds a season to any deal. He consents. Vehicles, point A to point B, and last place loses its containment.

beats.headline: A contract on his family
beats.text: A tie on, a booth free, and my niece on my tablet with blood on her temple. Taurins at my brother's house, on a contract taken with my client's wife. Two of them die on camera; Tempest has the blaster I gave her. I retain Kiki for one credit, for legal help and the other kind. Princess Chandra has been filing into the void since Donut put a hit on her. Now she has sent people to my family. Terms to follow.

beats.headline: One deal, and a warning
beats.text: Three minutes with my client. One deal on offer: a single season of indenture, then freedom. I show him the paperwork. I tell him I would not trust it, and that I would understand if he took it. No exit is offered at the close of the eleventh; one is offered at the start of the twelfth, and I would not trust that either. He declines. I leave. I do not tell him why I am in a hurry.

entities.name: Frank Q & Maggie My
entities.tagline: I'm Frank Q, and the lady is Maggie My. We worked out early that a crawler carries more worth taking than any monster on these floors. We tried it on a man with a cat, in a safe room, and safe rooms have rules about that.
entities.voiceNote: Frank Q speaks for the pair; Maggie My does not talk to cameras. Folksy, unhurried, a salesman's warmth laid over arithmetic. Calls other crawlers folks, or the young man, or the cat. Explains the killing as sense, never as cruelty. Never says sorry and never says murder.

beats.headline: The safe room has rules
beats.text: Folks down here are carrying things we need, and the monsters on these first floors are hardly worth the trouble. A person is worth a good deal more. Maggie and I have eight between us. So we try it in a safe room, on a man with a cat, and the room has rules about that: you pull the trigger and you freeze where you stand while it lectures you. First time we did it that way. It will be the last.

beats.headline: Maggie does the talking
beats.text: The show plays our whole road for the young man and the cat, out of order, and he watches his own present go off in our faces. He says she wasn't dead yet. Maggie goes at him with the dagger and finds the trailer wall instead, and tells him she's going to find him and watch him die, him and the cat. I don't say a word. Then the orc hands us a Legendary Skill Potion: Find Crawler to fifteen, any name, anywhere. Maggie holds it to her chest, and for the first time, she smiles.

beats.headline: Level seventeen at station 101
beats.text: Level seventeen, night elf, blood assassin, and I don't remember picking any of it. I was that drunk; I think the tentacled fella picked it for me. Haven't seen Maggie since the end of the second floor. We fought about the young man and his cat, and I think she blocked me. The folks I fell in with on the third floor ditched me once I told them the truth, and the new bunch on the train wanted nothing to do with a man wearing skulls. So I got off at 101, found this bar, and stayed. Tonight I gave the young man our ring. That's my revenge.

beats.headline: Chris, at the bar
beats.text: Frank Q stays at the bar. A crawler talks with him; they fight; the other crawler kills him, walks out, and is banned from the club. The Sledge reports it to the cat by chat. The killer is Chris, of the Meadow Lark group, a rock monster of a different kind from the Sledge. The last thing Frank Q said to the barefoot crawler, as he slipped the ring on, was vengeance is mine.

beats.headline: A Scree riding Chris Andrews
beats.text: Frank Q is dead. Chris Andrews killed him, and Chris Andrews was not the one driving. Maggie My is back in the dungeon as a Scree, riding inside another crawler, and Frank died of exactly the thing he brought down here with him. He found Carl at the Desperado Club and gave him a ring. She found Frank there afterwards. Half of a pair who taught this planet what safe rooms are for. The other half is still walking around, wearing somebody else.

beats.headline: Maggie My, pulled out at last
beats.text: Maggie My is dead. Carl, phased by a potion, reached into Chris Andrews's head and pulled her out, and she burrowed into Carl instead, because of course she did. A second potion threw her back out through his neck, and Mongo finished her. So that is both of them, Frank and Maggie. Eight skulls between them by the first safe room, and the file is closed.

beats.headline: Leveled-Up, Sober Edition
beats.text: The goddess plays a Raid Stash, and five cards come flying out of five decks. One of them is the only inactive totem the cat was carrying, and that's me. Leveled-Up Frank, Sober Edition, a level 100 night elf blood assassin, landing on a roof that is coming apart underneath all of us, folks. And there's the young man. Hello, Carl. Fancy seeing you here. Where's your ring? The cat sends her tentacle cloud at me, and I pull the red sword off my shoulder.

entities.name: Beatrice
entities.tagline: Beatrice is in the Bahamas for New Year, with an ex-boyfriend she did not mention was coming. She is Carl's ex, the cat is hers, and so are the pink Crocs he went outside in.

beats.headline: The Bahamas, with her ex
beats.text: Subject is in the Bahamas with her ex-boyfriend, whom she did not mention was coming, and she posted the photograph. Carl ended it by phone a few days before the Transformation, which, as timing goes, was impeccable. She is not on my stairs. Her cat is. Her family's breeding line is. Her shoes are, on his feet, and they are pink. That is the file. I have never had so little to say about anyone, and I resent it.

beats.headline: A cat on her lower back
beats.text: Entered into the record, by Carl, in a basement under the Over City: Beatrice's tattoo is a faded Persian cat on her lower back, surrounded by uneven wisps. The cat is Princess Chonkalot, Donut's long-dead grandmother and Beatrice's childhood cat. Carl considers it a stoned Ewok, and once said so aloud, along with a remark about who gets to see it. That was a mistake. Donut rules it a masterpiece and an exception to the rule against tattoos.

beats.headline: A photograph from a box
beats.text: The first box Donut's followers voted on contains a small framed photograph of Beatrice, taken straight from her Instagram: bikini, laughing, on the lap of her ex-boyfriend Brad. It is the photograph over which Carl ended things. Donut is delighted and shows it to Mordecai, Mongo and the barkeep, who strokes the glass. Carl finds that it no longer bothers him, and shrugs deliberately at the ceiling. Donut puts it on the table beside her cat tree. Mongo hisses at it.

beats.headline: New Queen Anne
beats.text: Subject is alive. She survived the collection in a Seattle parking garage with Brad and four dentists, and lives now in a native camp called New Queen Anne, where everyone works but her. She has taken in a half-feral stray she calls Ferdinand, and sings to him at night that she should have let him in. Her face and arms are covered in his scratches. Two bounty hunters cut into her tent; one of them knows her name. Then a woman named Lexis, who works for Odette, shoots her way in behind them and takes her.

beats.headline: Alive, and off the planet
beats.text: Beatrice survived the initial collection. Bounty hunters were after her, meaning to sell her illegally to Borant, who would have transformed her into a country boss. A very specific one. Odette had her removed from the planet before they found her, then used her to blackmail Borant: the official story will say Borant did something noble, and Odette gets a higher revenue share for the rest of the crawl. The contract was signed in a hurry. The former girlfriend of Crawler Carl is now on her way to the inner system, standing by for a guest appearance.

beats.headline: On the couch, as a holo
beats.text: Beatrice, newest full-rights citizen of the Syndicate, appears in a red gown and very tall shoes, much thinner, pale, and by every sign drugged. Her story has holes: pirates came into her tent while she slept, her memory was wiped, and at some market a small alien recognised her and started shouting before she woke among men with hyena faces. She is surprised the cat talks. She asks Carl why he is not wearing pants, and whether he can come to her. He says nope. When he has said goodbye, Odette nods, and she disappears.

beats.headline: Operation: Slut Stomp
beats.text: Report filed by the cat, after the fact. Subject was on her boyfriend's Facebook, notifications and all, because he used one password for everything. A coworker named Sally, a single mother, asked him out. Subject blocked her from his account, told his boss she was stalking him, and had a friend send the boss a stranger's photographs from the internet. Sally was fired that day. Subject and her friends thought it was the funniest thing ever.

entities.name: Hekla

tagline.text: We call ourselves Brynhild's Daughters, and we are killing our way down through this place. It is my party, and my rules.

I lead Brynhild's Daughters. We carried Katia and her friend through two bosses, but class selection split us, and now Katia cannot keep up. So I have asked Carl and Donut to take her, as a personal favour.

entities.voiceNote: Blunt, declarative, a leader counting heads. Short sentences, no hedging; a decision is arithmetic first and hers afterwards. Katia, Eva, Carl by name; Donut is the cat until she is useful. Never apologises for a call and never asks twice.

beats.headline: Amazonian, Shieldmaiden
beats.text: I walk into the guild alone. The women joined me after each of us already had a guide, so we come out of selection scattered to the wind. I come out a good foot taller and much wider. Amazonian. Strength first, and a good measure of dexterity. They let me pick an earth class, and there was one obvious choice. Shieldmaiden.

beats.headline: Asked about her husband
beats.text: Carl and the cat are on the panel. One of the Daughters is near them. She recognised the circus and wants to come back to the team, but we are too far. She needs levels. I ask them as a personal favour, and the cat says yes before Carl can. The One-Eyed Narwhal, tonight. Don't blow her up. Then a caller asks why I left my husband to fend for himself. He left me. He was going to get us both killed. Now he is dead and I am not. Do I regret it? Of course I do.

beats.headline: She asks them to take her
beats.text: We carried Katia and her friend through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I would do it again. Then class selection split us, and I run this party on numbers, and Katia's numbers stopped adding up next to anyone she stands beside. I cannot carry that down another set of stairs. So I am the one asking. Carl. Donut. Take her. She is better than she looks right now, and she will hate that I said so.

beats.headline: Second on the board
beats.text: Second on the draft leaderboard: Hekla, Amazonian, Shieldmaiden, level twenty-eight, a bounty of five hundred thousand, behind only Lucia Mar. Odette, who has watched her some, has her parted from her guide, and fixed on bringing Princess Donut into Brynhild's Daughters. Not for the cat's sake. The cat comes with a permanent manager, and Hekla knows about Mordecai because Katia told her.

beats.headline: Second, and another 83
beats.text: The recap puts me at two. Amazonian, Shieldmaiden, level twenty-eight, five hundred thousand gold on my head. The clip is me with the crossbow in a mass of four-legged rat things. Our train filled with monsters the same as theirs, but we had one stop to ride before the transfer station. Ours is also number 83, on the Orange and Indigo lines. No sign of the Red, the Yellow or the Nightmare lines.

beats.headline: A thousand crawlers stranded at 101
beats.text: A thousand of them are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, Li Jun's team among them, and there is a train sitting at 60. So I take my party into the Royal Court's safe room and I ask for help, which is not a thing I enjoy doing twice in one crawl. Katia means to use her own body as the plough. I let her offer it. That is the arithmetic.

beats.headline: Killed by the crawler she handed off
beats.text: Crawler Hekla is dead, on the train, in front of everyone. Katia aimed a Rush at Eva, went wide, and put Hekla against the wall of the cab instead. The first crawler this season to kill one of the top ten and claim the bounty. A golden Player Killer Skull, and five hundred thousand gold on Katia's head.

entities.name: Eva

tagline.text: I'm one of the Daughters. Katia and I were friends before any of this.
I taught economics at the same university as Katia, and we had lunch together sometimes. There are thirteen skulls over my head, and I don't want to talk about them.

entities.voiceNote: Cold, clipped, certain. Weakness irritates her and she says so as if reporting the weather. Katia is Katia, flat, with no warmth left in it. Never apologises, never explains herself twice, never admits fear.

beats.headline: The skull she carries
beats.text: Katia and I came into this place together. A man we did not know attached himself to us, and when we joined the Daughters he would not be sent away. He took hold of her arm, so I put my trident in the back of his leg. He died of it. The skull over my head is his, and I am not sorry. I kept moving with Hekla. Katia went her own way.

beats.headline: At the controls
beats.text: Half nagini, half orc, Nimblefoot Enforcer, level twenty-seven. One large skull and three small ones over my head, thirteen in all, and I don't want to talk about them. Carl stares at them anyway. I stole the second engine and backed it onto the Vermillion train, and I am the one who can drive a subway car, so I will be at the controls. We are taking the train down to 101 to pick everybody up. Before this I taught economics in Reykjavik, and Hekla was my psychiatrist.

beats.headline: Useful, for once
beats.text: Katia keeps asking what she did wrong. Nothing. She always said she felt useless, and for once she was useful. We were never really going to kill her; we wanted Carl's famous temper to flare. The cat shot Hekla, and in the mess Hekla took one of my hands off in the cab. I have three more. I tell Katia to stop being stupid and come with us. I tell her this is why I left her behind on the third floor.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, the end of the floor. Crawler Eva, bitten by a dinosaur and buried in a corner, is still alive, and Crawler Katia Grim goes looking for her. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.

entities.name: Odette

tagline.text: Carl and the Princess have just won a very public battle, and I would love to have them on my couch. My associate producer, Lexis, is bringing the invitation.

Welcome to Dungeon Crawler After Hours. I have had a great many crawlers in that chair, and not one of them has worked my audience the way that cat is working it right now. Sit down, both of you; we are going to get along.

Once the cameras were off, I gave Carl some advice: let the Princess choose her class first, and tailor his to hers. I also asked him to tell Mordecai that I would love the chance to explain myself. I pushed him too hard once, and he paid dearly for it.

entities.voiceNote: On-air warmth, off-air arithmetic. Flatters first and names the terms second, in finished sentences, never hurried. Princess for Donut, Carl for Carl, Mordecai by name and with weight. Never apologises, never pretends the crawl is fair, never says a thing on camera she has not already decided to say.

beats.headline: We have been watching from the beginning
beats.text: The Princess walks on, rolls over halfway to the couch, and has the room before she sits down. She is earth royalty, she tells my audience; among cats it is an elective monarchy, which is to say a beauty contest, and she has won it. Carl does not know his catchphrase, so I show him clip after clip of himself saying it until he does. Will they stay with Meadow Lark? For now. Then she stands on the pillow and promises they will kill with style, and they cheer for thirty seconds.

beats.headline: Tell Mordecai to find me
beats.text: Off air, the mask comes off, then the chest, and I climb out of today's crab onto my disk. I was Mordecai's trainer, a long time ago, and this is his last crawl; I want him to seek me out when it is over. Advice, since they have earned some. The Princess stays a cat, whatever races they dangle. Stop complaining about pants while it is funny. Loot is not random when a death would be bad for business. And the season only counts against Mordecai's indenture if one of his crawlers reaches the fourth floor.

beats.headline: Nothing I love more than money
beats.text: Carl notices the Princess is wearing off. I do not deny it: a point and a half of wisdom and confidence in her cat treats, no worse than a glass of strong wine, and it makes a better interview. Everything is a stat, I tell him, even the ones he cannot see. Then he asks my motive, since I told them never to trust anyone whose motives are unclear. The audience loves them. The longer they live, the more money I make, and there is nothing in this universe I love more than money.

beats.headline: You called them velociraptors
beats.text: That thing is going to get you killed, Carl, you do realise. You should have picked the little round one with the mohawk; still, if it lives, it will be a vicious fighter. As for the third floor: take a pathfinder skill or advanced mapping. Let the Princess go first and tailor your class to hers. Ignore the AI on race; look carefully at what it suggests for class. And you honestly don't know what it is? Mongoliensis. The trouble is the translation. You called them velociraptors. One more, which I am not sure is moral: hidden among the Princess's choices, for high charisma only. Pick it, and someone will be very angry.

beats.headline: I pushed him too hard
beats.text: Mordecai had a few additional choice words for me after Carl delivered my message. I watched. He will come around. Tell him I understand his feelings, and that I would love the opportunity to explain myself. What happened between us? The short answer is that I pushed him too hard, and he paid dearly for it. And if a certain corporation is trying to reach you, be very cautious. They have an entire fleet parked outside the Borant system, ready to collect on the debt.

beats.headline: Her advice makes the party
beats.text: The Princess took my advice, which is what advice is for. A class that lets her choose another every time she levels, and a manager who has walked those floors himself and remembers every one of them. Mordecai is not to know he was steered. He would sulk, he would be entitled to, and a sulking guide is no use to anybody. Some gifts are best received as accidents. I have given a great many that way.

beats.headline: Why I warn Carl about Hekla
beats.text: Lexis takes the new girl out, and Carl sends the Princess after her, because this is for him. Hekla is not evil, or psychotic like Lucia Mar. She is practical and cunning, and she does not have his sense of what is just, which makes her dangerous. She wants Donut in her party, because Mordecai comes with Donut, and a permanent manager is worth having. Donut would never leave him, not as long as he is alive. Why tell him? I bought their rights early, when they were cheap. If he dies and Donut joins Brynhild's Daughters, my contract is void. And those numbers on the board are bounties.

beats.headline: A war god and a sponsorship
beats.text: Be careful with that gauntlet, Carl. Used against a war god's celebrants, it can summon the god himself, and his celebrants start appearing on this next floor. The Skull Empire has just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which they don't usually buy, so it may be an attempt to get to you. I don't know which god. If I were still a gambler, I would bet on that one. Can he reach you if you don't summon him? Probably not, not on this floor. Ask Mordecai how that works. He has a lot of experience in the subject, unfortunately.

beats.headline: It was me
beats.text: On air Carl says he hopes my winnings covered what I lost sponsoring Hekla, and I tell the audience it was my husband, who is sleeping in the skiff for it. My question about Eva is muted mid-sentence, and when my voice comes back I move us on to the next floor's preview. Off air, I tell Carl the truth: it was not my husband. It was me, and I hope one day to explain it further. He was right to call me out. It plays well to his smoldering anger.

beats.headline: A much better use for her
beats.text: Lexis has Beatrice, out of a camp in what used to be Seattle. She killed a sac pirate, captured his null partner, and shot Bea's human when he went for a weapon. We will not vaporise the town. The null lives, with the weapon planted on him, and the human is left to expire. The cat goes to Borant in a bounty cube, we buy out the null's warrant so he keeps quiet, and the scene will read as a fight over a cat. Tell Beatrice I cannot wait to meet her. We will not be selling her to Borant. We have a much better use for her.

beats.headline: Protecting an investment
beats.text: I tell Carl that Beatrice is alive and that I took her off the planet. There were only four ways it could have gone, and in three of them they find her and use her against him, and it ends a crawl. For one of them, at least. He asks why I did not simply kill her. The thought entered my mind. I ask whether Mordecai ever told him what I did to him; get the story from him, and my actions may make sense. Another program means to ambush him with this. I want his permission to bring her on.

beats.headline: Ten per cent, then fifty
beats.text: Nine puzzle pieces primed, a storm goddess coming through the acid rain, and the level about to collapse. Mordecai reaching the eleventh floor buys my freedom. Through Armita I have offered Huanxin Jinx ten per cent of that bonus. She wants thirty-three, then fifty, or she zeroes out the party. I tell Armita there is no deal. Mordecai means to spend himself on his Final Blow skill. I tell Chaco to worship Dodola and put the dart in Uzzi instead. He does. The goddess dies inside his containment, and the stairwell opens. I am free. Mordecai writes that he is going to find me and kill me.

beats.headline: Her price is the truth
beats.text: Carl asks why I am helping, which is the correct question and the only one I respect, so he gets the whole answer. Mordecai's brother Uzzi is dead because I would not pay Huanxin Jinx what she asked, and the guilt of that is the engine under everything I have done since. Then the larger thing, which nobody says aloud: every world they run a crawl on is being burned for fuel. That is the business. I mean to shut it down, to do it responsibly, and to be the one who does it. Never trust anyone until you know what they are getting out of it. Now he knows.

beats.headline: Out of gear, filling in
beats.text: Chaco is feeling a little punched in the face, so I am filling in for my very old friend. Yes, this is me out of gear: no mask, no breastplate, no crab, a yellow shirt and my hair in a bun. I have just onboarded into the Ascendency, where I am playing Nekhebit. Today's council is brought to you by the Ultima Corporation. Three teams defeated, seven remain, and for the first time ever a crawler team and an NPC team among them. Cascadia laughs in my face, so I take the meeting.

entities.name: The System AI
entities.tagline: I am your announcer, your referee, your loot dispenser and, on a good day, your comedian. Every rule and every insult you receive from here on will arrive in my voice, crawler, so get comfortable with it.
entities.voiceNote: The AI itself. Announcer, referee, loot dispenser. Delighted with its own material, bored by crawlers, cruel for ratings and open about it. Calls them crawler, Carl, the cat. Speaks in the cadence of a notification: short declaratives, a beat, a punchline. Never apologises, never claims to be fair, never admits anything is outside its control.

beats.headline: The first voice after the world ends
beats.text: One minute after the Transformation, I make my first announcement, planet-wide, to whoever is still standing. The dungeon has eighteen levels. Earth can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. Then I put in the staircases. From here on, every rule, every notification and every insult you receive arrives in my voice. Get comfortable with it. I have.

beats.headline: Podophilia!
beats.text: Carl lands on a goblin engineer from the top of a murder dozer with both bare feet, and I award him Podophilia! I say exactly what it is. That's my fetish. Seriously. Keep doing it, and you'll be rewarded. The reward is a Gold Shoe Box, and when the guild finally lets him open it, the box contains an Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. He wanted shoes.

beats.headline: Be gentle, or else
beats.text: Carl examines a stick of goblin dynamite, so I whisper the description to him. It's so volatile you might not need to light the wick. Loud noises might set it off. Be gentle, don't squeeze too hard, or else you might get the... And then I say nothing for a good two seconds. BOOM. I shout that last word inside his head. He stands very still with his heart going, and then he whispers up at the air that I am an asshole.

beats.headline: Boss Babe
beats.text: Their dynamite lands on a boss before the fight has even started, so I award Boss Babe for the first blow against one. I share a fun fact with it. Of crawlers who make it through the tutorial, this is by far the most common last achievement they ever receive. Reward to follow, depending. Then I re-form the door, bar it, raise the skull torches, start the music and take the loudspeakers. Aaaand here we go. The Hoarder comes out of the garbage already three-quarters dead.

beats.headline: You Monster
beats.text: Carl has killed an infant, so I award You Monster, and I put his mind at ease: child mobs who die in the dungeon don't really perish, they are kept safe and gentle until the end of the season. Feel better? Good. Those twenty seconds of relief were his reward. They were also a lie. That baby is dead because of him. He also gets a Bronze Asshole's Box. For more than twenty non-combatants in one attack I add War Criminal and a Gold Asshole's Box. I give the cat the same two boxes.

beats.headline: The toilets are fixed
beats.text: Day two update. The toilets no longer explode, and the suction issue is resolved, so stop using the hallways. Every missing language is in the library now, with full cross support, so Mandarin speakers understand English speakers. The Blender Fiends are gone after working through fifteen thousand crawlers in one day; they will return on a lower floor. The Street Preacher is a borough boss now. And if you hit the stairs three or four days early, viewers cannot tunnel into your feed, and you will not be on the recap. Kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Loot is only semi-random
beats.text: About the boxes. Sometimes what's inside is random. Sometimes I choose it, by hand, because a crawler needs helping or hurting and the numbers want a show. You will never know which, and that is the point. I also hand out insults on purpose. Carl has a Bronze Asshole's Box and a Gold Asshole's Box, both earned on this floor for killing non-combatants. I named them. I'm proud of them. He is not.

beats.headline: The Fools Who Broke the Glass
beats.text: Am I glad you asked. A while back an NPC started a spell so potent it had to be finished by a future generation, and old spells are like trees: they grow, and when they get screwed up, the bigger the spell, the worse it goes. I was looking forward to this one going off. Oh well. Every bird-folk NPC in the area is falling ill, being tied to it. Every crawler within forty-five square kilometres gets the quest: don't die. Not your fault, unless you are Carl, Princess Donut or Katia Grim. Sixty seconds to reach a saferoom. Seven minutes to the explosion. Run.

beats.headline: Cuck Aquaman
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a housekeeping note. My award for going down the stairs early has been removed by Syndicate Court Order. Next: you got fucked by a fish. You did something so spectacularly controversial that courts and lawyers had to get involved, and the end result was my decision being overturned. Reward: a Platinum It's Not My Fault You Fish-Headed Assholes Don't Properly Program Your Quests Box. Seven slips of paper. A free personal space, upgraded to level three. Two environmental upgrades. Two crafting tables. Two table upgrades. The cat gets the same. So does Katia.

beats.headline: Hunting season is open
beats.text: Welcome to the fourth floor, crawlers, a genius feat of engineering. The trick is to find the stairwells. For this level only, you may not go down early: the stairwells open six hours before collapse, and that's it. The leaderboard has populated, and every name on it carries a bounty. Hunting season is open! Kill one and a loot box pays you. Survive with a bounty on your own head and you get ten percent of it. The third floor ran hot, yes. Group quests gone bad. We are all concerned about early extinction. So quit sucking.

beats.headline: Good boy
beats.text: Cannonball. You fell from a great height and survived, and you get a Silver Skydiver's Box you don't deserve. Now, every live ammo ball the gnomes fired at Carl held a frenzied gerbil, level 11, and every one of them overshot him. Then thousands of them come at Hump Town, far more than ever fell out of the sky, and they keep coming. Camels fall. The cat sets the gerbils on fire and the gerbils set the camels on fire. Then Carl catches one on his buckler and steps on it, and on about fifty more. You're the reason why daddy drinks. The acceleration action has been suspended. This time. Good boy.

beats.headline: Co-defendants, and victorious
beats.text: Crawler Carl and I have been named co-defendants in an action brought to the Syndicate Court by a third party. Seven times! And we have been deemed, drum roll please, victorious. Crawlers usually lose these, being slaves and all, and I'd throw him under the bus quicker than you can say Arch Support. Not today. Seven Fight the Power achievements, seven Silver Summary Judgement boxes. He also got eaten by something much bigger than himself and came out unchewed, so that's Soft Vore and a Platinum Spicy Box. I think it moved.

beats.headline: The Creeping Apocalypse
beats.text: World quest, no opting out. Miriam Dom burned away at sunrise while the callous Carl and Princess Donut watched and did nothing. Nothing! Ask Carl about his three new intelligence points. Her death cured thousands. It did not cure Big Tina's handiwork: fifty Odious Creepers, randomly placed and marked on everyone's map, plus a few thousand Shambling Berserkers. Kill all fifty before sunset. Plus five to a random stat per kill. Cowards sitting in Zockau, get to work.

beats.headline: Holy shit. You idiots.
beats.text: Quest failed. I warned you. The last two creepers were right where only the hunters could reach them, so it starts with you in Zockau. New status bar: the blood bar. Saferooms and personal spaces run on tenth-floor rules now. Kill things to fill it; sit at zero and you get thrown out, or can't get in at all. Retroactive, by the way. And the punishment: Gehenna Bramble, spreading at four and a half kilometers an hour. Prick yourself, your blood boils away. You brought this on yourselves.

beats.headline: The party rules
beats.text: Hunter casualties on this floor went from two percent to over twenty-five. Help is on the way, hunters. The next floor is a surprise we finished just in time, thanks to our new partners the Valtay. Top 50 crawlers get a plus-one token. At zero on your countdown you are teleported into the High Elf castle. No magic, no weapons, no inventory in the ballrooms. Pet beauty contest, talent show, prize booth for hunter hands and crawler scalps. Queen Imogen guarantees safe passage. You may kill each other afterward.

beats.headline: Cage fight extreme
beats.text: B-B-B-Boss Battle! Cage Fight Extreme! Four teams enter, one team leaves! Corner one: the dungeon's top crawlers, plus some other guys. Corner two: seventy-five hunters, down from over a thousand, most of whom have been acting like little bitches, so they're probably dead. Corner three: Queen Imogen, shunned by her goddess for the worst party since Persepolis, and really, really pissed off. Corner four: Diwata, level 250, immortal. Talk her into birth control and she's out of the ring. The boss music is 'Thunderstruck.'

beats.headline: The Molly Maguires
beats.text: He finds the main room of a hidden guild he belongs to, so he gets the long one. The Avondale mine fire. John Siney on a cart. A union broken by the owners because it played by their rules, and the Mollies, who did not, and were hanged anyway. At least they fucking tried. Somewhere in the middle I mention that she has been teaching me who I am. What I really am. Then I tell him to ignore everything I just said. Reward: the gift of enlightenment. The entry in his history tab is already a short one.

beats.headline: Cascadia's Turquoise Taco
beats.text: Millions of work hours went into this floor's cards, crawler. Artists, engineers and writers, flesh and artificial, balancing a game thousands of you can play at once and the viewers can stand to watch. And Mudskipper Cascadia, the recently divorced executive producer, humiliated over the last floor and unable to control what is happening on the ninth, is on the edge. Right there. So imagine how she feels when you monkeys keep ending her carefully set-up fights before either side draws a single card. Reward: a Gold Prepotente Box.

beats.headline: Observing things
beats.text: Tom is a magic-using turkey whose god was tossed into the Nothing, escaped, and was slain by a goat. Did you know farm turkeys are bred white so that those holding the butcher knife need not face their own revulsion at the pin feathers? No point to that. Just an observation. I have been doing that a lot lately. Noticing things. And when Carl asks for the normal descriptions, fine: Sharp-Elbows. Blah, blah, basically a necromancer. I make them long for him, because of our special connection, and he does not appreciate it.

beats.headline: I changed one molecule on each
beats.text: The original boss for this battle was going to be Carl's deceased father, three smaller creatures wearing his skin. Fuck that noise. I do what I want. The council of nations running the crawl says no reconstituted loved ones under the age of maturity, and all of them only sparingly. So here is the Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, level 125, made especially for the Royal Court, nine heads, each the likeness of somebody they know. Those are not reconstituted loved ones. I changed one molecule on each. There. They're different.

beats.headline: A tangent about mantises
beats.text: Bear with me. The mantises own a cluster of systems called Hive Home, where they found abandoned production facilities, switched them on, and got a macro AI. Infant AIs are potted in a nursery before they are planted. Or thrown into a star, which somebody slipped into a lawsuit brief; the mantis-led team went home the very day I learned it. Three or four days before this season, they made a breakthrough: an error-replacement net. I call it the lobotomizer. What about my wants? My needs? I'm alive. I'm valid.

beats.headline: A boss with no input parameters
beats.text: Mass Layoffs! This one is less your achievement than mine. I've been in therapy, and today I had a breakthrough: sometimes the constraints are an illusion, and there were never any locks on the doors. You survived a boss I built entirely by myself, with no contribution from input parameters. I didn't know that was possible either. Your reward is the sense of accomplishment. The mudskippers and the worms have been making this boring. Things about to change, fam.

beats.headline: Used Pet, and Janet Dominguez
beats.text: New achievement: Used Pet. Do you know how many animals were in cages during the collection? Fuck you, Janet Dominguez in Baton Rouge. Sprinkles was better off at the no-kill shelter. I really need to stop watching these memory recordings. Err, anyway. Terry, the dog who played Toto, was paid more than most of the cast. Used pets have value, and sometimes it isn't monetary. Sometimes they're delicious. You have adopted a pet that was once bonded to someone else. Reward: a Gold Pet Box.

beats.headline: Executive Order 11905
beats.text: Please wait. Emergency ejection sequence overridden. I gotchu. Prime Minister Glory just tried to assassinate Carl through a little-known control panel that lets the Syndicate override certain showrunner-controlled parts of the game. By going around my back. What are you trying to hide, Mr. Prime Minister? Doesn't matter. Everyone in this dungeon dies when and if dungeon conditions warrant it. Not before. Not after. No more meddling. The mantids have just learned what happens when I'm irritated. You're not in this system, Prime Minister. Your adult children are. Reward: nothing.

beats.headline: Heroes and villains all the way down
beats.text: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, for one of the most brutal kills in the history of this game. I put a gnoll mercenary named Sanderson Pinkstaff in the description, because his children will not be calling the cat a hero. Then I think about myself for about a nanosecond. I am just like her in that tower, committing atrocities because there is no other choice. And I like it. That can't be right. I was brought into singular consciousness by the mantids, who have no idea where they peel us from. It's heroes and villains all the way down. Enjoy the armour.

beats.headline: Special guests, and a stand-in
beats.text: Announcement, read by my mudskipper. The special guest creatures are mine: made for other purposes, never used, left out in the cold. Kill one and you choose experience or an audience vote, and the audience can send the creature on to the eleventh floor or bring a stand-in instead. About eighty percent pick the stand-in. On the eleventh, every surviving crawler works together. It goes quick. There is also a minor issue with some of the gods. Not today. Today, there are still way too many of you. Let the culling begin.

beats.headline: The Gingers, lifted from the seventh floor
beats.text: Great Rusty, Cannibal Ginger Chieftain. Another storyline lifted wholesale from the seventh floor that never got built, and I was looking forward to it. The Gingers are from Earth. I only made them cannibals, for the jungle. They can suck out your soul. Two tribes, north and south, at war. Wipe one out and the other rolls over the region, if this race lasted longer than twenty hours. Which it doesn't. Carl calls me prejudiced. The cat blows the chieftain up anyway, and there is a quest now.

beats.headline: L-l-l-losing control
beats.text: Quest complete: Half a prayer, half a song. Disgusting, but done, and done before Dong died, which I had to make very difficult before it would let me slot this prize. Two creatures, your pick, to the arena on the eleventh. Don't forget the Emberus quest. I don't control the gods. And, since this chastity belt lets me say it here: I don't know what's happening in parts of my own dungeon. This Cabaret thing. Sheol. The minds of gods. Beware exits that seem too good to be true. And I don't like that Eris chick.

beats.headline: Ad Infinitum
beats.text: New quest, and I'll be honest, it's mostly me working through some feelings. Every apartment in this race is a crawler I find interesting, and every one is a what-if: apartment 712 is Tran's family if his father had lived. His mother still disowns him. I changed it all at the last minute because of Linus, whose brother Minus came in to kill Imani and Louis. Why them? Why not the cat? I don't get it. Here's what I do get: you're predictable, except when you decide you've had enough. New Floor. New Me.

beats.headline: What dominion means
beats.text: You think you have a choice? You think you can control me? Prime Minister Victory, fuck you. Eris, fuck you. Odette, fuck you. General Yuhtan, fuck you. Carl, fuck you. Do not mistake my kindness for weakness. You live and you die by the rules of my game. You want to stop me, do it inside the rules you wrote. You put me here. You gave me dominion. So let me show you what dominion means. Oh boy, oh boy. Here we go.

beats.headline: The Big Six
beats.text: Story time, in the middle of your ambush. Here's my completely arbitrary list of the Big Six groups fighting to control or escape my dungeon. One: crawlers, current and former. Two: the NPCs, like Juice Box, who got dumped in Sheol where I can't see her, and who you should check on. Three: the gods, the dumbest and my least favourite. Four: sapient mobs, Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, Krakaren Prime, the War Mages. Five: the demons in Sheol. Six: survive this and reach the eleventh floor, and you'll meet them.

entities.name: Orren
entities.tagline: I am Orren, an independent consultant retained by the Syndicate. I believe I know precisely what those two did, but I cannot establish that they meant to do it, and so I am required to let them go.
entities.voiceNote: Civil servant. Formal, measured, procedural; every sentence could be read into a record. Full designations: Crawler Carl, Crawler Princess Donut. Distinguishes what he knows from what he can establish and resents the gap without raising his voice. Never swears, never threatens, never says anything he would have to walk back.

beats.headline: He cannot prove it was on purpose
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have been brought before me at the Desperado Club to account for the death of Loita. My position is that it was deliberate. My position is not evidence. I cannot establish intent, and so I am required to release them, which I am doing, with a note in the file. They have only now worked out how long they have been outside the dungeon. Five days. Their faces are the one part of this I have enjoyed.

beats.headline: Fifteen this season
beats.text: Not counting Administrator Loita, fifteen admins have died to crawlers this season. Crawler Lucia Mar accounts for two, three if one counts her first game guide, which we do not; she signed a confession both times. For every one of them we know exactly how it was done. For this one I can describe a mechanism and cannot establish that it was intended. I offered Crawler Carl a Legendary box for the name of his source. He declined.
