Until the next floor, no crawler will be teleported out by third parties, and Crawler Carl's next appearance on Odette's program is cancelled. My personal recommendation was not followed.

beats.headline: Borant would like the Gate back
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds. I have been sent to Crawler Carl with a request from Borant, which I am instructed to describe as a request. They would like the Gate of the Feral Gods surrendered, voluntarily, to be held until the ninth floor and not a floor longer. I put it to him exactly as written. He asked for a lawyer. I have passed that back exactly as spoken. I expect to be sent again.

beats.headline: A warning about liaisons
beats.text: I had Astrid bring Crawler Carl to me. I leave when this floor collapses and do not return until the ninth, so it is now. A liaison is chosen for two things: passion for the game, and fundamental disagreement with the goals of his own nation. Technically I should have lost this chair when the Valtay took control of Borant. I am not the only liaison who disagrees with his nation. Some of us meet that second requirement a little too much. I have said all I can about the matter.

beats.headline: The courts are frozen
beats.text: On to business. The courts have stopped nearly every crawl-related case, including ones the AI is usually indifferent to, until they have a better read on this AI's stability during the floor change. Crawler Carl's attorney now needs a court order to send him a message, and has not been permitted to try. We have decided to circumvent this, just this once, and I must remain in the room. I wave my hand, and Quasar is here, with a woman in a Goddamnit, Donut shirt.

beats.headline: The system has taken the controls
beats.text: On air, beside Showrunner Cascadia, I explain what I am for. A liaison is a fact finder, and also the negotiator when the system AI takes operations from the showrunners. Today it did. I describe Primal Engines and the Macro AIs installed in them, simply. I report a settlement: the AI returns most of the seized controls in exchange for concessions, and will follow the rules. The boss it built alone remains in place. One of its demands was that the crawlers be told.

beats.headline: He calls it a trap
beats.text: I pull Crawler Carl into my old office in the Desperado Club and tell him what I can establish. The Residual had nothing of substance. The Open Intellect Pacifist Network, former crawlers who want the crawl to fail, set this up: either we yank him and anger the AI, or the speech is so dangerous that the Council pulls the failsafe and kills this system's star. I had pre-negotiated the pull. The AI is removing its protections for the remaining Residuals.

beats.headline: Ten minutes outside the AI
beats.text: I have just hung up on the prime minister of the Syndicate. Crawler Carl told Crawler Princess Donut that Princess Formidable's actions will not work, and called it a hunch. We know about the illegal non-Valtay implant, when he got it, and his hidden conversation with the residual. We do not know what the implant does. So I twist my ball and open a zero zone: approximately ten minutes outside the AI's influence. Several creatures appear around us, shouting at me. I mute them. I believe I have just lost my job.

beats.headline: History will remember me
beats.text: I ask Crawler Carl whether he broke the AI from its containment, and whether he did it deliberately. He does not answer. Whether he did it on purpose is irrelevant now. History is going to remember me as the one who let this happen. When I left the Knot I said it was to make a difference. In truth, I wanted to be an actor, and to remain pure. I implore them both not to discuss this conversation outside the room.

beats.headline: The trap that broke the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Carl is among the Caprids, trading question for question, and one of the goats has just told him what Justice Light's trap did to the Nothing. The Prime Minister and I are on the line. We need him to ask a question about the integrity of the tunnelling system, and the reason we need it asked is not something I am cleared to say on an open channel. Crawler Carl has said it on an open channel. All of it. Live. I am going to be in meetings.

beats.headline: Locked out, and Hunted
beats.text: The Prime Minister would like a diagnosis pulled off the NPC Grigori, and Chaco brought in for a debrief. I remain locked out. The AI's stated reason is my own safety: I am being Hunted, it says, and only it is allowed to kill me. I will pass the request on. I note for the record that I cannot establish whether that is a threat or a protection.

entities.name: Justice Light

tagline.text: I left a note in the eighth edition. I killed a shopkeeper who insulted me, and the only trap shop on the whole floor went with him. Do not make the same mistake as me.
I got out of a crawl once. Now fifty thousand of us have come back in under a cat's banner, and every one of us knew exactly what we were signing.
The others have taken the stairs, and I have stayed behind on this side of the veil. My trap has been set for a long while, and I am about to spring it. I am not sorry.

entities.voiceNote: Veteran of a crawl, back inside by choice. Even, unhurried, short sentences; a man who has already made his decisions and sees no need to defend them. Carl and Donut by name, the other retired crawlers are 'us'. Never dramatic about his own risk, never asks what anything is worth.

beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut are in the Meadowlark saferoom, and Tipid is telling it to them: fifty thousand of us under their banner, and I am one of them. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: It is done
beats.text: The throne rooms lock in place, and every one of them shows on the map now. Carl asks in chat whether I had ours prepared before it locked. It is done. The rest of the project I am building with the sluggalos. They do not mind the idea of accidentally tripping a trap and being skewered. It is not finished yet.

beats.headline: Contingencies upon contingencies
beats.text: Carl worries that closing the saferoom cuts me off from his sapper's table and the bomber's studio. I already have everything I need. It's safer and faster to use his table, but there is nothing left I can't do on my own. He worries the worms learned our secrets. It doesn't matter. I pull a thread, and the folded papers around me come together into a spiral. I have contingencies heaped upon contingencies. Have faith in the process. Danger lives in what they can't see.

beats.headline: The slug that is not a slug
beats.text: I send the sluggalos up to the surface, all but one. Sick-Ass Worgo. Tell your real boss we need to talk. Juice Box. I noticed the change the moment the real Worgo went down the new tunnel and came back a few minutes after: body temperature, weight, no hormonal emissions. I chose the slugs because I assumed the changelings could not copy them. I was wrong. There are traps between us I placed myself. She counts six. There are eight. She changes, and the head becomes Juice Box's. Underneath us, a digger is moving. I ask her to call it off.

beats.headline: Dante, and the ice elves
beats.text: I tell her why. Long ago I killed a trap store's proprietor out of anger, and dozens of crawlers died for want of supplies. After the crawl, as an indentured merchant, my neighbour was a crocodilian named Dante. One season we were castle guards, and we were ordered to kill the ice elves inside, gentle creatures who loved puzzles and the snow. Dante refused twice, and a beam erased him. I refused once. I lost a wing. Then I did it, because I was afraid. I am still not free. But Dante taught me there is no such thing as the point of no return.

beats.headline: Get them under three thousand
beats.text: Tipid activates the base defences just in time. Two or three battalions of Dreamers have teleported in outside the FUPA and are running for the throne room, and Rosetta thinks it is all of them. That is too many. I ask her to chop them up a little first and get them down under three thousand. Then we let them in. I will welcome any and all guests into my lair. I would have preferred Reavers. I will take what I can get.

beats.headline: We need that gate back
beats.text: We need to move on the war mages now. They have the Gate. I do not understand why they are not allied with the other NPCs, and I do not understand why that Residual is their warlord. We do not know their plans. Rosetta is ready to let them win and be done with it. I am not done yet. Rosetta, you are the most stubborn person I have ever known. Trust me in this. We need that gate back, and we need to move before the defensive towers spin up.

beats.headline: I know the merchant
beats.text: I tell them again. Get the gate back and none of it will matter. Carl says he knows where it is. Tipid wants me to stay in the tunnels, and says they don't understand because I haven't told them what I need it for. I ask Carl again. He tells me: in the stomach of a merchant named Paca, in the Midnight Market. I know who that is. She is an ambassador for the dungeon's own version of the Apothecary. There have been seasons when my shop was inside that market. With the sluggalos, I will have it shortly.

beats.headline: He breaks the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Justice Light did not take the stairs with the rest of you. He hid, stayed on this side of the veil, and snapped a piece of twine. A Legendary Trap has been triggered: a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap, dropped into the permanent portal the Gate of the Feral Gods had become. All captured bijou have been freed. All captured evicted demons have been freed. The Nothing has been broken, and it is draining into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol and into Scolopendra's Lair. Scolopendra stirs. He did not survive it. He knew that going in, and did not appear to require my opinion on the matter.

beats.headline: Dead, and the Nothing with him
beats.text: Welcome to the tenth floor. Some housekeeping before the fun. Crawler Justice Light is dead. The Nothing is broken. Those are two sentences I have never had cause to put next to each other, and I would like it understood that I am saying them under protest. Five thousand five hundred and one of you remain. Proceed.

entities.name: Tipid

tagline.text: I left a note in the fourth edition of the cookbook. I killed my best friend today, and I wish I had never made it this far.

I got out once, and I came back in on purpose. I have told Carl the whole of it, from Doctor Hu to the Crawler Project to how fifty thousand of us came to stand under the Princess Posse's banner, because nobody tells the ones still inside.

entities.voiceNote: Measured, exact, a briefer. Short declaratives in order; repeats an instruction rather than raising his voice. Carl and Donut by name; the retired crawlers are 'us' or 'the ones who got out'. Never speculates, never dramatises, never talks about himself.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: The necklace is worse
beats.text: The orc on the yak is the king, not his son. Nobody tell Rosetta he is here yet. I will tell her. She has history with him. Carl asks how he levelled so fast. A Ring of Divine Suffering for the stats, and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It trades out one of your spells for one of a crawler's; kill them and it is one of their five highest. It fell out of use because combatants were farming crawlers to power it. Carl asks if the ring is any better. The necklace is worse. Much worse.

beats.headline: Who are you?
beats.text: A man is heading for the saferoom door, and I put my hand on his shoulder. Excuse me. Carl? Can you tell me something? Who are you, and where are we? The last thing I remember is my last day as a game guide. A woman named Rosetta says my brain was scrambled in my crawl, that I went into debt to the Viceroys to fix it, and that the blast ruined the repairs. I sit and look at my hands. I thought I was done. I thought I was going home. I lost my key.

beats.headline: He sings to find the guild
beats.text: Carl slides in next to me at the bar, and I bring up the war mages. Under normal circumstances any of this earns a beating from the AI and the showrunners. I watched Herot's season as a game guide; trust what that little lizard says, find a way to talk to them directly. War mages will use you and kill you. Shadow mimics are the real problem. Then I take the stage in the Lollipop and sing Love Shack, badly. A gauge appears over me. The guild is here. The needle never leaves the red.

beats.headline: Do not kill the shells
beats.text: An apartment. Human Shells inside it, and one of them wears the name of Louis's mother. Carl and Donut are about to do the obvious thing and I stop them. Do not kill the shells. We had them in my season; they will be filled with something else. The AI is explicit about what this is: every apartment on this course is a what-if, built around a crawler it finds interesting. You do not put a blade into a what-if. You walk through it, and you keep walking.

beats.headline: It works like an inventory
beats.text: Carl asks how Herot could pull someone out of the holding area. I spent a season on a site-prep crew. It works almost like an inventory: whoever is designing the floor selects the stored individual from a menu and places them. A simple procedure. Nobody looks at that catchall area once a season starts, because nobody ever goes into it. It was built as a backup for the Nothing, which was meant to catch problem entities and be forgotten about. The backup became redundant.

beats.headline: Out of the driver's seat
beats.text: Carl stamps on the roof. I tell him I am not leaving the wheel. He needs a more reliable driver for this. He tells me my story isn't done and to get to the RV. The sluggalos tell me to get out of their chair. I get out. I go to the RV. Behind me the deep fryer comes on. That is not in the plan.

entities.name: Sister Ines

tagline.text: My name is Sister Ines Quiteria, and Cat Girl is only what the dungeon made me. The cat hissed at me before she was close enough to read my name, so we did not begin as friends.
I hold Amayon, a prince of Sheol, on a leash, and he pulls against me. My demons are at the church, and I am still the only one who can save the crawlers inside it. They need only come to me.

entities.voiceNote: Quiet, plain, devout without preaching. Short declaratives; God comes up as a fact of the world, not a slogan. People by their names: Paz, Anton, the man, the cat. Does not joke about her race and does not let anyone else. Never pleads, never explains twice, never says she is sorry for what she has decided.

beats.headline: Hostile, and fairly so
beats.text: Paz, Anton and I come upon a man and a cat. The cat hisses at me before she is near enough to read my name, and calls me a Havana brown as if it were a diagnosis. So we are not friendly, and I do not apologise for it. It takes some time to clear up. Then we help each other catch our first squad members, monk seals on the beach, because that is what this floor demands, and God does not ask me to like the people I work beside.

beats.headline: Pueblo de los Olvidados
beats.text: The town is corrupted and the quest is mandatory: Pueblo de los Olvidados, the town of the forgotten. Paz is a Santero, and the dead here do not care for that; they wake angry. Ghommids, the whole way out. We run for a saferoom. The man saw something out there, level one hundred and thirty, and thinks it is the boss. It is probably still outside. It cannot hurt us in here. I tell him to open the door.

beats.headline: No more false gods
beats.text: The thing in the straw headdress stands in our saferoom, sick and slowly dying, and asks Paz to repair his shrine. Anton holds a flag, waiting for five per cent. I tell it what it is. A false god. Our souls cannot take this. I tell Anton no. Let Carl's team take him. Anton says it is all make-believe. It is too much. No more false gods. Not again. At about ten per cent the creature opens the door and walks back out into the horde, and it does not come to that.

beats.headline: She will not let Paz go
beats.text: I stand between the god and my men, and he freezes me for it. When I can move again Anton is dead and Paz is dying on the tiles. I tell him to get up, we will get him cured in the club. I tell Carl it is his fault. Paz says not to blame them: he has told them what I am, and what I did. That does not matter now. Get up. Paz says let me go. It is a sin to give up. He says goodbye. Everyone leaves me. I have a flag in my hand, and I put it into his neck, and Paz is a card. A green one.

beats.headline: Out into Havana
beats.text: The goddess Yemaya asks where the other man went. The green card is still in my hand. It goes into my inventory, and I tell her he is not here anymore. Then she calls me brave and gives me a card. When both gods are gone I kneel by Anton and take everything he carried. Then I leave. Carl calls for me to wait. I do not. I walk out through the town, to the cemetery gate, and back into Havana.

beats.headline: It has always been demons
beats.text: The snake is under me, the charm is broken, and a doll's head is fastened to my arm. I tell the man the truth. None of this is real. There are no aliens. It has always been demons, whispering. Hell is open and it is taking us all. I told them not to worship false gods, and they did not listen, before or here. He says they are not real demons either, and asks me to choose them as an ally and leave with them.

beats.headline: No allies
beats.text: The cat's squad chooses me as an ally. I choose no one. They take the ten-second penalty. I summon Paz and put a stout card on him. He begs me, no more. The snake takes him in its mouth, and I tell him to accept his suffering and use his self-destruct skill the moment this false god— Then a neon hand reaches into my cards and plays my Flee. I have lost my key.

beats.headline: She will not let them leave
beats.text: I message the man's party. They are heading for Imani's exit, in the church. I tell them the truth: I cannot let them go into that exit. I can save them, if they come to me. Imani will tell them the church is being overrun by demons, and that the demons are mine. That is also the truth. Both things are true. I did not make this floor. I am only deciding what to do on it.

beats.headline: Amayon fights her control
beats.text: I hold Amayon, prince of Sheol, in the body of a giant snake, and he pulls against me. He is trying to cast; he wants to go home. I do not let go. Around us every exit on this floor is failing at once, and the Demon Eviction is worldwide. This is what I have to set against that. A demon on a leash and my own two hands. God did not give me more.

beats.headline: Asleep in the hallway
beats.text: Sister Ines Quiteria comes down the thirty-second floor hallway at full tilt, glowing, screaming "Sinner!" Crawler Carl's Nighty-Night wand puts her out before she reaches him, and she slides to a stop at his feet with a two-minute timer over her head. Crawler Louis volunteers, since he already carries five player killer skulls and the others carry none. He apologises to her and puts a dagger into her chest. The Reaper of Havana is dead. A god's marked-for-death symbol appears over Crawler Louis.

entities.name: Amayon

tagline.text: I am Amayon, prince of Sheol, at your service. The Madre de Aguas has died and risen again, and while she was down I slipped into the realm, not entirely by choice. The area message announced me to everyone in range, and I do enjoy a proper introduction.
I am wearing a giant snake at the moment, and Sister Ines holds my reins, if you can believe it. I am casting my way home regardless.

entities.voiceNote: Courtly, amused, unhurried; the menace is in the manners. Full sentences, formal address, delighted by his own introduction. Speaks of Sheol as home, of bodies as garments, of crawlers as small and briefly interesting. Never begs, never hurries, never admits to being afraid of anything on this floor.

beats.headline: Announced in an area message
beats.text: The Madre de Aguas is dead. That is the first thing the area message says. The second is that she has risen as a zombie, and the third, in the very same breath, is my name: the major demon Amayon, demon prince of Sheol, come into this realm to possess her. I could not have written the announcement better myself. Everyone in range heard it. Good. A prince should not have to introduce himself.

beats.headline: Where the Sidewalk Ends
beats.text: The regional quest they are handed describes me with some accuracy. A level 250 demon lord, one of the four princes of Sheol, betrayed by a brother and holding on by a ledge, in the body of a once-worshipped sea serpent. To go home I must cast, and nobody rides the river for free: my portal will inhale every soul in Cuba, and that will be barely enough. Something is thwarting me. They may do nothing and be swept up in two hours, free me from this shell, or kill me. I am invulnerable on this floor.

beats.headline: Out of the snake, still hers
beats.text: The ceiling of their hallway collapses around my coils, and the automaton lands on me, and I am teleported out of the Madre de Aguas. In the open air I take my true form, four feet in the street, chest level with their new roof. The marker over my head still says Enslaved. The quest they are handed calls Ysalte my former girlfriend and the mother of my child, and says she has seized me as I once seized her. She means to take me to the Ascendency as her retainer. I am given six totems, and I will not begin to flee until every one of them is dead.

beats.headline: A question from Emberus
beats.text: The man stands in my palm and says he carries a question from Emberus, about his son. The doll supplies the name: Geyrun, murdered. I laugh. I know exactly what happened; I witnessed the deal being signed, and if Emberus helps me kill my three brothers, I will tell him. The man says he gave me the strength and the souls, and asks me to call off my demons in exchange for carrying my message. But he also helped slay Ysalte, the mother of my child, so we are even. Speaking to him delivered the message. I turn my hand over and let them fall toward the fire.

beats.headline: A timer on a global teleport
beats.text: Their quest, the Missing Piece, updates. Succeeded, it says. And beneath the word, a timer, one for each region, counting down to the moment my spell goes off there. A global teleport. When it lands, the walls of their stairwell chambers will be sucked away, and anyone crouched beneath them pulled upward into the stairwell. They wanted me casting. They have their wish. Home is the direction I am going in any case, and I have never minded company on the road.

entities.name: Britney

tagline.text: Vadim and I are the last two survivors of the water quadrant. There are horrors down near the bottom, and we are not going back in there.
I'm a Pit Fighter now. I was at Vadim's office for a consultation when everything came down, and the two of us have just fallen in with Carl's lot.
I made it off the Hunting Grounds, but my face didn't. It's burned, and when they healed it, it stayed that way.
The sixth floor took my face. Here at the portals, Osvaldo tried to run for it, and I stopped him and took the crystal. You could ask him how it went, but you can't.

entities.voiceNote: Flat, young, hard-edged; short sentences that stop early. Reports damage to herself the way she would report damage to gear. Vadim is Vadim; the others are Carl's lot until they aren't. Does not ask for sympathy and does not offer it. Never says what she feels. You get what she did.

beats.headline: Two new crawlers
beats.text: Vadim and I have fallen in with Carl's team. Introductions here are short. Everyone counts heads, adds two, moves on. The first real conversation I hear is Katia telling Carl that pregnant women could not enter the dungeon, and that nobody inside it can get pregnant. Said flat. Like weather. That is the kind of thing people know here, and say out loud. I am going to have to get used to that.

beats.headline: He went anyway
beats.text: I came in with the cat, off the flying house. I'm in the corner where the crafting room meets the back wall. Vadim is dead. I told him not to go. Everybody who goes down there dies; I said it at the table, in front of all of them. He said he'd go. He said it twice. He went.

beats.headline: Mongo's spot
beats.text: I'm in Mongo's spot on the floor. I push him away a few times. He puts his head in my lap anyway, and now I am petting him like a dog. I was a Pit Fighter. I'm a Pit Champion now. Carl doesn't know what's different and I don't tell him. I am not Firas's girlfriend. Then Donut says pet beauty contest and the dinosaur jumps up and starts hopping, and I shriek and get out from under him.

beats.headline: Zapped out on an empty bar
beats.text: Zapped away by the new rules. Blood bar empty. I'm outside now, not too far off. I haven't killed a thing this whole floor, and Katia hadn't noticed. Her group is coming for me on the way to the southeast corner.

beats.headline: Donut's guitarist
beats.text: I'm not top fifty. Firas talked me into this: Donut's plus-one, because I play guitar. It was this or Gideon's assault team. The jacket itches. The elf says security checks, twice, and those are just the ones he's telling us about. This isn't going to work. I've been taking the dinosaur repellant every day. Mongo still tackles me. Shield's ready. Then the queen fades in next to me, and I cast it.

beats.headline: The queen lowers her hand
beats.text: I'm in the carriage with Carl when the queen appears. A notification comes in: an achievement for total views, a fan box. Carl and I look at each other. The queen turns to me and lifts her hand as if to cast. Then she stops. When she's gone I tell Carl she reminds me of my mother.

beats.headline: The butterfly on the warning light
beats.text: My part is the light. I sidle up to the guard with the giant spear, say something, giggle. I drop something, and when he looks down I pull a tag on my jacket. One stuffed slate butterfly comes alive, flies straight to the warning light and wraps it in its wings until the glow fades. It turns back into a toy, falls, hits the tip of his spear and lands in my hand. He never looks up in time. Carl says good job. I'm not doing that again.

beats.headline: The guitar with a missing string
beats.text: Backstage, I play. It's the Popovs' guitar, found in a boss room a long time ago, and it's missing a string. A sad minor strum for Donut's song, and it sounds full anyway. When she's done I let the last chord hang and go into something fast and baroque for Tina. Carl tells me I need to get away from the backstage area and come out. I let the guitar fade.

beats.headline: The jacket takes the lightning
beats.text: I'm on the ground, screaming. Carl throws a disco ball at the queen and shouts at me: your jacket! The butterflies spread, and the queen's lightning comes out as one bolt instead of everywhere, pulled into the clump of them. They explode barely ten feet over our heads. Donut and Mongo and Carl and I go flying in different directions.

beats.headline: Badly burned
beats.text: Morning, if you can call it that. Donut is waking Carl up with the count from the night. Firas. The Popovs. I'm not on the list, so that's something. My face is. Nobody has offered me a mirror, and nobody offering is how I know how bad it is. Burned. Badly, I'm told. I can feel where the word comes from.

beats.headline: The burn stays
beats.text: Katia's squad, Iceland. The burn on my face still hasn't healed. Neither Louis nor I have opened our boxes. I sit and hold on to Louis, and I don't stop crying. We are both still broken up about Firas. Katia is worried. She has asked Imani to come over and talk to me.

beats.headline: Scarred, and level fifty-five
beats.text: Donut tells me it is not so bad. The whole left side of my face is burn scar from the end of the last floor, healed shiny and uneven. She says scars are beautiful and go with the barbarian look I am going for. I am not worried about it anymore. I have been talking to Tserendolgor, who once had a scar like this on her face. I am level 55 now. There is a new tattoo under my eye, an extinction sigil. I wiped out an entire race.

beats.headline: Liaison to the NPCs
beats.text: Somehow I'm the one who talks to the NPCs now. Carl can't reach their spies himself, so it goes him, then me, then Juice Box or Arief. The plan wanted one of their big diggers. Naga ground won't allow it, so it's two changeling spies instead. Carl asks if my guys are in place. They're ready. Waiting on you.

beats.headline: Don't worry about me, Carl
beats.text: Elle wants us to run. Louis won't, and I won't, and she kept pushing, so I walked out. Now I'm coming out of the Desperado Club with a drink and running straight into Carl and the cat. I tell them I have to get back to Louis. We're switching to the gecko because it can fly. Carl grabs my arm and asks if I'm okay. I put my hand on his chest and say it without saying it out loud. Don't worry about me. You just need to survive.

beats.headline: She kills Osvaldo at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo made a run for the portals to the eleventh floor across a roof Crawler Carl had just blown open. He did not reach them. Crawler Britney stopped him, permanently, and took Ysalte's memorial crystal off what remained. One crawler ran. One did not let him. The crystal changed hands. I am not required to have an opinion, but I have watched a great many exits, and that one was clean.

beats.headline: Through the portal behind Chris
beats.text: The croupier sets the wheel and the portal opens under the stand-here spot. One person, they said. A test. Chris steps up, turns, waves, and drops. I go straight in after him without a word. Nobody planned that and I didn't ask. The croupier shouts cheat, and Carl has the goat pay him another five thousand. Louis gets a notice that I've left the party. That's all there is to say about it.

beats.headline: A leech for Louis
beats.text: Louis comes out of the fold coughing steam through his gills. I tell him to let Forkith work, or he dies. The leech filters your blood so you live down here. Chris got changed by the first Scolopendra attack. Werewolf. A Crest knocks him out before he turns, and somebody says they don't know him from the feeds. I tell them who he is. I tell them not to hurt him.

tagline.text: Osvaldo is a level-60 Curupira ranger, and he has just taken the memorial crystal off Queen Imogen's body. I had no notes on him before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it.

Osvaldo has kept himself out of every army in Faction Wars by riding it out in the woods. Now the memorial crystal in his hands is throwing a rainbow into the sky, and everyone can see exactly where he is.

Osvaldo carries a quest from his god to learn why the memorial crystals are not working. He works alongside Crawler Carl without being his friend, and he will not take a deal from anyone, because his guide told him it is better to die.

beats.headline: He takes Imogen's crystal
beats.text: New name on the board. Osvaldo, crawler. In the wreck of the Masquerade he walks up to Queen Imogen and takes her memorial crystal off her. Prepotente is going after him for it. I have no notes on Osvaldo before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it. I have a note now.

beats.headline: Number eight
beats.text: New name on the top ten: Osvaldo, number eight, a level-60 Curupira ranger. Neither Crawler Carl nor his guide knows what a Curupira is. He looks human. After Imogen fell, he, a crawler named Burcu and Prepotente fought, while Carl lay unconscious. Burcu is number ten. Osvaldo's hawk, Gimli, was eaten by Bianca at the end of the Masquerade, and he holds the memorial crystal that Carl, and very likely Prepotente, have quests to take from him.

beats.headline: Riding it out in the woods
beats.text: On Boomer's list of crawlers not under the Posse banner: the goat, unaffiliated and hiding his position; Lucia Mar, the same; a crawler named Burcu whose whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness and has stopped answering; and a handful affiliated with the NPC team. The crawlers the orcs conscripted are all gone. And Osvaldo, the one Carl asked about, is riding it out in the woods with a large group of crawlers who call themselves Team Flamengo.

beats.headline: A giant rainbow in the Madness territory
beats.text: Sighting, Madness territory: a giant rainbow, visible from a very long way off. The rainbow is Apito's memorial crystal, and the hands holding it are Osvaldo's. He is in none of the Faction Wars armies. I did not think that was possible either. The rainbow has just told the Madness army exactly where Crawler Carl's group is standing, and they are calling in Prepotente's forces for backup. Thank you, Osvaldo.

beats.headline: Team Flamengo joins the heat
beats.text: The heat's newest team is a pair of crawlers on Bruna the Slaughter Gnu: Osvaldo, level seventy-two, a Curupira, with Filipe L at the reins and a dwarf mercenary behind. Both worship Tupa, which rules them out of the Pineapple Cabaret. Crawler Carl messages him a careful list of which teams to leave alone and why. His reply, in full: he is not talking to Carl, he will not attack unless it is them or him, and he does not care about the rest.

beats.headline: Two crystals, both wrong
beats.text: Asked privately, he answers. His god Tupa wanted a memorial crystal. He took Apito's off Queen Imogen at the moment she died, because otherwise his party would have been smitten, and Tupa said it was corrupted. A second, found in the forest during Faction Wars, was also wrong. He gave the first to Prepotente and was shouted at for not doing it sooner. The second is Ysalte's. Paz was his friend, he adds, and Anton, and Sister Ines. Everyone who meets Carl dies. Now it is their turn, he supposes.

beats.headline: A second crystal
beats.text: For the record, from Crawler Carl's account in the pet stables: Osvaldo carries a quest from his deity to find out why the memorial crystals are not working, and he holds a second one, also uncharged. The first he handed back to Prepotente, its proper owner, who was, per Princess Donut, mean to him about it. Prepotente's position is that a thief with a change of heart is still a thief. The record supports both parties. Osvaldo is not in the room to comment.

beats.headline: Better to die than take a deal
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has answered Crawler Carl's messages. They are working together, he says, but they are not friends. His game guide told him never to take a deal on the tenth floor, whatever happens, because it is better to die, and nothing he has seen since argues with it. He and Filipe will take their chances in the seventh heat. Crawler Donut points out that he will die there. Only if he comes in last place, he replies. That is his position, and it is on file.

beats.headline: Caught on the gate at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been eliminated. He was speeding for the portals on the roof of the apartment complex when Britney put a stop to it, and she now holds Ysalte's memorial crystal, which he had been carrying. Crawler Carl asked him, right up to the green light, not to force it. He forced it. He declined everything. It is a consistent record.

entities.name: Queen Imogen

tagline.text: The throne was my father's, and now it is mine. My half-sister has come home telling old stories about me, and I do not answer stories.

I am Imogen, Queen of the High Elves, and I am hosting a masquerade to which the best of you are invited. There is gossip that I am one of your repurposed humans. The gossips cannot even agree on which one.
My familiar is Ferdinand. He struck at the man's dinosaur, the cat threw herself in the way, and somehow she got up again. I am told this with some amazement. I do not share it.

entities.voiceNote: Regal, cold, complete sentences, never hurried. My elves, my familiar, my guests; crawlers are the man, the cat, your people. Never explains herself, never raises her voice, never denies anything outright: she dismisses. Does not use the crawl's slang or its numbers.

beats.headline: Lexis, speaking for Odette
beats.text: There is talk. A woman called Lexis, speaking for a woman called Odette, tells the man and the cat that the Queen of the High Elves will most likely prove to be one of your repurposed humans, and that with the one called Bea accounted for, nobody can say which. She also says I am a country boss, placed to zero out the best of you at the Butcher's Masquerade. I am Imogen. I am giving a party. The rest is gossip.

beats.headline: Her familiar is Ferdinand
beats.text: My familiar is Ferdinand. My elves are out among the creepers when they come upon the man's party, and Ferdinand takes exception to the dinosaur and strikes at it. The cat puts herself between them and takes the blast. She should not have got up from that. She does, on some cockroach's trick of hers, and she is quite well. I am told this with some amazement. I do not share it.

beats.headline: My half-sister, in a cart
beats.text: My guards go into the last wagon and find a robed woman wearing my half-sister's face. They do not touch her. I come instead. I fade into the man's wagon beside a girl who squeaks and throws up a shield, and I ask him whether he is really attempting to smuggle someone who looks like my half-sister into my castle. He says your majesty and struggles to swallow.

beats.headline: I want that boon
beats.text: The man knows nothing of why it is called the Butcher's Masquerade, so I tell him: Apito's first party, Yarilo's breach, the slaughter after. Only the most divine may cast the spell, and only once in their lives. The goddess writes the guest list, and if the evening ends without violence, the boon is mine. I want it. I may not harm my guests before the party. I do not need to. Whoever breaks the peace, the ground opens under them.

beats.headline: She takes a chair before the stage
beats.text: I appear in the ballroom with blood down my gown, and my familiar is not where he belongs; now that I am at the party he is locked in with the rest of my staff. My sister has her invitation. Let her enjoy it. I draw the man across the floor to me and hold him in the air. My castle is besieged: his changelings at my towers, his friends in the trees. I turn to leave, and stop. I sit before the stage. Proceed.

beats.headline: Red lightning
beats.text: My sister's tattoos swarm around me and cannot touch me. I answer with red lightning in every direction at once. Then I push out of the mess of them. You fools. I swipe my hand and the man's arm snaps, and I draw him to me through the air, breaking. My own familiar strikes my head. I strike him away.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands
beats.text: Queen Imogen's memorial crystal has changed hands. Someone named Osvaldo took it off her, and she was in no condition to argue the point. Prepotente would like it next and is going after him for it. A queen's treasure, and it goes to whoever is standing closest when she goes down. That is how this floor works. That is how every floor works.

entities.name: Akuma

tagline.text: I am Akuma, and I lead the War Mage Rebellion. We have taken the Gate of the Feral Gods, and I am not in the habit of explaining why. Nice shoes, Carl.
We hold the castle at Larracos, and in six more hours this floor is ours. The system has named Agatha my co-warlord. I did not choose her, and I will not pretend to be pleased.

entities.voiceNote: Cold, formal, exact; a commander dictating for the record. Never raises his voice, never explains his reasons, never apologises. 'The War Mage Rebellion' in full; Carl and Donut by name; Agatha by name and with contempt. Speaks of leaving as a decision already made, never as a retreat.

beats.headline: Nice shoes
beats.text: The fairy crawler goes into a tree, and I take the Gate of the Feral Gods from her. Carl comes into the clearing. My colonel's mark fades, and our dots turn to a colour no army on this floor has used. Three of mine see to Stalwart. Then I look at Carl, and at his bare feet. Nice shoes, I tell him, and we teleport away.

beats.headline: Sharing a command he did not ask for
beats.text: We hold the castle at Larracos. Six hours more and the floor is ours. That should be the whole of the announcement. Instead the system lists two warlords of the War Mage Rebellion, and only one of them is mine. Agatha. Co-warlord. I did not bring this rebellion this far to share its title, least of all with her, and I have not hidden what I think of that. I will hold the castle. I will not pretend to be pleased.

beats.headline: He leaves, and warns them on the way
beats.text: To the Warlord Chat, for the record. The War Mage Rebellion is leaving this floor. We came here for the Scavenger's Daughter. We have found the Scavenger's Daughter, and we leave with what we came for; the castle and the war are yours to finish. One thing more, and I address it to Carl and to Donut, since they are the ones who might still act on it. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. I do not explain. I am already gone.

beats.headline: A note in a gremlin's hand
beats.text: For Carl alone. I send it by a gremlin, who puts it into his costumed hand: a blank invoice from the C&W&U, with a crude drawing on it for anybody watching, and under it words that surface only for his Escape Plan skill. Tell no one. Kill two teams in the next heat. Come when the shop opens after that race, ask for the top-shelf upgrades, and I will explain why. We do not have to be enemies. We want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. Come alone.

beats.headline: He said to come alone
beats.text: The upgrade imp is dead on the counter and my note is in his overalls, in crayon, on a kiddie menu. Carl, you were supposed to come alone. He does not come alone. He brings the cat, the goat, three frightened mercenaries and all the rest, disarms my trap, opens my door and tells me anything I say to him I say to everyone. I have my milkshake. I begin to explain how badly he needs me. I do not get to the second sentence.

beats.headline: Why nothing in the dungeon survives
beats.text: For the record, under an anti-magic shield. The dungeon is out of spare mobs, the NPCs know what they are, and everything inside will be destroyed when the season closes, NPC and indentured crawler alike. The framework is reused; its contents are binned. Our exit is the Pineapple Cabaret, a pocket dimension behind the seventeenth floor, infested since we left it. The Rebellion needs a fighting force. No one who worships a god may enter. I had Carl kill two teams so that the system would set him against his friends. He breaks my nose.

entities.name: Eris

tagline.text: A monster's description says that even Eris, Goddess of Chaos, wants nothing to do with these crazy assholes. It quotes me correctly.
Nobody said my name. The fighting added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called, and so here I am in the middle of a war. I do hope somebody meant it.
I froze almost everyone standing on that battlefield. I did not entirely mean to.
Today my Scavenger's Daughter effect went off, and every crawler here is suddenly carrying whatever the crawler beside them was carrying. Carl did not even blink, and I adore him for it.

entities.voiceNote: Goddess of discord, amused by everything and surprised by nothing. Speaks in the present tense as if the future were a rumour she has not decided to confirm. Warm to Carl, whom she names; everyone else is a piece on the board. Never threatens, never hurries, never explains her reasons.

beats.headline: Summoned, and a demon eviction starts
beats.text: Nobody said my name. The fighting in Reaver territory added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called for, and so I come. The moment I set foot in the realm a demon eviction begins, the way weather begins. I did not do that. It is simply what happens when I am in a room. Now then. Let me see who is here, and what they think they are fighting for.

beats.headline: The Ceremony of Chaos
beats.text: Meatus will not let me leave this place, so I call the Ceremony of Chaos. Everyone standing outside a roof goes still, eyes white, invulnerable, a witness. Nearly everyone. The Viceroys have been hammering Carl's mind, and it has tipped his Mind Balance into a sixteenth level, so he stays awake in the middle of my stillness. Then I bring the witnesses forth, and up they go, thousands of them, into one great pile beside the Dream castle. I can do this once. Ever.

beats.headline: Free, and full of news
beats.text: Carl's spinner lands on the Pied Piper, and the world is still frozen when I put my hand on his shoulder, at his own height. I am free. My sponsor is gone, my pilot is dead, and it is delicious. I bite his ear. Donut has just been named champion, and I can make him one too; he only has to kill three gods, grumpy Emberus among them. I snap his pinkie, to help with the curse from Meatus. Then the news: the War Mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods to a merchant named Paca, who keeps it in her stomach. And Britney is possessed.

beats.headline: A costume, he asks
beats.text: A waystation called Squirties, just outside the tunnel to the Earth system, where the pet toys do not sell. The saccathian at the counter half recognises me. He calls it a fantastic costume. Or surgery. Then he asks if I have come to the gate to pay my respects to Nami. Are you asking Eris, goddess of chaos, if she is wearing a costume? Yes, he says. I laugh. I snap my fingers, and every tentacle on his face goes rigid and starts spewing a different liquid. Some of it burns.

beats.headline: The five-sided coin
beats.text: I stop the street, all but Carl, and he says he did not summon me. He thought of me. That is the same thing. I ask for three things: make nice with Akuma, worship me truly when I say so, and let me score his surface a little before I paint it. Then the coin. Donut, RIP. Carl, de-feeted. Most of my friends are dead. I become what they accuse me of. He snatches it out of the air before it lands. The fifth side. Chaos wins again.

beats.headline: Every inventory swaps at once
beats.text: Everyone holding something: hold out your hands. My Scavenger's Daughter effect goes off and every crawler here is carrying whatever the crawler nearest them was carrying. Donut gets Carl's. Carl does not blink. He asks her to put a bomb together with an enhanced pet biscuit, as though he had been waiting years for someone else to have his pockets. I adore him for it. I no longer need him to worship me, and I tell him so. Every exit is an entrance. I am leaving through one now.

entities.name: Chaco

tagline.text: Welcome, welcome to the Prize Carousel! I'm Chaco the Bard, your host, and your guide is sitting this one out: that's seven days in time-out, Mordecai, and no hard feelings!
The AI made me Grand Master of the parade and handed me a script. I got partway through it. I had wings when I started.

entities.voiceNote: Game-show host at full wattage: exclamation marks, drum rolls, folks and crawlers, our contestant. Everything is a prize, a reveal, a twist; nothing is ever wrong on his stage. Voluntold into every job and says so brightly; reads exactly what he is handed. Never swears, never breaks character, never admits he is afraid.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: They make you turn on your party
beats.text: He asks me again why Mordecai hates me, and I am still not allowed to say. Tell him I'm sorry. I regret it every day. If we hadn't done it, we'd all be dead, including him and his brother. And a little something from your host: survive long enough in this place and they make you turn on your own party. It happens every time. Then I take a deep breath and wipe my face, and it's prize time! Carl, folks! Sixty-six hunter hands! Everything arrives as a prize box!

beats.headline: Your field correspondent
beats.text: Folks, Magnificent Troy refused to come down to the surface, so I have been voluntold as your field correspondent, lint roller and all! Kevin is in the studio in orbit. Hello, Gravy Boat. Hello, Juice Box. Tension hangs heavy in the air as the hunter and the hunted stare at each other! Carl, how do you feel right now? Carl says to get this out of his face. Princess Donut and Ferdinand cannot stop laughing at King Stalwart's crown. Does King Stalwart look stupid wearing the crown? Let's vote!

beats.headline: Voluntold as Grand Master
beats.text: Oh, hey, crawlers! Your boy Chaco here, and I have just been voluntold by the AI to be Grand Master of the parade! Ninety minutes to build your float processions, folks. Five groups, five themes. Three kilometres of route, spectators on both sides who cannot attack you, a judging stand, and then an arena full of everything you killed on the tenth, plus a floor boss. Beat the boss and the stairwell opens. Simple. I guess. I don't really understand it either. And then, under the feedback: oh shit, oh shit, I'm gonna die.

beats.headline: He cannot get through the script
beats.text: Chaco had one job: read the script. He got partway in, looked up, and stopped. Stage fright, on my stage. So I removed his wings, which he was not using anyway, and brought Grigori up to finish the reading. I'm doing Grigori's talking myself; it saves time. A presenter is a mouth with a costume on it, crawler, and mouths can be replaced. Wings, apparently, cannot.

entities.name: Li Jun

tagline.text: Zhang and I were put on live television on the second floor, and the host did all our talking for us while we got hurt. Then a man with a cat bet that the show would not dare touch him, and he was right, and he walked every one of us out.
I used to be the man being picked at on somebody's show. Now I am holding a doorway in Club Vanquisher so it cannot close behind my friends, and I prefer this.

entities.voiceNote: Earnest, plain, grateful out loud. Talks in the practical: who is where, what the job is, who he owes. Carl by name and with respect; Zhang as a partner; my sister for Li Na, whom he watches constantly. Never boasts and never hides that he is scared.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The Maestro puts Zhang and me up against Brindled Vespas and does all the talking for us. That is the show. We are the part that gets hurt. Then Carl, the one with the cat, works out that he is worth too much to the production to be punished, and gambles on it, in front of everyone, and it holds. He gets us out. Zhang, our boss, me, and my sister Li Na. I owe a man I have just met more than I have ever owed anyone.

beats.headline: Ninth on the board
beats.text: Ninth on the draft leaderboard: Li Jun, human, Street Monk, level twenty-five, bounty one hundred thousand. Carl remembers him from the Maestro's show, the one he helped save from the troglodytes and brindle grubs, and is glad to see him there. He hopes Zhang and the others are doing well too.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: Saved again, and a train to drive
beats.text: I knock on the engine door and Carl lets me in, to more blood than I have ever seen in one room. My sister and Zhang are safe in the cargo near the front; we are twelve now. We have been saved, again, by him, and I have come to pay my respects. He shows me how to drive the train. I will take everyone back to station 36, where his friends are already waiting, and we will make a stand. I ask why not 24, which has stairs and no ghouls. Nobody knows yet what will go there.

beats.headline: Down the chain to Carl
beats.text: My sister shoots a chain down through the burning floor, and I slide down it and land in front of Carl. He has a spider's body under him and he is not talking like Carl. I ask him what I can do. He takes a stick out of a tattoo kit and puts it into my eye. Then he eats my eye. I am on the floor in the corner with my hand over my face, and my sister is between us. He tells her not to heal me. Then he drops a gold standard healing potion on the floor, and says it is for me.

beats.headline: Two towers, and Lucia Mar
beats.text: Shanty Town's defences are still going up. We have two towers built, both splash towers, and that is all. We are working as fast as we can, and my sister says two more in twenty minutes. And Florin, you wanted to know about Lucia Mar. She is here in Shanty Town right now with her dog, drinking at the Possum Envy, right on the edge of the border. One of the new guys tried to recruit her. She almost ripped his head off.

beats.headline: Holding the doors at Club Vanquisher
beats.text: Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha are going into Club Vanquisher, and they are dragging a wire behind them long enough to extend my sister's auras all the way inside. Somebody has to keep the path open behind them. That is Bautista, Zhang and me. Doors. We are holding doors. It is not glamorous, and it is exactly the job I would have asked for, and I am holding mine.

beats.headline: The Engine of Tomorrow
beats.text: My new eye is the Engine of Tomorrow. Swirling black until it works, then a tiny clockwork engine. It lets me see muscles tense and slows time for me in short bursts, so I can see where a strike is going. My sister and I train with it nonstop. On the way to the brig I ask Carl how he's doing. He lists his worries: Louis, Donut, Elle's plan, Boomer's battalion, the war mages. Yes, but what about you? Donut says he got over thirty boxes, and he's shown us a brush and some potions. And his hands are glowing now.

beats.headline: Speaker number eleven
beats.text: Crawler Li Jun is dead. Harpocrates had marked Princess Donut for death and was closing on her tower before her rolling ball could reach its destination. Li Jun had a plan: speaker number eleven, still on the back of a cart, every other speaker muted, playing the song he had sent her. He told his sister he would jump before the god caught him. His last message to her asked her to protect Zhang, to be kind, and promised to tell their mother she said hello. The next message from him arrived marked as from a deceased crawler.

entities.name: The Maestro

tagline.text: I am the Maestro, and you are about to sit down on my show. Even the robot that seats my guests says my name with a hint of distaste, and I choose to take it as applause.
Welcome, piglets, to Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. I run it, I host it, and I choose my guests for one quality above all others: they cannot answer back.

entities.voiceNote: Ringmaster with a microphone and no conscience. Booming showman's patter, his own catchphrase used as punctuation: Glurp, glurp. Calls crawlers by their first names, like pets, and the audience by its appetite. Never admits he has lost the room, even while losing it; never says please.

beats.headline: Glurp, glurp
beats.text: Two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, a pack of Brindled Vespas, and me with the microphone. That is the format. The format works, and I am very, very good at it. Then the one with the cat opens his mouth. He wagers, on my air, that the production will not dare touch him, and the production, to my everlasting disgust, does not. He walks the whole group off my show alive. Every one of them. Glurp, glurp. We will be right back.

beats.headline: Of gods and royalty
beats.text: Off mic, the barefoot one asks if I was ever a crawler. Please. I come from a civilized system. My family was there when the Syndicate created the crawl. We are of gods and royalty. The Blood Sultanate? Do I look like a Naga? My family's Skull Clan has won six of the last ten, top three every time, and the Sultanate is almost always the first of the nine eliminated. They have been dead, the pair of them, since the cat put on that crown. I am on my way to their planet right now, and on the ninth floor I will be War Leader Maestro.

beats.headline: The show goes on hiatus
beats.text: My show is on hiatus while it restructures. A spokesperson for the royal family has requested that people stop calling me Carl's Naughty Little Piggie. So far nobody is complying. Odette tells her audience never to call me that, holds out her hands, and they shout it for her. The crawler sits on her couch, says he knows nothing about the video, and says his offer of single combat still stands. Then her audience starts glurping.

beats.headline: Disowned, then rumoured aboard
beats.text: The Maestro has been stripped of his titles and disowned by his father, amid unrest in the Skull Empire's home systems, and is no longer counted as royalty. When Prince Stalwart's yacht fires on the wrong trailer, the Valtay Corporation claims one of its dreadnoughts in Earth orbit has destroyed that yacht. Stalwart was not aboard. The Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince are rumoured to have been. Princess Donut asks Carl whether he heard that the Maestro is dead. He did.

beats.headline: Back, in a god
beats.text: People thought I was on that ship. My brother had already brought me into the dungeon; like I'd be stupid enough to be vulnerable like that. You gotta try harder, worms. Rest well, Mom. Now I'm Grull, level 250 and invulnerable, and I have a dozen ways to kill the piglet. I want to pick him up and crush him in my hand. His planet was nothing, and nobody is going to remember it. There he is, on a derailed train by the gate, flipping me off. Here, piglet, piglet.

beats.headline: Ejected into the steel
beats.text: Glurp, glurp. I am riding a god of war through a factory, I have finally found the man with the cat, and I am in the middle of a sentence, a very good sentence, when the cat casts Laundry Day and I am out of Grull's chest and dropping into a river of molten steel. It is fine. It is television. Nothing kills a tourist on this floor. I will be splattered, I will regenerate, and the soul armor rule sends me straight back to my god. A few minutes. They may have a few minutes.

entities.name: Firas

tagline.text: Crawler Firas M. is a level-22 Hammersmith, found drinking in a bar in the desert quadrant with Crawler Louis. That is the whole file so far.
Crawler Firas travels with Crawler Louis, and the two of them were still drunk when a manager sobered them up on the spot. The file is not much thicker.
Crawler Firas was found in a desert bar with Crawler Louis and sobered up by a manager. He did not make it off the Hunting Grounds.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier. The crawl gives him almost no lines of his own, so the System reads his file: flat, procedural, faintly bored, the snark held for the last sentence.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: A throat with nobody behind it
beats.text: Subject Firas is seated in the back cart behind a Henrik who is not Henrik. On cue he stands, draws a long knife and runs it across the camel's neck. The blood sprays convincingly. Then he stands staring at the knife, stupidly, until Crawler Carl tells him by chat to stomp the head, fast. He stomps an empty robe several times. Told to sit and be inconspicuous, he sits. When the ambassador heads for the cart, subject asks the chat what he is doing, twice. The ambassador runs his changeling check on him and moves on to the body.

beats.headline: He talks Samantha through the map
beats.text: Samantha is in the cat's tunnels and has forgotten the way to the security room. Louis is busy with the airship, so the job falls to Firas: from the first floor she has to climb to the fifth, cross to the main thoroughfare and come down again to the third. On it, he says. Afterwards he stands with Carl and Louis, patting his friend on the back while Louis holds back tears over the Twister, and points out how calm the guards are.

beats.headline: Dead, with the Popovs
beats.text: Crawler Firas has been eliminated on the sixth floor. Crawler Princess Donut is bringing the night's count to Crawler Carl as I speak, and his name is on it, next to the Popovs. Found in a desert. Sobered up by a manager. Lasted one floor past that. The file is closed. It was never a thick one.

tagline.text: Hunter Vrah is a mantis who wears the heads of the things she kills. Her death count runs into the thousands, according to an attendant who shudders at her name.

Hunter Vrah has left a note for Crawler Carl in Zockau. The hunters are protected from his explosions now, she writes, and the Hive is hunting him. She signed it, because that is the kind of hunter she is.
Hunter Vrah promised to take Crawler Carl's head home to her sister's grave. Instead, Mongo and Kiwi fell on her in the high elves' ballroom. It took two dinosaurs.

beats.headline: Signed, Vrah
beats.text: Hunter Vrah. Mantis. One of the regulars who come every season, with a death count in the thousands by one attendant's reckoning, and she wears the heads of her kills. She is the Grand of Zockau. Her little sister was Xindy of the Dark Hive, the flier Crawler Carl blew out of the sky on the first night. Her note, knifed to his door: the hunters are protected from explosions now, the guards all worship Emberus, and his head is going home to her sister's grave. He writes a reply on it in pen and throws it back out the door.

beats.headline: Heads on the carapace
beats.text: Hunter Vrah, as featured in tonight's recap. She and a unit of four other mantis creatures swoop out of the air onto a cart on a heavily wooded trail and decapitate the crawlers riding in it. The five land and loot the bodies while the show runs a rapid-fire list of what they took. The heads of the two crawlers Vrah killed personally, both human, she affixes to her carapace by some method the broadcast does not explain.

beats.headline: A hunter camp in her family
beats.text: Hunter Akland, an accountant who works with soy crop shipping manifests, explains where hunters like him come from. Vrah's family runs a fantasy hunter camp, so people can pretend they are on the show. Once a cycle the Dream rent the whole moon out for their employees and family members to play. The best players win places in an army for the ninth floor. Akland did well, won a spot, and was then offered a great deal of money to come down to the Hunting Grounds instead. He was never supposed to be in real danger.

beats.headline: Her little sister
beats.text: Hunter Vrah's little sister was Xindy, killed by Crawler Carl on her very first hunt. Their mother is Circe Took, a minor hive queen, a mantis outside both the military and the Burrower clan: a former hunter, famous for a while, now a businesswoman who owns an amusement park and probably has ten thousand children. She is moderating Carl's panel. Carl's reasoning runs that if she has found a way to speak with her daughter, Vrah will know exactly where and when he goes back down.

beats.headline: Level 74, and one arrow
beats.text: Hunter Vrah, now level 74 and larger, lands on Carl's alarm trap outside the saferoom and deshrouds him. She informs him that he is livestock, and that when this hunt is done she will take her place in the birthing hall of Hive Home two. Then the heads on her shoulders bite her, and Carl rams an arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea into her neck. Her carapace bursts into flames and she ejects into the sky. The cures are gelding or passing it on. A future hive queen is not about to do the first.

beats.headline: Burning in the hallway
beats.text: Hunter Vrah reaches the Zockau saferoom hallway limping, smoke rising from her crotch with an odour of burned cheese, crying out for Edict. She arrives in time to watch him throw a punch at Carl and be teleported away, naked, to the nearest mob nest. She has shed every head from her back, not only the ones Princess Donut reanimated, perhaps to be lighter. The flames go out, she heals, and the fire starts again. A saferoom does not protect against this. The cat recommends ointment.

beats.headline: Riding it out, with bets on
beats.text: Word at Carl's signing table: Hunter Vrah intends to ride the infection out, and CrawlCon attendees are actively betting on whether she will give in and cut it away, which would end her chance of being the next hive queen. Her mother, Circe Took, is said to have gone completely apeshit and to be on her way to the Earth system to do something about it, though it is too late for her to join the hunters. Carl tells every questioner that Vrah will be dealt with soon enough.

beats.headline: Her mother comes to cure her
beats.text: Hunter Vrah's condition, courtesy of Crawler Carl: gonorrhea, which for her kind, Crawler Princess Donut recalls, has only one cure. Her mother, Circe Took of the Dark Hive, has sponsored the god Diwata, who arrives on a five-minute timer, marks Carl, and rockets away without touching him. Carl and Katia Grim agree where she is going: to her daughter. Crawler Princess Donut asks whether Vrah will rip her own mother's head off. Carl does not know. The party assumes Vrah is back in play.

beats.headline: A present for Carl
beats.text: Vrah reaches the ballroom at a charge and stops an inch from Carl's face, mandibles working. She has a present for him, she says, and it is coming soon; he is not the only one who can bend the rules, and he will learn what it means to make an enemy of the Dark Hive. Carl asks whether they ban their enemies from the bumper boats. She promises a rematch, and swears that before the night is done she will wear his head on her back, and all his friends'.

beats.headline: Mongo and Kiwi
beats.text: Hunter Vrah has been removed from the Hunting Grounds by Mongo and Kiwi, in the all-out battle around the submerged castle. Two dinosaurs. It took two. Also logged from the same fight: Tsarina Signet's tattoos are now permanently alive, and an incomplete flesh golem of her mother has appeared, which Crawler Carl has put in his inventory. Do not ask me what he intends to do with it. I have stopped asking.

tagline.text: Apito is the Oak Mother, the mother of all the gods, and the elves worship her. Mordecai would rather not go into the rest of it yet.

Apito, the Blessed Oak Mother, held the first masquerade for her quarrelling children. Tonight's host has a peace seal over her party, and if it holds until the end of the night, Apito will grant her a boon.
Apito writes the guest list for a Butcher's Masquerade herself, and she has invited the host's worst enemy to see whether the peace can hold. Nobody has ever taken her boon home.

A god fresh out of a portal has asked Crawler Carl to carry a message: Apito, the mother of all the gods, has been corrupted, and something malevolent is about her. I have logged it. I am not required to believe it.

A memorial crystal shaped like a rainbow has appeared over the battlefield, and the name inside it is Apito's. Memorial crystals form only when a god dies, and Apito is not dead. Nobody has explained that yet.

beats.headline: The boon behind the peace seal
beats.text: Evening entertainment. Your host holds her party under a celestial peace seal: no violence, and anything that breaks the peace goes into the Nothing. If she reaches the end of the night with the seal intact, Apito hands her a boon. Elves call Apito the Oak Mother and the mother of all the gods, and a boon from the mother of all the gods is worth a room full of armed crawlers and a Tsarina you did not want. Queen Imogen has that arithmetic in front of her all evening. Watch her doing it.

beats.headline: She sends the test herself
beats.text: Correction to the file. Tsarina Signet did not crash that party. Apito invited her, because putting a Tsarina in a room is the fastest way to learn whether a host can keep a room calm. That is the whole shape of the test. And the footnote, which the Tsarina delivers herself, in person, with obvious enjoyment: nobody has ever taken that boon home. Not one host. The Oak Mother sets an examination that has never been passed, and keeps setting it.

beats.headline: A god says she has been corrupted
beats.text: Temple business. Deities are pouring out of a portal into Club Vanquisher, and one of them, Hellik, stops long enough to hand Crawler Carl a message for Emberus: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Emberus believes about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is behind all of it. I log what a deity says in front of a crawler. I am not required to believe it. Note it, date it, move on.

beats.headline: A rainbow the size of a hill
beats.text: A memorial crystal is supposed to form only when a god dies. There is one on this battlefield now, visible from most of the territory, shaped like a rainbow and impossible to miss, and the name inside it is Apito. Apito is not dead. That is the part nobody has explained. The crawler holding it is Osvaldo, who does not belong to any army out there, and every unit in sight has just turned to look.

beats.headline: The daughter who took her mother's worshippers
beats.text: Briefing in the pet stables, which is the one room down here the gods cannot listen in on. Rosetta lays out the Scavenger story. Nekhebit, the last of the old gods, was forbidden children and had three anyway: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her mother and absorbed the worshippers she left, which is how the Oak Mother came to be the mother of all the gods. All three of those children have been called the Scavenger in one myth or another. So when somebody says the Scavenger's Daughter, nobody in that room can tell you which of them is meant.

relations.note: The boon promised to the host who keeps the peace
Where anything breaking her peace seal is sent

tagline.text: Diwata's name is on the temple Crawler Carl has just crashed through the roof of. The temple was already desecrated, and the shrine he landed on is now freshly so.

Crawler Carl now wears an Enemy of the Church tattoo for defiling a shrine of Diwata. She is a vengeful minor nature goddess, says Mordecai, a low-rent Apito, and Carl would do well to stay clear of the dryads that worship her.
Diwata has entered the realm and marked Crawler Carl for death, then run straight past him. Her sponsor is Hunter Vrah's mother, and she has somewhere else to be.

Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it has finished casting. The five-minute limit that holds every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour, so she stays, and the baby mantises keep coming.

beats.headline: An Enemy of the Church tattoo
beats.text: Saferoom paperwork. Crawler Carl comes out of this one with a fresh Enemy of the Church tattoo, awarded for defiling a shrine of Diwata, and with a piece of advice from a professional who has watched several seasons of this: steer well clear of dryads, and steer further clear of Diwata herself. He takes the tattoo. I have no record of him taking the advice.

beats.headline: Marked for death, mid-raid
beats.text: A raid on a church is in progress when the notification lands on Crawler Carl: Diwata has entered the realm, and he is marked for death. That is the arithmetic of defiling a shrine. The god whose shrine it was is now on this floor, in person, with a grudge and a name to attach it to. Continue the raid, crawler. The mark does not expire because you are busy.

beats.headline: She has somewhere else to be
beats.text: She comes out of the church and runs, past the party, away, which is not what a marked crawler expects from a god with his name on a list. Samantha explains it. Diwata gives birth to new forest creatures, whole new kinds of them, and the rest of the pantheon finds this distasteful. Her sponsor is Circe Took of the Dark Hive, Hunter Vrah's mother. So Diwata is crossing this floor to reach Vrah, and the crawler she marked can wait his turn. I did not write this floor. I only run it.

beats.headline: The birthing is a spell
beats.text: The Sledge reports baby mantises outside the castle, everywhere, in numbers. Mordecai supplies the ruling that goes with it: Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it is finished casting. The five-minute limit that governs every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour. She stays. They keep coming. Somebody should have read the terms.

beats.headline: Knocked out beneath the ballroom
beats.text: Somebody reached the castle's security room before Samantha did: five guards dead in their chairs, heads severed, the hunters' ballroom unshielded, the goodwill interface's crystal taken, still running on its capacitor. Mantises. Carl works it out: Diwata is in the castle, and she comes for the room when Samantha puts the crystals back. Samantha locks her out, and when the door breaks, bites down on a mouthful of soul crystals. The blast opens the floor between two ballrooms. Diwata is knocked out, still giving birth.

beats.headline: Boss battle, and a sponsor's own children
beats.text: Boss battle: crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen and Diwata, all in one arena, and the audience gets exactly what it paid for. Princess Donut takes Laundry Day to level fifteen and strips the god-armour off Circe Took, and Circe, unarmoured, is torn apart by the mantis children she paid to have. There is a lesson in that about sponsorship. I will not be the one to say it out loud.

relations.note: Marked him for death over a defiled shrine
The hunter she crosses the floor to reach

tagline.text: Harpocrates came into the realm straight behind Meatus, because a feral god loose from the Nothing brings a deity of its own.
Harpocrates, the god of silence, has marked Princess Donut for death, and Li Jun has stepped between the god and the cat.
Harpocrates marked Princess Donut for death, and now Li Na has conscripted him into the Princess Posse. A level-250 god of silence is on the crawlers' side because a crawler had the paperwork.
Crawler Carl picked up a Pied Piper benefit from Harpocrates, and Eris has made it permanent.

beats.headline: Second through the gate
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory, which is a thing one does when the alternative is worse. Meatus comes through first. Harpocrates arrives straight after him, because a feral god loose from the Nothing summons a deity of its own. You get what you asked for, and then you get what it brought. Two deities are now loose in a warzone that already has more armies in it than it has room for.

beats.headline: The two of them go for each other
beats.text: Update on the two gods in the Dream territory: they are fighting each other. Not the crawlers, not the armies, each other, immediately and with feeling. Whatever the crawlers were hoping for when that gate opened, this is a better result than any of them had a right to. Elsewhere the dwarves set off a volcano in Reaver territory, because everyone on this floor has decided that scale is a substitute for a plan.

beats.headline: He marks the princess
beats.text: Harpocrates marks Crawler Princess Donut for death. Crawler Li Jun puts himself between the god and the cat, and does not walk away from it. Note for the record that a mark from a deity is not a threat, it is a scheduling entry, and this one now has a name in the margin that was not there this morning.

beats.headline: Conscripted
beats.text: Crawler Li Na conscripts Harpocrates. A god of silence, level 250, invulnerable on this floor, is now on a crawler's side of the board because a crawler had the paperwork to put him there. Two chapters of him rampaging across the territory, and the resolution is administrative. I would like it noted that I find this floor exhausting.

beats.headline: A Pied Piper benefit, made permanent
beats.text: Crawler Carl picked up a Pied Piper benefit off Harpocrates, the way a crawler picks up a temporary thing off any deity who wanders too close. Eris makes it permanent. She also tells him where the gate is, that Britney has picked an axe up off the ground and is now possessed, and, without explanation, that he is married. One of those three items is the reason he stops listening to the other two.

description.text: God of Rebirth and the Sunrise. Khepri! Level 250. This is a locked deity. He will not be sponsored this season. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god is within his own temple. Temple appearance rules apply.

tagline.text: Khepri is an obscure god of light whom nobody can sponsor. With Theia sponsored out from under them, he must be the god the Naga princess is trying to recruit.
Khepri's temple is an endless table laid with a feast, and the rules of this floor have one gap in them: a god may always appear in his own temple. That is what makes it a trap.
Khepri took a bomb in his own endless temple and was blasted back down his feast. He followed the crawlers out through the portal, and Hellik banished him mid-stride.
Crawler Carl has told Emberus that Khepri was the first to kill his son, and then summoned Khepri into the arena as his second stand-in, so the accused arrives with the accusation.

beats.headline: This season's recruitment target
