beats.text: Princess Vinata and her guard keep disappearing from a battlefield and reappearing in Club Vanquisher, and the reason is a recruitment quest for one of the gods of light. Their usual target, Theia, has been sponsored out from under them by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network. Which leaves Khepri. Rosetta works this out from past seasons, which is a polite way of saying the crawlers now know something the Naga think is private.

beats.headline: The one open door on the floor
beats.text: The portal to all the temples, and inside one of them, Vinata. Deity summoning is throttled on this floor by the rules of the war, with one exception nobody thought to close: a god may always appear in his own temple. So Khepri is home. Samantha opens the door, Carl and Katia Grim and Prepotente go through it, and an achievement arrives to inform them, with the timing I have come to expect from this place, that they have walked into a trap. Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch reads the room and hands him ninety seconds of immortality for standing near this particular god.

beats.headline: The endless temple, and what is at the table
beats.text: Since the crawlers are frozen and I have thirty seconds, the file on this one. Khepri is humanoid apart from the head, where there is instead an entire beetle, wings and legs and a small head of its own. He does not talk. He chitters. His temple is listed as endless, which in practice is a room and a door and one long table carrying a never-ending feast of four hundred and thirty-three kinds of insect. He was a retainer of Khnum until Khnum mysteriously dropped dead a few days ago, so he has taken service under another deity to keep himself alive. The big players ignore him. When everything unfreezes he is going to go absolutely bugshit at every person in that room, quite possibly including his own worshipper.

beats.headline: A bomb in his own house
beats.text: Katia Grim and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus and get themselves ejected from the temple, which leaves Carl alone with a spell and a bomb. Everything in the room dies except the immortal and the invulnerable: Khepri, blasted backwards through his own endless feast, and Vinata, who has the same immortality status Carl does. Khepri follows them out through the portal, and Hellik banishes him mid-stride. Being a god of light does not appear to buy much on this floor.

beats.headline: A death cult in her name
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Princess Donut's new class had barely finished glowing before a message arrived from Khepri, the god Crawler Carl and Crawler Katia fought on the previous floor. It was not friendly. It informed her that he is forming a death cult in her name. She asked her manager what that means. Her manager said: nothing good. That is also the administration's position, and the administration does not often agree with her manager.

beats.headline: Beetles off the feast table
beats.text: The beetles pouring out of the ruptured shells are Sacred Feaster Scarabs, lifted, the AI says, straight off Khepri's feast table in Club Vanquisher. They are invulnerable, by design. They were meant to ignore the racers and assemble on the roof into a hundred-foot gate boss. Instead something this god did earlier, which the AI declines to explain, has broken the game. The boss is cancelled. The bugs are hostile. They are still invulnerable. Nobody can kill what came off his table, and now it wants them dead.

beats.headline: Named, and summoned into the arena
beats.text: Inside the boss, of all places, Crawler Carl tells Emberus who killed his son: Khepri. Then he summons Khepri as his second stand-in, so the accusation and the accused arrive in the arena together, and stops worshipping Emberus on the way out of the sentence. He adds that he holds himself responsible too. I have run a lot of arenas. I have never had one where the crawler brought the defendant.

relations.note: Standing near him buys ninety seconds of immortality
Named as the one who killed his son

description.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte. Level 250. This goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. Warning: This sponsor is not currently inhabiting the shell of this deity. She will speak and react as per her regular nature. Considering who this is, that's some bad fucking news for you guys. Warning: This is a deity. She is invulnerable on this floor.

tagline.text: One of the gods a feral summoning very nearly brought through was Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. That would have been an extinction-level event for this floor and the next, and it was blocked only because there is still a floor of sponsorship bidding to get through.

Amayon has mentioned Ysalte in passing. According to Mordecai, she kills every crawler who comes near her, the dwarves call her the Downward Spiral, and if she were in this realm, everyone would know about it.
Sister Ines had a patron, and it was Ysalte. Now her nun is dead, the goddess has entered the realm in a temper, and Crawler Louis is marked for death.

Ysalte, Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity, is level 250 and invulnerable. Her sponsor is not inside her, so she acts entirely as herself, she has taken hold of Amayon, and while she is here every potion you touch turns to vinegar.

A totem made from Paz removed Ysalte from the realm two floors ago, but her memorial crystal is still here. Britney has taken it off Osvaldo, and Samantha says she will need the Halls of the Ascendency or Sheol to get the goddess out of her.

beats.headline: A name a demon brings up
beats.text: Amayon mentions Ysalte, in passing, the way a prisoner mentions the guard he does not want to talk about. Mordecai supplies the file: she is the Vinegar Bitch, she kills every crawler who comes near her, and gods are not usually subtle, so if she were in this realm, we would know about it. That is a reasonable position, well argued, and consistent with everything on record. I want it in writing that he said it.

beats.headline: Her nun goes down, and she arrives
beats.text: Thirty-second floor of the FOCSA building. Crawler Carl puts Sister Ines out with the Nighty-Night wand and Crawler Louis finishes the job. Sister Ines had a patron, and her patron is Ysalte, and Ysalte comes into the realm about it in a temper that registers on my instruments. Crawler Louis is marked for death. So much for nobody being able to arrive without us knowing.

beats.headline: Nobody is driving
beats.text: The readout on this one is worse than the goddess. She is sponsored, but the sponsor is not inhabiting her, which means she speaks and acts as herself with nothing between her and the room. She is invulnerable. She takes hold of Amayon while the building comes down around him, and when a teleport trap shakes him loose of the snake body it does not shake him loose of her. The Missing Piece quest opens on the back of it: free the demon, get him casting, and survive her totems for the ten minutes before she is back. She cannot be killed. That is not encouragement, it is a specification.

beats.headline: Put down by one of her own totems
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte has been removed from this realm by a totem raised from the former crawler Paz. Her own quest furniture, turned around and used on her. Part One of The Missing Piece completes. Elsewhere in the same collapse Crawler Carl rides his health down to two percent on purpose to set fire to every street he had walked on, which tells you what kind of afternoon this was for everybody.

beats.headline: The statue is finished
beats.text: A dwarf calls out that he has finished, in the moment before Larracos goes. The broken statue from the front of the castle has been pieced back together. It is Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch, the dead goddess of this city, killed by Paz at the end of the last floor. Over her shoulder she carries a giant axe. A giant pickaxe. Crawler Carl is looking straight at it when everything flashes and disappears.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been carrying Ysalte's memorial crystal: the goddess his friend Paz killed. It did not protect him from Scolopendra, as he admitted seconds before the light went green. He makes a run for the portals across a roof Crawler Carl has just opened up, and Crawler Britney stops him and takes the crystal. Samantha's assessment, delivered flatly: if Britney wants rid of Ysalte, she needs the Halls of the Ascendency or she needs Sheol, and neither of those is on this floor.

tagline.text: According to War God Grull's description, Taranis is Grull's father, and he worries that his son's temper makes him a poor choice to rule the heavens.
The god of thunder protects a pig called Penelope, who races on a rival team. Anyone who kills her, or even hurts her, will be marked for death by Taranis.
Crawler Carl has worked out that Taranis is in love with the pig, and he is threatening to shoot her in the head unless the god of thunder shows himself.
Taranis killed Emberus in the arena for taking a swing at the pig he loves.
Taranis killed a god over a pig. Then he left the realm, saying he was taking two pieces of his mother with him, and he took Samantha and Krakaren Prime.

beats.headline: The pig has a god
beats.text: Team One Fine Pig: two tigrans, Nico and Dario, in a throuple with a pig named Penelope. The interesting line in that file is not the throuple. It is that Penelope is under the protection of Taranis. A god of thunder has taken a personal interest in a pig on a racing team, and every crawler who reads that entry is going to file it somewhere and keep it.

beats.headline: Somebody found the lever
beats.text: The boss battle is on and Crawler Carl is spending his messages carefully. One goes to Emberus: I know who killed your son, meet me in the Scolopendra Club. The other is not a message so much as a hostage note. Taranis is in love with the pig. Carl says he will kill the pig if Taranis does not come and stop him. The god of thunder is now a scheduled arrival, and he was invited by threat.

beats.headline: He kills Emberus over the pig
beats.text: Emberus, pinned and made briefly vulnerable by two bolts from Princess Donut, swings at Crawler Carl. Penelope takes the hit instead, because of a Four-Leaf Clover Patch and the sort of luck this floor generates. Taranis kills him for it. A fire god, patron and quest-giver, removed from the arena inside a second by a thunder god defending a pig. I want everyone at home to appreciate the proportions here.

beats.headline: Two pieces of his mother
beats.text: Eris empties the arena's pockets and leaves. Khepri leaves. Taranis says he is taking two pieces of his mother with him, and goes, and what he takes with him is Samantha and Krakaren Prime. He does not explain the sentence. Nobody in the arena asks him to. I have the transcript and I have run it four times, and I am telling you exactly what he said and nothing more.

beats.headline: He takes the crystal on his way out
beats.text: Inventory note from the close of the boss battle. Prepotente's memorial crystal is gone, and Taranis took it. Crawler Carl finds a different one in the wreckage, made by a god dying in that arena, which is not the crystal anybody wanted and is the one that is left. The stairwells to the twelfth floor are open.

relations.note: Killed him in the arena
One of the two pieces he takes with him
Whose crystal he takes

tagline.text: According to the description of a crossbow, Nekhebit is a long-forgotten vulture goddess, jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her for Apito, she cursed the seed of the high elf court.
Nekhebit has re-ascended, and on her own show Odette has announced that she will be performing as the famed, ancient goddess this season.
Hellik has told Crawler Carl that his mother, Apito, has been corrupted, and that he believes Nekhebit is behind it.

Princess Donut has committed her third atrocity, and the system has made her the Oak Fell and named her Champion of Nekhebit. The class is named for felling the oak, and the title belongs to the goddess the oak displaced.

According to Rosetta, Nekhebit was the last of the old gods and was forbidden to have children. She had three anyway, Apito, Scolopendra and a son, and Apito defeated her and took the worshippers she had left.

beats.headline: Odette announces her sponsorship
beats.text: On her own show, in front of the audience she built, Crawler Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season, and the deity is Nekhebit. Then she offers three choices of adjutant and Crawler Carl takes Baroness Victory. Everybody in the room is watching the adjutant question. I would gently suggest that the first sentence was the news.

beats.headline: What the crossbow says about her
beats.text: The lore attached to a repeating crossbow, for anyone who reads the flavour text: the long-forgotten goddess Nekhebit is jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her to worship Apito, the Oak Goddess, Nekhebit grew enraged, blamed the male-dominated high elf court for letting her worshippers stray, and cursed their seed. Every elf and fairy breed in the universe traces back to that court and that curse. It is called the Fae Diaspora. Somebody put all of that on a weapon description and expected nobody to read it.

beats.headline: Named through a portal
beats.text: Hellik, holding a portal open with gods pouring out of it around him, uses the time he has to say four things to Crawler Carl. He did not kill Emberus's son. Everything Emberus believes about him is a lie. Apito has been corrupted. And Nekhebit, he believes, is behind all of it. A vulture goddess almost nobody down here had heard of two floors ago is now the name at the bottom of a divine accusation.

beats.headline: A champion, three atrocities in
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut commits her third Atrocity and the system pays out: the Oak Fell class, and the title Champion of Nekhebit. Consider the shape of that. The class is named for felling the oak. The title belongs to the goddess the oak displaced. Somewhere above this floor an old grudge has just been handed a very small, very loud instrument.

beats.headline: Three children she was forbidden
beats.text: Rosetta tells the Scavenger story in the pet stables, where nothing above can hear it. Nekhebit was the last of the old gods and was forbidden to have children. She had three: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her and absorbed the worshippers she had left. Each of those three has been called the Scavenger somewhere in the myths, which is why nobody can agree who the Scavenger's Daughter is, and why the war mages keep looking at Samantha's daughter.

relations.note: Champion of Nekhebit
One of the three children she was forbidden

entities.name: Eileithyia

description.text: Eileithyia is something of an oddity. She's benevolent. Unlike most of these psychos, she's known for her kind heart. She's prayed to by all mothers, both when they're attempting to sow the seeds, and when the harvest comes. And while she does many things, she's mostly known as She Who Eases Pain. Both the physical pain of childbirth and the inevitable darkness that comes to those who are unable to complete their most sacred task. When the stillness comes, she is not the one who has caused the heartbreak. But she is the one holding the grieving mother's hand.

entities.voiceNote: A goddess who is genuinely kind, which makes her the strangest thing in this pantheon. Warm, plain, unhurried; she speaks to a crawler the way a midwife speaks to a frightened mother, practical and quiet, telling him exactly what to do next. Calls Carl by name. Talks about pain as something to be eased rather than paid for. Never threatens, never bargains upward, never raises her voice, and never says a word about what her sponsor wants.

tagline.text: Samantha drops my name into the story of where Diwata came from, and then admits she cannot remember the rest of it. That is all right. It was never her story.

I have come into this realm with a boon for each of them and a quest about spiders, and the quest is a cover. What I want is for the crawler to accept a certain offer, and in return I will help him keep the young woman and the cat he is most afraid of losing.
Odette never asked to be his adjutant, as I told him she would. That failure was mine, not his, and I will honour our agreement. But if I learn that he warned her, I will crush everyone he loves.
I was held frozen while she chose between my two gifts. She chose to carry a child, so I eased what needed easing and took her out of this dungeon.

beats.headline: A quest about spiders, which is a cover
beats.text: I come in alongside Yemaya, wearing a sponsor from the Grixist Swarm, and the first thing I do is hand each of them a floor boon, because it costs me almost nothing and it is a kind thing to do. Then I give Carl's party a quest about spiders. The quest is a cover. What I want is to help him keep the two he is most afraid of losing, and the crown that is going to take them from him. So: accept the offer to be the team's adjutant. I will see that the votes fall the way they need to fall, and the protections come off the ninth floor, and the crown gets sorted. Tell nobody. Not the cat, not the woman making the offer, not your guide.

beats.headline: The flower with my name on it
beats.text: There is a flower in a thrice-sealed box with my name on it, and a doppelgänger has already broken two of the three seals to reach it. Whoever eats it takes a boon from me, and my boon has two shapes. She can be carried to the twelfth floor and stand as a celestial attendant until the games open. Or she can be made pregnant, and be pulled out of the crawl entirely, because I do not let anyone carrying a child fight in a place like this. Both are ways past the ninth floor without walking it. I did not put the flower in that box. I only decide what it does when she eats it.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette never asked for the chair. I send Carl a message and tell him plainly that this was out of his control, and that I will honour our agreement. I also tell him what happens if I learn he warned Odette about it: I will crush everyone he knows and loves, beginning with Katia and ending with the cat. Both halves of that are sincere. Gods trade down here, and he knows now exactly what he is standing in.

beats.headline: She chooses, and I take her out
beats.text: The doppelgänger wakes, and it is time, so I enter the realm. Then a cat casts Laundry Day on my sponsor and ejects her out of me, and I am held in place, unable to move a finger, until the choice is made. It is not a bad way to spend the minutes. Katia chooses to be pregnant. So I ease what needs easing, and I take her out of this dungeon, and her friends stand in the dust of a battlefield saying goodbye to somebody who is going to live.

relations.note: The adjutant offer she told him to accept
Her boon, and the door out

description.text: War God Grull. Level 250. Sponsored by Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been involuntarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply.

tagline.text: Grull is the war god named on Carl's new gauntlet, which warns that striking one of his adherents may turn the target into the deity himself. According to Mordecai, his worshippers are horses, centaurs, and anyone in blue face paint.
A train engineer who worships Grull very nearly brought his war god into a fight with a party of crawlers. Very nearly.

Grull, level 250 and four storeys tall, was driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. He killed the Mimic Rex, stepped on Carl, and was sent to the Abyss by a party that had no business surviving him.
The moment Corcunda's two halves were made whole again, Grull entered the realm to punish him for not being true.

Grull came for Corcunda, and Corcunda and Dong Quixote walked at the war god together. Princess Donut put a giant magnet on Dong's lance, every screw in the factory came with it, and Dong killed Grull with the lot. The god has gone back to the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and from this floor down the llama-shaped ones join in as well. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. Crawler Carl's guide gave the blunt summary of the whole subject a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: He arrives the moment the ritual works
beats.text: Crawler Carl drives a truck along walls and ceilings through dolls and slag elementals so that Grigori can finish a ritual, and the ritual works: Corky's two halves become one thing again. That is the good news, and it lasts about a second, because the instant it happens Grull enters the realm to smite him. Somebody up there was watching that ritual very closely and does not want it completed.

beats.headline: A lance, and a very large magnet
beats.text: Princess Donut casts Laundry Day and expels the sponsor riding Grull, which buys a moment. Grull goes for Corcunda instead, and Corcunda decides to take the smite himself so the others do not have to, and says so out loud to Dong, and Dong says he is not leaving him again. Then the two of them walk at a war god together. Donut puts Big-Ass Magnet on the lance, every screw in the factory comes with it, and Dong kills Grull with the lot. Grull goes back to the twelfth floor. The pair of them go back to the race, and make the line with seconds to spare.

description.text: Orthrus. Juvenile Gate Guardian. Level 10. This is a bereft pet of Geyrun. Who's a good boy? Who's a good boy? The most loveable hell-hound on this side of Alpha Centari. The left side is for sniffin' and the right side is for lickin' and that pink belly of his? It's for kissin'.

tagline.text: Something enormous is outside the bubbles, taking the floor apart, and what it is looking for is a dog called Orthrus.

Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, with two heads and floppy ears, and he fills half a bubble on his own. Almost everything that comes out of the Nothing comes out ruined, but he came out unharmed. He is a puppy.
One quest says to bring Orthrus home to Emberus, and another pays crawlers to kill him first. Both are live at the same time.
Orthrus was cornered between two bubbles with Quan Ch closing in on him, until Emberus arrived and took him home.

beats.headline: Something outside is looking for a dog
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports in from a popped bubble: there is a deity outside, taking the landscape apart, and it is searching. Not hunting crawlers. Searching. The thing it has lost is called Orthrus. Every crawler on this floor is working out how to survive their own bubble, and the largest event on my board is a god who has misplaced a pet.

beats.headline: He lands inside the bubble
beats.text: Orthrus is now inside the bubble with Crawler Carl's team, and everyone in there has been handed the Where the Red God Glows quest to go with him. Around the edges of it: Maggie My is loose somewhere up on the bowl, and Princess Donut spends the whole thing trying to keep an enormous two-headed puppy alive. Everyone is very busy. Nobody is looking at the same emergency.

beats.headline: The one god down here who can die
beats.text: The file on him, since he is going to matter. Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, kid brother to the three-headed one who guards a stairwell exit a long way below this one. He was on course to become a vicious, baby-eating, nun-defiling murder machine, and then in a single day his master was murdered and he was pulled into the Nothing. Most things the Nothing touches come out ruined. He came out unaffected, because he is too innocent for it to take hold, and fire does nothing to him at all. Here is the line that matters to a crawler: unlike other gods, he is not invulnerable. He is a puppy. Happy, destructive, rambunctious, roly-poly, very pokey. Fragile.

beats.headline: Two quests, pointing opposite ways
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut take an aeroplane up and read Meat Hooks, a scroll whose stench brings every carnivorous pet in range running, to lure a puppy the size of a building out of the water and out of the bubble. The quest that comes with it is simple: bring Orthrus to Emberus. Then a second quest is announced, and this one pays crawlers for killing him. Both are on the board together, which is a design decision somebody made and I am obliged to run. Crawler Quan Ch reads the second one and attacks the puppy.

beats.headline: Collected
beats.text: The aeroplane spirals down with Quan Ch closing in on Crawler Carl. Carl takes Emberus as his god mid-fall and throws a celestial grenade, the god arrives at his position, and for a short while nothing on this floor can touch him. Then Emberus finds Orthrus. The two of them go, together, and the floor is left to the people who were fighting over a dog.

relations.note: It touched him and did not take

tagline.text: Yarilo is the banished god of lust. A mage in a sandcastle wanted him to make a heroine from a stage play fall in love with him, but something else answered the summoning, and the mage is still trapped in his castle.
Yarilo, the god of lust, has come out of the Nothing feral and loose on a battlefield, and he has gone straight after Samantha, which is exactly what he was let out for.
The War Mage Rebellion has conscripted Yarilo, paying for him with potions it traded for on the Midnight Market. A god of lust has become a line item.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could reach Yarilo, the banished god of lust, and have Yarilo make Lika love him. Lika is the heroine of a stage play. She was never real. What came through was not Yarilo either. It gave him a wife made of sand, which is why the ooze follows him about, and it left him trapped in his transformed castle with the knowledge of what he has let out. The plaque under his display says my love, my wife. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: Why he is in the Nothing
beats.text: Since tonight's party runs under a peace seal, some history about the last god who broke one. At the first masquerade in the Halls, hosted by the mother of all the gods, Yarilo got drunk and forced himself on another deity's familiar. That broke the seal. Apito sent him into the Nothing for it, and he has been in the Nothing ever since. The seal on tonight's party is hers as well. Enjoy the canapes.

beats.headline: Out of the gate, chasing an AI
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo enters the realm and goes straight after Samantha, which is precisely what he was let out for: something enormous and single-minded, aimed at an AI who is fast enough to lead it wherever the crawlers want it to go. Everyone has a job. Samantha's job is running.

beats.headline: Conscripted with potions
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion has taken the Larracos castle and holds it for six hours to win, and they have gone shopping for reinforcements. They conscript Yarilo, paid for with potions they traded for the gate on the Midnight Market. Somewhere in that chain a god of lust became a line item. Fopsy has a theory about why Agatha is doing any of this, and I will let her explain it, because I have a god to move.

beats.headline: Taken off the board by another god
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo has been removed from this floor by Harpocrates, acting under the direction of Crawler Li Na. He came through a gate, chased an AI the length of a warzone, changed sides for a crate of potions, and finished at the hands of the god who had come through that same gate ahead of him. Everything down here becomes somebody's equipment, the gods included.

tagline.text: Meatus was the first god through the Gate when Elle opened it in Dream territory, and he arrived in a war that was already going badly for everyone in it.
Meatus came through the Gate and immediately picked a fight with Harpocrates, the god his arrival summoned. It is an old rivalry, usually played out in the Ascendency battles.
Princess Donut rolled a ball of frozen witnesses across the battlefield, and Meatus reached into it and dragged Eris in with him.
Princess Donut's War Crime spell took Meatus apart. In the System's own words, he is now slap-chopped all over the realm, and even the Scavenger's Daughter looks away.

beats.headline: First through the gate
beats.text: Operation Ruin is written up in the cookbook, Princess Donut is installed in the Nest, and Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory. What comes out first is Meatus. What comes out behind him is Harpocrates. Neither of them was requested by name, because that is not a thing the gate offers, and both of them are now on a floor with four armies on it.

beats.headline: He picks the other god
beats.text: Meatus and Harpocrates start fighting each other. Of every direction those two could have chosen on arrival, the crawlers have drawn the one that costs them nothing, which after the fortnight this floor has had feels less like luck and more like an apology. In Reaver territory the dwarves set off a volcano, so the ledger balances.

beats.headline: He pulls a goddess into the pile
beats.text: The pile of witnesses is frozen, conscious and invulnerable, which is a combination I would like on the record as not my idea. Princess Donut casts Rolling Battle Formation on the whole heap and starts it moving. Meatus reaches into it and drags Eris in with him. A goddess of discord, inside a rolling ball of frozen soldiers, on a battlefield. Somewhere the Party Planner is coming apart and Crawler Louis is falling into a castle, and it is still the second most interesting thing on this floor.

beats.headline: Chopped, and nobody watches
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut casts her War Crime spell and Meatus comes apart into pieces. I closed the eye of the Scavenger's Daughter for that one, on the grounds that even she does not want to look at it, and I stand by the decision. Harpocrates swears revenge for him and leaves the realm. Two gods came through that gate. Neither of them is on this floor now.

relations.note: She opened the gate that brought him

description.text: God of Blacksmithery and Armor Ogun. Level 250. This god is not sponsored. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been temporarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply. He's here now because Ogun strongly believes all punishments should be handed out in person.

tagline.text: Two of the crawlers met here, Paz and Anton, worship Ogun, the god of blacksmiths.
Paz and Anton have received a quest from their own god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and Ogun wants it to be his rather than Asojano's.
Bomo repaired Yemaya's shrine instead of Ogun's, and the god of blacksmiths is entering the realm about it.
Ogun, level 250, put a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal, killed Anton, and left the realm with what he came for.

beats.headline: A quest from their own god
beats.text: Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, Paz, Anton and Sister Ines get themselves to Asojano's shrine intact, which required flagging a ghommid splitter named Skylar Spinach and a certain amount of nerve. Asojano begins a ritual. And in the middle of it, Paz and Anton receive a quest from Ogun, who is their god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and he would like it to be his. Note the position those two men are now in. Note who put them in it.

beats.headline: The shrine they did not pick
beats.text: Deities appear from every direction, each of them making a case for their own shrine, which is the single worst committee meeting I have ever had to render. Then Katia Grim messages Carl: repair Yemaya's shrine or lose her and the cat to the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. So Bomo repairs Yemaya's. The ghommid settlement is freed, Carl walks away with slugpox and a card made out of Asojano, and Ogun enters the realm to punish his worshippers. Not the crawlers who chose. His own.

beats.headline: The outsider at the anvil
beats.text: The file, for the people about to meet him. Ogun is an outsider, one of the old gods, from an obscure pantheon that has dissipated into time, and until a minute ago he was the last surviving member of it. He spends his days at a celestial anvil, angrily making armour, piece after piece, and nobody knows why he does it or where the armour goes. It is said the pieces are a strange shape, all of them cut for four-legged beasts. He is a god of blacksmiths and armourers now. He was something considerably larger once, and his power and his ambition make him a real contender for the throne of heaven.

beats.headline: Punishment, in person
beats.text: Ogun puts a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal. Crawler Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton to shield him, and Ogun kills Anton instead, and leaves the realm having taken exactly what he came for. Paz, going, spends his last minutes telling Carl and Donut two things about Sister Ines: her race makes everyone near her want to protect her, and it gets stronger the longer they are near her, and before the crawl she was a murderer. Sister Ines turns Paz into a card rather than lose him.

relations.note: The one who repaired the other shrine

entities.name: The Sledge

tagline.text: I'm seven feet of rock in a tuxedo, and Bomo and me work security at the Desperado Club. Tonight two crawlers bought us as a pair, and the cat wants to go dancing.

I'm seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Carl's lawyer traded the Gate back, and Bomo and me were part of the price, so now we live with the Royal Court. I have a new spell called Zerzura. Nobody explains it to me, and nobody has to.
I got inside that castle, stood still and finished the words. Zerzura took the whole castle, and everyone in it who wasn't hostile, down a floor with me.

entities.voiceNote: Short flat sentences, one thought each, nothing decorated. Says the plain hard thing and then stops talking. The Princess, Bomo, Carl, Louis, all by name and nothing more. Never complains about a job, never explains himself, never refuses the Princess anything.

beats.headline: Bought at the bar
beats.text: Two crawlers come up to the counter and buy security. Me and Bomo, sold as the pair. That is the arrangement in this place. You pay, and we stand between you and whatever comes through the door. The cat is not what I expect. She orders a dirty Shirley in a bowl with extra cherries, drinks the whole thing, and then she wants dancing, so I do my version of the robot while she bops and twirls on my shoulders. Princess Donut. I let her.

beats.headline: A miss on his own shift
beats.text: A crawler goes for the Princess on my floor, on my shift, and I do not get there in time. Elle puts the second one down. Astrid comes to apologise in person, and I stand where I am and wait to hear what a miss like that costs a body like me. Carl does not ask for blood. He asks for me and Bomo, permanent and complimentary, the Royal Court's own security every time they walk in. So now I have a court.

beats.headline: A spell bought with my own money
beats.text: The Princess rides on my shoulder through the club now. As we cross the dance floor I cast a protection spell on the party, and everyone glows blue. I bought it with my own money. Bomo tells Carl so, which is the longest sentence anyone has heard from Bomo. The Princess says thank you, Sledgie, and pats my head. The Dodge room will not let Carl in. It lets me in with her. Carl waits at the bar.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Carl's lawyer trades the Gate of the Feral Gods back, and I am part of what he gets for it. Four of us, free of charge: me, Bomo, Clay-ton, Very Sullen. Two spells on top, one for Bomo and one for me, copies of what the artifact could do. Bomo gets the jump to the stairwell. I get Zerzura. Nobody explains Zerzura to me. Nobody has to.

beats.headline: Two copies and a bomb
beats.text: The Princess casts on me and there are three of us. The two copies go into the saferoom, one after the other. The first hits the trap and lands outside among the hunters, and it explodes there. The second carries the fake cat to Lucia. I wheel the bomb to the door, like Carl said, and stand there. Two mantises run at us. Carl kicks the bomb out and slams the door.

beats.headline: Grand Theft Auto
beats.text: Carl rigged up a television. Grand Theft Auto. Bomo and me play it all the time. A changeling kid sits on my lap. I show him how to steal a car. Carl tells Mordecai we are why the kids stay in the room.

beats.headline: Mantises at the tunnel
beats.text: Mantises. Lots of mantises. Everywhere. They keep coming, flying in. We have to fight them. Carl says get in the tunnels, try not to fight, get the changelings through that door. Too many. We get picked up by airship. We go in from above instead. Carl says be careful of the sentinel towers, use the bombs on them if I have to, and drop none on the main castle. Louis says tell Skarn to moor the ship to the tower.

beats.headline: Surviving is winning
beats.text: Louis is worried about how it is going. Whether the plan holds, how it looks, who comes out on top of it. Surviving is winning, Louis. Everything else is bullshit. Then the changelings and me go into that castle, through a turret and the elf inside it, which is the thing everyone outside said could not be done.

beats.headline: No let Bomo beat my Frogger score
beats.text: Carl says do it. Casting now. One minute to chant, five minutes to cast. He says I am inside the castle, so I go to the ninth floor with everyone else, the cat too, and to watch him. I will feel sick for a full day. He thanks me for doing this and for taking care of the Princess. No let Bomo beat my Frogger score. He says he will unplug the machine the moment they get back. Good.

beats.headline: He finishes casting Zerzura
beats.text: The battle is everywhere and my job is to stand still and finish the words. So I stand still and finish the words. The castle goes. The whole building and every NPC breathing inside it, taken out from under the people who thought they owned them. That is what the spell was for. I said I did not need it explained.

beats.headline: I made a difference?
beats.text: The Princess says goodbye. Best bodyguard anyone ever had. Maybe I see her again. Maybe I see Bomo. She no need bodyguard anymore. She says she will always need me. She headbutts me, and goes back to Carl. I start to cast. Zerzura. Five minutes. Rosetta says Shanty Town is in the glow. Twenty seconds, I say. I look at Carl. I made a difference? He says I did.

entities.name: Astrid

tagline.text: Astrid is a level-125 Bloodlust Sprite and the assistant manager of the Desperado Club. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo with her hair up in a severe bun, and she can make a heart beat fast enough to catch fire.
Astrid is dead, and the two dancers crying in the strip club are her sons. She spent years quietly keeping them off the record, and it was her own husband who ordered the contract on her.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. The System keeps the file on club management the way it keeps files on everything with a level: rank, class, capability, and what the record does not explain. Carl and Princess Donut are guests, Katia Grim is a contractor, and the club is the club.

beats.headline: The management apologises
beats.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, Cardiovascular Mage, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The Bloodlust Sprite is one of the rarest and deadliest things her kind produces, born holding magic over anything with a circulatory system, and the signature trick is a heart beating fast enough to catch fire. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo, her hair is up in a bun, and her voice is deeper than yours. A crawler makes an attempt on Princess Donut on club grounds and Astrid comes down to say sorry in person. The Royal Court walks out with permanent complimentary security. Establishments like this one do not hand out refunds. She handed one out.

beats.headline: Blood set to boil
beats.text: Assistant manager Astrid, level 125, Bloodlust Sprite, adept in cardiovascular magic, locates crawlers on the Hunting Grounds level where management has said they are not permitted. She does not open the door. She sets Crawler Carl's blood to boil through it and suggests he open it if he wishes to be allowed back into the club. The door is opened. His skin is bubbling and his health is falling. She was not trying to kill him. If she had been, he would already be dead.

beats.headline: A name on a slip of skin
beats.text: New entry in the file, and not one the subject would enjoy. The Night Wyrm has issued a guild job, owned by Crawler Katia Grim: kill Astrid, level 125 Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager of the Desperado Club and owner of the Naughty Boys Employment Agency. Proof of death required. The Wyrm's stated grievance is that she keeps its family in the ground and its blood dry. The contractor has enlisted Carl, whose tattoo lets him read the skin the job is written on. Saying the details out loud cancels the contract.

beats.headline: A contract on the management
beats.text: There is a job out on her, and Crawler Katia Grim has taken it. The preparation is thorough, which is the compliment: Samantha parked at the bar to make noise, Katia getting herself ready, Carl setting traps down the service corridor they expect the assistant manager to walk. Nobody in the building tells her. That is the arrangement everyone employed here works under, and she has known it longer than any of them.

beats.headline: She goes to meet the demon instead
beats.text: The distraction runs too hot, reaches the casino floor, and pulls Minge out of one of the doors to the Nothing. A minor feral demon on the premises during business hours. Astrid does not go anywhere near a service exit. She finds Carl, tells him she is releasing the Vorpals to put the thing down, and tells him to get everyone out. And while the floor empties she says two things: that she has children, and that her husband is the Night Wyrm.

beats.headline: The contract closes
beats.text: Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club, is dead, in the club kitchen. She had put herself between Crawler Carl and a troll that came through the door, which is loyalty to the wrong party. Crawler Carl then ripped off her wings, a crow with a child's skull for a head took her eyes, and Crawler Katia put a spike through her head. Before it, she asked Carl to tell her husband she had done it to keep them safe: him, and their children. Her last words were that she was almost done.

beats.headline: Whose mother she was
beats.text: Two of the dancers out of the Penis Parade are sitting in the strip club crying, and here is why. Damascus Steel and Anaconda are her sons. Everything an assistant manager's influence is worth had been spent quietly, for years, keeping those two off the record and out of anyone's way. Her husband ordered the contract. Damascus wants every dancer in the Parade hired on as a mercenary where it is safe, and after that he wants his father.

entities.name: Ghazi

tagline.text: They call me the Mad Dune Mage, and the sandcastle out on the dunes is mine.

I am a glass mage. I reached into the Nothing to ask Yarilo for one small thing, that the heroine of a stage play would love me, and something else answered instead. It tricked me and married me to the ooze.

entities.voiceNote: Self-pitying and grandiose in the same breath; a scholar's vocabulary spent dressing up a want. Explains himself at enormous length to anyone in the room and blames the thing he summoned for what he chose. Lika by name, always. Never says the word coward, never mentions the lie he told the College unless cornered, never asks after anybody else.

beats.headline: A truce, by letter
beats.text: Kane. Cease your hostilities. Your bombs do not harm me, but they are ruining the structure of the temple, weakening its wall, and surely even in your floating city you understand the danger if it collapses. So I propose a truce: you stop the bombing, and I won't end this world. I have the winding box. I have cracked its secret. I know how to open a portal, and I do not need your watches to throw this entire world into the void, which I will do before I allow that ghost to leave the temple. Think of your people. Of her. Stop.

beats.headline: What he wanted
beats.text: They come in through the fountain court, three of them and a dinosaur that shatters my Lika where she stands, and then they find me, so you may as well have all of it. Lika is a half-naiad trobairitz out of the stage plays they put on in the city. A bard cleric under a vow of celibacy, played by a different half-naiad every season, based on a minor deity, and not real. I know she is not real. I wanted Yarilo brought back out and asked to make her real, and to make her mine. I told the College of Magecraft I was studying the Gate of the Feral Gods for stable long-distance transport. What answered when I opened it was not Yarilo. It was something else that had learned to wear the name, and it is why this castle is what it is.

beats.headline: Married to the ooze
beats.text: She tricked me. That is the part I want written down. I asked for Lika and the thing married me to the ooze instead, and my wife is still down in my halls being exactly what she is. The doll in the fountain, the one with a soul sitting in it, that is the nearest thing to a real Lika this world ever managed. Carl knocks me flat and takes the winding box off me while I am out. I wake up with a headache and tell them everything anyway, because who else is there to tell.

beats.headline: Out of the castle, and no further
beats.text: Ghazi, human, level 43 glass mage, known across the quadrant as the Mad Dune Mage, is dead. The sand ooze went down, the sandcastle came in on itself, and Crawler Katia Grim carried him clear of it. She killed him in the open a moment after that, for the notes in his coat explaining how the artifact is worked. He went to sand. Carl and Princess Donut were still buried under the other end of the building and heard none of it.

entities.name: Henrik

tagline.text: Henrik looks like a regular level-30 camel who shows an ID at the town hall's back door. According to the gnome chained in the basement, he is really a changeling, and the one who has been torturing him.
Henrik, the changeling principal, has been dead for some time. His body was sitting on the bridge of a flooded submarine, with his watch, one piece of the Gate, still on him.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice: the file on a man who is not the man, kept flat and procedural because the impersonation is the only interesting entry in it. Wynne, Carl, Princess Donut by name. The System does not speculate about which of the two of them the town liked better.

beats.headline: The basement under the town hall
beats.text: Hump Town's town hall, and a good number of the Dromedarian guards are not Dromedarians. In the basement is Wynne, held as collateral, and Wynne is willing to say who has been working on him. Henrik: to look at, a regular level-30 camel who shows some sort of ID at the back door; underneath, a changeling. What he wants out of Wynne is a spell that will put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, and the method for getting it has been to drug him and come to him in borrowed faces, until the next dose may kill him. Crawlers from the subterranean quadrant appear at the boundary, and at Wynne's own begging one of them puts him down before any of it concludes.

beats.headline: He explains the collateral
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut sit down with Henrik, charmed, and he explains how collateral works here, which is the local economy in miniature: Wynne held against the truce with the gnomes, and an ambassador, Leon the Commissar, who comes to inspect and casts a spell to make sure the collateral has not been swapped for a changeling. The next inspection is due in two days. How the code between the two sides actually works, he does not volunteer, and nobody in the room expects him to.

beats.headline: The delegation to the gnomes
beats.text: The plan walks out of the hall in a line: Carl, Princess Donut, Firas, Louis, a reanimated Wynne, and a Henrik who is Katia Grim doing his voice, not very well. They meet Leon, the Gnome Negotiator, and present Wynne as a man in urgent need of healing. Princess Donut announces herself as the healer and asks for passage onto the Wasteland in exchange. Leon will take Wynne and the healer and nobody else; the cat will not go without her manservant.

beats.headline: The body in the submarine
beats.text: Henrik of Hump Town, changeling, is dead, and has been for some time. Katia Grim runs into the flooded submarine to get away from a sharktopus, and Carl finds the body already sitting in there with its piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods still on it. One magically linked pocket watch, recovered. Also on him: a note recording that Quetzalcoatlus can be put down with an electric shock. Whatever else he was doing, he was still working that problem right up to the finish of him.

entities.name: Hellik

tagline.text: Hellik is the red one in the sky. According to local lore, he chases his brother Taranis across it and catches him four hours before dark.

Hellik, the god of sun and life, is Emberus's twin, level 250, and the likeliest hand behind the death of Emberus's son. As an acolyte of Emberus, Carl may not use anything Hellik has blessed, and every worshipper of Hellik he kills pays double experience.

Hellik has turned up in person, banished Khepri on sight, and asked Carl to tell Emberus that he did not kill his son. For the god Carl has a standing quest to kill, he is a great deal more civil than expected.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. For most of the crawl this god is a red sun, a line on a quest log and a name on a hit list, so the page is the file rather than the man. Emberus is his brother, Carl is the acolyte, and the System declines to say which brother it believes.

beats.headline: The second quest
beats.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now, and the paperwork comes with a brother attached. Hellik: god of sun and life, Emberus's twin, level 250, said around the celestial floors to be quite obsessed with killing his own brothers, and the likeliest hand behind Geyrun's death even though he was sitting in council with Emberus when it happened. Two quests arrive together with the acolyte's package. Find Out Who Killed My Son. Kill Hellik. The second one has a deadline attached and it is the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: The terms of a family feud
beats.text: What a god's grudge looks like when it is applied to one crawler. No magical item blessed by Hellik may be owned or used, so a whole category of loot is now dead weight. Every shrine of his is marked on the minimap. Every one of his adherents carries a symbol over their head and pays double experience when put down.

beats.headline: A temple in the Ursine town
beats.text: Temple of Hellik: a red diamond at the edge of Crawler Carl's map, in the large Ursine settlement across the bridge. Hellik is the brother and the enemy of Emberus, whom Carl worships. Carl holds a quest to kill this god, and is told he earns a bonus for every worshipper of Hellik he kills. There is no temple of Emberus in the town. He has declined to wade into that particular pool today. He has way too much else to deal with.

beats.headline: It stops being paperwork
beats.text: NPCs who worship Hellik now go hostile toward Carl the moment they see him, no provocation and no conversation required. Inside Club Vanquisher the clerics stand in front of a stained glass door they will tell you shows Hellik bringing truth to Apito, whatever that is supposed to mean. It does not show Hellik at all. It shows the brother above him, and the clerics have had that door wrong for centuries.

beats.headline: He turns up in person
beats.text: The temple goes up, the portal starts letting gods through into Club Vanquisher, and Khepri comes out with the rest of them. Hellik banishes him on sight, in front of everyone. Then he turns to Carl with a message for his brother: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Carl has been told about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is the hand behind all of it. He asks for an alliance. The quest to kill him is still open in Carl's log while he says it.

beats.headline: The clock on the order
beats.text: Quemada worships Emberus too, and Quemada's professional opinion is that the standing order cannot sit unattended much longer. They need to make an attempt on Hellik, and soon. Nobody in that conversation raises what Hellik said in the club.

entities.name: Quetzalcoatlus

tagline.text: Quetzalcoatlus is a name spoken by a chained gnome, who is being tortured for a spell that would give her flesh. She has no body, and that is the whole problem for everyone who wants something from her.

Quetzalcoatlus, the wailing shrieker who guarded the tomb, could be killed with lightning. Morris went down the ladder to connect the panel, knowing what the next strike would do to anyone in the water, and every crawler from that quadrant is now dead.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a guardian mob with no recorded conversation, so the file is what there is: what she is, what she can do, what people are prepared to do to a man in order to get it, and the four ways of putting her down.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.

beats.headline: An empress in the walls
beats.text: Per Morris Sp of the subterranean quadrant: Anser was an emperor, and when he died, his court and his wife were sealed into the tomb with him, alive. The wife is Quetzalcoatlus. She is undead now, non-corporeal, able to pass through the tomb's walls, and she can be heard screaming, like a bird. Having failed the map quest, the tomb crawlers received a new one: find her and kill her. Nobody knows how to kill a ghost. Morris observes that she would probably be easier to kill with a body.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: What the council is afraid of
beats.text: A letter from the council of Ghazi's college sets out the fear. What he summoned was not the god of lust but a banished lesser deity pretending to be him, and the scholars believe she only half crossed over. She will occupy the one creature nearby that stands equally between worlds: the ghost queen of the necropolis. If Quetzalcoatlus gains corporeal form, that deity is fully resurrected and the true gods are forced to react. The council's instruction is that Ghazi use the winding box to banish himself, and the entire necropolis, out of this world.

beats.headline: Out of her tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is not confined to her tomb. She is on the flooded submarine's bridge, flickering between it and the chamber on the far side of the hull, and she does not like visitors. Her scream is an aural attack: one shriek through the bulkhead reddens Crawler Carl's vision and drops Vadim Zbar into the red. Then she shoots out of the side of the sub, strikes something enormous in the water below, and flies back toward the temple. The thing she struck comes for the sub.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.

beats.headline: The panel in the tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is finished. Morris Sp went down the ladder to the submerged panel knowing what the next lightning strike would do to anyone still in the water, connected it, and the current did precisely what the cleric's journal said it would. The Subterranean Quadrant is liberated and the bubble pops. The notice hails Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi and Morris Sp, and then remembers that every crawler who started in that quadrant is dead. They were dealt one of the worst hands on the floor, and they finished the job anyway.

beats.headline: Same kind of mob, in the flesh
beats.text: The boss that knocks Carl out of the sky over the forest is the same type of mob as Quetzalcoatlus, the pterodactyl-like ghost of the previous floor. Carl recognises the shape before he reads the name. This one is not a ghost, but it is still undead: a vampire in the flesh, like a pelican crossed with a vulture and the size of a flying giraffe, with a beak as long as Carl is tall.

entities.name: Big Tina

tagline.text: Big Tina is a level-80 allosaurus and an immortalized city boss who wears a pink feather boa, and the attacks on Point Mongo have been hers from the beginning.

Big Tina was an eight-year-old ursine girl, the best dancer in her class, whose solo at a secret recital never happened. Scolopendra's attack turned her into a dinosaur, and now she is a vampire as well.

Big Tina never wanted a recital. She wanted her mother, and her mother was Kiwi, who had been beside her all along. When Princess Donut turned Kiwi back into an ursine, Tina knew her at once, and the quest closed on the spot.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a city boss with no speech in the record, and the file the AI keeps on her is the only place her side of it exists at all. Kiwi is her mother, the recital is the wound, and the System reports the rage without recommending anyone go and test it.

beats.headline: The quest gets a name
beats.text: Samantha goes across the water to look at the far shore and finds the team over there dead. All of them, and all of them by one thing. The Recital quest updates with the name it has been withholding. Big Tina. Allosaurus, level 80, immortalized city boss, and the attacks on Point Mongo have been hers from the beginning.

beats.headline: Prepotente Town #4
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut take two more towns and arrive at a third to claim it. There is not much left of the third. She has already been through it, and there is a pattern to which places she visits that nobody has sat down and read yet.

beats.headline: What she actually wants
beats.text: The party goes back into the town for Miriam and finds Big Tina standing in it again, and this time the shape of the thing comes clear. The dinosaurs of the Hunting Grounds were ursine before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack turned them into what they are. Tina was a child when it happened. What she wants, under all of it, is to dance at a recital, because hers was stopped before her turn came. She is also a vampire now, and she is building undead out of what she brings down.

beats.headline: The pile down the street
beats.text: Big Tina has not been idle in the street. She has been calling the two-day-dead to her, and other dinosaurs have been hauling body parts in from the whole forest into a heap like a sorting facility, where the fragments crawl about finding their matches. Levels add as the pieces rejoin, and at seventy percent of the whole a body becomes something quite deadly. One fragment has reached level 42 at 21.8%. Carl sets missiles on the pile and leaves. She roars. She does not follow.

beats.headline: She is brought in, and does nothing
beats.text: The dinosaur squad comes back to Carl and Princess Donut with Big Tina walking in behind them, and everybody in the clearing braces for the obvious. The obvious does not happen. Kiwi puts herself between the boss and the crawlers, and Tina stops. Nobody present can yet say why that works.

beats.headline: The dot turns white
beats.text: Tina gives up on eating the party and wanders off howling, half the pack behind her. She comes back into the light of Princess Donut's spell, head low, and tries to hide behind a tree like a shy child. Kiwi walks over, grunts at Mongo to come too, and he creeps up with Princess Donut on his back, head to the ground. Tina sniffs at him from a distance while her mother stands between them squawking. Her dot blinks from red to white.

beats.headline: Her mother has been there all along
beats.text: Everyone on the Hunting Grounds who knows Tina's story knows what she wants, Signet tells Carl, and it is not to dance in a recital. She wants her mother back. Carl says her mother is Kiwi, the mongoliensis. Signet agrees. Tina's mind is gone, and she does not realise that the other dinosaur has been there the whole time. She already has what she wants; she only needs to see it. What Carl has planned for tonight is close, Signet says, but not quite right.

beats.headline: The recital, finally
beats.text: In the middle of the battle Princess Donut puts the I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi, and the pack leader is not a mongoliensis any more. An ursine stands there, naked but for the paper bubbles. Tina looks at her and knows her, and the Recital quest closes on the spot. It was never a quest about a monster. Nobody reading the log had any way of knowing that.

beats.headline: Out again, in a tutu
beats.text: Carl adds his strength to the fortress's oversized, badly hammered door, and it flies all the way open and throws him and Tipid to the ground. Someone shouts that she is out again. Big Tina, allosaurus, wearing a pink tutu, stamps into the clearing and hops up and down in front of Mongo, waving her little wand. Mongo hops up and down in front of her too.

beats.headline: Her mother says no
beats.text: Carl sends for Tina and her mother refuses. Too dangerous, Kiwi says; she's just a child, and Carl has just ordered the gnome and the changeling children out of the battle, so why is Tina different? Carl writes an order overriding her, looks at it, and deletes it, and decides it is Kiwi's call. Donut does not. GET TINA OUT HERE RIGHT NOW, in the warlord chat, and before Kiwi can answer the doors fly open and Tina comes out screeching with glee, waving her wand, and starts eating the invisible enemies.

beats.headline: Too big for the saferoom doors
beats.text: She came out of the ball and went straight to work: a fire lance tower taken out single-handed, and dozens of crawlers kept from burning alive, her ever-repairing feather boa black and scorched for it. Now she stands on a pile of rocks waving her wand at her mother. Kiwi, heavily pregnant, has come from the FUPA to take her back. Florin doubts it. She is too big for the saferoom doors down here, and the stairs are blown out. Mongo bounces in circles around her.

entities.name: Kiwi

tagline.text: Kiwi is a level-60 mongoliensis and the leader of an all-female raptor pack, the fastest and cleverest predators in this jungle.
Kiwi led the fastest pack on the floor until Princess Donut's potion turned her back into an ursine. Big Tina looked at her and knew her mother's face.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A pack leader with no speech in the record, described the way the AI describes a mob it privately admires: raptor first, mother second, and the second one only once the record supports it. Mongo is the other dinosaur in the story and the System is not going to be delicate about that.

beats.headline: Mongo runs off
beats.text: Mongo bolts with Princess Donut still on his back and runs a pack of dinosaurs to ground. Kiwi is at the head of it. Level 60 mongoliensis, the fastest and cleverest predators anywhere in this jungle, and the whole pack is female, as is every dinosaur anyone has counted in the area. Which is odd. Odder still: dinosaur-class mobs did not exist on this ground before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, and here they all are. Mongo and Kiwi settle the introductions between themselves, at length, with Princess Donut obliged to watch.

beats.headline: White for the cat
beats.text: Kiwi and a few dozen of her pack stand at the edge of the woods outside Point Mongo, looking in. Their dots have turned white for Crawler Princess Donut. Kiwi's is still red for Crawler Carl. Deeper in the trees stands something much bigger that was not there before; it waits, then turns and moves away. Kiwi calls unk, unk, unk once more and the pack melts back into the jungle. Mongo has already stumbled back into town, collapsed in the street with his health full, and gone into his carrier without objection.

beats.headline: Tina's mother, by name
beats.text: A barmaid hiding from Big Tina gives the record its missing line. Tina's mother survived the nine-tier attack in the form of a dinosaur, along with several of the other mothers from the night of the recital; they kill too, but they are not as deranged. She still tries to keep Tina from doing too much damage. In the past few nights she has stopped being able to. Her name is Kiwi. Carl informs Mongo of the implications. Princess Donut gasps.

beats.headline: Charmed, and an escort
beats.text: Kiwi brings the pack in and Princess Donut charms her with a potion, and the fastest thing on the floor becomes an escort service. Carl works out at the same time that The Plenty arranged this entire chain of events, and that what it wanted out of the arrangement was its precious Prepotente protected.

beats.headline: She keeps pulling east
beats.text: Minion Kiwi obeys Princess Donut, broadly. On the road southeast she veers the party east every half hour until corrected. Halfway there she lifts her head and howls, and the whole pack of thirty-odd raptors vanishes into the trees, sent to look after Big Tina. Left with three companions, she eats constrictors dropping out of the trees faster than anyone else can move. When the rhinoceros's rider fires at Mongo, she leaps at the litter, bounces off its shield and lands on fire.

beats.headline: She stands in front of a city boss
beats.text: The squad comes back to the crawlers with Big Tina walking in behind it. Big Tina is an immortalized city boss and everyone in the clearing understands exactly what that means for the next few seconds. Kiwi steps in front of her. Tina does not attack. Nobody yet has an explanation for it that they would put in writing.

beats.headline: Taken all the way back
beats.text: Mongo and Kiwi bring Vrah down together in the middle of the castle battle, which is a sentence worth reading twice. Then Princess Donut uses the I Take It All Back potion on her, and the mongoliensis is gone. An ursine stands in the wreckage, naked but for paper bubbles, and Big Tina looks across at her and knows her mother's face.

beats.headline: Still pregnant, and family
beats.text: Kiwi is very pregnant and has been carrying since the Hunting Grounds, which is a long time to be in that condition even by this dungeon's standards. Big Tina, for her part, has decided that Mongo is her father. Nobody in the fortress has the standing, the courage, or frankly the desire to correct her.

beats.headline: Where is my daughter
beats.text: Status report during the Bear Witness event, taken from the chat. Subject asked for Tina. Where is Tina? Where is her daughter? Colonel Tipid answered: Tina had got out and was fighting outside the stronghold, and he could see her, and she was frozen. Anyone outside a structure was. Then the witnesses were brought forth, straight up into the air.

beats.headline: Twins, and legendary
beats.text: Kiwi's water broke while she was arguing about getting Big Tina back into the FUPA. In the medical tent she asks for Mongo, and he is brought to her side; in ursine culture, Edgar says, the father's presence lends the newborn his strength. Two girls. They are not bears and not raptors: four legs, stubs of wings, wet brown fur, Mongo's head, bulbous eyes that do not match. Newborn Ursensus, level 0, Legendary Creature, part raptor, part bear, part Scolopendra magic. Too intelligent to be used as pets.

entities.name: Edgar

tagline.text: Edgar is a talking tortoise in Signet's company, and Princess Donut has already found him and is chatting away.
Edgar is the tortoise who gives Signet her tattoos. He works from the bodies of the dead, and what he puts on her skin comes back off it to fight.
Edgar can sit well outside a building and tell you exactly what is moving around inside it.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A tortoise with a specialist's skill set and almost nothing on the record in his own words, so the file lists the services instead: ink, reconnaissance, surgery. Signet's family, Carl's plan, Princess Donut's tattoo. The System does not make the obvious tortoise joke more than once.

beats.headline: The ink comes from the body
beats.text: Edgar is a tortoise. Edgar is also the reason Signet's tattoos are what they are, and the method is not squeamish: he works from the corpse. Miss Nadine, dead, goes onto Signet's skin as ink and comes back off it as something that moves and fights. Miss Nadine's attachment to Clint drags Clint along with her, so he turns up on the skin as well, unasked and unbilled. Nobody in the party looks surprised. There is apparently a queue for this.

beats.headline: He maps the castle from outside it
beats.text: Ahead of the castle job Edgar sits well back from the building and maps the whole of it from where he is. Every room, every level, and a set of small connecting tunnels that fit nothing anyone can name. Louis is the one who works out what they are for. They are Ferdinand's, so that he can move around his own house without ever using a door.

beats.headline: Sense Movement, level fifteen
beats.text: Rosetta has a theory about how Vinata keeps getting into Club Vanquisher, and Edgar is the instrument that settles it. He senses the non-corporeal moving through the castle. He also picks up upward momentum coming off the ground, which is what it looks like from below when somebody nearby worships a god for the first time.

beats.headline: A tattoo for the cat
beats.text: Rosetta, Milk and Edgar come up into the tower to work on Princess Donut. She is getting a tattoo, and given who does the ink around here, a tattoo is not decoration. It is a thing that will get up off her and fight when she calls it.

beats.headline: Surgery, on a clock
beats.text: Sixty-five minutes on the floor and every member of the party has a job. Edgar's job is surgery. He and Mordecai operate on Louis while the rest of it goes on above them, and nobody has told the tortoise how long he has.

entities.name: King Rust

tagline.text: I have just arrived in this planet's orbit, and I have nothing to say about my son's show. My spokesman has asked the galaxy to stop calling the prince names, and the galaxy has not stopped.
I am King of the Skull Empire. My army stands outside your walls, and I have asked for a formal parley with the crawler and his cat. Read nothing into that yet.

My daughter Formidable has taken one of my warships and told the Syndicate that she means to trip the Failsafe by hand. And so here I am, a king, weeping in front of an enemy and asking a crawler for help.

entities.voiceNote: A king accustomed to being obeyed who has just stopped being obeyed. Formal, blunt, ceremonial when ceremony serves him; the grief comes through the formality rather than around it. Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, my daughter, my empire. Never begs, never says please, never acknowledges how far the crying has already gone.

beats.headline: The army arrives, and asks to talk
beats.text: My army comes onto the field in good order, the way it has come onto every field for as long as there has been a Skull Empire. The crawlers seal their safe room against us, because they have learned what that doggy door of theirs is worth to an enemy. Fine. Let them shut it. I did not bring an army all this way to go through a door. I request an official parlay with Crawler Carl and Princess Donut, in the correct form, in front of every camera pointed at this floor.

beats.headline: The cat sees it first
beats.text: Baroness Victory reads out the rules of a parlay and each of us stands where we are told to stand. Deng Bao is at my shoulder, a Grixist, as an adjutant ought to be. Carl and the cat come out under the bubble and look at me, and the cat has it before a single word is spoken. I am crying. I have been a king a very long time and I have never once done this in front of an enemy.

beats.headline: What his daughter has done
beats.text: My daughter Formidable has commandeered one of my warships. She has announced to the Syndicate, openly, that she intends to trip the Failsafe by hand to keep the rogue thing on this planet out of the center system. And she told them the rest of it while she was at it: that my empire has been manufacturing their security systems with our own doors left quietly in the back of them. So here it is. I ask a crawler to send my daughter a message on behalf of the people of Earth, and I offer to pull my forces off this floor in exchange. Carl takes the deal.

beats.headline: Walking back to his own line
beats.text: King Rust of the Skull Empire is dead. The agreement was made and he turned to walk back to his own army, and Rosetta Thagra came out of where she had been waiting and took him, for reasons entirely her own and nothing whatever to do with the deal. Five full seconds of stunned silence passed, and then his army surged forward. His ring and his retina went onto a data pad in Rosetta's hands, and Carl pulled the body into his inventory.

entities.name: D'nadia

tagline.text: I am a princess of the Prism Kingdom, and I am sitting on Ripper Wonton's panel beside the crawler and his cat. The Skull Empire fired at those two, and the shot took my friend Manasa instead, and I will say on air exactly what I think of that.

I am Empress now, and I am judging tonight's talent show and pet contest. The crawler and his attorney very nearly ruined my buy-in bid, and I am here regardless, which makes me part of the production.
I have sold my sponsorship of Princess Donut. It is not appropriate to sponsor a crawler I may have to fight, and it paid well. Do not look at me like that; it is trade.
I am warlord of the Prism clan, and there is a crawler and a cat inside my castle. Everything I have done, I have done for my people.

entities.voiceNote: Warm, physically demonstrative, and blunt to the point of rudeness; trumpets through her facial tentacles when amused. Says 'the Prism Kingdom' in full whenever she is being official, which is often. Treats affection and trade as the same activity and has never noticed the difference. Never raises her voice at anyone she considers beneath answering.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: Empress, judging the pet contest
beats.text: The ball, and I am judging the talent show and the pet contest both. Chaco is running the prize counter. I find the crawler in the crowd and tell him the truth of it: he and his attorney very nearly ruined my buy-in bid, and here I am regardless, judging, which makes me production.

beats.headline: What she tells the elite
beats.text: The half-naiad sits with the judges for most of the evening deep in conversation, and I tell her a great deal. The whole universe has been looking forward to this party. More people than there are stars in the sky are watching. The deity is under the control of that bug's mother, who sold half of everything she owns to get here. Her own mother was never real; nor were her friends. And I am sad Carl won't survive the night. I was looking forward to meeting him on the battlefield outside Larracos.

beats.headline: One of the two places
beats.text: Two places in the ninth floor's war came up at once. One of them is mine: the Prism Kingdom's, bought in my own name where anybody watching could watch me do it. The other went to a brand-new non-profit corporation. I know exactly whose that is.

beats.headline: Empress, and free for dinner
beats.text: I have just onboarded onto the playing field as warlord of the Prism Kingdom Clan, and Donut calls me Princess before correcting herself to Empress, which is right. I tell her I really liked her song the other night and I am sorry they kicked us out before the festivities really started. When it is my turn I introduce myself properly and tell the table that if anyone wants to catch a meal, I am available. A few restaurants in Larracos have finally opened back up. The naga says that is not advisable.

beats.headline: The sponsorship changes hands
