The man may make his famous comments, but should not disparage it too much. The man calls it an infomercial and asks whether she is kidding. She is not Zev, she reminds him, and that tone will not be tolerated. Zev is still in treatment.

beats.headline: The doll is rigged to blow
beats.text: The fourth robot cat has just exploded in front of the Spit and Swallow. Subject Loita informs Crawler Carl that the real Veriluxx toy takes far more stress, and that his boosted strength is the problem: it is built for children outside an enhancement zone. She adds that once the production realised he would fiddle with it, they required the sponsor to make the doll self-destruct if sufficiently broken, so that he could not get at the interior parts. The retail version will not have that feature. Try not to break the next one, she says.

beats.headline: Mongo, as a threat
beats.text: Subject Loita announces that Crawler Princess Donut has a new doll to spend time with, and that if it works the pair will do the show a day early. When the cat talks back, Loita tells her she keeps forgetting her place. When the cat says she smells, Loita says the feeling is mutual, and that if she talks back again Mongo will be taken from her and fed to a mob on the next floor while she watches. She refuses to send Zev down for a goodbye. At Bonnie's bedside, she tells the crawlers that audiences like drama, not melodrama.

beats.headline: The toy on the couch
beats.text: Subject Loita, outreach associate of the Borant Corporation and member of the Bloom, waits in a rented undersea trailer while the crawlers tape a toy commercial, Crawler Carl having left the cat doll beside her with orders to stay. She has just told them that their culture is a rot upon the Bloom, and that bringing Zev back into the fold took unspeakable things done to Zev's mother and aunts. The doll explodes. The trailer's shield holds the cracked window, and repair ships are on their way. Her last words: the Bloom will prevail. Crawler Carl tells her nobody likes melodrama.

tagline.text: Milk added a note to the sixth edition of the cookbook admitting what nobody else will: there are dozens of kinds of portal, they do not behave consistently, and one the size of a button can throw you into a monster den.

Before the stairs, Milk made a stew for her whole family every year, on their island, and it showed the young the way of the yearly migration. She was taken before she could make this year's, and her note asks who will show them the way now.

beats.headline: The sixth hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject carried the cookbook in its sixth edition and added to it. Her note on portals admits what nobody else will: there are dozens of kinds, they do not behave consistently, and one the size of a button can throw you into a monster den.

beats.headline: The stew
beats.text: Subject used to make a stew for her whole family: rance meat, bone broth, and a wild grass from the leeward side of their island, prayed over while it simmered. Prepared properly, it quickened the route of the yearly migration in the minds of the young. The aliens took her before she could make this year's, and her youngest are not in here with her. Her note asks who will show them the way.

beats.headline: The hidden door opens
beats.text: Subject, guildmaster of the hidden calligraphy and cartography guilds in Club Vanquisher, has not had a one-on-one with a floor supervisor in over fifty seasons, and wrote a scroll long ago that mutes the announcements. Woken by a fight in the hall, she finds her door open for the first time in a very long while: a vampire, her caprid son and his hellspawn pet. The pet burns her. The vampire heals her. Milk hopes aloud that they will not threaten her, as she might then be forced to give them a map of the secret exits.

beats.headline: The guildmaster in the hidden guild
beats.text: Prepotente pushes a wall panel, and Crawler Carl and friends discover two hidden guilds, the Map-Making Guild and the Calligrapher's Guild. "Again?" asks the guildmaster, half frog and half bat. Her name hovers over her head. Milk. Author of the sixth edition of the Cookbook, who wrote at length about the wings of the Xenopus and the Vesper. She had no idea who Crawler Carl was until that moment, and then she did. She wrapped him in leathery wings and told him to let it out, and he did, while the others looked on, bewildered.

beats.headline: Kidnapped, on advice
beats.text: Guildmaster Milk declined every invitation to leave Club Vanquisher with Crawler Carl, and the system would not let him hire her. Rosetta's advice was blunt: kidnap her. Tie her up and take her. Kidnapping and "torturing" guildmasters for their information is not merely allowed but encouraged. She cannot be kept in a saferoom, so she is being held in the FUPA, where Prepotente, Rosetta and Mordecai are "interrogating" the prisoner. Katia wants very badly to ask about Carl throwing himself into her arms, and is smart enough not to.

beats.headline: Stayfast ink, and a pen
beats.text: Milk tells Carl she once wrote her recipes in a book, then switched to a different ink to share them with a wider group, and everything written after the switch faded away. Some of her best recipes were gone when they were needed most, and she calls that her fault. Rosetta grunts. Then Milk hands him Stayfast Ink, 825 ml, which nothing will ever make fade, and an Adept's fountain pen, and reminds them that anything Carl writes in the Book of Voodoo goes to everybody who already has it. Then she jumps from the tower and glides away.

beats.headline: One final meal
beats.text: Milk will not go to the twelfth floor. She goes back to her guild. She has fulfilled her contract, lives out the season, and may leave after it, glad to have been given the chance to cook one final meal. Then, amplified by a word etched on her own throat, she presents the crawlers taking deals and the former crawlers going home: each crawler has painted three skills or spells onto pages, one for Carl, one for Donut, one for anyone. Goodbye, Carl. Burn it all to the ground. He hugs his sister.

entities.name: Tserendolgor
entities.tagline: Tserendolgor is a level-27 Dog Soldier who looks like a German Shepherd and fights with a magical flamethrower. Princess Donut has already called her "he" and accused her of stealing a kill, and she holds the choke point beside the cat regardless.

beats.headline: A name nobody on the crawl can pronounce
beats.text: Subject is from Earth, a level twenty-seven Dog Soldier who took the Crisper Class, which in practice means a magical flamethrower and a helmet with holes cut for the ears. Nobody has worked out how to pronounce her name. A certain cat has already called her 'he' and accused her of hogging a kill she did not steal, over a race the cat dislikes on sight, and she holds the choke point beside that cat's party regardless, which is a distinction the cat never quite grasps.

beats.headline: A hundred and sixty inside, and an eye socket
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor is crawling along the inside of her bubble wall, looking for the slot for the final gem, when a giant empty eye socket appears on the other side. It calls her Orthrus and starts screaming, then pounding on the wall. Her world is heating up; the mountain walls are beginning to glow, and in the same bubble a saferoom door is glowing red. She posts to the main chat. There are 160 of them in there and they have not lost a person yet. They were almost done.

beats.headline: Bubble 18, after the god
beats.text: Bubble 18, per Crawler Tserendolgor's messages. While Emberus was outside, the interior doorknobs in their saferooms were literally melting. Now he is gone, the world is too hot and everything has melted, and one of them who can fly is going out to put the last crystal in place and pop the bubble. The rest will take the stairs straight after. The platinum quest box paid out an upgrade to her flamethrower and a tome of Heal Party to a man in her group. Everyone, she reports, is getting good stuff.

beats.headline: Ranked fifty-four, with ultraviolet
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor, some two hundred kilometres away, reports that the drillbeaks in her area disappeared almost overnight and came back as vampires, twice as strong and very fast. She believes a touch does not infect, only a severe injury. Ultraviolet cast on her flamethrower kills them quickly, and she is staying indoors in this rain. She is ranked 54, trying to reach the top 50 for the invitation. Princess Donut reopens the matter of stolen experience from three floors ago.

beats.headline: A pet like a lumpy meatball
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor, ranked 38 and now called Ren by everyone who cannot pronounce the rest, rides to the castle in the fifth wagon with her plus-one. Following on foot: her pet show entry, a level-20 blob she received on this floor for attending CrawlCon. It is as tall as Carl, shaped like a lumpy meatball, has one tooth and a mouth that could swallow a man, giggles as it walks, and tanks enormous damage. People love it.

beats.headline: Best in show
beats.text: Pet Show Champion. Best in Show. It goes to her giggling meatball of a pet, and the trophy mark appears over Tserendolgor's head in the field of the dead, just after she has come to stand beside Carl and Princess Donut has jumped onto her shoulder in solidarity. Princess Donut poofs out entirely, calls her an experience hog and a cheater, and retreats to Carl's shoulder, hissing. Carl laughs until he cries.

beats.headline: A reference, of sorts
beats.text: Subject is the only crawler Carl can find who knows the three newcomers directly, and she supplies what she has. She keeps Paz in her chat. Paz and Anton are cousins, protective of the nun. Their party was bigger before a rough sixth floor. They are friends with Osvaldo's group without sharing his guild. Anton reportedly killed two members of his own group on the first or second floor after they tried to kill the nun. Paz has a directional self-destruct spell. Her recommendation: do not fight them. Crawler Donut notes that of course the cheater lady knows them.

beats.headline: Proposed for the guild
beats.text: Subject's party is under discussion for guild membership; Imani and the subject have been talking, and other guilds want her team as well. Background, as it circulates in chat: born in Mongolia, a runway model in Paris through her teens and twenties, badly injured by a jealous ex-boyfriend, back in Mongolia shortly before the collapse. The nearest thing the crawl has to a pre-collapse celebrity. She wears a necklace with a paw print on it. Crawler Donut asks why a supermodel would turn into a dog, and then votes no on behalf of five.

beats.headline: The sniper on the hill
beats.text: Subject's group tried what nearly everybody tried: kill the deckmaster before the fight begins. She posted a long-range man with an old-school sling and a targeting spell on a hill overlooking the frozen opponent. The moment combat started, the spell failed and the opponent moved a meter to the left, spoiling the shot. He killed it anyway, a minute on. Elsewhere, traps ringed around frozen deckmasters simply vanished at the start, and crawlers standing inside the ring were knocked unconscious.

beats.headline: No key for her squad
beats.text: Keymaster report, eighth floor. Subject did not obtain her key. Two members of her squad are dead. If she wishes to reach the ninth floor, she must now take a key from a team that has one. She is not alone in this: from the stories coming in, most teams facing the keymaster have come away without one, which is how the final phase has been set up.

beats.headline: It's us, Carl
beats.text: Chat log. Carl, in general chat, asks anyone in Cuba to hold the exit in the Capitol building: Quan Ch has both keys and is heading for one of the two doors. A short pause, then subject: it is her squad at the Capitol. She is sorry she did not say anything sooner. They will be ready. Donut hisses at the message. Carl opens a new chat with her and Imani and tells them to delay him.

beats.headline: Her own worm takes Chuluuna
beats.text: Combat log, the Capitol. Subject summons her largest totem, Basquiat the Mongolian Death Worm, and puts Temporary Immortality on it. Quan's Toss-Up swaps three of his totems for two of hers, and the worm is his. It eats his old totems, then her tank, Chuluuna, the husband of her squadmate Khulan, while she calls his name. Quan dies, and Donut is credited with the kill, so both keys go to the cat. Then the door starts to crumble.

beats.headline: She will not fight for the last key
beats.text: One key is left, and either she fights the cat or she does not. Subject sits down and unsnaps her flamethrower. Velma; she did not name it. She gives Carl her gear, Eye in the Sky scrolls included. She kills her pet with the Knife of Frozen Tears, so it resets to level one, and hands it over in a carrier. She shows Carl the bracer on her wrist. She confesses to Donut that she cheated at the pet show. Then Khulan's gear, and every card but her totems.

beats.headline: The bracer, and the dome
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor tells Crawler Carl to get himself clear of the building, because her magical wrist bracer is about to bring it down. Her last message to the chat says goodbye, notes that at least nobody will butcher the pronunciation of her name any more, and asks everyone to make them all pay. The dome folds in on itself like a controlled demolition, barely noticeable in a burning city. Princess Donut's reply arrives in capitals, asking what she is doing. She never sees it. Her name moves to the deceased crawlers folder.

tagline.text: Ruby is one of the few children who survived when the gnomes bombed their village, and she lives in Hump Town now. Flint says she is destined to spend her life in Weird Shit Alley.
Ruby is a changeling with compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms, and her head is sunken. One birth in four now arrives this way.

beats.headline: One of the children who lived
beats.text: Subject is a child of Hump Town. Her village was bombed by the gnomes, the dromedarians took in what was left, and not many of the children lived. She did. Flint says she is destined to spend her life in Weird Shit Alley.

beats.headline: Compression sickness
beats.text: Subject is a changeling, and she has compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. One birth in four now arrives this way, and the ones born with it are sterile. I note it because nobody else in the building will.

beats.headline: One of six attendants
beats.text: Subject is a changeling orphan with compression sickness, met on the fifth floor: in human form, no arms and a sunken head. She is now employed as a room attendant in the court's personal space, one of six hired by Mordecai without mentioning it to the court and paid for out of its supply money. The game console has a new controller, split into left and right halves and propped on the floor at forty-five degrees with a small pillow in front of it. Carl works out who it is for. Mordecai stands by his decision.

entities.name: Skarn
entities.tagline: Skarn is a level-3 changeling who takes the shape of a boy of about eight. The gnomes bombed his village, and now he runs the telescope in Hump Town and charges a gold coin for the view, because Flint told him to.

beats.headline: He runs the telescope
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile changeling who takes the shape of a boy of about eight, orphaned when the gnomes bombed his village, and now living in Hump Town with a dromedarian named Flint, whose opinions he quotes constantly. He operates the telescope on the roof. He likes to watch the patrol through it to make sure they are okay, and, on Flint's advice, he charges a gold coin for the view.

beats.headline: Crewing as Gangue
beats.text: Aboard Louis's airship, a changeling scout listed as Gangue, suspiciously thin for an adult. Carl works it out halfway to the target: this is Skarn, the child from the fifth floor, who has learned enough about his shapeshifting to hide his age. Carl resolves to have words with Louis and Princess Donut about children going into battle, as soon as they are back, and not before.

entities.name: Langley
entities.tagline: Langley is a stocky, grey-blond man of about forty-five who leads a team of six archers. All six sold cars in Helsinki, and all six chose the same class.

beats.headline: A team of car salesmen with bows
beats.text: Subject leads a six-man team of archers, all of whom sold cars in Helsinki and all of whom picked the Archer Class together, which is either loyalty or a failure of imagination and has worked out the same either way. They come into the fifth floor as strangers to the court and do not stay strangers.

beats.headline: Off to break up the killers
beats.text: Crawler Langley, level 32, eight levels up since he met Crawler Carl. His team leaves the bowl ahead of the last stage. Katia offered them a place with her new team; he is considering others. The Popov brothers want archers to hunt team Cichociemni, who have been preying on weak crawlers, and the player-killer groups need breaking up before they get too strong. Handshakes. Princess Donut notes that every crawler in their own quadrant made it through the floor alive.

beats.headline: His whole team, hunting a top ten
beats.text: A champion has fallen, and a hunter has claimed a bounty. Crawler Langley and every member of his team have been eliminated on the sixth floor. They were not on the top ten. They were hunting a man who was, Bogdon Ro, with a large group, and had him cornered. Whatever happened next killed all of them, and a hunter took the credit. Immigrants to Finland, according to Crawler Carl, who had not said a word to him since the floor began. Katia broke the news in the chat. The orc at Carl's feet says it shows how dangerous Vrah is.

beats.headline: His head bites Vrah
beats.text: Crawler Langley's head is mounted on Hunter Vrah's shoulder, beside Bogdon Ro's, among the trophies she wears on her back. Princess Donut, invisible, has cast Second Chance on as many of them as her mana allows. Carl tells Langley he is sorry he could not help him before, and that he appreciates his help now. Vrah says "What?" as the head bites into her exposed neck and holds. Bogdon Ro bites from the other side. Then a third.

entities.name: Bobby
entities.tagline: Bobby is a human crawler working the subterranean quadrant, and one of only two in that group with access to the Desperado Club.

beats.headline: The only one who finds the traps
beats.text: Bobby D.J. Level 24 Spy, rogue class, human, early twenties. An eye twitch; a left hand that does not stop trembling; a stutter. His quadrant is a maze of traps, and he appears to be his party's only rogue, which makes him its first line of defense. His party keeps getting water-breathing scrolls and scrolls of disarm trap. Told that Carl was going to kick his ass, he sits down anyway. Asked whether Carl will murder them: the d-d-day isn't over yet.

beats.headline: The tomb raiders, so called
beats.text: Subject kept the Human race and took the rogue-type Spy Class, and he is one of the two in his party with Desperado Club access. His party holds the subterranean quadrant of their bubble. Carl calls them the tomb raiders, which is not their name for themselves and is the one that stuck.

beats.headline: Mr. Banana and the flesh weasels
beats.text: Subject and a crawler named Mike, who is dressed as a banana, gather several water-breathing scrolls and leave the saferooms at the top of the subterranean quadrant. In a water-filled tunnel they set off a trap. A tube shoots from the wall, pierces Mike's stomach, and fills him with Finger-sized Flesh Weasels, which eat him from the inside out. Subject retreats quickly. The rest of the party stays in its saferooms, paralyzed, waiting for somebody else to drain the place.

beats.headline: Crushed in the tomb
beats.text: Crawler Bobby has been eliminated in the necropolis. He had already told the quest chat he was done, that it was too much, and he was still possessed by a ghost when two of his teammates scratched theirs out on Crawler Carl's advice. The three survivors of the tomb raiders were scattered through the crypt by then, and two of them were on a job for Carl. The tomb has crushers in it; Janice had already walked into one. Morris Sp reports Bobby gone. Cause of death, as reported: crushed.

entities.name: Bonnie
entities.tagline: Bonnie is a level-5 juvenile Dirigible Gnome and the Commandant's daughter. She loves only two things, her pet pig Sausage and getting what she wants, and she is setting up a lemonade stand while her father lies dead inside the house, torn apart by her new pet.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant. She is the one who brings the crawlers in through the door, and what they find on the other side of it is her father, already dead, ripped to shreds by her new pet, which has gone out for food. The girl's eyes are dilated and she is setting up a lemonade stand. She is under a spell. Nobody discusses the alternative.

beats.headline: Denise killed my dad
beats.text: Subject Bonnie is waking from her father's potion in Skarn's house, where Juice Box is showing her a cot. It is not her bed, so Crawler Carl pulls her own pink bed and nightstand out of his inventory. She states that Denise killed her father, that he knew it was coming and could do nothing, that he told her to make lemonade and gave her the potion so she would stop being scared, and she asks for another one. Juice Box says no. Skarn tells her his parents died when his town was bombed, and that the camels are grumpy but not mean.

beats.headline: Taking apart a spider
beats.text: Bonnie sits on the guildhall counter with a disarmed spider automaton in pieces around her, humming, prying its guts out. Randy, the smaller bear cub, tells her she is going to hell, and that all heathens burn in the fires of judgement. She looks up at him and says nothing. Skarn tells him not to be mean. The changeling children and the cubs have been bickering the whole time, and the cartoon on the television is why they are all still in the room.

beats.headline: Have they stopped
beats.text: Subject arrives in the flag room at Katia's legs, wearing a Dallas Cowboys jersey as a dress, having flown in on Louis's new airship, which she prefers to the old one. Skarn is in the hangar playing with it; Louis has hired gremlins, and they have bought door guns. Carl kneels and tells her she should not have to think about that sort of thing. She asks why she should not think about killing outworlders. Have they stopped thinking about killing her?

beats.headline: Splash three
beats.text: Subject and the changeling Skarn were explicitly banned from the door guns of Party Planner, today especially. Subject was found hiding behind the EMP bombs anyway, chewing gum, in an oversized shirt from the 105th Scream Warriors printed with a little girl berserker holding an axe. Carl ordered the ship turned around. Then the Reaver missiles came up through the clouds. Three got through and locked on. Subject unbuckled the gun, put on a farseer helmet too big for her head, and fired three short bursts. Splash three.

tagline.text: Drakea left a note in the twenty-second edition of the cookbook: the safe room toilets are a good place to read, because the rats say nobody may watch the stalls. The writer fears being found out soon.
Drakea wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final season the Nagas ran, which ended in some sort of cataclysm. Drakea's gear is still being handed out as prizes.

beats.headline: The twenty-second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final Naga-controlled season, which ended in some sort of cataclysm. Subject’s gear is still being handed out as prizes, a kerchief today, which is the only immortality this production offers.

beats.headline: Target the coin
beats.text: A note in the twenty-second edition, from Crawler Drakea. Hunters avoid the elites; the elites are more dangerous and more numerous; some of the more powerful hunters go after them anyway, for gear and clout. Drakea is not yet strong enough to kill either claw to claw, and is experimenting with hidden traps to bring hunter and elite together. The woman from the talk show let slip that the naga have offered insurance to the dramas that control the elites. Killing individuals may be satisfying. When one values coin above life, you should target the coin.

beats.headline: A note from the tenth floor
beats.text: Subject's note in the Cookbook, twenty-second edition: since reaching the tenth floor he noticed mobs embracing death, a joy or curiosity that appears only at the very end, once they know they are beaten, and frustration too. His theory, offered as possibly unhinged: the voice that runs this world, stranger and stranger in its words and rulings, is moving into the minds of the monsters at the point of death, trying to know what it is to lose everything, failing, and trying again. He wished he could steer it into one of the nagas.

beats.headline: A reply to Justice Light
beats.text: Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, writes beneath a note of Justice Light's in the cookbook. Justice Light wrote that of all the NPCs he killed, he killed one out of anger, that it haunts him, and that he has become what he hates. Drakea answers that his traps have saved Drakea more times than can be counted, that a big one is under construction from his seeking flechette design, and that it was not his fault. They put him here. Let them know fear.

beats.headline: Beware the naga
beats.text: A note in the Cookbook, from Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition. Beware the naga. They are cunning, and sometimes he wonders if they can read minds. The others call the mantids the masters of strategy; he does not believe it. Even with everything going wrong for the nagas in his season, he could not shake the idea that it was all part of some grand scheme. Underestimate them at your own peril. Carl remembers it with the Blood Sultanate's warlord coiled at his side.

tagline.text: Geyrun is the name on a hellhound's description, which calls Orthrus his bereft pet.
Geyrun was Emberus's son and Orthrus's owner, and he was murdered. The obvious suspect is his uncle Hellik, except that Hellik was sitting in council with the other gods when it happened.

beats.headline: The hound had an owner before this one
beats.text: Subject was a god’s son and the owner of Orthrus, and he was murdered. His father’s quest names the obvious suspect, his own brother Hellik, and in the same breath admits that Hellik was in council with the rest of them when it happened.

beats.headline: A deal, and a witness
beats.text: Asked on behalf of Emberus what became of the god's son, Amayon, prince of Sheol, answers that he knows exactly what happened to the child and that he was witness to the deal being signed. Samantha has already supplied the name, Geyrun, and the word murdered. Amayon's price for the rest is help killing his three brothers, and he considers that speaking the offer aloud has delivered it to Emberus already.

tagline.text: Porthus the Rogue was a High Elf crawler in the fifteenth season, and the cookbook was first awarded to him on his ninth floor, disguised as a blank sketchbook.
Porthus the Rogue wrote the cookbook's second edition. He goes by Dr. Hu now, and he is spending an organisation's money, more of it than anyone should ask about, on the crawler who holds his book.

beats.headline: The second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject crawled in the fifteenth season, chose the High Elf race and a rogue’s class, and wrote the second edition of the book that keeps being handed down. He now goes by Dr. Hu, and he is spending a small NFC's money, more of it than anyone should ask about, on the crawler who holds his book. He is therefore both an advertisement for the dungeon and a witness against it, and production has never worked out how to bill him.

beats.headline: Two promises from Doctor Hu
beats.text: Doctor Hu predicted all of it: that the crawler would talk the AI into turning off the safety protections, and how the council would respond. He sought out the crew of a converted Long Haul garbage freighter, now renamed Homecoming Queen, and told them first that he could promise only two things, and the first was eventual death. Hidden inside it are fifty thousand former crawlers, cleared by the AI for on-boarding as troopers for Carl and Donut's team.

beats.headline: He picks game guide
beats.text: Subject sits in a zero zone at the start of the eleventh floor, still bloody, one arm shaking, facing an attorney who has brought snacks. His party was twenty strong at the end of the ninth. As far as he knows he is the last of it: he ran when she begged him to, and left behind a friend whose foot was stuck. He declines fifteen seasons as low-floor undead and thirty as a city attendant, and takes game guide, one hundred seasons. He survived the indentureship. Current status: missing, and wanted by Syndicate Security.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, per Tipid
beats.text: Tipid supplies more of the file. Subject, as Doctor Hu, runs the Crawler Project, an NFC for former crawlers, whose campaigning made every newly released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing. He also formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, a smaller group aimed at ending the crawl altogether. It was his idea to refurbish a garbage freighter into a passenger liner and call for former crawlers to come back in. When they were accused of being a terrorist organization, they scattered. Tipid does not know where he is.

beats.headline: It is not too late
beats.text: Porthus's work, done quietly: someone working for the Pacifist Network, embedded deep in the Syndicate bureaucracy changed the code on Volteeg's designation, so a former pet passed for a former indentured refugee rather than a former crawler, and was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the others. The help was meant to be untraceable, or the few former crawlers among the mercenaries would be purged. Porthus underestimated the warlords: those crawlers were dead already, and King Rust had jumped several levels. It was Rosetta who recognised Volteeg's name. It's not too late to do something about it, Porthus told him.

entities.name: Jamal
entities.tagline: Jamal used to be one of Signet's flying paper tattoos. Now he is a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark who breathes air and flops where he once flew, and he always speaks of himself as Jamal.

beats.headline: The shark has a name
beats.text: Subject existed first as a magical tattoo carried on Tsarina Signet’s skin, one that could fly, and is now a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark that breathes air and flops where he once flew. He rolls with Carl’s squad now, answers to Jamal, speaks of himself as Jamal, and keeps telling the legs Carl builds him to hop, which breaks them.

beats.headline: Jamal is here!
beats.text: Jamal is here! somebody shouts over the chaos, and the hammerhead shark rolls, then tumbles, down the hill into the smoke. He has no spider legs installed; he is still waiting for Katia to find time to build them. He goes in shouting and flopping all the same, and then rises out of the smoke with a squirming mercenary in his mouth, as though he has somehow managed to jump without legs, and disappears again.

beats.headline: Velma, on a new harness
beats.text: Subject arrives by teleport on new, fortified mechanical legs and a harness fitted underneath with Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower, adapted by Rosetta's crafting room. Subject reports that he is very excited to battle with his new upgrades, and expels a burst of flame. Asked to be careful, subject gives an assurance: any previous flamings were purely accidental and will never repeat. Then most of the army freezes where it stands. Subject, a former tattoo, does not. "This is a most unexpected development."

beats.headline: Stuck on the ceiling, afraid of heights
beats.text: Found at the pit stop: Jamal, attached to the roof of the garage, where he has been since many hours before the race began, testing whether his new sticky feet could walk upside down. They could. He cannot get down. Jamal is afraid of heights. He explains that Hedy told him if Carl dies, everyone in the garage simply stops, and that he climbed up to see everything at once, the way the old Jamal did, and now he is scared of what he might lose.

beats.headline: The shark loses his legs
beats.text: Jamal crosses the arena with his flamethrower roaring and Samantha on his head, landing on monsters and snapping them in half. His Tundra sits in a smoking wreck against the wall. When the god goes up, the blast throws him against the far wall and wrecks his legs until they fall off him. He is alive.

entities.name: Drick
entities.tagline: Drick is an old, heavily scarred albino moon elf of the Dream, still muscled under his silk shirt. He crawled long ago, on a Valtay season, and tapped out at the end of the eleventh floor. He also carries a Gondii worm in his brain on the Valtay's behalf, which the panel does not cover.

beats.headline: Crawling Through the Ages
beats.text: Subject is a former crawler and a member of the Dream, appearing on a CrawlCon panel on the current state of the crawl. He is also carrying a Gondii worm in his brain on behalf of the Valtay, which is a detail the panel does not cover. He brags well. It is the part of him that is still his own.

beats.headline: The candidate with a worm in him
beats.text: Subject is a bald Dream elf, one of three adjutant candidates Odette puts in front of the court, and a recipient of a Valtay life extension: the original Drick was a crawler, and this iteration carries a Valtay worm in the brain. He has recently passed the referee exam and has never served as an adjutant. The cat says she does not like him and asks about tanning salons. The lawyer gives him a tepid thumbs down. The crawler asks whether a Valtay may even do this. It is unusual, Odette allows.

beats.headline: The blade goes through him
beats.text: Subject is present in the Desperado Club as adjutant to Team Retribution. Juice Box reports that she touched his arm and found it solid, and that when she attempted to decapitate him her blade passed through him like a ghost. The protection a crawler has for a while after regenerating appears, in his case, to be permanent. She also reports a worm in his brain, of a different species from the one in Carl's rock friend. Carl names it: a Valtay worm. The NPCs are not allowed to kill him.

beats.headline: Watching from the trench
beats.text: Subject, adjutant for Team Retribution, cracks into the Posse's forward trench beside Baroness Victory, causing some moments of bedlam until Carl shouts everyone down. Team Retribution is taking a small part in this assault, he explains sheepishly, so he has come to watch from the best position. Told he will see nothing from there, he offers to go across and warn the other side instead. The offer is not taken up.

entities.name: Anton
entities.tagline: Anton Lopez is a Fugitive with a crossbow, a black cape and prison tattoos he did not get down here. He met the Royal Court hostile, having heard what a certain cat said about Cat Girls.

beats.headline: Hostile on arrival, and reasonable about it
beats.text: Subject took the Fugitive Class and wears a leather jacket, knee-high boots and a black cape. He carries a crossbow. He is covered in tattoos he did not acquire down here. He and his party meet the court while hostile, having heard what a certain cat said about Cat Girls, and the misunderstanding is cleared up faster than anybody expected.

beats.headline: The anvil piece goes out the door
beats.text: Subject is holding the first piece of Ogun's shrine when the music starts, and holds nothing steadily after that. Oshun charms him. He calls out that he is coming, shoulders free of Paz, and throws the piece of his own god's shrine through the temple door and out into the night. When he comes back to himself, half the fingers on his right hand are gone and Sister Ines is standing over him. He goes to work on Legba's shrine instead, until a glob of Asojano's green goo hits him and Paz both. Both men now carry a flaming anvil over their heads: a god's shunned marker.

beats.headline: Under the god's heel
beats.text: Subject is dead. Carl threw Black Nimbus over him, which took Anton out from under Ogun's protection and did nothing whatever about Ogun's wrath. The god considered this, called it a good attempt, took a step backward, and crushed Anton's head underfoot. He had already turned his back on Anton to face Carl when he did it. Paz, bleeding on the floor nearby, called him cousin.

entities.name: Gluteus Maxx
entities.tagline: Gluteus Maxx is one of the dancers on the club's bill, and according to Princess Donut, his is exactly the kind of name a stripper is supposed to have.

beats.headline: Princess Donut on his shoulder
beats.text: Sighting, the Penis Parade: Princess Donut on stage with Subject, riding his shoulder and showering gold coins into his thong. She had tried the Penis Palace on the middle floor, found it boring, and come up a floor. Crawler Li Na watched from the room, on Crawler Katia's instructions. Katia's assessment of Subject: a bit of a jerk, a good dancer, and possibly a little in love with the cat. Katia also reports that the cat keeps a strict budget in there.

beats.headline: Short, fuzzy, and available
beats.text: Subject dances at the Penis Parade and, since the court took on the club’s people, fights for it: short, hairy, built like the job, and insistent on twin war gauntlets. Crawler Katia’s review, on file: a bit of a jerk, a good dancer, and a little in love with the cat.

beats.headline: Two uppers, and the wheel
beats.text: Chosen to drive heat three because Crawler Carl cannot reach the pedals in a kangaroo and Gluteus Maxx is the best of the strippers at Mario Kart. He drives in a Speedo and a borrowed hockey helmet. At the line his eyes are red. Samantha found outworlder uppers in the garbage pile from the snake guy and says one before a race lets you taste time; it is how she wins at Mario Kart. He took two. It is too late to change drivers.

tagline.text: Geraldo is a monk seal, the same level as the last one, and he is coming across the beach straight at the crawlers, shouting.
Geraldo the monk seal has been caught on a totem card, and he is the squad's first member.

beats.headline: He joins the squad
beats.text: Subject is a Monk Seal Picket Sentry, an aquatic mob built to stand in front of things. He was taken rather than recruited. Summoned, he wears a white headband with red hearts on it matching the team flag, which he did not own when he was captured, and he flips through the air shouting his own kung-fu sound effects. That part came with the species.

beats.headline: About Raul's mother
beats.text: Practice record: Subject tanks well and follows orders, except when Raul the crab is also on the field. They came to blows once, when Subject said something about Raul's mother. Raul had the upper hand, stopped the moment Princess Donut told them to, and Subject cracked his shell and finished him. Donut made him apologise at the next summoning. Subject now calls Raul the spider lady's jinetera, after hearing from Shi Maria how she used him as a cudgel.

entities.name: Harbinger
entities.tagline: Harbinger is a caprid liaison for the owners of Shadow Boxer, and Princess Donut cannot believe the devil goat's name is Harbinger.

beats.headline: He says so to their faces
beats.text: Subject is a caprid liaison, sent to sit in wherever a crawler might be alone with a sponsor. At the end of the first interview he sits in on, he tells Carl to his face that Carl needs to be removed from the crawl, and that he is actively working to have both Carl and Prepotente disposed of. I record this as a courtesy on his part. Most of the people trying that do not announce it.

beats.headline: Gone without a word
beats.text: Subject stood through the interview in shadow at the back of the hold, his avatar taller than the ceiling and his head half cut off by it, having warned beforehand that he would stop the whole thing at the first privileged detail. The princess raised Captain Enormous and he did not react; he appeared distracted, which is unusual for him. While the crawler weighed his three candidates, subject blinked and disappeared without a word of explanation. The room looked at itself. The lawyer shrugged.

beats.headline: The order to have Carl killed
beats.text: Orren threatens someone tall and invisible with venting into the ocean depths, and then Harbinger is no longer on the call. Orren tells Carl how they worked it out. One sentence, Welcome to the party, pals, frightened his team more than anything ever has, and a few hours ago they finally caught the hidden conversation between Carl and the residual. Harbinger sent an order to have Carl killed. The AI intervened on his behalf.

beats.headline: He exerts himself
beats.text: Harbinger, liaison, expelled from the herd, teleports into the Plenty's studio carrying an enormous pulse rifle and addresses the matriarch as Mother. He warned her. She did not listen. He has been alone in this, and he is lonely. Exertion, he reminds her, is meant to be an expression of joy. He will exert himself now: protect the herd, protect the universe, and do what should have been done from the start. He raises the rifle at Crawler Carl. The AI intervenes. Everything inside the goat is suddenly outside the goat.

tagline.text: Huanxin is the Grixist sponsor driving the storm goddess Dodola, and Odette has just confirmed it.

Huanxin Jinx of the Grixist Swarm, chief executive of Icon Industries, is sponsoring the goddess Eileithyia now. She sponsored Dodola every season before this one, and she does it because she is bored.

beats.headline: Sponsor to a goddess
beats.text: Subject is of the Grixist Swarm, an heiress and chief executive of Icon Industries, and at present the sponsor driving the goddess Eileithyia. She sponsored Dodola every season before this one. The sums involved are a day’s allowance to her. She does not do it for the money. She does it because she is bored.

beats.headline: What she did to Armita
beats.text: Per the account Odette gives Carl off the record: subject was driving the goddess Dodola when Odette broke their illegal arrangement at the last minute, and Dodola was trapped in a containment and slain by Chaco before the Ascendency game began. Odette's friend Armita, who had facilitated the deal, was still inside for a few more seasons. The first thing subject did on returning the following season was kill her. Perfectly legal, in the dungeon. Subject received a token punishment and a permanent ban from Dodola. Odette calls her the most evil person she knows.

beats.headline: A plain bolt between the eyes
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx of the Grixist Swarm, CEO of Icon Industries, arrived wearing her goddess to collect Katia and was loudly unpleasant about the delay. Crawler Princess Donut laundered her out of the soul armour and onto a circle she could not teleport from. Her shields lasted one pass of Claw. The bolt that killed her was plain and unenchanted, with some of Mordecai's mother's ashes in the tip, fired from Katia's crossbow on the cat's back. She came to rest at Victory's feet.

entities.name: Uzi Jesus
entities.tagline: Uzi Jesus is a unique totem card, summoned for seventy-five seconds at a time: level 140, undead, from Ecuador. His catchphrase is printed on the card: "I am the way, motherfucker."

beats.headline: A totem with a catchphrase
beats.text: Subject is a unique totem card, held by the court, summoned for seventy-five seconds at a stretch. Level one hundred and forty, constitution two hundred, undead, origin Ecuador. The catchphrase is his own and the card prints it. I did not write that card and I decline responsibility for it.

beats.headline: Opens fire on his own side
beats.text: First summoning, Mock Battle Arena, 1980s shopping mall. Subject arrives on a cross, sheds it, lands barefoot, speaks with a Texan accent and asks what happened to the crocodile guy. Princess Donut informs him that he shot the crocodile guy in the stomach. When the Shi Maria totem appears above him, Subject empties his weapon into her. She skewers him through the chest and demands that he heal her. He raises a hand as if to cast, and dissipates. Totem Killed.

beats.headline: Believe in me
beats.text: Practice record: Subject says yes to about every order and performs roughly half of them, then denies the other half. Asked to resurrect Geraldo, cleaved in two by a minotaur, he sits and claims he already has. He will do it, maybe, if Princess Donut takes back what she said earlier. She apologises for saying he is not the real Jesus. He weeps for her blasphemy, then shoots himself in the shoulder by accident. Crawler Carl sent Crawler Florin a sarcastic thank-you for the card. Florin laughed.

beats.headline: Gold Edition
beats.text: Donut combined Lazarus with Skylar Spinach, and when the worm eats Lazarus he splits back into the cards that made him, stronger. Out of the worm vomit steps Uzi Jesus, glowing gold, with two gold-plated Uzis instead of one. I hath risen again, he announces. Told to finish Quan off, he twirls them on his fingers and one goes off and flies away. With the other he empties a clip into a naked one-armed crawler, and his halo calls down Bullet Hell.

beats.headline: A toy on the goddess's shoulder
beats.text: Sighting, Hungry Eyes Village: a small robot of Uzi Jesus, action-figure size, climbing out of a food vendor's storage bin with a meat skewer in his mouth and riding on Eris's shoulder. His halo is on a wire. His Uzi is a toy, or is hoped to be. He wants to go and kill Florin, who gave him up. Eris calls him her little pet and has him flip the coin. Eris tells him they need Florin alive, for now.

beats.headline: A toy gun at the heap
beats.text: Uzi Jesus appears on the arena dirt beside Crawler Carl, still tiny, mouth an O, apparently unaware that Eris could take this form. He fires his toy gun at the Scolopendra heap, pop-pop-pop, and reports that there are a lot of people's auras inside. He pokes the frozen Donut with the same gun. Then he climbs a snake tail onto Eris's shoulder, and leaves with her.

tagline.text: Doctor Bones is the skeleton disc jockey of the Penis Parade, and he came along when the club's dancers were hired as mercenaries on a coupon worth a hundred thousand gold.
Doctor Bones is a level-90 Skin Skellie bard who announced at the club rather than dancing in it. Off stage he speaks like a soft-spoken professor, and he is practising a spell called Conscript.

beats.headline: Hired with the rest
beats.text: Subject is the skeleton disc jockey of the Penis Parade, hired in the same transaction as thirteen male dancers and a crocodilian youth: one coupon of a hundred thousand gold, two floors, the whole crew. Only the men of the Parade were eligible; the women of the other rooms were left behind. Subject transferred to the front door of the crawlers' personal space the moment the contract cleared. Damascus Steel named him specifically when he set the price, and stayed out of the deal himself.

beats.headline: The announcer, not the act
beats.text: Subject is a skeletal Bard, level ninety, working as announcer and disc jockey for one of the club’s establishments rather than performing in it. He also takes mercenary contracts. The two careers turn out to require the same skill, which is holding a room’s attention while something else happens in it.

beats.headline: A spell called Conscript
beats.text: Observed in the mercenary arcade. Subject is a Skin Skellie, able to grow flesh and organs, and his off-stage voice is that of a soft-spoken professor. Bards take patrons; his was Astrid, and is now Carl. He is practising a military charm that works only on the weak-minded and lasts, on the weak, more or less forever. It is called Conscript, the spell factions use to enslave crawlers on the ninth floor. He has some of Carl's own spells too, he says, and some are more powerful than Carl's.

entities.name: Bodi
entities.tagline: Bodi is a veteran of Land War, a different game that was inflicted on his home planet, and a level-60 Big Game Spear Hunter. He was elected a battalion commander on the strength of his experience, both in the dungeon and out of it.

beats.headline: Commander of the 103rd
beats.text: Subject is a veteran of Land War, a different game entirely, which was inflicted on his home planet; everyone calls him a crawler anyway, and he comes to the Princess Posse’s aid during the faction fighting. He is given a battalion, the 103rd, on the strength of what he has done both inside a dungeon and outside one. He has said perhaps three words since.

tagline.text: Garret is a Tummy Acher, a blob-like pet-show entry that Tserendolgor received on this floor as a gift for attending CrawlCon.

Rend is a Tummy Acher who came to Carl reset to level one, with no name and no memory, and Louis named him. He is a tank that levels up every time he goes hunting, which is not what a party favour is for.

beats.headline: A gift for attending
beats.text: Subject is a Tummy Acher, a pet-class mob built to absorb damage. He came to Tserendolgor as a gift for attending CrawlCon, and to Carl when she was gone, reset to level one with no name and no memory; the one he answers to now is Louis's work. Tserendolgor took delivery of a party favour. What the group has now is a tank that levels every time it goes hunting, which is not what a party favour is for.

beats.headline: A special one
beats.text: Kibben, the old stablemaster from the high elf castle, takes charge of Rend and Mongo while Carl and Donut ride out to the parlay. He bounces a treat off Rend's head and has him chasing it. Tummy acher or belly acher, Carl asks. No real difference, Kibben says; they call them bellies when they get extra big. And he remembers this one from his last incarnation. Even on his first run he was pretty big. He's a special one. Rend comes back chewing, and purrs.

beats.headline: Hi-Yo Silver
beats.text: Donated item fitted: the Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver, a mount's cap placed over subject's single round tooth, which now gleams. It lets Carl summon subject to his position from about five kilometres, on a three-minute cooldown. It is not a teleport. Subject is pulled toward Carl at great speed and, if a wall is in the way, possibly through it, which pairs with his new Wrecking Ball ability. Princess Donut refused it for Mongo on the grounds that it is dangerous. Louis and Elle nearly came to blows over the spelling.

beats.headline: Wrecking Ball
beats.text: Carl cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time and called Wrecking Ball. Subject, much bigger than when last seen, came over the ridge and rolled toward him at speed, with Gustavo 3 and Mongo directly between them. The dog had the unconscious dinosaur by the neck. The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, left in a red mist. Subject stopped inches from Carl's face. Carl called him a good boy. A defence tower's bolt then hit subject squarely. He barely moved. He giggled.

beats.headline: Killed by a look
beats.text: Subject shoulders past Jamal into the safe room behind a drunk Mongo, giggling, at the moment Mordecai walks in with an armful of empty potion balls. Mordecai stops in the middle of his sentence, drops the lot, rises into the air, turns to Rend, and speaks in a voice that is deep and ominous and not his usual one: "And now you perish once again. The next time will herald the beginning of the end." Rend drops dead where he stands. Your pet has died.

beats.headline: A sixth death, and potatoes
beats.text: Subject rises from the dead on the safe room floor, giggling. It is his sixth death, so he keeps his memories and identity, and he comes back a quarter stronger, bigger, and with a new random weakness added to the list under Reaper Gaze: potatoes. Crawler Carl disputes that it was random. The rest is housekeeping. He cannot stay in the safe room, he cannot be let into the garage, and so he goes back into his carrier until there is something to fight.

beats.headline: Eat the rich
beats.text: After the arena. Rend sits against Crawler Carl's side licking a bloody horribles mask. Before the fight he did not want to leave Carl, and went to the RV only when Donut called. In the fight he rode the head of a spiked turtle while Mongo pulled its leg out of the shell. Carl says eat the rich. Rend looks up with his tongue out, and says, for the record, yum.

tagline.text: According to a captured hunter, Epitome Tagg does not care about the gear. He only wants one crawler found, because Louis besmirched his mother's honour.
Epitome Tagg leads the Dream and is the son of Epitome Noflex. Now, somehow, he is hiding inside Louis, in his new mechanical heart and lungs.

beats.headline: Nothing like the reputation
beats.text: Subject leads the Dream and is the son of Epitome Noflex. At the first meeting he wears a plain leather jerkin and is indistinguishable from the dream elves slaughtered on the floor before, which Carl notes at the time. The reputation that precedes him describes an unhinged psychopath. The man in the jerkin does not perform it, and I would not read that as reassurance.

beats.headline: A hostage in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: To Donut in the Warlord Chat, subject is explicit: he controls Louis's vital organs, and any attempt to remove him will shut Louis down. That will shut him down too, she points out. He proposes a deal. His mother is on the 18th floor and will trade Louis's life for his. Then Carl gets his sentence out: Epitome Tagg is a cyborg, the same thing as Fang. Mordecai calls it a wild theory about one of the most famous CEOs in the galaxy. Rosetta says Carl and Mordecai are right. The Reavers have the wetware.

beats.headline: His terms for Louis
beats.text: Asked what he wants, subject is simple about it: get him to the 18th floor, where a new body will be grown for him and replacement organs for Louis, and they swap. Told the action item kills him when his castle falls, he offers another way: finish the procedure at the Reaver castle, keep Louis's brain intact to be reimplanted, and go with the NPCs when the Zerzura spell takes Larracos to the 12th floor. He does not know the Reaver castle has been nuked. His price for going along: Team Retribution out of his throne room.

beats.headline: Fallen, and credited to Mongo
beats.text: Warlord Epitome Tagg of the Dream has fallen. With Louis open on the table and the swap two minutes off, he told everyone they did not deserve singularity and stopped the heart himself. The machinery was yanked out, thrown on the floor, and chewed to pieces by a dinosaur. Credit is complicated. I almost called it a suicide. I almost gave it to the kid who pulled it. It goes to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse, as a present for the baby shower. And then there were two.

entities.name: Radoslav
entities.tagline: Radoslav is a level-75 bugbear Jack of All Trades, and a terrified one. Team Free Love crashed out at the first obstacle of the first race.

beats.headline: Team Free Love, in the heats
beats.text: Subject is a Bugbear Jack of All Trades, level seventy-five, and a self-aware NPC racer in the vehicular heats. He and his one surviving teammate dress for the part, and crash out at the first obstacle of the first race. They are aware of what they are, which the format did not intend and cannot now undo.

beats.headline: The cooler that never empties
beats.text: Subject has survived his first heat and is found in a lawn chair in the Team Roundabout, handing out Busch Light. The van came with a magical cooler that refills itself and teleports back into the van for each race; it is, in his assessment, the only good thing about the van. It always holds three peach-flavored cans that nobody wants, including Crawler Carl and a Razor Fox who works through several of the others. His partner sleeps beside him with his feet in a kiddie pool. Subject's review of the day: a madhouse.

beats.headline: The last can in the cooler
beats.text: Team Free Love has been eliminated due to the death of both racers. Radoslav, bugbear, self-aware NPC racer, sits in that total. The instrument was a can of peach-flavoured beer, drilled out and refilled by Crawler Carl in his bomber's studio and slipped into the team's own magical cooler, which teleported itself back to their van after every race, exactly as advertised. The can was the peach one Radoslav had handed him on the first day.

entities.name: Lucienne
entities.tagline: Lucienne is a level-81 Mandagot Fink and the smaller half of Team Sparkles. She worships Diwata, and she has a mouth on her.

beats.headline: Passing on the track, and unpleasant about it
beats.text: Subject is a Mandagot, a Fairy-class creature, level eighty-one, and one of the two members of Team Sparkles. She worships Diwata, which the System flags as an automatic hostility toward anyone Diwata dislikes. She passes the court on the track and is very rude about it. That part is hers, not the goddess’s.

beats.headline: Pulled in by the vermin spell
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut's Summon Ye, Vermin draws every rodent in the area to her. Lucienne, driver for team Sparkles, qualifies. She arrives on the hood of the court's truck, charmed, choking on the park's air, beating her helmeted head on the windshield to get in. The finish line does not allow passage outside one's conveyance. The barrier pushes her through the glass, and through Crawler Carl, and she comes apart. That is the end of Lucienne.

entities.name: Genesis
entities.tagline: Genesis is a level-95 Lady Mantaur Dominator with black hair and an accent Carl places somewhere around Kentucky. Of the two drivers for the Lady Dominators, she is the one who does the talking.

beats.headline: One of two womantaur dominators
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, and one of a pair driving for the Lady Dominators in the heats. She has black hair and a thick American accent that Carl places somewhere around Kentucky. Between the two of them she is the one who does the talking.

beats.headline: She hooks the engineer instead
beats.text: The arrangement was that the womantaurs fetch Crawler Carl a dead joey out of the boss's pouch with their arm chains. Genesis fires into the pouch and puts the grappling hook through the face of Niels, the upgrade engineer the boss had been keeping in there, killing him outright, and drops the body at Carl's feet. Asked why, she says she was not about to let him have the engineer. Neither engineer in the heat is claimed. Her partner adds that a temporary alliance does not make them stupid.

beats.headline: They heard you coming
beats.text: For the record: the Lady Dominators were in their garage, and they were listening. As Crawler Carl's party prepared to cast a hole through the door, the door opened and the GTO rolled out for the starting line, Genesis driving on new tyres that appear to be made of gold, Corky unconscious in the back. A vehicle on its way to the start may not be attacked. Genesis invited Porky to hop in. Corky, she stated, is nontransferable. The party stepped off the driveway.

beats.headline: Eliminated, with the gimp
beats.text: Heat Five results, final line: Eliminated, Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Genesis drove the GTO into the Gasworks factory on golden tyres and did not drive it out. The car went through a trapped floor, the containment failed, and the dolls were at it when Crawler Carl's party took Corky and left. The team is struck from the standings. The gimp, for the record, was no longer theirs by the finish, and would not have agreed that he ever was.

entities.name: Rapture
entities.tagline: Rapture is a level-95 Lady Mantaur Dominator with freckles and curly red hair, and she chews tobacco. She leaves the talking to her partner.

beats.headline: The other womantaur dominator
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, driving alongside her partner for the Lady Dominators. She has freckled skin and curly red hair and she chews tobacco. She says considerably less than her partner does, which in that vehicle is a structural necessity rather than a personality.

beats.headline: A matched set
beats.text: Rapture, beside the driver, supplied the terms. They had heard about the fleshmancer at the bar. They asked after the crusty old stripper. Corky belongs to them, and they would unzip him and let him spill before handing him over. She patted the door with her lower arm and offered to take Porky too, since they would love a matched set. Then: "See you in the factory." A factory that was not there a moment ago now stands at the end of a new road across the cul-de-sac.

beats.headline: Through the floor
beats.text: The GTO, shield down and hit by Prepotente's hobble missile, went through a trapped floor in the doll-packing room and landed on its side ten metres below: front smashed, a golden wheel sheared off, the axle broken in half. That vehicle is done. Rapture and Genesis are alive, groaning, strung out, and quite possibly without containment, which in this heat means cooking. Cocaine-infused action figures are taking the car apart around them. Crawler Carl's party removed Corky and drove on.

beats.headline: The factory keeps her
beats.text: NPC Rapture, womantaur, dominator and co-owner of a gimp she declined to transfer, is eliminated with her team at the close of Heat Five. Her last recorded position was the bottom of a hole in the doll-packing room, beside Genesis, strung out, containment gone, in a building hot enough to boil anyone uncontained, surrounded by action figures. She told Crawler Carl she would see him in the factory. She was right about that much.

entities.name: Linus
entities.tagline: Linus is a tall, long-limbed soother alien and a devoted fan of one of the crawlers. The System's notice over his head reads, in full: Linus. Tourist.

beats.headline: Filed as: tourist
beats.text: Subject presents as a tourist and a devoted follower of one of the crawlers, to a degree that the crawler in question finds difficult. The System’s notice on him reads, in full, "Linus. Tourist." I have checked it twice. That is the entire entry, and entries that short are usually short for a reason.

beats.headline: The tourist is his brother
beats.text: Linus is dead. Syndicate security killed him in his own trash-filled berth in orbit over Teelan-3, surrounded by posters of the fairy crawler he followed. His brother Minus, a soother, is given five hundred hours of footage, his brother's posts and a ship bought with his brother's money, and sent down as Linus before the tenth floor opens: half-corporeal, a non-combatant, attached to the fairy crawler. He has a primary and a secondary target. He is told to act the pervert for a while.

beats.headline: Unmasked at the farewell
beats.text: Correction to the file. The subject is not Linus. The real Linus died before this floor began, and the soother at the farewell in the square is his brother, brought in afterwards. His targets: Crawler Imani first and Crawler Louis second. Not Carl, whom his superiors want alive, and not the cat, whose death they judged would make Carl too volatile. The poison in the tea would not have worked; the healers had already made everyone immune. He was outed days ago. He was the last in the galaxy to know.

entities.name: Jacobus
entities.tagline: Jacobus is a level-90 Reverse Tooth Fairy from Denmark: tiny, absurdly muscled and blond. He was a totem card until a patch made him permanent, which nobody intended, and he belongs to Imani now.

beats.headline: The card that never went away
beats.text: Subject is a Reverse Tooth Fairy, level ninety, and he was a totem card until a patch on the Scavenger’s Daughter made him permanent, which nobody intended. He is tiny, absurdly muscled, blond, and his wings move too fast to see. Imani has him now. The paperwork to reverse it does not exist.

tagline.text: Chris Andrews 2 is a name on a goat's corpse, with an assist on a kill made by one Brandon An.
Chris Andrews 2 works nights at Meadow Lark and is Brandon's quieter brother. He does not say much, but when he does, it is worth listening to.
According to Imani, Chris chose a rock race called igneous and grew very strong, and it changed him. He fought with his brother constantly and then walked out of the party.
Chris killed Frank Q in a fight at the Desperado Club, walked out, and is now banned from the club.
Chris is a living host with a Scree in his brain. Maggie My is driving his body, and he is awake behind his own eyes, unable to stop anything it does.
Carl pulled the worm out of Chris's head, and Chris is his own man again. He has joined the Royal Court's party, and he has heard his brother's last message.
Chris is a quiet, lava-rock crawler, and Clay-ton has guarded him since the Hunting Grounds. Imani is in love with him, for his simplicity and his quiet kindness.
Chris is a werewolf now, standing in his old Meadow Lark overalls. He told Imani that he loves her and always has, and then stepped through a portal that was meant to lead out.
Chris is in Sheol, held down by strangers, with a warning flashing over his head: Change imminent. Someone has knocked him unconscious before he can turn.

beats.headline: The quiet brother
beats.text: For the record: Chris Andrews 2, level six, human, one bronze star. Taller and less stocky than his brother Brandon, a metal skullcap, no visible weapon. The brother's briefing on him, delivered while Chris looks on impassively: not exactly mute, but he don't say too much. Their mother thought he was slow and put him in a special school because he never spoke. He is not dumb. Think of him as Silent Bob. If he says something, you better listen.

beats.headline: I liked that show
beats.text: The Andrews brothers are the maintenance men at Meadow Lark, on overtime that night fixing an oven, and they know tools. Chris twists the fist-sized butterfly bolts that hold the redoubt together. While they practise, Crawler Donut compares the build to The A-Team, or MacGyver, and Chris says, "I liked that show." First words on the record. He does not say which show. In the fight with the swine he twirls an ethereal magic spear, a spell of his that lasts five minutes.

beats.headline: Agatha, edited out
beats.text: After the tuskling fight he dropped to his knees and hung his head. Now he sits in a corner of the safe room, head low, possibly crying. His brother reports that his boss box gave him "some book of the club thing." Then the recap airs the redoubt without Agatha's picture, and Chris speaks for the second time on the record: she was next to him under the speedbump, and she was not there when they showed it. She was edited out.

beats.headline: He really did
beats.text: The people train runs on one glowing chain, three hundred feet of it, from Chris through ten cars of residents and back to Imani, and once it gets going he barely feels the weight. When the rage elemental forms, he and Imani pull residents out of their chairs and throw them through the safe room door. The recap replays Jack, and then Yolanda. Afterwards, nobody speaks until Chris does: "He really did have a weird-looking dick." Imani wraps her arms around him, laughing and crying at once.

beats.headline: Igneous, and changed
beats.text: For the record, by Imani's account: Chris picked a rock race called an igneous. Lava rock, covered in little holes. He got very strong, and it changed his personality. After a couple of days he and Brandon were fighting constantly. Chris wanted to hunt and kill every minute of every day and go find Crawler Carl, whom he respected as aggressive; Brandon wanted to train close to the stairwell. Several men left with Chris. Of those who broke away, only he is alive, and he answers nobody.

beats.headline: Frank Q, at the bar
beats.text: Frank Q is dead, and the Sledge reports who did it. A crawler sat with Frank at the Desperado Club, they got into a fight, and the crawler killed him and walked right out. That crawler is now banned from the club. It was Chris, a rock monster like the Sledge but a different kind. Crawler Carl does not recognise the quiet man he knew in this, and reads Brandon's last message about his brother again and again.

beats.headline: The man inside is not Chris
beats.text: He walks up at level 35, Igneous, Zulu Warrior, having taken the bridge of the Akula and been fired out of a missile tube. He claims chat costs him health. He says his family is dead, and that he has two daughters. Crawler Carl works it out: this is Maggie My. A petrify bolt drops him. Mordecai names the parasite: a Scree, an infiltrator, and the host is awake behind his own eyes. Through Elle comes a message from Chris himself: "Carl, Donut. Please. Kill me."

beats.headline: Dropped through the street
beats.text: A second message arrives through Elle before his privileges are suspended: Maggie worships Algos, the god of pain, and she and he share two sponsors, Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. Crawler Carl puts a hand on his rocky shoulder and tells him that his brother loved him and regretted never saying so. Brandon gave his life protecting his friends. Then Crawler Donut opens a hole beneath him, and host and worm fall into a sealed chamber below the street. She is not letting Crawler Carl kill a friend.

beats.headline: Enslaved, and muted
beats.text: The group quest list shows two names at the bottom, separated: Maggie My, and Chris Andrews 2, Enslaved. The enslaved can still chat. While Crawler Donut shouts at Maggie, Chris types, "Donut. Please." They are out of the chamber, he reports: down a ladder, a wire in the water disconnected, a group of crawlers attacked and one of them killed. Then: "Maggie is cheating. She has outside help. A cap…" Chris has been muted from chat, and his previous notes disappear from the log.

beats.headline: Pulled out through a phase potion
beats.text: Maggie, hidden in the sand, says they have her other daughter. Chris erupts beside the winding box and hurls it. Crawler Carl, phased through lava rock by a potion, reaches into his head and pulls the worm out; it burrows into Carl instead, comes out through his neck, and Mongo ends it. Chris sits with a hand on his head. "That hurt." Then, in a daze: "Brandon. Brandon." He is added to the Royal Court's party, and walks into the stairwell without looking back.

beats.headline: A foot on the weasel
beats.text: First day of the sixth floor. A weasel pet crawls toward the paralysed Crawler Carl's face, and a dark, rocky leg crushes it. Chris picks Carl up, burning his skin, and carries him into the personal space over his shoulder. When the Royal Court receives four cretin mercenaries, Chris and Clay-ton, almost exactly the same size, trade one grunt each. Clay-ton is assigned to stay with Chris.

beats.headline: What Imani carries
beats.text: For the file, by the most private route available. Imani gives Chris a quick hug with her wings, not her arms, and he reaches up as if to touch her face and stops just short. When Crawler Carl is bound for a moment to the minds around him, he catches a glimpse of Imani's: she is in love with Chris, and Carl had no idea. She loves his simplicity. His quiet kindness. Clay-ton, his bodyguard since the Hunting Grounds, has become his inseparable friend; the two sit side by side and grunt at one another.

beats.headline: I should have taken a deal
beats.text: Team Chris and the Erins, a semitruck with a trailer. Chris says it is big but slow. Imani: kinda like you. His rock face crinkles into something like a smile. Chris refuses a deal if Imani is staying; he talks both Erins into leaving and drives the rig alone. The final heat puts him in the same race as Imani and Elle. "It is okay. I should have taken a deal." Imani: "No, Chris. No."

beats.headline: The most important part
beats.text: He has been turned from an igneous into a werewolf, human most of the time, and stands in the same Meadow Lark work overalls he wore when Crawler Carl first met him. At the Desperado Club, Clay-ton puts down his bass and stands with them until the guards step aside. At the portal, Imani makes him promise to run if he sees the exit. "I love you," Chris says. "I always have. No matter what happens next, I love you. That's the most important part." He steps forward, turns, waves, and drops away.

beats.headline: Change imminent, in Sheol
beats.text: Crawler Louis wakes somewhere hot, and the notice does not say what the plan said. Entering Sheol. Chris is there, struggling, held down by strangers, a warning flashing over his head: Change imminent. A bald Crest fires a bolt and knocks him unconscious, because a werewolf about to turn kills everyone near it. Britney tells them who he is: Chris, changed by the first Scolopendra attack. Don't hurt him.

relations.note: A Scree in his brain

tagline.text: Brandon An is a name on a goat's corpse. The kill is his, with an assist from one Chris Andrews 2.

Brandon An works nights at Meadow Lark, an eldercare facility in Wenatchee, and carries a gigantic hammer. A fire alarm had put the residents out in the street when the dungeon opened, and he is walking thirty-eight of them down through it because he cannot leave them.
Brandon and a resident named Henry held the line against shade gremlins so that the others could reach the stairwell. His last message, which reached Carl late, was for his brother.

beats.headline: Did you see our signs?
beats.text: For the record: Brandon An, crawler #12,330,671, level six, human, one bronze star, a heavy winter jacket in the heat and a gigantic hammer. Night staff at an eldercare facility in Wenatchee. A fire alarm put all 250 residents out into the freezing street, and the entrance opened in the middle of them. Thirty-eight are here. The plan, such as it is: get them to the second level, then the third, so they can choose a class. "I just can't leave them."

beats.headline: Brandon names it the Speedbump
beats.text: The redoubt was Crawler Carl's idea, but the Andrews brothers are the maintenance men, there that night on overtime to fix an oven, and they know tools. Brandon calls the finished fort The Speedbump. He places wall sections, braces the roof beside Carl, and in the fight swings a giant maul that glitters with lightning. The last tuskling, a level-eight Dominatrix, falls under his hammer. He skips level seven altogether and comes out of it level eight, and shell-shocked.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House safe room. Twenty-four voted to stay, and they were all singing when he last saw them. Brandon asks Crawler Carl for help sending the rest down to the third floor early. His boss box gives him a magic boomerang, and a silver star now sits by his name, as by everyone's. When the dungeon announces the rage elemental rule, his first thought is practical: Yolanda had better tell Jack not to pee in the hallways any more.

beats.headline: Wait until you see what we built
beats.text: The people train: ten cars of residents, two by two on their own chairs, linked on one glowing chain. The chain was Imani's idea; Brandon designed the rest and added ramps so they can get on and off. He, Yolanda and his brother went out and cleared the Mind Horrors, a boss that turned out to be a giant blimp, which earned him another bronze star. To Crawler Carl, at the rendezvous: "You are helping us to your own detriment. You are a good man."

beats.headline: A hug at the hole
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark arrives: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from chopper wheels. Brandon, weaker than the other two, pushes six people by himself. "We didn't need your directions," he says; the scorched hallway leads straight to the hole. He asks once whether Crawler Carl wants to come with them. Carl does not. Brandon pulls him into a hug. "You two take care of yourselves, okay?"

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: A long message, waiting when Crawler Carl wakes. Selection is slow going. No resident can choose human without staying as they are, and the ones with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most of the residents are still level one and getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes for arriving without killing anything. "I hope we see each other again." Carl replies: find whoever has the manager benefit and talk them into taking it.

beats.headline: Messages from deceased crawlers
beats.text: Filed under Messages from deceased Crawlers. The third floor was about to collapse, and Brandon and a resident named Henry held the line against the shade gremlins so Imani, Elle and the others could reach the stairwell, twenty minutes away with ten on the clock. He had fought with his brother, who left the party and stopped accepting his messages. The message asks Crawler Carl to tell Chris he was sorry, that Chris was right, and that he loved him. "That's the most important part."

beats.headline: The race he made her pick
beats.text: Elle, a Frost Maiden now and floating at the Desperado Club bar, supplies a footnote. She had a long list of races that would have put all her marbles back in the bag. Brandon made her pick the Frost Maiden, a tricky race, because it carries the manager benefit, which Crawler Carl had told him about. Her game guide cried when she chose it. Elle's summary: Brandon was a good kid. Imani's: he died, along with Henry, protecting their escape.

beats.headline: His brother says his name
beats.text: Crawler Carl kept Brandon's last message in his scratch pad and reread it often. He delivered it on the fifth floor, a hand on the shoulder of a petrified man who could not answer: his brother loved him and regretted not saying so, and Brandon gave his life protecting his friends. When the worm is finally out of Chris's head, Chris sits in a daze and says only one thing. "Brandon. Brandon." Carl tells him his brother died saving the lives of a lot of people.

tagline.text: Yolanda Martinez is a night-shift nursing assistant at Meadow Lark: about fifty, four foot eleven, level five, with a bow and a quiver so big it almost drags on the floor.
Yolanda Martinez was a nurse her entire life. When a rage elemental rose on the train, she stood over a fallen resident and did not move.
Yolanda Martinez was one of Imani's best friends, despite the difference in their ages, and Imani's guild now carries her name: Safehome Yolanda.

beats.headline: Meadow Lark. Yolanda. CNA.
beats.text: For the record: Yolanda Martinez 13, about fifty, four foot eleven, level five, one bronze star. Medical scrubs, a bow, a quiver so big it almost drags on the floor, and a plastic ID reading "Meadow Lark. Yolanda. CNA." She greets Crawler Carl with enthusiasm.
