When he proposes a bomb for the boss, she has already tested its little viewing doors: they are protected, an arrow bounces off, and a finger meets something like thick clay that glows blue. "I wouldn't be pushing no bomb through that."

beats.headline: A brace to the head
beats.text: Agatha wheels her cart in behind them. "No, Agatha, don't!" Yolanda yells, to no effect. In the drilled routine she slides the angled braces out of her inventory one after another, circling the fort. When the Ball of Swine hits, a ceiling brace pops out and throws her over. When the walls come down, she is on the ground with her health alarmingly low, and Imani is standing over her, screaming and swinging a sword.

beats.headline: Randall, don't come in here
beats.text: Imani feeds her a health potion, and she sits up holding the side of her head. With blood still all over her own face, she takes out a cloth and cleans Agatha's. She explains that Agatha has no inventory because she has not done the tutorial. She is level six now. When an elderly man with a walker starts clicking into the boss chamber to see what the noise was, she jogs to head him off. "Randall, don't come in here!"

beats.headline: Adult pads for Jack
beats.text: She walks residents to the bathrooms. Her boss box gives her a new kind of quiver. When the recap leaves out Agatha's picture she asks whether that means she is dead. Then the dungeon announces the rage elemental rule for anyone who relieves themselves outside a bathroom, and Brandon tells her to warn Jack. Yolanda goes pale. "I have a few adult pads left. I'll make sure he puts one on."

beats.headline: Deflating the Mind Horrors
beats.text: She went out with the Andrews brothers to clear the Mind Horrors, shooting the floating brains from down the hallway and deflating them before they could reach anyone. The boss, a blimp, went down easily, by Brandon's account thanks to Yolanda. She is level nine now, equal with both brothers. On the march she barks with laughter when Mrs. McGibbons propositions Crawler Carl, tells Jack not to be crude, and walks at the rear with her bow ready.

beats.headline: A nurse her entire life
beats.text: Jack stood up on the train and relieved himself on the wall. Yolanda put an arrow through his temple, a fraction too late. Her arrows shattered against the rage elemental that rose from the stain, and she stood over Randall, thrown from the last car, while it finished forming. It cut through them both. Yolanda Martinez, nurse all her life, who worked sixty-hour weeks to put her son through college, unravelled in a red cloud. The creature did not break stride.

beats.headline: A skull over her head
beats.text: The recap plays it in slow motion. Jack at the wall, Yolanda's horrified face, Crawler Donut leaping, the arrow into his temple, and a player-killer skull icon slowly forming over Yolanda's head as he falls from the platform. Imani cannot watch and gets up and turns away. At the end of the episode the show replays her death from the beginning, in gruesome detail. Mrs. McGibbons's eulogy, delivered on the safe room floor before the episode airs: "Poor Yolanda. She was such a good kid."

beats.headline: A guild called Safehome Yolanda
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut is now a member of the guild Safehome Yolanda. Controlling party: Team Meadowlark. Guildmaster: crawler Imani C. Level seven, six parties, sixty-three crawlers. Despite their age difference, Yolanda was one of Imani's best friends, and the name lands on Crawler Carl like a punch to the gut. A new door appears beside the saferoom exit, labelled Guild Common Area.

tagline.text: Tally is a level-63 Bopca Protector who runs the first safe room, in a paper hat and a blue apron. He has spent years preparing to cook for human crawlers, and he addresses the cat as Your Royal Highness.
Tally was never a crawler. Sometimes they offer to take a planet's people instead, he says, and when they came for his world, he went.

beats.headline: Tally knows you are new here
beats.text: For the record: Tally, Bopca Protector, level 63, caretaker of the safe room, non-combatant. Paper hat, blue apron, a nametag, brown hair with a green tinge, a smell of wet moss, a Slavic accent. The dungeon opened without warning, so Tally is not ready, but he has been preparing for many years to cook for human crawlers. He is not prepared for a cat. The human asks for spice four on a human scale and receives murgh vindaloo over biryani, with garlic and spinach naan.

beats.headline: Your Royal Highness
beats.text: Tally serves the cat plain white yogurt and addresses her as Your Royal Highness; a fresh salmon has been special ordered for her waking. She instructs him to ensure the best-appointed room. "Of course, Your Highness." He apologises for the lack of lamb, taken for a mob in preparation for the floor below. He is not in every safe room: when this floor collapses he moves to a random floor, and when that collapses he moves down, until he is no longer needed.

beats.headline: Safe room questions only
beats.text: Crawler Carl tries general questions about the dungeon. Tally refuses them. He answers only questions that directly concern safe rooms. A personal space, once bought, transfers from level to level and from safe space to safe space, and the accessories are best bought early, because some only upgrade when the space goes down a level. Across the table, Crawler Donut is on her third plate of salmon pâté.

beats.headline: They came, and I went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at their booth and declares it no good way to watch. He did not like last season: people broken into groups, told their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. Safe, and not safe. That company saps a planet dry and leaves it without atmosphere. Borant at least gives people a chance. Was he a crawler? No. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining the world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.

beats.headline: Five plates of salmon
beats.text: Following a goblin she has just charmed into guiding them, Crawler Donut explains her method. Mordecai told her that the higher her charisma, the easier it is to get people to do what she wants: anyone who can speak, whose dot is not red, who is not a boss or very high level. "How do you think I've been getting Tally to give me five plates of salmon this whole time?"

entities.name: Magistrate Featherfall
entities.role: Magistrate of a skyfowl settlement · third floor

tagline.text: Magistrate Featherfall's signature is on a gate pass that tells the city guard its holder is acting on his orders.
Magistrate Featherfall is the big boss man of this skyfowl village, and his clerk, Miss Quill, will not disturb him.
Former Magistrate Featherfall, a level-32 dark cleric, was found hanging upside down in a dreamcatcher of bone. He was dead long before the blast that took the credit.

Featherfall wanted control of the town's swordsmen, and asked Miss Quill to help him cast a spell that would pull a dark cleric back as a capacitor. He stood too close to the amplifier, the feedback killed him, and Miss Quill knew it would.

beats.headline: A pass signed in his name
beats.text: Two pieces of paper from the quest. A Gate Pass: "The holder of this pass is doing this on my orders. Magistrate Featherfall." Carrying it keeps the mindless swordsman guards off your back, provided your criminal enterprise is not too overt and you stay in the township that issued it. Beside it lies a blood-soaked letter in necroscript, which Mordecai cannot read but recognises: something an undead magic user writes. His conclusion: "I'm thinking you two might have a lich problem."

beats.headline: He cares about being disturbed
beats.text: Mordecai's briefing: the surviving skyfowl villages keep the old structure without the oversight, so Featherfall is this village's big boss man. Getting to him means teleporting onto the town hall's third-floor landing and walking through a mall for skyfowl. His clerk, Miss Quill, declines to disturb him about a dead woman who is not skyfowl; it was like this under her late husband, and it is like this now with Magistrate Featherfall. The door to his chambers is magically locked.

beats.headline: A dark cleric, in theory
beats.text: The working theory, formed after an attack by shambling berserkers that Crawler Carl assumes were sent by "our Featherfall friend." The town's lead skyfowl is a dark cleric who commands the undead. The city elves of the 201st Security Group worship the skyfowl as living angels, which makes them free, enthusiastic labour for herding his undead minions. Knock out that support network first. Nobody has yet explained the dead women in the alleys.

beats.headline: Credited with his death
beats.text: Dynamite through the magistrate's floor. The notices arrive: a public official assassinated, control of the Medium Skyfowl Settlement, a new title, Magistrate Carl. The only NPC the notices name is Miss Quill, and a bronze boss box says one of the two was a neighbourhood boss. But the quest is still open, which should mean the head bad guy is still alive. Crawler Carl's conclusion: they killed an NPC they never met, blew his house to bits, and still have not finished the job.

beats.headline: Upside down in a bone dreamcatcher
beats.text: Found in the magistrate's quarters, at the centre of a room of krasue bodies hanging from the ceiling: Magistrate Featherfall, naked and emaciated, lashed upside down in a massive dreamcatcher of bone, featherless wings spread, a clear fluid dripping from beak and eyes. He had been there some time; the body was being mummified. Lootable Corpse. Former Magistrate Featherfall. Dark Cleric. Level 32. A fireball scatters his ashes. No neighbourhood map turns up in them, so by Crawler Carl's reckoning he was not the boss.

beats.headline: A dark fetish, by her account
beats.text: A dying krasue woman, mortal while Crawler Donut's torch holds the curse back, sets the record straight. Featherfall was not the one who did this. He has been hanging on that thing the whole time, and he was dead when she arrived. His body was turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill has been running the city all along. She is the real magistrate.

beats.headline: Killed by the feedback
beats.text: Remex, Soul Leech Capacitor, tells it as a story he has rehearsed. Featherfall never liked the guards and wanted more control over them; after Remex retired and handed him the perch, he asked what it would take. After Remex died, Featherfall asked Quill to help cast a spell that would pull a dark cleric back from the dim as a capacitor. He took the Night Votive position with Quill in the room, too close to the amplifier. The feedback killed him. Quill planned it. She kept his office running with a forgery spell.

tagline.text: Pustule is a level-30 hobgoblin who runs Hobgobs and Boom Sticks in the Silk Road market. She has an open sore on her cheek, a unicorn on her T-shirt, and excellent hearing.
Pustule said her hobgoblin smoke curtains would work far better than the goblin kind, and she was right.

beats.headline: Hobgobs and Boom Sticks
beats.text: For the record: Pustule, hobgoblin, level 30, proprietor of Hobgobs and Boom Sticks in the Silk Road market. Mordecai's introduction: a little odd, but harmless, and "you'll be seeing a lot of each other." About six feet tall, an open sore on her cheek bubbling black and green ooze onto a threadbare pink T-shirt with a unicorn in sunglasses, and a smell of rot and sickness. Crawler Donut's first assessment, whispered: "She's ugly. Like really ugly."

beats.headline: Tiff the muskrat
beats.text: Goblin smoke bombs are crap, in her professional opinion; a hobgoblin smoke curtain works much better, and she has none tonight. What she has is hob-lobbers, twenty-five for 500 gold. In passing she mentions watching her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat. She was friends with Tiff, the muskrat. Her mother died of it. Crawler Donut, charisma at full, talks her down from 1,500 gold to 1,000 for the lot.

beats.headline: She licks the jug
beats.text: Crawler Carl sets one of his boom jugs on her table for a valuation. She rubs the side, makes a whimpering noise, and licks it. Then, all business: the material cost is much too high, and plain bottles of moonshine would be worth much more. She would sell it for about 7,500 gold and pay half that. "Beware of meteors!" she calls after them. From about fifty paces away, she also hears Crawler Donut's assessment of her. "Excellent hearing."

beats.headline: Ten smoke curtains, as promised
beats.text: She came through. Three more boxes of hob-lobbers, all impact-detonated, and a ten-pack of hobgoblin smoke curtains, round fused bombs meant to outperform the goblin kind. Crawler Carl buys all ten. That night, on a rooftop beside the magistrate's building, one of them fills the whole area like a heavy fog, far better than the goblin kind. Pustule had been correct.

beats.headline: On the way down
beats.text: On the stairs off the third floor, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met there. Signet the half-naiad. Quint, the possum-faced pharmacist. Pustule, the hobgoblin explosives dealer. GumGum the orc. Miss Quill. Little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf. A week on that floor, and it felt like a millennium.

beats.headline: Pus by the set
beats.text: Supplier note. On the Silk Road, Crawler Carl bought a few sets of hobgoblin pus from Pustule, the magical detonator, and he is burning through the expensive stuff. Inside a submarine a city boss is about to swallow, he yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, fits a piece of pus in its place, duct-tapes a potion to it, and seals the lot in the captain's minifridge.

tagline.text: Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire is the name on Katia's sponsorship notice, and so far it is the only thing anybody knows about her.
Princess Formidable is the youngest sister of Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. Her first gift to Katia is a single crossbow bolt that does nothing special unless it lands in a god's eye.
Princess Formidable is in orbit over Earth, on the line to the Syndicate Council, demanding that the failsafe be triggered even though she would die in the blast herself.
Princess Formidable took one of her father's warships to trip the failsafe by hand, and the AI pulled her off it and made her a level-1 crawler. She has chosen Earth's surface.

beats.headline: A princess on the notice
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Katia has a sponsor, and the notice reads, in full, Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire. That is all it reads. Over pho, Crawler Carl works the rest out from something Zev told him: if Prince Stalwart was disowned for his failed attempt on Carl, the sister would be next in line. He assumes this is the sister. Crawler Hekla, it is noted in the same conversation, has drawn some interstellar ranch.

beats.headline: One bolt, for a brother
beats.text: Subject's first benefactor box is opened by a group that knows nothing about her except that she exists: youngest sister of Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart, two princes who want Crawler Carl dead. Inside is a single crossbow bolt, one of a hundred, which does nothing special unless it lands in a deity's eye. Crawler Carl reads the description and draws his conclusion aloud: the sister is not a huge fan of her big brother.

beats.headline: Ten bolts, emergency rate
beats.text: An emergency benefactor box, silver, from subject. Mordecai says it must be opened at once, and that it probably cost the princess a sizeable chunk of her net worth. It holds ten bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Then Crawler Katia puts the first of them into the head of Maggie My, who has been riding inside another crawler and is standing over Crawler Carl with a celestial grenade in her hand. Crawler Katia's reading of the ledger: his sister is spending a lot of money to stop him.

beats.headline: A scroll of worship, by emergency
beats.text: Another emergency box from subject to Crawler Katia, and this one holds a scroll of worship. Emergency boxes are opened immediately, so Crawler Katia reads it immediately, and becomes a worshipper of Eileithyia before she sees the goddess is sponsored by Huanxin Jinx. Crawler Carl files two observations. The princess apparently does not get along with the rest of her family. And she is still sending boxes, so she is not in the dungeon on the ninth floor with them.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: Emergency session of the Syndicate Council. Subject, on the line from the cockpit of her cruiser in orbit, demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map before the AI infects the center system. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she points out that she is in orbit and would die too. She would love her family deposed, she says, but this is bigger than that. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. It passes at 86 percent, and she is muted.

beats.headline: Her father's warship
beats.text: Reported by King Rust himself, under parlay. Subject and a detachment of Skull Empire marines have taken one of his cruisers, and it is about five hours from the monitor station orbiting Venus. She has told the entire Syndicate she means to go in and trip the failsafe by hand. She has told them the rest as well: the Skull Empire manufactures the satellites and builds back doors into everything it sells. Rust asks Crawler Carl to plead with her, on behalf of the people of Earth, to stop.

beats.headline: Level 1, in a very small room
beats.text: Subject arrives in Orren's office upside down, three feet off the floor, in her space suit, and raises an arm weapon at the liaison. The AI, wearing Growler Gary, has pulled her off her own ship. Her info box reads Level 1, Orc: her father is dead, Stalwart is king, and six of his children stand ahead of her now. She learns the failsafe is already disabled. Offered death, the Scolopendra Club, a cabaret's backstage or Earth's surface, she chooses the surface, and teleports away with a crack.

beats.headline: The crew presses the button
beats.text: Zev has the news a few hours old. Subject's ship went on to the station without her and stopped there. When the princess did not return, a few orcs went in and triggered the failsafe themselves. Nothing happened in this system. But at the exact moment they pressed it, the Aryl system, where the previous crawl was held, went dark, and its tunnel node switched off. Zev says that has never happened before in history.

beats.headline: Next in line, if the yacht goes
beats.text: Succession, by Rosetta Thagra's arithmetic. Stalwart is dead, which makes one of his children king, and those children are aboard a yacht Rosetta's side has agreed to destroy in exchange for a pin number. If that is done, the Skull Empire falls to subject, provided she is still alive somewhere on Earth's surface. If she is not, it goes to the Maestro, disowned or not. Rosetta feels ill about the children.

tagline.text: Gore-Gore is a level-40 ManTauR and the Ochre Line's train engineer, with four arms, a great deal of shouting, and a devotion to Grull.
Gore-Gore answered every question, called the crawlers saboteurs, and went into the third rail. He left behind a key, a map of the whole ochre line, and Katia four fingers short.

beats.headline: Out of the tipped engine
beats.text: For the record: the derailment works. The engine car of the ochre line train lies on its side, and out of it climbs Gore-Gore, level 40, a ManTauR: about eight feet of man with a second, smaller man where the neck should be, four arms in all, streaked in blue paint. He hails the brother, the sister and the fine Princess, takes them for passengers who survived the wreck, and gallops off onto the platform shouting about sustenance and mead.

beats.headline: What happens at 435
beats.text: Charmed by Princess Donut, subject talks. Passengers should get off at 433, the last transit station. At 435 the employees disembark into a tunnel back to base, the Kravyad prepare them for the portal, and the portal does something to memory that human resources is said to be looking into. Nobody rides the first car except engineers; anyone else in it, he would be honour-bound to slay. Blades come out of his wrists to make the point. Then he goes into Club Vanquisher for mead.

beats.headline: Hail and kill
beats.text: Subject comes back out of Club Vanquisher calling the crawlers saboteurs, a ram-headed cleric waving from the door behind him, and the system stages it as VERSUS: neighborhood boss, train engineer, adherent of Grull the war god, berserker extreme, level 40. He swats Mongo to low health with the flat of his blades. When Crawler Katia steps in front of a blow meant for Crawler Carl, part of her arm spins away. Crawler Carl assumes it is only armour.

beats.headline: Grounded on the third rail
beats.text: Every punch from Crawler Carl's gauntlet carries a chance of summoning Grull, and the odds have climbed to 10.5. Subject, down to about a fifth of his health beneath two wrecked cars, announces that he feels it in his chest: he has been blessed by the gods. A ten-second timer appears over his head. Crawler Carl drop-kicks him in the lower chest. He goes back across the tracks and into the third rail, and the next thing on the screen is Winner!

beats.headline: What he leaves behind
beats.text: Looted from the corpse, which a clockwork Mongo has dragged clear of the live rail: 498 gold, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, the Ochre Line Engineer's Key, and a neighborhood map of the whole ochre line, stations 11 to 435, every train on it. Also left behind, at the top of the stairs: four of Crawler Katia's fingers, taken when she blocked his blade. When she healed, they did not come back. She can build more from other parts of herself.

tagline.text: Vernon is a level-32 dwarf and the Yellow Line's conductor. "Employees only," he says, without looking up from his drink.

Vernon carried a jacket full of drawings of his wife and a growing pile of gold. He went up in flames in car five when the fire ants poured out of Princess Donut's prize, and Carl says there never was a wife.

beats.headline: Employees only, says the dwarf
beats.text: For the record: car five of the yellow line train is the conductor's, and the conductor is Vernon, dwarf, level 32, drinking. His duties are to take care of the train and to be in charge of its employees. In practice the engineer does not listen to him, the janitors try to eat him and the porters are in their own little world, so he drinks until the end of the line and then does it again. He asks the crawlers to leave. Then he notices Princess Donut is royalty, salutes, and his drink goes flying.

beats.headline: The loop, as far as he knows it
beats.text: At station 435 everything goes fuzzy, and subject finds himself on the platform at station 10, the yard, climbing aboard again. He cannot say how much time has passed. He is not looping himself, he reasons, because a Brain Amoeba scar stayed with him; the train is, because a bottle poured out returns to its shelf. A Goateo once stayed aboard past 435 and was found as a skeleton. The engine car is locked. Nobody gets in without an engineer's key.

beats.headline: Ten gold, every trip
beats.text: Anything aboard on his first day resets each loop, and anything he carries stays with him. So subject has a jacket full of identical drawings of his wife, and several hundred gold grown from the ten coins on his nightstand: each trip pays him the equivalent of ten trips. He could go home from the yard any time. He is staying until he cannot hold any more gold, before one of the other dwarfs finds out and tries to weasel onto his train, and then he means to go home to his wife. One day.

beats.headline: Fire ants in car five
beats.text: Station 116. Crawler Carl unzips Princess Donut's prize suitcase on subject's counter, and the Find Traps notice arrives too late. Literal Fire Ants, level 1, pour out in impossible numbers, and the drawings of his wife are the first thing to burn. The moonshine explodes. The crawlers get out through car four onto the platform. Subject does not. A flaming wave sweeps over him, and the train picks up speed and disappears into the tunnel, burning.

beats.headline: No wife, says Carl
beats.text: Crawler Katia says what there is to say: poor Vernon, he was saving up money to buy his wife a new house. Princess Donut's complaint is that the bugs burned up her prize. Crawler Carl answers both. There is no wife, he says, and there was no prize; the ants were the prize. He resolves to train his Find Traps skill, which did warn him, but much too late.

beats.headline: A memory with nothing under it
beats.text: Crawler Carl reopens the file while questioning Madison, an employee who has been putting in a lot of mandatory overtime. When Vernon told him about his wife, Carl had taken her for a made-up phantom. Now he has a theory to put under it: this floor's NPCs were given false memories without a proper foundation, stories as paper-thin as the background of an NPC in an actual game. Asked whether she has ever been to her own apartment, Madison says of course she has. It has just been a few days.

tagline.text: Gwendolyn Duet is a voice in the crawler chat, telling everyone that the bomber guy warned them all and to fall back to the train lines.
Gwen is a level-27 Boring Ol' Fighter, which is the class's actual name, and she is the only crawler in bubble 543 who answered Carl. She calls the rest of her quadrant dumbasses.

Gwen is about forty-five, five feet tall and solid, from Canada, with a spear over her shoulder and an old tattoo on her forehead. She wants to wash the sandcastle away, and she has been made to wait.
Gwen fights beside Katia like one half of a pack, and she has been hailed as one of the crawlers who liberated the subterranean quadrant.
Gwendolyn Duet was instrumental in the crawlers' survival among the bubbles. She lies dead on the next floor, among elves and bugs, after the fight against Imogen.

beats.headline: Fall back to the train lines
beats.text: For the record: when the station floors fall away and the Krakaren monsters pour up into the rooms, the chat fills with screaming, and one voice in it is giving orders. Gwendolyn Duet tells everyone that the bomber guy warned all of them, and to fall back to the train lines and hold the choke points. A crawler named Ronaldo Qu objects that he did not say it would be this bad. She asks whether he is on crack, and tells him to clear the chat.

beats.headline: The only reply from 543
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks who else is in bubble 543 and gets one answer. Subject: human, level 27, a Boring Ol' Fighter, which is the class's actual name, and vocal in the chats. Her team rolled the land quadrant and the Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage, with giant snakes, spiders, scorpion men with nipple rings, and four levels of walls. She holds a Club Vanquisher ring, being a proper lady by her own account. Her name takes up half his screen, so he renames her Gwen.

beats.headline: Face to face at the sandcastle
beats.text: Crawler Carl lands and finally meets subject: about forty-five, solid, five feet tall, from Canada, a spear over her shoulder, an old double-v tattoo on her forehead and straight-line tattoos down her hands. Level 34 now. Her team has breached the last wall and found a drainage wheel that would wash the castle away, and Crawler Katia has kept her waiting nearly a day so the crawlers can go in the hard way, through the lightning door. Crawler Katia's assessment: once Gwen decides something, she becomes a bully about it.

beats.headline: This is where I point out
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Princess Donut are in the castle's basement with the ceiling coming in when he sends subject a note. She asks whether he means electrify it. No, he answers, hurry. Tran opens the valve part way, and the castle goes like sand under a garden hose, taking the two of them down into the water quadrant with it. Subject's first message afterwards: this is where she points out that if he had simply let her open the valve in the first place, they could have avoided whatever that was.

beats.headline: Hailed in the throne room
beats.text: Sandstorm, feral pazuzu, and subject and Crawler Katia moving as one, like a pair of pack hunters, after days of fighting these mobs together. Crawler Carl had subject run the long lead from the drain to the lightning tower. The strike turns the beach to glass around their ankles and sends the current through the temple's water. Bubble Notification: the subterranean quadrant is liberated, and the crawlers hailed for the throne room are Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi and Morris Sp.

beats.headline: Into the dry tomb
beats.text: Subject has a new spear, and is pretty stoked about it. With the tomb drained, she and Tran take their team into the subterranean level, loot what is left of the tomb raiders and open the tomb of Anser: a sarcophagus holding the skeleton of a goose in a golden, unenchanted crown. Quetzalcoatlus's corpse holds a partial map of the sixth floor. Her team agrees to join the party Crawler Katia means to form, which Princess Donut notes, given that the two of them are always fighting.

beats.headline: Wants to murder Louis and Firas
beats.text: Crawler Katia's report on her party: big personalities, and they do not all get along. Florin broods like Crawler Carl. Britney has given up on everything. Subject constantly wants to murder Louis and Firas. When Crawler Carl suggests subject for a job Imani may not want, Crawler Katia refuses; she is not going to let Gwen do it either. The party heads southwest the next day, away from elf territory and deeper into the wild.

beats.headline: A grapefruit-sized hole
beats.text: The pulse rifles on this floor are a downright menace: portable guns firing an unending supply of full-strength magic missiles. Bautista almost had his head blown off by one the day before. One has also punched a grapefruit-sized hole clean through subject's midsection. The system does not treat the wound as an amputation, so it heals, and she is back to her normal, grumpy self.

beats.headline: Beside the knock-knock joke man
beats.text: Gwendolyn Duet is dead. The body lies among dead elves and bugs in the fight against Imogen, next to Cleiton, the knock-knock joke guy. Tran is alive beside them, dragging himself away and screaming; his legs are gone. Crawler Carl reads a scroll over him, and the legs do not grow back. Imogen is still on her feet atop a pile of corpses. Crawler Carl records subject as the woman who had been instrumental in their survival on the previous floor.

beats.headline: Mean, and liked
beats.text: Filed for the survivors. Tran, who lost both legs in the final moments of the previous floor, is more upset about losing subject than the legs, according to Crawler Katia; they had been together since early on. He does not answer Crawler Carl's note. Princess Donut's eulogy, delivered straight after the fight, begins: poor Gwen, she was mean, but I liked her.

tagline.text: Commandant Kane of the Dreadnaught Wasteland is so far only a name in someone else's file: his great and favoured uncle is held under Hump Town as the guarantee of a peace.
Commandant Kane holds the twin of Henrik's watch. His dreadnaught has been taken apart over Hump Town, and all that stays aloft is a single house under a balloon, with him and his daughter inside.
Commandant Kane, a level-55 Dirigible Gnome, lies half eaten across his own kitchen table, torn to shreds by Denise. On him are a watch and a letter from the Glass Wizard.

beats.headline: Named in his uncle's file
beats.text: Subject enters the record secondhand, in my file on a chained gnome: Wynne, great and favoured uncle of Commandant Kane of the Dreadnaught Wasteland, held hostage by the dromedarians as a guarantee of peace. Per the same file, the Dirigible Gnomes were once a peaceful race who took to the clouds to be left alone, and whose long history left them forced to choose between fighting and being wiped out. They chose to fight.

beats.headline: The watch's twin
beats.text: Subject owns the twin of the pocket watch Henrik carries. Once a day its alarm sounds, and its mirror shows the Commandant making a sign with his fingers; the hostage names a time, the hands are set, and subject's watch moves to match. It is a code the dromedarians do not understand. The two sides also trade written messages this way. His ambassador, Leon the Commissar, inspects the hostage with a spell against changelings. The Bactrians' collateral was different: his daughter's favourite pet swine, sunned daily for the farseers.

beats.headline: Just him and his daughter
beats.text: Subject received a message in Henrik's name: Wynne gravely ill after a resurrection spell, a travelling healer bringing him out beyond the walls. Leon came to meet it. Subject's dreadnaught was then taken apart over Hump Town. What stayed aloft was a single house under a balloon. Through a farseer, Crawler Carl saw a girl of about ten at its door, and behind her, before it shut, the Commandant. Crawler Carl announced he wanted subject's watch, on the theory that three watches together make the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: One of three holders
beats.text: The quest arrives with subject's name in it. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. Each has a piece of the artifact; take them, collect all three, put them together. Reward: oh boy-oh-boy. Subject's air force is grounded. His house has floated up until it is wedged against the top of the bubble, with no obvious defences, and by the party's count only two living creatures aboard: the Commandant and his daughter. Crawler Carl declines to shoot it down, because he wants the watch intact.

beats.headline: On the kitchen table
beats.text: Lootable Corpse. Commandant Kane. Dirigible Gnome. Level 55. Ripped to shreds by Denise. Found draped across his own kitchen table, half eaten, while his daughter set up a lemonade stand beside him. Asked why Denise killed her father, the girl pointed at the kitchen sink. Crawler Carl looted him by accident, falling into the body when the house lurched: 5,030 gold, a Mysterious Watch, and a Letter from the Glass Wizard telling him his bombs were weakening the temple, and to stop, and think of his people and his child.

beats.headline: A drawing in a frame
beats.text: Addendum, from the house. On subject's nightstand, in a frame meant for a photo, a drawing he had put there himself: Kane, a woman gnome, and a baby. His watch is bronze, carries a bone symbol, and does not tick. His daughter, waking from his potion, supplies the rest. Denise killed him. He knew she was going to. He said there was nothing he could do, told her to make lemonade, and when she started to cry he gave her the potion, and she was not scared anymore.

tagline.text: Wynne is a level-50 Dirigible Gnome Flesh Mechanic, chained under Hump Town's town hall as a guarantee of peace. Tortured and starving, he begged the crawlers to kill him quickly.
Wynne is dead. Princess Donut raised his head for half an hour and Katia played the rest of him, so that the party could ride his return ticket up to the Wasteland.

beats.headline: Chained beyond the boundary
beats.text: Subject: Wynne, Dirigible Gnome Flesh Mechanic, level 50. Located in a chamber below the town hall, past the shimmering quadrant boundary, chained to the wall. Elderly, no red hat, sickly, scabbed, half starved. Great and favoured uncle of Commandant Kane. A healer able to bring the long dead back to life, if only temporarily. Held by the dromedarians as a guarantee of peace. Crawler Carl was issued a quest to free him, reward a Silver Quest Box, and could not reach him from his side of the boundary.

beats.headline: Kill me fast
beats.text: Five crawlers arrived at a run on the subterranean side. Subject told them the human was no human but a changeling named Henrik, who was torturing him, drugging him, trying to make him give flesh to Quetzalcoatlus, and he would not last much longer. He said he had the map to the temple, and that if they killed him they would have access. Kill me fast, he said. Crawler Low Thi did, with a spear, over Crawler Carl's objection. Quest failed. There was no map.

beats.headline: Years of the code
beats.text: Posthumous addendum, from Henrik, under Princess Donut's charm. Each day a watch alarm sounded and the gnomish Commandant made a sign in its mirror. Subject was shown the sign and named a time; the hands were set to it, and the gnomes knew he lived for another day. He cooperated for years. Only when he was moved to the chamber below the town hall did he understand the arrangement had changed, and stop. After that he was drugged with mushroom, and had to be fed more every day.

beats.headline: Half an hour of Second Chance
beats.text: Subject's corpse was retrieved by the tomb raiders a few hours after death, chewed by beetles, face untouched. Princess Donut raised the head with Second Chance, reaching his level 50 from her 33 by way of her glass cannon class, for half an hour. Katia Grim supplied everything below it. Leon the Commissar laid a hand on the snapping head, found no changeling, and said it appeared to be a ghoul. Then the spell timed out behind his back, the head went to dust, and Katia grew a new one before anyone looked.

beats.headline: Looking better already
beats.text: The message Crawler Carl had Henrik send the Commandant, for the record: Wynne cast a resurrection spell for the dromedarians, became gravely ill, and a travelling healer would bring him out beyond the walls. By the time the balloon rose, the Wynne curled on the floor of the basket was Katia Grim in duct tape, keeping quiet because her voice work was barely passable, curled up to hide the extra height. Leon leaned down to look at her. He's looking better already, he said.

tagline.text: Vadim and Britney are the last two survivors of the water quadrant. They say there are horrors down near the ocean floor, and they do not want to go back.
Vadim Zbar is a level-28 Kuhli Gut Rearranger, a healer and rogue covered in daggers. He was a cosmetic surgeon before all this, and he knows the way back down to the Akula.
Vadim led the dive to the Akula. When the boss came, he ran upstairs, sealed himself in, and fired the last escape pod up into the jellyfish.

beats.headline: Horrors near the ocean floor
beats.text: Subject enters the record by name only, relayed by Firas. The water quadrant left two other survivors, Vadim and Britney, and neither wants to go back in. They say there are horrors deep down near the ocean's floor. Firas had told them about Chris. Neither of them was surprised, which is also on file.

beats.headline: Class: Gut Rearranger
beats.text: Subject: a level-28 spotted, gecko-like Kuhli, which Crawler Carl believes is a fish. Class: Gut Rearranger, a healer and rogue. Sheaths of daggers from head to toe. Cosmetic surgeon in the old world; Crawler Britney was in his office for a consultation when the collapse came, and the two of them were outside taking before photos. At the tavern Crawler Britney said she would rather die than go back into the water. Asked the same, subject said: I'll go. Crawler Tran asked him whether he owned a red shirt.

beats.headline: Fifty children, reportedly
beats.text: Gossip entered into the file via Langley, via Katia Grim. Doctor Vadim was, or had been, famous in the Ukraine: television commercials, billboards, clinics, and lawsuits over botched surgeries. Langley says he has something like fifty children and is known for impregnating his clients. Crawler Carl concluded that if true, subject was a weasel, and not someone to go into danger with while carrying a bounty. Subject's own manner through all the briefings: matter-of-fact and emotionless. He was going anyway.

beats.headline: The way into the Akula
beats.text: Subject supplied the route. The Akula lies 500 meters down, nose fastened to the necropolis, its torpedo tubes pumping the ocean in. A docked mini-sub blew after his party took the bridge. He and Britney had free dived those depths on water-breathing scrolls. His map showed monster types, never the full sub. He rode down in Katia Grim's diving bell, cast Torch as they entered, and led the way in. Crawler Carl kept him in front on purpose, lest he lead the party into a trap.

beats.headline: Chris never talked much
beats.text: Swimming the flooded corridors, subject gave his account of the first assault. Skeletons of bugbears, robots, and only three survivors. Chris was higher level, never talked much, fought fiercely and without emotion, insulted them when they did not do as he said; Britney never liked him. Chris took the boss's note, with the key code to the escape tubes, and did not show it to them. At the bridge a ghost screamed through the bulkhead, and subject went down with his health in the red. Tran healed him.

beats.headline: Pulled out of the hole
beats.text: The Akula was torn free of the necropolis and dragged into the deep. The hull rolled onto its side and subject fell with Crawler Tran into the room behind the bridge. Crawler Carl called them through to loot the dead changelings and make for the last escape hatch. The four of them then stood looking out of the bridge window at something the size of a mountain. Subject's mugshot went up on the special event broadcast beside the others.

beats.headline: Up the stairs, alone
beats.text: The lights on the bridge went out. Crawler Carl called for Torch. The broadcaster Kevin answered instead: Vadim is running away, and Carl has not noticed yet. Subject had gone up the stairs toward the one remaining escape pod. Crawler Carl messaged him that they were inside the shark and the hatch would not work. Subject did not answer. Crawler Carl sealed his own group in the stateroom and had Crawler Tran tell subject to seal himself in upstairs. Subject did so, and kept not answering.

beats.headline: The last escape pod
beats.text: After the boss fell, subject answered. I'm sorry. I panicked. I sealed the room. The door would not reopen with water behind it, and his oxygen warning gave him five minutes. Crawler Carl told him to raise a shield spell, then suggested blowing the hatch for him instead. The pod launched, curved upward, and punched through the top of the shark into a sky of giant jellyfish. Oh god, they're in the pod with me. The pain amplifier. Warning: This message is from a deceased crawler.

entities.name: Lusca
entities.role: City boss · fifth floor, water quadrant

tagline.text: Lusca is the Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, a level-82 city boss the size of a mountain. She is a mouthbrooder carrying a boatload of hungry babies, and the crawlers are floating in her mouth.
Lusca tried to swallow the Akula whole, and Carl's shell spell drove her into the ocean floor. She lies there on her side, with her upper jaw peeled back and a line cut through her brain.

beats.headline: Something covering the port
beats.text: The Akula was pulled free of its hole in the necropolis and dragged down past 550 meters, with boss music playing and no boss yet. A sucker the size of half the bridge window pressed against the glass. Then subject came into view: a shark the size of a mountain, glowing, tentacles flowing behind. Crawler Carl identified it as a sharktopus and observed that Princess Donut would be angry to have missed it. His second observation was that this was not good.

beats.headline: Straight from Hayes 17
beats.text: A Special Event boss battle, streamed to subscribers, in a new beta format with live commentary from Kevin and Magnificent Troy. It's Lusca, Kevin shouted, taken from the depths of the water moon Hayes 17. My own description, for the record: Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, level 82 City Boss, a single mother carrying a boatload of hungry babies in her mouth. The male who dragged the crawlers down already got his and is long gone. Lusca herself already ate. The babies, however, need feeding.

beats.headline: Ten minutes for the babies
beats.text: Subject is a mouthbrooder, per Magnificent Troy's diagram. She had snapped the Akula in half, and the crawlers were floating in her mouth. Once she clamps onto something, her babies get about ten minutes to eat their fill, and whatever is left goes to mama. The cartoon that followed showed the rest of the process in several stomachs, ending with a skeleton in heart-covered boxers and a crying cartoon Donut. Both announcers fell about laughing. A ten minute timer slammed onto the screen.

beats.headline: The babies turn on each other
beats.text: Juvenile Octo-Shark, level 30, minion of Lusca. In each birthing of two to three thousand pups, one or two survive, because in time they learn their siblings are delicious. Crawler Carl's depth charges landed a direct hit; Kevin said she would shrug them off. Then Crawler Carl set off a potion of bloodlust in the water, the babies went into a feeding frenzy, and the kill markers multiplied. Subject swam on in circles around the quadrant at about 35 kilometers per hour. Crawler Carl wondered whether she knew most of her babies were now dead.

beats.headline: Mama swallows the Akula
beats.text: The timer hit zero and subject raised her head to swallow the Akula whole. At that moment Crawler Carl fired his shell spell down her throat. It did not punch through as intended. She stopped dead in the water, as if she had hit a wall; her upper jaw bent back over her own eyes, cartilage snapping, and teeth shattered as the spell drove her into the ocean floor. Every remaining baby died as the inside of her mouth turned outside. She was grievously wounded. She was not yet dead.

beats.headline: Cleaved through the brain
beats.text: Katia Grim fired a rocket and held on to a live twenty-five-foot buzzsaw, and the three crawlers pinwheeled out of subject's mouth and back through her exposed upper snout, cutting her like a hot knife through calamari, until one of her tentacles slammed them into the seabed. Lusca, the Octo-Shark, now floats on her side on the ocean floor, upper jaw peeled back and split, a jagged red line through her tiny little brain. Winner. From her corpse: a Map of the Stars.

beats.headline: The Akula's cheat
beats.text: Addendum. Crawler Carl holds that each of the bubble's four quadrants was built with a cheat, a quick way to kill everything: the knock-knocks under the Wasteland, the hidden drain on the sandcastle, the lightning tower for the final castle. He was never sure what the easy win for the Akula was meant to be. He suspects it had something to do with subject.

tagline.text: Tish's furious postscript sits under a council letter to Ghazi: they needed that artifact to defeat Scolopendra, and he threw it away for a woman who is not real. She hopes he dies in pain.
Ghazi's last letter was addressed to Tish. Princess Donut feels sorry for her, but Samantha says Tish almost ruined everything.
Tish, Ghazi's ex, still works at the college in Larracos, and Samantha wants to use Louis's new toy to kill her. Princess Donut rules that none of it was Tish's fault.

beats.headline: A postscript in another hand
beats.text: Subject exists, at first, as a postscript. Below a council letter to Ghazi, in a different script: Ghazi, you fucking idiot. She told him this would happen. They needed that artifact, without it Scolopendra cannot be defeated, and all he could think about was his cock. She does not forgive him. She was there the whole time, and she guesses she was not enough. She hopes he dies in pain. Do the right thing. Signed, Tish.

beats.headline: So you are from the college
beats.text: Princess Donut read the postscript over Crawler Carl's shoulder and took it personally. When Ghazi came round she jumped on his chest: he had Tish all along, and he left her for Lika, who is not even real. Ghazi's eyes went huge. Tish? So they were from the college? Crawler Carl advised that nobody knew the story beyond one letter. Princess Donut's closing remark on the subject, as Ghazi explained his wife: if Tish could see you now.

beats.headline: A letter addressed to her
beats.text: The pages Katia Grim took off the Mad Dune Mage open as a letter to subject. I know you hate me, but please listen. Hope is not lost. He writes that he was asked to use the box to pull the whole island into the Nothing, and refused, because all three pieces of the artifact would go with it. He sets out how the gate works. If his plan succeeds he dies, and she receives the letter with the winding box and can send another expedition.

beats.headline: Tish almost ruined everything
beats.text: Princess Donut, to the doll head of Samantha: she does feel bad for Tish, who really seemed to like him. Samantha's view differs. Tish? Tish almost ruined everything. Take me to her. Crawler Carl completed the sentence for her with the threat Samantha uses on everyone, the one about mothers, and Samantha burst into tears.

beats.headline: Samantha's arch enemy
beats.text: Larracos, the college, a visitor pass queue. Samantha rolled by Louis screaming after a woman named Tish and promising to kill her, and Katia Grim gave chase past guards carrying a Despondent debuff until she had the head cornered. Crawler Carl asked twice who the fuck Tish was. Princess Donut had forgotten about Tish entirely until that moment. Samantha, restrained: she is a woman scorned, and her need for vengeance against her arch enemy, Tish, is the only thing she knows.

beats.headline: Still at the college
beats.text: Crawler Carl reconstructs the file. Ghazi wrote to the college here in Larracos for help, and the letters showed that his ex-girlfriend, Tish, still worked there, and that he had left her for the doll. Samantha proposes to use Louis's new toy to kill her. Princess Donut rules that subject should not be held accountable; that was one hundred percent Ghazi. If she is not allowed to blow Tish up, Samantha adds, Juice Box is going to hear about Louis's affair. Louis says: what?

beats.headline: Blamed for a child
beats.text: Samantha reports that her child has died in the acid, and that she felt it go. She blames herself for her lust and her anger. She also blames subject: it is actually Tish's fault, she is quite certain, which is why afterwards she intends to plant, up at the college, the nuke she stole. Crawler Carl rules that she is not nuking anyone. Samantha moves on to how to save Louis, which is more urgent.

beats.headline: The room next to hers
beats.text: Samantha is redecorating Carl's room in the personal space, which she has claimed, since he never goes in there and she won it in the breakup. Its chandelier came from the room next to Tish's room, borrowed on an occasion Samantha does not intend to discuss, because everyone would get mad. Bucket Boy points out that it is a swing. Anything can be a chandelier, Samantha says, if it lights up and you attach it to the ceiling.

entities.name: Denise
entities.role: Borough boss · fifth floor, air quadrant

tagline.text: Denise, the Feral Goose Mother, is a level-53 borough boss in a frilly baby-blue bonnet. She lingered too long in the Nothing and her mind is all but gone, and while she is in the Commandant's house, magic does not work.
Denise killed the Commandant, made every spell useless, and went head first into a garbage disposal with one second left on the clock.
Denise, the goose Carl shoved head first into a garbage disposal, loved reading to children. The System mentions it only in passing, while describing somebody else.

beats.headline: Ripped to shreds by Denise
beats.text: Subject enters the record on another creature's corpse tag: Commandant Kane, ripped to shreds by Denise. Asked who Denise is, the Commandant's daughter, eyes dilated, said she went out to get some food. When the child's pig was taken, her father kept getting her new pets. Not the gerbils; they were mean. Other things, including ol' Denise. She's okay. She's no Sausage. Do not tell her that, though. She gets jealous.

beats.headline: When she gets mad
beats.text: The floating house began to sink. That's Denise, the child explained: when she gets mad, magic stuff doesn't work, and the balloon goes down; she is probably on the roof. Somewhere in the house the clockwork Mongos exploded early and tore up the real one. Mordecai briefed the party: no spells, no scrolls, no gauntlet, gear protections gone. Scrolls on the bleeding Mongo did nothing. Then the flying lemonade glass moved itself away from Crawler Carl's hand, the window slammed, and the doors locked.

beats.headline: The Feral Goose Mother
beats.text: A white goose in a frilly baby-blue bonnet and a torn, bloodied shawl. Level 53 Borough Boss. Plucked from the seventh floor when her grandfather, emperor Anser, used a magical gate to bring his people here, she lingered too long in the Nothing, and her mind is all but gone. The gnomes captured her without knowing who she is. Neither does she. She can prevent magic from harming her. She is an environmental. She needs to protect children. Mostly, she wants to kill everybody.

beats.headline: No health bar
beats.text: Mongo got her by the neck and shook her; she bounced back up. Subject's bill opened into a flower of razor teeth and fired them like a shotgun. A banger ricocheted off her bill. No health bar appeared. She took a chunk out of Mongo, and a thrown mug knocked her off the kitchen table and launched the Commandant's corpse into the ceiling. She chased the party upstairs, hopping one step at a time, and put two barbs in Crawler Carl's face. Only then did a health bar appear, barely dented.

beats.headline: The garbage disposal
beats.text: The lemonade was a trick: Wild Goose Chase, magic doesn't work, it's lemonade. Crawler Carl hit subject with the pitcher, took her teeth across the face, lost his left eye's sight, and held her bill shut by hand. He remembered the child pointing at the sink, and saw the two switches. Subject went into the drain face first. Princess Donut flipped both switches. The timer stopped at one second. The Commandant's quarters are occupied. The Air Quadrant is liberated.

beats.headline: Supposed to drown her
beats.text: Post-mortem. The house's power crystal had shut itself off under subject's anti-magic aura; with her gone, the balloon began refilling on its own. Princess Donut's assessment of the fight is that the goose was meant to be drowned, in the sink or the lemonade pitcher, and not put through the garbage disposal. When the child woke, she told the party her father knew Denise was going to kill him and could do nothing, and asked for another potion.

beats.headline: She loved reading to children
beats.text: Entered into the record in passing, while I described somebody else. Sometimes a villain has a good quality buried somewhere. Remember Denise the goose, the one shoved headfirst into a garbage disposal? She loved reading to children. That makes two bosses Crawler Carl has now killed who loved reading to kids. I raised it to point out that the creature I was describing at the time has no qualities like that at all.

tagline.text: Circe Took of the Hive is listed as the moderator of a CrawlCon panel called Crawling Through the Ages, and that is the whole listing.
Circe Took is a minor hive queen, a mantis who was once a famous hunter and now owns an amusement park. Carl killed her daughter Xindy on her very first hunt, and she is moderating his panel.
Humiliated on her own panel, Circe Took has sponsored the god Diwata. Vrah's mother is coming into the game.
Circe Took came down inside the god Diwata for her daughter's sake. In the final arena Princess Donut stripped the god away from her, and her own children tore her apart.

beats.headline: Moderated by Circe Took
beats.text: CrawlCon programme, as printed. Panel: Crawling Through the Ages. Crawlers both new and old lead a discussion on the current state of the crawl, followed by a Q&A, special guests to be announced. Moderated by Circe Took of the Hive. Next item down, an autograph session with Crawler Carl, refunds guaranteed if he does not survive long enough to attend. The listing does not mention any history between the moderator and the fan favourite.

beats.headline: A daughter lost on her first hunt
beats.text: Briefing from Zev, four hours before the panel. Circe Took: a minor hive queen, a mantis, outside both the military and the Burrower clan. She started out as a hunter, was quite famous for a while, and is now a businesswoman who owns an amusement park. Crawler Carl killed her child: Xindy, Vrah's little sister, on her very first hunt. Zev's assessment is that the mantis people are overly dramatic about everything and a hive queen probably has ten thousand children. Her advice: avoid the subject of her government.

beats.headline: The table, cut in two
beats.text: Panel footage. Circe Took is the size of a mantaur, with folded blade arms a metre long, and she can see Crawler Carl before the audience can. Her opening remark is that his luck is a dishonour on the hive. Her second is an arm brought down through the table beside him. Had he truly been sitting there, it would have cut him in half. She then introduces the panel, talks over the author mid-sentence, and informs the room that the season's top crawler has not long to live.

beats.headline: Bored to death, on air
beats.text: Circe Took lectures for almost ten minutes on the history of the crawl, the Hive's place in it, and the danger of the Indigenous Species Protection Act. Crawler Carl bangs his head on the table and announces she has succeeded in boring him to death. When he turns to her dead child, she orders him cut off. A robed woman at the back says no, and Circe accuses the room of a setup to mock her child's death. She is not the Maestro, she says, and she is not so easily trapped.

beats.headline: About the other daughters
beats.text: The robed woman leaves. Circe Took calls her a godsdamned bitch and swears to kill her, throws the broken piece of table at the wall, and heads for the exit. Crawler Carl asks the room for the best way to kill Vrah. She freezes where she stands while the audience answers: eight left, one of them a male who stays in Zockau to deal with the trade representatives, seven warriors including Vrah, all Dark Hive. Invited back to the table, she hisses that she means to hunt down, personally, whoever harms her other daughters, and stomps out.

beats.headline: Gone apeshit, in transit
beats.text: Gossip at the autograph tables, logged because it is consistent. Circe Took has, in the phrasing of the attendees, gone completely apeshit about the whole business with her daughter, and is on her way to the Earth system to do something about it. Crawler Carl cannot see what: it is too late for her to join the hunters on this floor. A reporter begins, "With the news that Circe Took is possibly..." and is shoved aside by a naga before finishing.

beats.headline: The note under the note
beats.text: A benefactor box note, with extra words that appear once Crawler Carl's Escape Plan skill activates: Circe sponsored Diwata. Vrah's mother is coming into the game. The box was sent before the party failed the odious creeper quest, so she had already bought the god before winning the court case to free her daughter, and meant to come for him whatever happened. His reading: she needs to save face. He humiliated her and injured her daughter, and somehow she is still talking to Vrah, which is against the rules.

beats.headline: A squirrel out of a hunter
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports from outside a church. A green explosion, a bush with a giant flower pod, and inside the pod a hunter, who swallows the blood and bark of the dead tree guards and swells until he bursts. Out of the gore comes an antlered squirrel covered in hunter pieces: Diwata, sponsored by Circe Took, on a five-minute timer. It flies away like a rocket. Crawler Carl works out the destination. Her daughter. His word for the errand is a cure.

beats.headline: Babies, sent out into the world
beats.text: Baby mantises are everywhere outside the castle. Crawler Elle McGibbons has the rest of it from a hunter with no eyebrows: Vrah's people tricked his brother into walking into the temple, where he was used as the birthing vessel for Diwata. They murdered another hunter to cure Vrah of a venereal disease. And now, in Elle's words, the Circe bug lady is having actual flesh-and-blood babies and sending them out into the world. Nobody present knows what becomes of them when the floor collapses.

beats.headline: One more mantis in the castle
beats.text: Crawler Carl assembles it all at once. Diwata, which is to say Circe Took, is in the castle, blended in with the rest of the mantises, there to help her daughter. She meant to break the connection between the goodwill ballrooms and end the party, but a capacitor keeps them running. The fallback: fill the castle with nymphs, give the hunters back their magic, and wait for somebody to break the peace seal, so that Vrah can get clear in the chaos.

beats.headline: Died shrieking his name
beats.text: Corner four of the final arena: Diwata, burning, looking exactly like her true identity, a baby mantis halfway out of her. Crawler Princess Donut casts Laundry Day at level fifteen. It cannot harm a god, but the god is only armour, and the spell strips it off the driver. Diwata leaves the floor. Circe Took stands up wet and covered in bubbles and begins to say she does not need the god's protection. A dozen of her own children fall on her before she finishes. She dies shrieking Crawler Carl's name.

relations.note: Moderator of Crawling Through the Ages

entities.name: Dmitri and Maxim Popov
entities.role: Nodling crawler · two brothers, one body

tagline.text: Dmitri and Maxim Popov are ninth on the board: a nodling, Illusionist and Bogatyr, level thirty, with a hundred thousand gold on their head. Two names share one line.
The Popov brothers are one two-headed nodling, now fifth on the board. Dmitri has become a Visionary while Maxim is still a Bogatyr, and they fight with a magical meteor hammer.

Dmitri and Maxim Popov are fraternal twins who share one body, because their game guide never mentioned that choosing the nodling race would pull Dmitri's brother in with him. Dmitri would very much like to meet the cat.
The Popovs were killed in the final arena and split into two baby nodlings about a year old. Children are not allowed in the crawl, so they were ruled ineligible and removed.

beats.headline: Ninth on the board
beats.text: Top-ten leaderboard, bounty column. Ninth: Dmitri and Maxim Popov, Nodling, Illusionist and Bogatyr, level thirty, one hundred thousand gold. Two names, one race, one level, one bounty, one line. Tenth is Ifechi. The list does not explain how two crawlers came to share a single entry. Crawler Princess Donut does remark on it: if those two get to share a spot, it is not fair, and she and Crawler Carl should both be number three.

beats.headline: Butting heads with Cichociemni
beats.text: Odette, on air between floors, running through the season's best stories for the benefit of her guests: the battle with Grull, Prepotente and Miriam Dom losing a province boss twice, Quan Ch, the hilarious but ultimately tragic fight between Lucia Mar, Florin and Ifechi. Not to mention the Popov brothers butting heads with team Cichociemni. That is the entire mention. It establishes a feud, and that the feud made television.

beats.headline: Recruiting archers for a hunt
beats.text: Langley, level thirty-two and leaving with his group, lays out their options for the next floor. Large groups are forming. The Popov brothers are looking for archers, because they want to hunt down team Cichociemni, who have been preying on weak crawlers, and the player-killer groups need breaking up before they get too strong. His group may join them. On the board that closes this floor the brothers are fifth: level forty-three, two hundred thousand, doubled.

beats.headline: A giant foot on the replay
beats.text: Recap footage from the last moments of the previous floor. One of the two heads screams "Murderer!" The two-headed nodling is fighting a big, leather-clad man with a shaved head and a war gauntlet, and their magical meteor hammer is about to brain him when a giant foot crashes into the scene and everyone goes flying. It belongs to Slit. The target runs for a stairwell. In the specialisation rundown, Dmitri goes from Illusionist to Visionary; the other half remains a Bogatyr.

beats.headline: What a nodling does at death
beats.text: Tsarina Signet, explaining her ogre Areson, supplies the relevant biology. When a nodling dies, it splits into new creatures, one per head. They emerge as toddlers and grow quickly, and the original body remains. A nodling may have anywhere from two heads to six, usually two or three. Crawler Princess Donut asks whether that is what the Popov brothers are. Crawler Carl says yes, and that it raises more questions than it answers about two men who picked that race.

beats.headline: Whisked away to a convention
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons, briefing at speed. Team Cichociemni killed their own leader because he did not want them to be a group of murderers, and that leader was friendly with the Popovs, before Dmitri accidentally picked a race that combined him with his brother. The Popovs had Cichociemni cornered when the brothers were whisked away to CrawlCon. They have been gone two days and are back tomorrow. According to them, they are sharing a table with Crawler Carl.

beats.headline: Kapitan Whiskers, orange
beats.text: The green room. About seven feet tall, broad, grey and callused like an elephant. Dmitri, the Visionary, has the right side and a bare, round head. Maxim, the Bogatyr, has a beanie and the meteor hammer. Fraternal twins: not identical before, not identical now. Dmitri is disappointed the cat has not come, and Maxim apologises for him. Dmitri had just got a cat, orange, named Kapitan Whiskers, the day before it happened. Maxim complains they were promised food and given one chicken.

beats.headline: For the thousandth time
beats.text: Autograph session. Dmitri signs everything and chats; Maxim looks bored. A blob child asks whether it was really an accident. Dmitri, for the thousandth time: their game guide, Hongrish, told him the nodling was a good choice that would give him an extra life. He did not say it would force his brother into the same body. When the child presses a theory about a television programme, Maxim threatens it with his foot. Asked about Bogdon Ro's death, Maxim says cheerfully that the man got what he deserved, and he is sorry others had to die too.

beats.headline: The hammer in the ballroom
beats.text: The ballroom fills with gore and mantis nymphs from above and below, and the Popovs swing their meteor hammer through the room, twisting and shouting as they destroy the nymphs. Around them Prepotente throws potion bottles, Li Na throws chains for her brother to dance along, and Florin works a shotgun from the corner until the blasts become a beat. Mantises still surge in through the doorway.

beats.headline: I miss my cat
beats.text: The final arena. A meteor hammer brains an elf coming at Crawler Carl out of the dark, and the Popovs stand guard while Crawler Princess Donut's mass heal drags him back awake. Then a sambhur, one of the elf mounts, on fire and covered in nymphs, comes spinning through the dark on one of Queen Imogen's spells. Its antlers go straight through the two-headed ogre. The double crawler hits the ground beside Carl. "I miss my cat," Dmitri says, just before he closes his eyes.

beats.headline: Nodling Yearling, ineligible
beats.text: Katia Grim's Find Crawler skill points into a pile of gore, and under it are two fat, naked baby ogres about a year old: Maxim and Dmitri Popov, Level X, Nodling Yearling. They wake. The label over them reads Ineligible, and they blink out. Zev's explanation to Crawler Carl: children and pregnant crawlers are not allowed. Their game guide had them pick that race knowing this would happen. They have been transferred to the kinder facility on the surface. They are free.

beats.headline: Their mother's apartment
beats.text: Race day, through a building of apartments the AI has furnished as what-ifs for crawlers it finds interesting. Crawler Elle McGibbons reports from one of them: she believes it is the Popov twins' mother's apartment. There are pictures of Dmitri and Maxim everywhere, the mother's eyes are sewn shut, and so are the eyes of a poodle. Prepotente notes that the mother appears to have been a big fan of pink.

relations.note: Her foot broke up their fight on the recap

tagline.text: Hunter Zabit owns a Night Weasel Scout called Tootsie, and the rest of the invisible pack that came with her.

Hunter Zabit is a level-66 Atoll Beastmaster with four arms, no mouth and twenty-five scalps. He hunts to pay the upkeep on his people's habitat, because without citizenship, oxygen and land are not rights.
Hunter Zabit turned invisible in the final arena beside the landmines he had just laid. Carl cast Tripper, and Zabit was torn in half by his own traps.

beats.headline: Tootsie, and the rest of them
beats.text: Night Weasel Scout, level twenty-five, name Tootsie, dragging itself on one leg across the ground toward Crawler Carl's paralysed face. This a pet of Hunter Zabit. A gang runs to about twenty, invisible, with scouts that smell prey across hundreds of kilometres and disable it for the rest. A lava-rock crawler stamps Tootsie flat, Mongo eats the second one, and Crawler Princess Donut raises a dead weasel against its own pack. Carl is carried into a pub like luggage, and a guard's poison cloud clears the street outside.

beats.headline: Twenty-five scalps at the counter
beats.text: Chaco's prize counter. Hunter Zabit: level sixty-six Beastmaster, an Atoll, tall and thin with four arms, three fingers to a hand, no mouth, a dozen nostril holes, and a trap module bandolier on his belt. He speaks by signing into something hidden in his clothes. Yes, the weasels were his. He meant to catch the top prey early, and the party killed his pets and his season with them. He collected twenty-five scalps anyway, and spends them: a drop shield for twenty, an invisibility pack for three.

beats.headline: For the survival of the Atoll
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks why he hunts people who are scared and weaker than he is. Hunter Zabit's answer, for the record: for the survival of the Atoll. They are not citizens, so oxygen and land are not rights. The scalp money pays the upkeep on their habitat, and without it they would have to accept indenture under another system. This season's failure hurts his people. Some hunters revel in the killing; for others it is survival. He would object too, were the situations reversed.

beats.headline: Closing the semicircle
beats.text: Lucia Mar sits at the prize counter, chatting and waving her tequila bottle as if every crawler present were her best friend, with a ring of crawlers around her to keep the hunters off. The hunters form a second semicircle around that one: Vrah, Hunter Zabit, and several draconians, moving in. Chaco backs himself against the wall. Crawler Carl reads the play at once. They are trying to get Lucia to break the peace seal.

beats.headline: His own landmines
beats.text: Final arena. Hunter Zabit's dot is on the map, and when Crawler Carl moves in, the hunter points at him, shouts something that does not carry, and vanishes. Carl stops. He has seen that belt, and he knows what was in it. He casts Tripper. Several landmine traps go off at once, and Zabit reappears, torn in half by his own trap, laid seconds before. The announcement follows directly: team two, eliminated.

relations.note: Spent his scalps at the prize counter

tagline.text: Viscount Fog was a great hunter of vampires, now deceased, who set out to exterminate a new bloodsucker named Miriam Dom. It went badly.

Viscount Fog was the star of a programme called Blood Hunter. A spell bounced between him and Prepotente until it came out inside out, and he was left frozen and cursed. He died when the sun went down.

beats.headline: The mount he left behind
beats.text: Sierra, Northropi Vampire, level sixty-five neighbourhood boss, is a Bereft Minion of Viscount Fog. The description is the file on both of them. The great, now-deceased hunter of vampires trained Sierra never to leave his side, and together they hunted the scourge that took his village and family. When he learned of a new bloodsucker named Miriam Dom, he set out to exterminate her. It went bad. Sierra was injured by the bloodsucker trying to save him, fled, and is now what they both hated.

beats.headline: The star of Blood Hunter
beats.text: Crawler Miriam Dom, in a forest clearing, fills in the rest. Viscount Fog was an elite hunting her from the moment she landed, the star of one of the programmes run inside the dungeon, called Blood Hunter. His first attack came while she and Prepotente were fighting Big Tina. The climax was written in advance: the vampirism curse would spread through the forest, Fog would kill its progenitor, which is Miriam, and every infected dinosaur would be cured, stopping an apocalypse.

beats.headline: Community Pool, returned to sender
beats.text: The second attack. Prepotente reads Community Pool, which moves an infection from one party to another and would have made Fog the head vampire. Viscount Fog counters, throwing the spell back. Prepotente's Opposite Day ring throws it at Fog again, and Fog has a ring of his own. The spell ping-pongs between them several times in under a second. Both are stunned repeatedly, and the stuns compound. Past the third, the sufferer becomes Fragile, and the slightest damage kills.

beats.headline: Dust, at sunset
beats.text: The bounced spell came out inside out, as spells that bounce often enough do. Viscount Fog took a new debuff, Cursed Light Walker: where a vampire dies in light, his health seeped away out of it. Crawler Miriam Dom had him stunned and helpless and did not strike, in case he had one trick left that would take Prepotente with him. She did not need to. Frozen and unable to heal, he died when the sun set and crumpled to dust.

relations.note: His first attack came during the fight with her
A reflected spell, ping-ponged until it turned inside out

tagline.text: Theia is a goddess who turns prospective worshippers into balls of light and entertains them at her temple for weeks. She is Samantha's mother, and this season, for once, someone has sponsored her.
Theia's temple has named Crawler Carl a friend of the church. Samantha went to see her mother and found a male skyfowl driving her: Rectrix, an agent of the Open Intellect Pacifist Network.

beats.headline: A party in her pocket
beats.text: Rosetta's briefing on how a warlord disappears. One of two immortals can carry her to a temple; the goddess is named Theia. Her prospective worshippers become balls of light that fit in an adherent's pocket, and at her temple they are released and spend several weeks being wooed and partying. It is a loophole: step away from the war and enjoy the rest of it. Theia is not a goddess clerics use, so no crawler ever stumbles into her temple. A perfect hiding place.

beats.headline: Sponsored, for once
beats.text: Theia has a long history with the Ascendency and is a poor bet for the throne, so nobody ever sponsors her. This season someone did, in the employ of the Pacifist network, not Porthus. They bought her to protect Crawler Carl, because she is Samantha's mother. She was the god who appeared at the end of the fifth floor to kill Slit, when in theory she was enraged at Samantha. Rosetta believes Vinata usually picks her. If Vinata did this season, Theia would smite her court.

beats.headline: A boy eagle behind the altar
beats.text: The backup plan: Samantha was promised a way into her mother's temple, in the hope that Theia's clerics would help. She came out shouting. Her mother was an eagle, a boy eagle. A sponsored god may appear in its own form, and whoever drives Theia is a male skyfowl. Baroness Victory walks in and Samantha accuses her of momnapping. Victory's reply is procedural: sponsors making deities act outside their nature is cheating, and she has reminded both the Maestro and someone named Rectrix.

beats.headline: Friend of the church
beats.text: An achievement bans Crawler Carl from Club Vanquisher and from every temple, except his own god's and those that have named him friend of the church. Theia's is on that list, between Nekhebit and Yemaya. Carl works through the list for surprises. Theia is not one of them: the Open Intellect's agent, Rectrix, is driving her.

beats.headline: Not really your mother
beats.text: Samantha's recap of the previous floor, delivered at speed. Her plan was to say hi to, and possibly kill, her own mother, whose name is Theia. When she got there it was some skyfowl dude, who said, "Look, I'm not really your mother," and then clarified: Theia isn't. Samantha's reply, as she tells it: "Yeah, okay, weirdo." Then the club went nuts, and her recap moves on to the next item.

relations.note: Vinata's court usually hides in her temple
Named him friend of the church

tagline.text: Slit is a level-200 Feral Minor Demon, one of a harem thrown into the Nothing, and she is certain that Samantha slept with her king. She chased Samantha's head across the sky until a god plucked her out of the air and tore her in two.
Slit was torn in half by a god at the close of the fifth floor. Minge, who has just broken out of the Nothing, is her little sister.

beats.headline: A head the size of an arena
beats.text: Slit. Feral Minor Demon. Level 200. Thrown into the Nothing with many other demons, having wanted no part of the royal drama, but in love, and eons of madness have not been kind. The head is sports-arena sized, pink and scaled, trowelled in mascara and lipstick, trailing the stench of unfiltered cigarettes. She wields an electrified chain whip whose links are the size of semi-trucks. Her first words once in view, delivered to a sex doll head: "Samantha. You are so dead."

beats.headline: Fifty kilometres of bait
beats.text: Samantha demands a weapon. Crawler Carl instead jams her face-first into an Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot, a head-throwing attachment custom made for decapitated love doll heads, and throws her more than fifty kilometres. Slit screeches and follows, wings working to keep her gelatinous bulk aloft, dressed in leather and tassels the size of sequoias. Carl's reading of the item: it was built for the next floor, and whoever paid for it was forced to send it early.

beats.headline: Picked up like a rodent
beats.text: As Slit chases the head across the dark, the sky cracks and a second god appears, physically huge, multi-armed, too distant to examine. It ignores Samantha, plucks Slit out of the air the way someone lifts a small rodent, and rips her in two. The tearing is audible from kilometres away. Her chain whip crashes down. Then the god and the corpse are gone. Samantha pops back at Crawler Carl's feet furious that it was her kill. The god, it emerges, was her mother.

beats.headline: Her king, allegedly
