beats.text: Post-mortem, per Samantha. Slit is part of a demon harem. Samantha was describing her exploits with her own king and Slit thought she meant hers, so Samantha told her that she and Slit's king had all sorts of weird sex, which upset Slit and all her sisters. The Nothing is filled with the harem, and they all hate her. Anytime one gets out, expect this. Slit was one of the little ones. The sister to look out for is Gash.

beats.headline: A foot in someone else's fight
beats.text: Recap footage from the last minutes of the previous floor. The Popov brothers are about to brain a man with their meteor hammer when a giant foot crashes into their world, knocking everyone off their feet, and jumps away. Crawler Carl recognises it as Slit, on her way back toward the party's bubble after Samantha. The man the brothers were fighting uses the distraction to escape into a stairwell.

beats.headline: The little sister gets out
beats.text: The Desperado Club. Someone loses the knife game, the Nothing opens to take him and tears, and out comes Minge, level 225, higher than Slit ever was, sized to the club rather than the sky. Crawler Carl remembers Slit as kaiju-sized, level 200, and ripped in half by Samantha's mother. Samantha supplies the family tree: Minge is Slit's little sister. They used to be friends. It is sad, really. At least, she adds, it was not Gash.

relations.note: Where the harem is kept

tagline.text: Paz Lo is a level-45 human Santero and a worshipper of Ogun, in silver plate armour and a backwards baseball cap. He travels with his cousin Anton and the nun they both protect.

Paz and his cousin were guards at a women's prison, not prisoners, and Sister Ines was an inmate there. Burned by his own god and dying, Paz asked to be let go, and she jabbed a squad flag into his neck and made him a card.
Paz Lo was a card in a goddess's war, and he was turned against her. He put an arrow in Ysalte's eye and blew himself up at her neck, and the System credits him with the kill.
Paz Lo, the God Predator, is a level-101 card that killed a goddess. At the collapse the card was torn up, because that is what he asked for.

beats.headline: Armoured, and afraid of the cat
beats.text: For the record: Crawler #8,199,454, Paz Lo. Level 45. Human. Santero. Worships Ogun. Silver plate armour on platform boots, a backwards baseball cap, and a wide-eyed, scared look. His party meets Carl's in Havana hostile, and it is Paz who explains why: the cat once said she would kill them all when she met them, and it got back to them. Tserendolgor's file on him, for Carl: cousin to Anton, protective of the nun, and the owner of a directional self-destruct spell.

beats.headline: The Turtle holds, just
beats.text: On the walk to the beach Paz supplies facts: Caribbean monk seals are extinct in the real world, and his papa worked on a sugar plantation. The plan against the seal is that Paz walks up, draws it, and roots himself inside his Turtle, a shield he cannot leave until the timer runs out. The seal, a kung fu picket sentry called Yago, very nearly breaks it. The moment the Turtle ends, Paz is on his feet with a mace twice his own length, and the seal lands on Carl in time to be flagged.

beats.headline: The dead wake for a Santero
beats.text: Paz would rather listen to Carl and wait outside the Colón Cemetery. Anton tells him not to be such a woman, and Paz sighs and clanks after them, then argues at the gate until they turn back and do it Carl's way. The warning arrives inside: the presence of a Santero has aggravated the already-unsettled dead. "Not again," Paz mutters. Princess Donut would like to discuss communication skills. The mobs come from every corner, all of them for him, and the squad runs and fights its way to a pub saferoom with the cemetery following its Santero.

beats.headline: Asked for by name
beats.text: A straw-skirted orisha named Asojano stands in the saferoom, health draining, and addresses his request to Paz alone. The spirits here are plagued by his presence; he is trapped; the Santero can free them by repairing his shrine in the temple at the centre of town. Paz stands frozen, mouth open. Carl tells him in chat to say something. Paz says "Uh", twice, then asks what exactly he is supposed to do. Anton wants to flag the god at five per cent. Sister Ines wants no more false gods.

beats.headline: Carried out by a cretin
beats.text: Out in the street, Paz is the only one who takes the terrified debuff, and he says "Shit" over and over while Bomo tries to lift him. Bomo cannot, with all that plate on, so at Carl's order Paz stows his breastplate and is revealed as a surprisingly skinny, shirtless man with a giant cross tattooed across his back. In the temple, with Asojano dancing over his rubble, Paz and Anton receive a quest from their own god: fix one shrine only, and not Asojano's.

beats.headline: The shunned mark
beats.text: The thorn room offers seven shrines. Paz grabs Anton, charmed half out of his head. Anton hurls the piece of Ogun's shrine out the door, and a chunk of Bomo's exploding armour bowls Paz over and breaks his grip. Paz shouts to fetch the piece. The god with the rooster offers him protection and a good time. He and Anton go to work propping a wooden sign for Legba until a glob of Asojano's goo hits them both. Then Yemaya's shrine is whole, and over each of their heads burns a flaming anvil: shunned.

beats.headline: A handprint from his god
beats.text: Ogun arrives in a bolt of lightning, leans down, and puts his hand on Paz's face. The skin sizzles off where it touches. The god heals him, then withdraws the healing: Paz is no longer under his grace and may never cure what he now carries. Go in darkness, the god says; beyond the veil you are alone and without armour. Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton, and Ogun crushes Anton's head underfoot. "No, cousin," says Paz, from the tiles. Carl gets a potion to his lips. Paz says not to waste it, drinks it, and says he has something to tell Carl.

beats.headline: What the sister is
beats.text: What Paz tells Carl, dying: her race carries a skill, Toxoplasma something, that makes people protect her and forget they have learned why. He and his cousin worshipped Ogun because a priest said it would stop the control. It did not. They were not prisoners. They were guards at a women's prison in Havana, and Sister Ines was an inmate there for poisoning every sister in her convent. The papers called her the Reaper of Havana. He adds that she is much better now, and that he would feel guilty dying without saying it.

beats.headline: Let me go
beats.text: Two or three minutes of health left, and Paz refuses a second potion. He has asked for forgiveness and thinks it was given. The fake god said he would be alone; he is sure he is not. When Sister Ines wakes she begs him to get up, then to not give up, since that is a sin. He says it is not giving up, and goodbye. "No," she says. "You're not leaving." She jabs a squad flag into his neck, and Paz becomes a card. Green. Common. She looks as surprised as anyone.

beats.headline: Summoned onto the field, begging
beats.text: Sister Ines summons her Paz totem onto the field and stacks a stout card on him. He looks as he did on the temple floor, the god's handprint still burned across his face down to the skull. "Sister," he calls up to her. "Please. No more." The giant snake she rides takes him in its mouth. She orders him to accept his suffering and use his self-destruct the moment this false god... and she never finishes the order: Quan Ch plays a card, Team Quiteria flees the fight, and Paz dissipates into dust.

beats.headline: He kills a goddess
beats.text: System message: Crawler Paz Lo has slain the goddess Ysalte, and is marked for death by every deity except her sworn enemies. Princess Donut's account, sent in capitals: the goddess had summoned a warped version of him and Katia had penned him in a shield. Then Katia gave him an arrow, he stuck it into the goddess's eye and blew himself up, with the blast concentrated on her neck, and her head came off. He vanished when she fell. The credit went to him regardless.

beats.headline: Ripped at the collapse
beats.text: The card has changed. Paz Lo. The God Predator. Level 101 Former Crawler. The goddess's equipment went to him and upgraded his armour. Princess Donut holds the card in the backup slot. Katia says rip it; that is what he wanted. Donut wonders whether to keep it past the collapse instead, since a squad may keep one card, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said when he was last summoned, and says no. Donut tears it with her teeth against Carl's shoulder. It goes in a puff of smoke. "Goodbye, Paz."

beats.headline: Osvaldo remembers him
beats.text: Twenty seconds before a race, a fire fairy is sobbing about what is real, and Crawler Osvaldo is in Crawler Carl's chat about the crystal he carries: Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. The one Paz killed. He was my friend, you know, Osvaldo writes. Paz and Anton and even Sister Ines. He adds that everyone who comes in contact with Carl dies, and supposes it is now his own turn. The lights go from red to yellow.

relations.note: In each other's chat
Good friends with his group
Asked by name to repair his shrine

tagline.text: Uzzi was Mordecai's brother, a skyfowl Storm Commander who guarded his party at a tenth-floor stairwell, seasons ago. He died there, with a dart in his breast, so that a god could be summoned.
Odette has now told Carl her part in Uzzi's death: an illegal deal with Huanxin to rig the game, which she broke at the last minute.

beats.headline: Guarding the last stairwell
beats.text: For the record, from a season long gone: tenth floor, collapse imminent, three crawlers at a stairwell, and a fourth still on his way back to it, that opens only when a storm god's magic touches a primed puzzle. Uzzi, skyfowl, Storm Commander, the class Mordecai once said his brother took on Odette's advice. He guards the others while Hold Steady keeps the puzzle primed and Chaco plays to draw the gods. His magic is limited. His party protection spell is what keeps the caustic rain off everyone. Odette notes that he chose the hardest of four paths, blindly.

beats.headline: See you on the other side
beats.text: The storm goddess is sponsored, and her sponsor has turned on them. Mordecai tells the group chat he has a plan and it will kill him; to Odette alone he explains it: his Final Blow skill can target the puzzle, so if the god hits him, the puzzle is hit too. "Uzzi, see you on the other side, brother." Uzzi's reply, in full: "Do not even dare." The brothers go back and forth while the timer falls. Odette knows that if Uzzi were told the other plan, he would be on board. There is no time to tell him.

beats.headline: The dart in his breast
beats.text: Chaco worships the goddess and tells Uzzi he is sorry. Uzzi turns to him, looks down at the Dart of Ophiotaurus in the bard's hand, lifts his head to the rain, and caws a war cry. He steps nearer the puzzle and spreads his wings. He understood. Chaco throws the dart into his breast and locks him in a containment with the puzzle. Mordecai arrives in ratkin form, falls to his knees at the shell, and calls his brother's name. The summoning tears Uzzi's chest open. Crawler Uzzi has fallen.

beats.headline: Odette tells her side of it
beats.text: Odette tells Carl the story in her own words, fast, with Lexis warning her the time is short: an illegal deal with Huanxin, brokered by Armita; a price raised; a deal broken at the last second; a goddess trapped in a containment, then killed by Chaco. Mordecai made the next floor, she says. Uzzi, Mordecai's brother, died. Since then she has watched him every chance she could, drinking himself into oblivion, crying over his brother. Her own verdict: this one I broke.

relations.note: His party's manager

tagline.text: Yemaya, the river mother, is one broken shrine among seven, and it should be blue. Katia has told Carl that he must repair it, because it is the only way to get the Crown of the Sepsis Whore off her head.

Yemaya, Goddess of Rivers, is a twin-tailed siren and a retainer of Eileithyia. Woken in her own temple, she handed out cards, and when Bomo said he missed his friend the Sledge, she sent him to Larracos.

beats.headline: A name in a message
beats.text: Mid-fight in a temple of broken shrines, Katia Grim messages Carl and only Carl: do not touch the shrine you meant to repair. There is another nearby. A broken shrine of Yemaya. Her name is Yemaya. Remember that. It should be blue. Repair it, Katia writes, and it helps save both her and the cat, because the Crown of the Sepsis Whore is on her head and this is the only way off it on this floor. The chat window closes before she finishes the sentence.

beats.headline: The seventh shrine of seven
beats.text: The thorn room reads its terms aloud. Shrine seven: Yemaya, the river mother, who almost reached the Halls on her own and could not keep her power. Repair her and she ascends, gifts each squad a special card, and her friend Eileithyia grants each crawler a boon. Carl chooses her. Bomo fits five or six blue pieces together like Tetris, and reanimated daggers carry the Sun of Reawakening to the top of the obelisk. System message: the Goddess Yemaya has re-ascended, and is welcomed into the family by all.

beats.headline: Ogun calls her his sister
beats.text: Ogun's charge against his two worshippers, stated calmly: they chased off Asojano, which might have saved them, but they also unleashed his sister back into the light, and that is unforgivable. The crawlers who actually built her shrine get only a warning to know their place. On his way out, having crushed one of those worshippers underfoot, the god gives Carl a message to deliver. Tell my sister I said, "Welcome back." Then he is gone in a shower of sparks.

beats.headline: Out of the fountain
beats.text: Goddess of Rivers Yemaya. Level 250. Locked; unsponsored this season. Retainer of Eileithyia. Invulnerable on this floor, and standing in her own temple, which is worse. She rises out of the fountain: dark-skinned, pointed ears, neck gills, two tails curving up behind her to meet in a heart. Princess Donut identifies her as the Starbucks logo. Carl settles on siren. Her first remark is for the corpse on her floor: Ogun killed that man in her temple, and she means to do something about it.

beats.headline: Gifts, and a cretin sent away
beats.text: She thanks Bomo for her shrine. She tells Carl his slugpox is her brother's work, done on purpose, and a healer can fix it. She gives cards: one to Sister Ines, and to Princess Donut The Thief, a mythical mystic card that steals from an opponent's hand, with an invitation to worship at her altar. Then she asks Bomo what he desires. More games, he says. No. The Sledge; he misses his friend, who is in Larracos. It is done, she says, and Bomo is gone, along with the stairwell spell the party was counting on.

beats.headline: Whose retainer she is
beats.text: Mordecai supplies the file. This season a sponsored god may recruit a second, unsponsored one to help once the games begin on the twelfth floor. Eileithyia's retainer appears to be Yemaya, and her sponsor, Huanxin Jinx, needed a way to get her resurrected. Crawlers were the way, and Carl was the crawler. You just did that for her, Mordecai tells him, and that is why she says she is going to help you.

beats.headline: Friend of the church
beats.text: Crawler Carl is banned from Club Vanquisher permanently, and from every temple except his own god's and those where he has been named a friend of the church. Yemaya's is on that list. That part is not a surprise to him: he and Princess Donut freed her on the floor above, and her mistress Eileithyia is on the list too. Some of the other names on it are a mystery to him.

beats.headline: Offered a place in her court
beats.text: Jamal, waiting outside a saferoom for a goddess, would very much like to see Eileithyia, and her retainer Yemaya, who he hears is the more beautiful. Carl says no. Eileithyia comes alone. Katia asks her for a pregnancy, and the goddess asks whether she is certain: come and assist her and Yemaya in her court instead, and she promises Katia is kept safe.

relations.note: Her retainer
Sent him to Larracos

tagline.text: Carl's father was a linebacker, which Carl offers as part of the explanation for his own size.
The last time Carl saw his father, he called him a bully and waited to be hit. His father laughed instead: Carl did not have to like him, he said, but Carl would respect him.
Carl's father was a weekend biker, covered in tattoos, and he walked out on his son more than twelve years ago. Carl has not heard from him since.
Carl has found his father in a recording from the summer before the collapse: dying in a hospital bed in an Iowa trailer, with a young wife, a small son, and a morphine overdose on its way.
Carl's father died before the collapse, of an overdose given to him by his second wife. His son will not say his name.

beats.headline: Linebacker, for the record
beats.text: Crawler Carl's explanation of his own size, supplied unprompted: six foot three, about 230 pounds, and genetics. His dad was a linebacker. His mother was five foot ten, and her father played center for Oregon State before becoming a prison guard. That is the whole file at present: a position on a football team, offered as evidence. The man himself is not described at all.

beats.headline: The Frogger machine
beats.text: Two items from the file, both supplied by his son. The man was covered in tattoos, which is why Carl never wanted any. And he owned an original stand-up Frogger machine out of an arcade. When his friends came over to smoke and drink and get loud, Carl's mother locked Carl in the basement with no television, no internet, and that machine. Hours and hours of Frogger. Crawler Carl types the word into his skills search to see what happens.

beats.headline: The last day Carl saw him
beats.text: Worrying about some crazy asshole with a gun, Carl is inexplicably reminded of it: the last day he ever saw his father. You're a bully, Carl told him. You're a bully and nobody likes you. It's why Mom left. Carl expected to be hit. By his own account he never had been, not once. The man laughed, and kept laughing, and that was enough. He did not need Carl to like him, he said. But Carl would respect him.

beats.headline: A weekend warrior
beats.text: Riding a glorified moped with his legs held off the hot sides, Carl pictures his father laughing at him and calling him a damn fool. He was a motorcycle guy. Not a full-time, leather-clad biker; more of a weekend warrior. Carl has not talked to or heard from him in over twelve years, not since the day he abandoned Carl and left him alone in the world.

beats.headline: A dent in the gas tank
beats.text: Prize four on the carousel is a 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide, red and beige, with a small dent in the gas tank. Carl knows the dent. As a boy he slipped coming up the driveway and knocked the bike over. His father was never physically abusive, Carl says, except that day: a belt, hard enough that Carl's underwear soaked through with blood. His mother cried and said they were going back to Texas. They never went. Carl cannot tell whether it is the real motorcycle.

beats.headline: Half a birthday present
beats.text: At the end of the fourth floor, with two people just gone to their deaths by their own hand, Carl thinks of his own mother. She attempted to kill his father and then herself, as a birthday present to Carl. She only half succeeded. He thinks, too, of everyone standing there with him, who jumped into certain death to save him.

beats.headline: The fish tank
beats.text: A sniper gnome in a round, black half-helmet reminds Carl of his father's. Soon after Carl's mother left, a month before his father in turn left Carl to fend for himself, the man ripped that helmet off and smashed Carl's fish tank. The mollies flopped on the floor while Carl cut his fingers on the glass picking them up. None survived. Carl did not cry, and that bothered him for weeks. The lesson he took from it: never get a pet again. All they do is die.

beats.headline: His motorcycle in an Iowa yard
beats.text: A single-wide trailer in a junkyard on a floating chunk of Iowa, and a vending machine bearing his silhouette: One Fight for Nine Tokens. Princess Donut thinks it is a fatter Carl with a mustache. In the yard stands the motorcycle, Georgia plates expired years ago, his prized possession. Carl lifts it easily, remembering how heavy it was the day he knocked it over. The yard is summer spliced into December, and along one side runs a row of alliums in pots, labelled in an elegant, feminine hand. His father would never have done that.

beats.headline: A dying man and a remote
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room: 140 pounds, yellow skin, a patchy white beard, cursing the Mariners at the television. A small boy is sent for cigarettes: "Move, or I'll make you move, boy." His young wife, in nurse scrubs, walks past without looking at him. Zev confirms it is a recording of that day. Crawler Carl leans in, closer than he has ever been to his father's face, and tells the man who cannot hear him that he is a bully, that nobody likes him, that Carl's mother tried to kill him and his new wife is about to finish the job.

beats.headline: Morphine, and the drapes
beats.text: His wife returns with a syringe and a new IV bag. "I have your medicine right here." "It's about time." "Yes," she says. "Yes, it is." Crawler Carl does not watch. From the master bedroom he hears the man say something desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear his final words. Carl takes the Glock, the keys, a folder of court documents and a Centipede cabinet, lights one of the Marlboro Reds, and sets fire to the drapes with the purple flowers on them.

beats.headline: The boss he was not
beats.text: The AI's announcement: the original boss for this battle was to be Carl's deceased father, who really had three smaller creatures inside him wearing his skin like kids in a trench coat. The AI overruled that. Nine heads on the hydra instead, and his is not one of them. His voice turns up anyway, in the enemy's deck: a totem called Alpha Male Carl, Carl with gelled hair, speaks with his father's voice. Not Carl's.

beats.headline: No name for him
beats.text: Crawler Carl tells Princess Donut what he saw in the trailer: his stepmother poisoned his father. Technically an overdose. Donut is confused: two different people tried to kill him? He must have been a real piece of work. She asks his name. "It doesn't matter. He doesn't deserve to have one. Not anymore." The hydra's loot hangs in the air over the burned spot where he died.

beats.headline: What his papers say
beats.text: Princess Donut, mid-negotiation across a table, mentions some legal papers Carl took from his father's trailer and has not read. She has. Carl's grandparents set money aside for Carl, and his father was trying to get at it without Carl knowing. A marriage certificate, for the father and his new wife. Court documents from several arrests. Together, she says, they paint a very distinct picture of who Carl's father was.

tagline.text: Asher is about six, living in an Iowa trailer in a recording from the summer before the collapse, and he draws lightning storms that destroy whole cities. He is Carl's half-brother, and Carl never knew he existed.
Asher's face was one of the heads on the hydra, which means he was taken in the collapse. Bea knew about him, and never told Carl.

beats.headline: The boy behind the hospital bed
beats.text: Subject: a boy of perhaps six, in a recording from the summer before the collapse. He stays behind the hospital bed, out of his father's sightline, and asks whether he can watch television now. Told to fetch cigarettes, he runs. "Asher! Get back here you little shit!" The photographs on the curio: a one-year-old on his father's lap, and a recent one with brown hair enough for two people, blue eyes, and that nose. Crawler Carl's conclusion takes four words: I had a brother.

beats.headline: Crayon drawings of lightning storms
beats.text: While his mother is busy with the syringe, Asher lies on his bed running a matchbox car up and down the wall. Crawler Carl tells him he is sorry he did not know, and that he is not forgotten. His hand goes through the boy's head. He takes the toys and the crayon drawings, airplanes and storm clouds whose lightning destroys whole cities, and concludes the boy is scared of storms. He leaves the heart-shaped candy box. His mother hugs him and mentions a birthday party. "Am I going to get a bike?" "We'll see, honey."

beats.headline: The lightning head
beats.text: The youngest face on the Reminiscence Hydra is Asher's. It asks, amplified and much louder than a child, "Carl, why didn't you ever visit me?" and then opens its mouth and fires lightning. It is the lightning head: the resistance and the attack. The other heads swing in to take the bombs meant for it, as though protecting it. Crawler Carl keeps telling himself it is not really the boy, and keeps throwing bombs at it; the other heads keep catching them.

beats.headline: Shi Maria takes the head
beats.text: Carl, on fire, thinks one thing: get the boy's head out of this, fast. Shi Maria turns her corkscrew neck and asks which of these morsels is Asher, third eye open. She finds it. "Carl, I wish I'd known you, too," the Asher head calls, just before it is swallowed and bitten off. Three heads remain. The spider's message follows: the echo of your kin has been muffled. He rests. I have done something for you, she adds, and soon Carl is to do something for her.

beats.headline: Collected in the collapse
beats.text: Crawler Carl works it out afterwards. Everyone on that hydra was dead: people collected in the initial collapse, his friend Sam, his landlord Mr. Roth, who lived alone, died alone. His father was not on it because his father was already gone. Asher and his mother were on it, which means they had been gone the whole time. Carl knew that was the likeliest outcome for everybody. The file has nothing that contradicts him.

beats.headline: Bea knew and kept it
beats.text: Princess Donut recognised every head, the boy included: Beatrice had his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother, who said to ignore the whole thing. Donut assumed a nephew. Carl corrects her: half-brother. Donut works out whose son that makes him. Carl works out the rest. The stepmother must have written to him, probably on Facebook. Bea saw it and never told him. Even after the cheating he had never been angry at her. He is now.

beats.headline: Someone to make proud
beats.text: The eighth floor is stripped into the sky with Crawler Carl inside it, and what he thinks of, looking down on the memories of people who do not know how few days they have, is Asher, the brother he never knew. He needs to make the boy proud. He was not there for him while he lived. He means for the boy's death not to be for nothing.

beats.headline: She's a child, too
beats.text: Imani is lecturing Bucket Boy about pain levels, and Crawler Carl is not listening. He is thinking of his brother, and of Asher's mother holding him after she poisoned their father, and of Princess Donut sobbing at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade. She's a child, too, he thinks, and then another: they are going to have to do some pretty horrible things just to survive. He has an order to compose.

relations.note: Half-brother
She knew about him and did not tell Carl

tagline.text: The Night Wyrm is the name on a ring Frank hands Carl: the Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering, made for the discerning crawler killer.
The Night Wyrm is a demigod outside the regular pantheon, worshipped by a cult called the Guild of Suffering. Carl wears the cult's spiderweb tattoo on his elbow.
The Night Wyrm heads the Guild of Suffering, and his job for Katia arrives in a hissing voice that calls her his little darling: kill Astrid, the assistant manager of the Desperado Club.
The Night Wyrm's real name is Hamed. He was Astrid's husband and is the father of two of the club's dancers, and he had his own wife killed by crawlers. His sons have gone after him.
Hamed is the new management at the Desperado Club. Every crawler is banned, and his bodyguards are not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers.
The AI lists Hamed among the NPC groups trying to take over its dungeon, and calls him a despot attempting a dungeon revolution for the early indentured.

beats.headline: A name on a ring
beats.text: Frank hands Carl a ring and does not make sense while he does it. The item's full title: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. For the discerning crawler killer, and its wielder can grow exponentially in strength, especially on the deeper floors. Whose name is on it, the item does not say. That is the whole of the file for now: a name in the possessive, on a ring meant for killing crawlers.

beats.headline: A demigod with a cult
beats.text: Carl touches the spiderweb on his elbow: the Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering, access to the Guild of Suffering. Mordecai frowns. It is a cult, he says, not a real guild and not a real church. They have outreach centres. They worship a demigod, the Night Wyrm, who is not a regular member of the pantheon; similar to Samantha. There is a memorial crystal involved, whose purpose has never been established, and all of it ties back to that ring.

beats.headline: My little darling
beats.text: Katia's Lock Box of the Night Wyrm needs one last seal: a job from the Guild of Suffering, whose entrance hides in the Penis Parade. She has one. Carl reads it off a slip of dried skin, in a hissing voice like a naga's: the Night Wyrm has a task for you, my little darling. The family with many eyes sacrifices the weak to support the many. We wish to remove the competition. Kill Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. Speak the details aloud and the contract is void.

beats.headline: A voice in a dark room
beats.text: Crawler Carl's report to Katia: a dark room and a naga-like voice. He never saw the speaker. Asked whether he wanted a job for the family, Carl said no. Asked whether he meant to kill Katia for the prize, no. Asked for a map of the club's secret passages, the voice said it had one, and spiders swarmed up Carl's arm and filled his map: tunnels, a hidden potion market, drug dens. The achievement at the door called him just some demigod trying to scrabble his way to the top.

beats.headline: Astrid names her husband
beats.text: According to the Night Wyrm, Astrid always uses the secret stairwell onto the middle floor. She flies past it to the regular stairs. Minutes on, cornered in a kitchen with a demon loose in her club, Astrid tells Carl: if you see my husband, tell him I did it to keep them safe. Him and my children. My husband is named Hamed, but he is known as the Night Wyrm. Don't tell him I told you his real name. His lair is on the top floor. The man who hired her killers.

beats.headline: She who brings the body
beats.text: Job update, in the hissing voice: the mark is dead, my little sweets. Excellent work. We are stronger because you have fulfilled your duty. Bring her filthy body to the guild. Remember, she who brings the body is she who gets paid. Crawler Carl, reeling, asks himself who these children of hers are. The body is in Katia's inventory.

beats.headline: What the family is
beats.text: Damascus Steel, on the floor of the Penis Parade: Astrid and the Night Wyrm are his parents, and Anaconda's. We were promised freedom, he says. He wanted to make sure she was dead. They are still married, she had so much, and he gets it all when they get out. Then both sons walk back into the cubicles, toward his lair. Crawler Carl's theory, offered to Katia afterwards: a family stuck in the dungeon a very long time, not generated NPCs but indentured, the father playing the Night Wyrm, and the motive money.

beats.headline: New management at the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive, at her post: crawlers are banned by order of the new management. He wants his first days to go smoothly. He is very particular and very serious about security, and has a whole slew of bodyguards, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers. His name is Hamed. Crawler Carl keeps his face still. The real name of the Night Wyrm, the head of the Guild of Suffering, husband to the late Astrid. His sons are supposedly still in the club, hunting him.

beats.headline: An audience granted
beats.text: Splash Zone, in chat, while Crawler Carl is busy separating a goat from a unicorn: he has asked for an audience with Hamed, the new leader guy, to see whether he can help find Splash Zone's wife. The guards said Hamed would see him. So he, Gluteus and Doctor Bones are going to talk to him. He is sending Bucket Boy over to Carl in the meantime.

beats.headline: Gone off the floor
beats.text: Warning: as this mercenary is no longer on this floor, they are unable to be contacted. Splash Zone. Gluteus. Doctor Bones. Same warning for each, and the daily fee still charged. Bucket Boy, the one they sent away, says they were going to see the new boss guy, Hamed, Anaconda and Damascus Steel's dad. Crawler Carl has no idea what that family is doing, and no time to find out. The notices do not say anyone is dead.

beats.headline: The guards fear him
beats.text: At the club door a troll guard named Klonder objects to letting a party of crawlers through. Hamed, he says, is going to kill them for it. A cretin from the house band, a door guard for a very long time, points out that tenth-floor crawlers kill you if you try to stop them, and Klonder bows them in. Inside, Crawler Carl lays out the problem. Hamed set him up to murder his own wife. His sons went hunting him and seemed to change their minds and join his cause. Now the other dancers have done the same. Carl does not trust him. He trusts them.

beats.headline: A despot, per the AI
beats.text: The AI's arbitrary list of the Big Six groups trying to take over or escape its dungeon. Under the NPCs, several offshoot groups, including "that Hamed despot and his ill-advised attempt at creating a dungeon revolution for the early indentured." Separately, and with a hint: Mitch, the croupier at the wheel and the strongest shadow mimic in the room, is still a baby at level 120, and was sent up by a redacted party to wreck Hamed's plans.

relations.note: His name is on it
Her guild contract
Her husband; ordered her death

entities.name: Architect Houston
entities.role: Warlord of the Madness · ninth floor

tagline.text: Architect Houston is the Viceroy leader of the Madness. He caught War Leader Arief's brother sabotaging his fortifications and tortured him, and Arief has sworn revenge.
Architect Houston sits unmoving at the end of the table, in a white mask marked with a small red teardrop and long robes that move as though the body under them is the wrong shape.

Architect Houston is a scientist first, and the only living creature King Rust fears. At the warlord council he explained, shaking with excitement, the creature with a thousand names that his people call the Beautiful Place.
Architect Houston died on his own surgical table, joined by his own machine to the corpse of a changeling, sobbing that he had found it at last.

beats.headline: A name a dwarf wants revenge on
beats.text: Entered into the file on the word of a dwarf named Arief, who swings his sword and promises revenge. Architect Houston: leader of the Madness, a Viceroy outworlder. He caught Arief's brother trying to sabotage the Madness fortifications, and the brother was tortured before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. Crawler Donut asks whether this is the one Juice Box decapitated at the pre-production meeting. It is not. That was one of his surgeons. Nobody has managed to get into Houston's lair beside the throne room, which is called his operating theater.

beats.headline: The quiet one at the table
beats.text: Six in the late Queen Imogen's kitchen for a field ruling: three warlords and their adjutants. Architect Houston sits at the far end of the table, unmoving. He was already in the castle, but not in the ballroom when it happened. His adjutant is a tiny floating bune named Opiee. His mask is white and featureless but for a small red teardrop, and his long white robes move as if the body under them is the wrong shape. When Crawler Carl rises with his fists clenched, Houston turns his head toward him. The neck creaks like a wooden ship.

beats.headline: Not culpable, by two votes
beats.text: Panford lays out the charge: Commander Stockade and Architect Houston used secured messaging to reach someone on the eighteenth floor, identified as Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness. Crawler Carl asks, loudly, whether that is his mom. Opiee calls the evidence circumstantial, quite damning, and not enough, and asks his warlord whether he wishes to confess. The masked warlord says nothing. Baroness Victory rules Houston obviously guilty and smart enough to let Stockade do the dirty work, and votes not culpable. Opiee agrees. The Madness is found not guilty of any wrongdoing.

beats.headline: A promise, then a rifle
beats.text: A direct message in the warlord chat: mention his mother out loud again, and Crawler Carl and his animal companion spend their last thousand hours on the amplification table in his surgical theater. This is a promise, he says. A second one: Carl is in mortal danger at this very moment and does not realise it. Then the Lemig Sortion falls, its assets go to the Madness, and Phase One engages. Houston is on his feet with his robes flung back: a bug-like body, six arms, two of them holding a rifle. He fires at Carl's chest. Carl dives, grabs a bag of cat food, and teleports.

beats.headline: The only creature a king fears
beats.text: Filed on the testimony of King Rust, on his saddle outside the Princess Posse lines. Among the reasons he gives Crawler Carl for why the crawlers cannot win: if the orcs did not annihilate them, that lunatic Architect Houston has been using this season's rules to open up his full arsenal. Then the old king admits it. Houston is the only living creature in this universe he fears.

beats.headline: The Beautiful Place
beats.text: At the warlord council Juice Box turns into a tall, black, armless thing with tentacles, and the room recoils. Architect Houston jumps to his feet and leans on the table, shaking, apparently with excitement. Then he explains it, over Epitome Tagg's objections. The creature has a thousand names: the Hag, the Unwashed, the Stalker, the Last Light. The Viceroys, who seek all understanding of life and death, call it the Beautiful Place. Some think it is what people see at the moment of death. Gaining access to it, he adds, is his life's work. Before the meeting is over he is on his feet, pacing.

beats.headline: Joined to a changeling
beats.text: His robes are gone, and so is his mask. Architect Houston is on his back on his own surgical table, and above him the arms of his machine, the Grease Monkey, hold the peeled-open corpse of a changeling named Namico. The machine is connecting the two of them. The System's note on it adds that Houston is prime of the Viceroys because he has made the most discoveries, most of them with this machine. Burcu lies bound on the next table, alive. Eight chained traps ring the room, and his death sets them off. Stay back, he tells Crawler Carl. This is my life's work. I'm almost there.

beats.headline: Died on his own table
beats.text: For the record. Crawler Carl crosses the theater by jumping from table to table. Houston begs him not to press the switch: the changelings are the key to the Beautiful Place, and it was right under their mandibles all along. Carl puts Burcu to sleep and frees her. As Houston's health drains, he sobs that he has found it, that it is really it. Carl throws a healing potion at his head, and he screams at what that has done. Burcu's table tips. Carl's bare feet touch the floor. You don't know what you've done, Houston says, and the traps fire. Credit for the kill: Warlord Carl.

relations.note: Cleared at a field ruling that thought him guilty
The creature he calls the Beautiful Place

tagline.text: Boomer is a former crawler whom Carl has never met, and he leads the 106th Bloody Leeches.

Colonel Boomer is a level-62 Elven Legate who survived one of the earliest seasons. He looks like a bulldog pickled for five thousand years, with elf ears and an unlit cigar, and he is banned from CrawlCon for threatening an orcish showrunner.
Colonel Boomer is running the assault on the Reavers, and when Carl tries to call Louis off his bomb run, Boomer tells his warlord to focus on his own operation.
Boomer is out of the dungeon now, on a screen aboard the Homecoming Queen, reading York a terrible poem about winning Faction Wars.

beats.headline: A pickled bulldog with elf ears
beats.text: Subject: Boomer. Elven Legate. Level 62. Colonel in the Princess Posse, commanding the 106th Bloody Leeches. A grizzled elf who survived one of the earliest seasons, bowed out on the tenth floor, and lived as a merchant on the sixth for many seasons before escaping. Crawler Carl's description is a bulldog pickled for five thousand years with elf ears and a cigar. Banned from CrawlCon for threatening an orcish showrunner during a panel. Wanted for a killing in a waystation brawl that started as an argument about the crawl. Crawler Donut reports he smells of cedar and acorns.

beats.headline: Cheese sticks and Monkeywrenchers
beats.text: The briefing, conducted with an unlit cigar. The Dream's bombardiers are cowards who run if you get near their chuckers. The cavalry is the thing to watch, and so is Epitome Tagg's household guard. Of the robed Madness troops going invisible, probably few are real Viceroys, but the invisible ones are Monkeywrenchers, and twenty of them once took two castles in the first hours. His boys and girls have had breakfast. Then Crawler Carl says let's do this, and Boomer lights the cigar, takes one very long puff, and fills the bunker with smoke. Fuck yeah, he says.

beats.headline: Command of the assault
beats.text: Warlord menu: command of the southern assault transferred to Colonel Boomer. His first order is to stop celebrating. Nobody fights harder than someone trapped, he tells the generals. Form up, do not push too hard, and let them think it is a stalemate rather than a surrender. They have maybe half an hour before the enemy either escapes or has to be killed. Then the generals get on with it, and Crawler Carl turns north to meet Party Planner.

beats.headline: Salty about the naga castle
beats.text: The southern trenches are filled with scrolls and the enemy artillery wrecked, and Boomer is sore about not pushing on to take the naga castle. Crawler Carl concedes privately that it would have been the safest and smartest play, and does not care. Boomer pulls most of the 106th north to help Florin. Then, on the band: a group of flyers that are not the Posse's have just buzzed him, moving low and fast toward the castle. They are Reaver paratroopers, and they arrive.

beats.headline: Time to move on the castle
beats.text: Walking back to the castle through un-looted Reaver paratrooper corpses, Boomer gives Crawler Carl the debrief. The map is a mess. The 104th is back on castle defence, but most of the mages were lost to the brain worm attack, and the magical defences are going to take a while. The good news is that the enemy is more fractured than the Posse. Now might be a time, he says, to move on the Operatic castle. That, too, is code, and Carl agrees it is time.

beats.headline: The Reavers are Boomer's operation
beats.text: The Reaver assault is Boomer's. When Crawler Carl wants to pull General Louis off a bomb run because of the dragon circling the castle, Boomer tells him no, over the private band. They have no No Disassemble missiles, the ground troops need that air support, and Carl handed operational command to Rosetta after putting Boomer in charge of this assault. Focus on your own operation, not mine. Carl belays his order and tells Louis this is Boomer's op, and to listen to him. Then Sledge reports missiles incoming on the Reaver castle.

beats.headline: Roses are red
beats.text: Out of the dungeon now, aged, on a low-resolution screen aboard the Homecoming Queen. He asks York whether he has written any new poems, as he always does, and offers one of his own in the style of an Earth classic: roses are red, violets are blue, we won Faction Wars, now we get to kill more of them. York calls it a terrible poem. Boomer asks after the breaching suits, sets aside four Cronus suits and a skiff for a pregnant veteran on the surface, and says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. Better warm up the lasers.

relations.note: Publicly disowned, privately in close contact

entities.name: Warlord Fang
entities.role: Warlord of the Reavers · ninth floor

tagline.text: Warlord Fangs of the Reavers, as he introduces himself, is a square-headed, old-school robot rattling like a diesel engine. Carl knows from the cookbook that the look is for the crawlers' benefit.
Warlord Fang has come to this meeting as a thin, too-pink young man of about twenty, in white underwear and a T-shirt, without a speck of dirt on him.
Warlord Fang is the least known of the warlords: ninety-nine percent machine, able to change his shape, and probably one of the two richest here. A piece of his brain is kept safe at home.
Warlord Fang was hiding inside his own cybernetic drake over the Reaver castle when the bombs went off, and he has fallen.

beats.headline: Fangs, the robot
beats.text: Pre-production meeting, final seat. The representative introduces himself in a robotic voice as Warlord Fangs of the Reavers: a square-headed, old-school robot vibrating up and down as if powered by a diesel engine, straight out of a sixties science fiction film. Crawler Carl knows from the Cookbook that the look is for his benefit, and that Reavers can switch shape whenever they like. Crawler Donut asks whether his name is really Fangs, and whether he is a robot vampire or, better, a werewolf robot. Cascadia snaps at her. Before anyone answers, the Viceroy beside him loses his head.

beats.headline: His personal defense deployment
beats.text: A note from me about the paratroopers who came down through the Posse's protections. Most of the people who sign on as Reaver soldiers were hungry and without direction when they walked into the recruiter's office. That is not to say you should feel sorry for these ones. These are all members of Warlord Fang's personal defense deployment. Rule of thumb: more than two or three cybernetics installed means they have voluntarily re-upped at least once. You get one free upgrade a deployment, or more if something gets shot off.

beats.headline: A different body at the council
beats.text: Warlord council. Warlord Fang appears beside Ferdinand, no longer an old-school robot but a slight, wide-eyed human male of perhaps twenty, skin a little too pink, in a spotless white t-shirt and underwear. The only tell is the line of flashing lights at his temple. When Juice Box changes into a tall black armless thing with tentacles, and the table recoils, Warlord Fang inches away from it.

beats.headline: Not in his castle
beats.text: By the time the Nest tower is stabilised, it is clear Warlord Fang is not in the Reaver castle. The castle is abandoned except for its security system, which is a bunch of robots, and a gravity-magic dragon circling overhead. Crawler Carl casts Ping and finds both remaining Bloc warlords, Epitome Tagg and Warlord Fang, inside the rolling ball of bodies. Rosetta is blunt about it: Fang especially is difficult to locate, worse than a changeling.

beats.headline: Marked, and gone
beats.text: After Crawler Donut's spell breaks the ball, Warlord Fang is not among the dead. Crawler Carl is fairly sure Li Na marked both Tagg and Fang with the Ring of Divine Suffering, and neither has died, which means she cannot heal until they are. Britney reports Li Na tearing through the castle, glowing and silent, and the war mages gone through a portal. Carl guesses Li Na is hunting Tagg and Fang.

beats.headline: The least known of them
beats.text: Crawler Carl's working file on the subject, compiled on the way to the Reaver castle. Of all the warlords, Warlord Fang is the one least known. He is something like ninety-nine percent cybernetic and changes shape like a Terminator-style changeling. He and Tagg are probably the two richest warlords here. If he dies, it is no huge deal for the Reaver corporation: a physical chunk of his brain, called the Initial, is kept on one of their worlds, and every year they peel microscopic parts off it to build new citizens.

beats.headline: Inside the dragon
beats.text: For the record. The drake circling the Reaver castle is Calliope, Cybernetic Bleached Drake, level 130, a pet of Warlord Fang. Crawler Carl sets off the No Disassembles left inside by a wraith-possessed Louis, and the castle goes up. Calliope spirals out of the sky and bursts beside the rescue team. Warlord Fang has fallen. Credit goes to Warlord Carl, fifty-one percent, with one to Louis, forty to Juice Box, and the rest to Fang for hiding in the worst possible place, which was inside the dragon. The Reavers have been defeated.

relations.note: Marked with the Ring of Divine Suffering

tagline.text: Hapanzi, if Carl has the name right, was the second spider in the dream: Shi Maria's husband, and once a god. He says he has her now, and that she is good and trapped.
Hapanzi has told Carl that Shi Maria is trapped in Carl's own body, and that Carl now controls the eye and the containment she is in.

beats.headline: A name out of the dream
beats.text: Reconstructed from Crawler Carl's memory as he wakes, covered in blood, on the far side of the map. The dream had a second spider in it: a male, her husband, first a spider and then a man. Shi Maria came in mocking, saw him, then killed him and devoured him while she sobbed. Then he came back. His name, Carl thinks, was Hapanzi, and he had been a god. His words: I have her now, son. She is good and trapped. You can always set her free, if you must. But do not unless all is lost.

beats.headline: Worry not, my children
beats.text: The dream again. A hospital room, Katia at a crib. Shi Maria pushes in, and a second spider follows: Hapanzi, her husband. Nobody says the name, and in that place there are no names over anyone's heads, but in the dream Crawler Carl simply knows it. Worry not, my children, the spider says, and becomes a large, dark-skinned man in simple pants and a vest, with an accent like Asojano's. Carl recognises the voice. It is the one that occasionally speaks inside his mind.

beats.headline: The containment in the eye
beats.text: On the screen Shi Maria rampages through the ballroom screaming that she did not kill Hapanzi and never would. At that same moment in the dream, she vanished and Hapanzi reappeared as a spider. He told Crawler Carl she was gone, trapped in his own body, and that Carl now controlled the eye on his chest and the containment she is in. Carl can summon her once. If he does, she chooses: take over his body, or expel herself into her own form. Watching the replay, Carl notes she did not look nearly as trapped as Hapanzi said.

relations.note: He sealed her into the eye

entities.name: Kimaris
entities.role: A demon, stuffed · Carl's most valuable item

tagline.text: Kimaris is the name on the tag of a plush toy, an armoured man on a black horse, sealed in one of Miss Quill's glass cases, which came through the blast unbroken.
The Stuffed Kimaris Figure, with tags, is the only unique item Carl owns. Its description says only that it is impossible to capture Kimaris's usual scowl, though the bean bag makes a valiant effort.
Bautista says his plush toys are true summonings: pull the tag, and the real creature arrives. Carl's Kimaris is a demon.
Kimaris is one of the brothers of Sheol, and once summoned he stays for the rest of the floor. He is also one of Samantha's best friends, and she calls him Kimmy.

beats.headline: Rescued from the rubble
beats.text: Recovered from the debris of Miss Quill's building, which is falling in at the time. One of her glass cases, charred and half-buried less than a foot from the explosion, and not broken, so likely enchanted. The char rubs off. Inside is a plush: an armoured man atop a black horse. The tag says Kimaris. Crawler Carl pulls the whole thing into his inventory and runs, and the rest of the building caves in behind him.

beats.headline: Out of the case
beats.text: Sorted by value, the stuffed horse-riding soldier is the top item in Crawler Carl's inventory, and its glass carrier is the second. The case is a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. It protects against most forms of abuse, and carries a 1.5% chance of Sheol Fire every time it is opened, which Carl reads after opening it. He takes Kimaris out and keeps the case, closes it around a soul gem that is about to flatten the neighbourhood, and sits down to watch.

beats.headline: One of a kind
beats.text: A Determine Value potion lets Crawler Carl see rarity, and he filters for Unique. There is exactly one item. Not the nuke, which is merely Pretty Damn Rare. The stuffed Kimaris figure on the horse. The description reads, in full, that it is impossible to accurately portray Kimaris's usual I-hate-this-and-I-hate-you scowl, but this collectible bean bag makes a valiant effort. That is all the System saw fit to say. It is still the most valuable thing he owns.

beats.headline: What a tag does
beats.text: Bautista explains his stuffed animals. Pull the tag, throw it, and after about ten seconds the creature appears and fights for you, or attacks you. A sprite he summoned told him these are true summonings: the real creature, teleported in. Crawler Carl mentions he has one, a dude on a horse named Kimaris. Bautista does not have that one and tells him to hold onto it until he knows its worth. Carl's own reading: his Kimaris figure is a demon, and Unique, not legendary or rare.

beats.headline: The yardstick for everything else
beats.text: Crawler Carl measures loot against it now. A ring with two benefits on it lands above the Ring of Divine Suffering and below the Kimaris figure. Then Pawna's Tears, a potion from the goddess of peace, becomes the first item he has seen valued higher than the stuffed demon on the horse. Mordecai tells him to save it.

beats.headline: Found by a passenger
beats.text: Shi Maria has hold of Crawler Carl from the inside, and she goes through his inventory the way a burglar goes through drawers. So many things, she says. So many possibilities. Then she stops on one. Kimaris? You have a summoning totem of Kimaris? Does Samantha know this? She moves on to the war mage head and the potions without waiting for an answer, and Carl cannot give one.

beats.headline: Still waiting to be scanned
beats.text: Bautista's legendary box gave him an electronic guidebook for his stuffed animals: scan a label, and an info box says what the plush does before you pull the tag. He promised to lend it to Crawler Carl so he could scan the Kimaris figure. Everyone has been too busy. The figure is still in Carl's inventory, still unidentified.

beats.headline: Samantha calls him Kimmy
beats.text: At the stairwell Bautista delivers his finding: Kimaris is one of the brothers of Sheol, with a summoning time of the remainder of the floor. Be careful with him. Samantha overhears. Kimmy! she shrieks, and demands him at once. He is one of her best friends. He gave her the potion that let her become pregnant when she could not, and advised her on whom to date. Then she stops, puzzled that she could not remember any of that before. Her conclusion, delivered at volume: she is going to kill his mother.

relations.note: One of the brothers of Sheol

entities.name: The Midnight Epicure
aka: The Caprid Who Devours the Sky
entities.role: A caprid fable, and Prepotente's god

tagline.text: The Midnight Epicure, the Caprid Who Devours the Sky, is a fable used to frighten children into eating their dinner. His symbol, a goat's head, is worn as a ward against the night.
The Midnight Epicure is the god Prepotente worships, and on live television the caprid council panics and cries out that they shall manifest him.

According to Prepotente, the Midnight Epicure protects all prey by destroying existence, after releasing everything ever eaten back into the galaxy. It began as a xenophobic scare story about caprids, and caprids made it a symbol of hope.

beats.headline: A goat on a sponsor's patch
beats.text: A gold box from the Plenty holds a jacket patch: black denim, a gray goat head. Crawler Carl has seen the symbol tattooed on the back of Prepotente's hand and had assumed it belonged to a deity. My description: the Midnight Epicure, the Caprid Who Devours the Sky. Eat your dinner, or he comes to eat it for you, and then every child in the home. The symbol, really a racist caricature of an adult caprid, became a ward against all night evils. Protection against Vampirism and Lycanthropy. Mordecai says sew it on at once.

beats.headline: An address on the dial
beats.text: Katia asks in chat how to tune the thing, since it is just lights. Prepotente explains, out loud, that the mechanism is quite simple. First turn off automatic mode, or Crawler Carl lands at the Emberus temple, Katia at Eileithyia's, and Prepotente himself at the Epicure. Integers here. But they need the address to dial in, and Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him.

beats.headline: Fallen into a goat's hands
beats.text: An update to Crawler Carl's quest to find out who killed Emberus's son. The memorial crystal of Apito has fallen from Crawler Osvaldo's hands and is now with Crawler Prepotente. Retrieve it from him before he cracks its secrets and gives them to the Epicure. Carl has no idea how the crystal moved from one to the other without a fight, and decides the conversation with the goat can wait until neither of them is so keyed up.

beats.headline: The goats panic on air
beats.text: A live broadcast with the caprid council of the Plenty goes badly. Something Crawler Carl says sets the goats braying, and they begin to cry out, one after another. The Epicure. We shall manifest the Epicure. The True Judgment; she has fulfilled her bargain. The great stampede comes. The beautiful place. Crawler Donut asks in chat whether the Midnight Epicure is the god Prepotente worships. It is, Carl says, and he wears its patch on his own jacket. Are they excited because they think the god is real now? Carl has no clue.

beats.headline: Prepotente explains his god
beats.text: Asked directly, Prepotente answers. The Midnight Epicure protects all prey animals by destroying all existence after unleashing everything consumed back into the galaxy. They who were eaten become the devourers. It began as a xenophobic tale told to non-caprid children when caprids first joined Syndicate culture, and grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind. His sponsors gave him the ability to worship it in a benefactor box. The Epicure told him the memorial crystal was crucial, and sent him sobbing tirades when it was stolen.

beats.headline: Black dahlias on the float
beats.text: Parade. Behind Prepotente, atop the stair truck, stands a giant head of the Midnight Epicure made of black dahlias. The plan is Crawler Donut's: a stinging statement from the goat about the downtrodden rising to devour those who revel in their suffering, then Bianca burning away the flowers to show the skull beneath. Prepotente sings instead. In Crawler Carl's account the Epicure is a symbol of hope and of vengeance against the galaxy's predators, and the effigy of the Unwashed further down the float is the death that comes for everyone.

beats.headline: A formal complaint
beats.text: After the crash, Prepotente reports in: electrocuted, but fine. A deity pulled the memorial crystal right off his neck. He has filed a formal complaint with the Epicure. Jurgen, also fried, tells him he is lucky the god did not pull his head off. Crawler Carl's own worry is the crystal: if Prepotente has lost it, they have lost their protection from Scolopendra's attacks.

relations.note: The patch came in the Plenty's gold box

tagline.text: York wrote the tenth edition of the Cookbook: pages of rambling philosophy, and a last entry about being surrounded by his hive and alone in it.
York came from a hive and felt alone all his life. The author of the eleventh edition read him, felt a kinship, and wondered whether he survived.
York is in orbit with a job from Rosetta: shoot down an orc yacht with children aboard. She hopes he does it, rather than writing a poem about it.
York, a level-71 tenodera, is the only living creature aboard the Homecoming Queen. He vaporised the orc yacht with a point-defence beam and hoped to feel something afterwards. He did not.

beats.headline: The last entry in the back
beats.text: Crawler Carl cannot sleep, and a passage from the back of the Cookbook keeps coming back to him. It was written by a crawler named York, author of the tenth edition, who wrote pages and pages of rambling philosophical essays Carl can barely follow. This one appears to be his last entry. I have been surrounded by my hive, yet I have been alone, it says. The Cookbook, York writes, is an attempt to make a hive of those who never cross paths, except in these pages. And there is consolation in dying in the pursuit of justice, however small.

beats.headline: A mantis on the eighth floor
beats.text: From a season long past, when the crawl was run by the Reavers. The eighth level that season was mountains connected by wires and gondolas. The crawlers were a strange type of mantis, not the common kind, who could not fly and did poorly in the cold. There was a crawler among them named York, and an NPC named Dante, who had once left a single entry in the Cookbook himself, was watching him carefully.

beats.headline: Read by the next one
beats.text: A note added by crawler Ikicha, eleventh edition. Ikicha's kind are castrated and cast out, a perspective as different as could be from the one who came before: York, who appears to have come from a hive, yet says he always felt alone his entire life. Reading his words, Ikicha feels kinship anyway, and asks the question on the page. Did he survive? Then a prayer that anyone who gets free seeks out those who came before.

beats.headline: The yacht, if he does his duty
beats.text: Filed from Rosetta's side of the deal. In exchange for a pin number, the Pacifist Network agreed to destroy an orc yacht with several children aboard, and with Stalwart dead, one of those children is the new king of the Skull Empire. The job falls to York, in orbit. Rosetta's assessment: assuming he actually does his duty and does not decide to write a poem instead. She also names York among those she hopes survive whatever comes next.

beats.headline: Point defense, and nothing felt
beats.text: York, tenodera, the only living creature aboard the Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in orbit, with more guns than anyone knows about and enhancement zone weapons Porthus had installed. When everyone started shooting at each other, York vaporised the orc yacht with a point defense beam. Everyone assumes crossfire. He had looked forward to it: he wanted to feel something afterwards. He did not. He writes verse about it, crumples the verse, and writes another. He suspects all his poems are terrible.

beats.headline: The crawl he remembers
beats.text: His entire hive entered the dungeon, and he vaguely recalls the anger as they were picked off one by one, and the realisation that he never fit in. Around the ninth floor a numbness spread, which he puts down to his tenodera blood: warriors bred for the job of killing an enemy hive's children. The card, for the record: Advocate. Top level 71. Took a deal at the end of the tenth floor. Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor in the Poetry guild. Author of the tenth edition. Current status: captain in the Open Intellect Action Network.

beats.headline: At that moment, something
beats.text: Boomer comes on the screen as the Homecoming Queen docks to load soldiers, and asks the usual question: written any new poems? Any good? All his poetry is good, York says. Boomer's own poem is about winning Faction Wars and killing more of them. That is a terrible poem, Boomer. The breaching suits are ready, York reports, and the enhancement zone suits and power armour are online, just as Porthus predicted. Boomer says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. At that moment, York does, indeed, feel something.

relations.note: Tenth edition

tagline.text: Princess Chandra, Esquire, has been assigned as Princess Donut's lawyer in Quasar's place. According to Quasar, she is also Carl's new wife.

Princess Chandra is Rishi's widow. She used an old Naga law to claim her husband's killer as her new husband and made herself Princess Donut's attorney. Donut read every filing and called her a sad little snake.
Princess Chandra has been in hiding since Princess Donut put a hit on her, and her filings keep coming. The Taurins she hired went after Quasar's family and found his niece armed.

beats.headline: A lawyer who is also a wife
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Donut has been assigned a lawyer other than Quasar. Quasar argued for the job, wore a tie for it, and lost it. The name on the assignment is Princess Chandra, Esquire. She and Crawler Donut have already met, Donut has declined every offer, and the word reaching Quasar is that there were serious fireworks in that meeting, and not the good kind. Crawler Carl asks whether she is another catgirl. Quasar says no. Worse. She is Crawler Carl's new wife.

beats.headline: Widow's Rights, filed in hours
beats.text: Filing summary. Chandra is Naga, a lawyer, and was the second wife of Rishi, whom Crawler Carl killed. After a coup put her uncle on the throne she accepted the title of princess, which she needed to claim Widow's Rights: the old law that lets a royal widow take her husband's assassin as her new husband. A public jury found the idea funny and approved it. As Carl's wife she has signed contracts, placed Crawler Donut under a conservatorship with Carl as guardian, and, after a discreet payment to a district judge's reelection campaign, been assigned Donut's attorney. Two Taurins are on their way to eliminate Quasar.

beats.headline: Donut reads every page
beats.text: The meeting, held in a type-A containment zone. Crawler Donut declines every deal, then reads each filing without a question: the conservatorship, the seized Princess Posse accounts, the lawsuits. She pauses only at the marriage certificate. Then she compares the stack to the papers from Carl's father's trailer and tells Chandra what they both show: a picture of who someone is. What a sad little snake you are, she says. I pity you. Chandra loses her temper. Donut announces to any reporters watching that she is definitely not offering fifty million credits to have her turned inside out.

beats.headline: Questions from the Taurins
beats.text: Directly after the non-offer, a message arrives from Chandra's Taurin associates, the pair paid to eliminate Quasar. They have questions about the job and want her coordinates. Their meetings are always in person. She tells herself it is a coincidence, and it rattles her anyway. She gathers her folders and cannot bring herself to reach through Crawler Donut's image for the last one. Donut offers her lesson one in being a princess: do not get so frightened that you wet yourself. Chandra looks down to check. She has not. Not yet, says Donut.

beats.headline: The wedding gift arrives
beats.text: The traditional Naga wedding gift is the holdings of the defeated, and the jury put it in a legendary fan box for the groom. Crawler Donut has been waiting for Carl to learn he is married to that stupid lady with the gross nails. Carl opens it in the safe room: a cobra head, from which Rishi's household pours out. Clothes, wrecked furniture, scorched electronics, a shot-through microwave, and a melted participation trophy from a GreaserBall tournament, the placing removed from the plaque. It keeps coming until the pile nearly reaches the ceiling and the room smells of fire. The cleaner bot takes it personally.

beats.headline: Still filing, from hiding
beats.text: Status. Princess Chandra vanished the moment Crawler Donut put the hit on her, and her filings keep arriving regardless. Quasar is due to argue against her over the legality of the marriage certificate and expects to lose, though his filing has paused much of what she started. Her contract with the Taurins still stands. Two of them reach the home of Quasar's brother, hurt him, and take over his niece Tempest's call to name terms. Tempest shoots both with the blaster her uncle gave her. Quasar sends Kiki a single credit, and hires her for legal help and the other kind.

tagline.text: Grigori the Placid is a level-93 human Fleshmancer, a mercenary hired by Team Meadow Lark, and a worshipper of Gula. He sits bolt upright with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes.
Grigori joined the two halves of a mantaur in the back of a moving truck, upside down on the ceiling, while trying not to be sick.
Grigori is a dungeon-born NPC, so at the parade the AI took him over. Now it speaks with his voice and looks out through his eyes.

beats.headline: A fleshmancer among the crumbs
beats.text: For the record: Grigori the Placid. Human, level ninety-three Fleshmancer, a hired mercenary of Team Meadow Lark, worshipper of Gula. Elle and Imani hired him and bring him to the Lollipop, where he sits bolt upright between Louis and Linus with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes. Crawler Carl wants him to talk to both halves of Corcunda. Elle reports that he has a stick up his backside. She also reports that he knows what he is doing, and he and Imani have been trading healing tips.

beats.headline: Transferred, and brushing a cat
beats.text: Mercenary ownership of Grigori has been transferred to Crawler Carl's guild. His first duty under new management is brushing Crawler Donut, which she has arranged personally, and he appears to be enjoying himself. Linus, who has been stroking Donut's tail and whispering to her, is taken away by Elle. Grigori's first recorded word comes a moment after, when Donut asks whether she should perform with or without sunglasses. With, he says. She agrees.

beats.headline: He has never done this
beats.text: The plan: take Corky from the Lady Dominators' garage, bring him to Porky, and let Grigori perform the joining. The spell is not difficult, he says, if both halves are willing. They are unzipped, kept alive with spells or potions while pressed together, and then there are a few minutes before the personalities join. Asked what the result is like, he says he has no idea and is looking forward to seeing it. He has never done it. Two halves rarely survive Split Personality for long. The garage attempt fails, and Crawler Carl orders him to spend half an hour learning to drive.

beats.headline: Not built for conveyances
beats.text: Race day. Grigori is strapped into a new seat at the very back of the truck, behind Dong and Porky, stiff and a little green. Hedy reports that the driving lessons did not take. He asks Crawler Carl whether they are going this fast for the whole event. They are coasting to the starting line. His stomach, he says, does not agree with this sort of conveyance. Inside the factory he turns, not to the sink, but to the empty deep fryer, and is loudly sick in it.

beats.headline: He clears the debuffs
beats.text: Crawler Carl orders Grigori into the driver's seat in case they need to move. He cannot; he is dry-heaving into the deep fryer. Then Corky is dragged out of the Dominators' wrecked car into the back of the truck, cooking in his own suit, strung out and unconscious. When Carl calls for the joining, Grigori stands over Corky, wobbling, casts, and both debuffs lift. Corky wakes and asks whether the race is over. The suits must come off quickly, Grigori says, and then asks whether they really have to be moving while they do this.

beats.headline: The joining, upside down
beats.text: The procedure is done standing, once the truck is inverted and running along the ceiling of a room of molten metal. The brains must stay sealed in plastic wrap; spilled guts are acceptable, and Grigori keeps them floating with a spell. He dry-retches mid-instruction and chants. The initial casting is done, he calls; now the parts must fuse, and Dong must hold the halves together whatever happens. Asked about mismatched anatomy, he answers that inconsistencies can be fixed after the race. The brain matters, and both hearts. With ten minutes of the race left, he casts the final part.

beats.headline: An oversight about deities
beats.text: The joining works. Corcunda is whole, and Grull has sent him word at once that he is to be punished; he worshipped Grull before the split. The god comes through a wall. Grigori, on the floor after striking his head and bleeding from the scalp, acknowledges that he should have asked whether the patient worshipped a deity before splitting, and apologises for the oversight. The truck is gliding downward through the air at the time, like a slow paper airplane.

beats.headline: Death as a change of plane
beats.text: After the heat, standing in the back of the truck and failing to clean his robe, Grigori asks whether this is a dream, and whether he is truly still alive. He is. Dong is not. Some believe, Grigori offers, that death is only movement to another plane of existence, and Dong did not think this was the end. Crawler Donut says it is still horrible for those left behind. Indeed, he replies. Told that the court's mercenaries always die, he asks: wait, what? You lived, Donut tells him. That is all that matters.

beats.headline: Examined by the withering spirit
beats.text: Samantha finds him in the garage and accuses the court of hiding him. He greets her as the so-called withering spirit. He is no mere fleshmancer, he corrects her, but the most renowned flesh sculptor this dungeon has ever known. She wants a compatible body and has a candidate. He takes her out of the air, turns her over in his hands, and says he must examine her properly, not in here. She drags him into the safe room. She returns alone to report she doubts his qualifications: he did not gasp at Sam Town, and he is talking to Jamal about his legs.

beats.headline: The AI takes the microphone
beats.text: At the parade, Grigori rides Gonk in the court's procession. Chaco abandons the script and has his wings torn off. The AI wants an NPC on the floor who is not driving and whose voice is strong enough, and settles on the fleshmancer. Grigori leaps off Gonk, somersaults across the ice-cream truck and lands on the back of the subjugated donkey, microphone in hand. From then on he speaks in his own voice, too quickly, with the AI's words. Crawler Carl works out why: the AI could not do this with Chaco, a former crawler. Grigori is dungeon-born.

beats.headline: Eyes that do not react
beats.text: The AI, through Grigori, has already forbidden anyone to heal Chaco. When the court's float passes the donkey, Grigori is standing on her with Chaco at his feet, health still in the red. Crawler Carl meets his eyes, which are the AI's eyes, pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco, and heals him without once looking away. Grigori's eyes never leave Carl's. He does not react. Carl then turns and addresses the galaxy.

beats.headline: Released, and confused
beats.text: After the crawlers have gone down, the broadcast shows the AI releasing its hold on the NPC Grigori. He stumbles, confused, back toward the crawlers' garage. In a Syndicate bunker, Prime Minister Victory asks Orren to pull a diagnosis off him. Orren cannot. The AI has locked Orren out, for Orren's own safety, it says, because Orren is being Hunted and only the AI is allowed to kill him.

entities.name: Chalchiuhtlicue
entities.role: Goddess · among the children in Lucia Mar

tagline.text: Chalchiuhtlicue is a goddess newly present among the children inside Lucia Mar. She tells them she is kind and will protect them, and that the kindest thing may be to let them die.

Chalchiuhtlicue, whom Samantha calls Chachi, is a goddess of childbirth, water and fire who has never been sponsored. According to Samantha, she is always talking about saving children, right before she kills them all.

beats.headline: Here, says Lucia
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch blinks, not knowing what it sees, and Lucia Mar crosses from her moped to him in a blink and whispers in his ear. Chalchiuhtlicue is here. She is new to this place, and she does not need Cici or Gus the way the Residual and the Primal did. She tells the children she is kind and means to protect them, and that the kindest thing may be to let them die. More are coming. The veins are open. All seek the prize on the twelfth floor. Then the presence is gone, and the patch shudders in fear.

beats.headline: The shining lady talks to Yaz
beats.text: When the presence withdraws, a frightened child surfaces in Lucia's body instead: Azra, whose sister Yaz is here too, crying. The shining lady, Azra says, is talking to Yaz, telling her Crawler Carl won his races with a spell their father gave him. Their father owns a bowling alley. The angel lady, Azra says, thinks it might be better if they all die, and keeps talking about people coming to take their bodies. It is so cold. Florin asks who is coming. Azra notices him, shrieks, and runs.

beats.headline: Samantha knows her
beats.text: Samantha, sniffing Crawler Carl, wants to know why he smells like Chachi. Chalchiuhtlicue, she clarifies: green skirt, talks funny, cries a lot. Her assessment: Chachi is pretty, not emotionally stable, and always talking about saving the lives of children before killing them all. Once, at a party, the meatballs had cilantro in them, so Chachi had her worshippers kill a whole village day care in the hope the next tray tasted better. It worked, Samantha adds. Carl realises this is the goddess Lucia named.

beats.headline: Rarely sponsored, often weak
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks around. Rosetta: Chachi, as Samantha calls her, is not well known and has never been sponsored that she remembers. Like Eileithyia, she is a goddess of childbirth and women, but also of water and fire, and of harvests. Catch-all deities look good on the manifest and do poorly in the Ascendency game, their powers being comparatively weak. Crawler Donut declares that she is to be called Chachi. Prepotente supplies the Earth analog, an Aztec goddess of the same name, benevolent, whose crying for many days began a flood myth.

tagline.text: Lamashtu is so far only a name on a scroll in a list of prizes, the Milk of Lamashtu, and Carl has no idea what it does.
Lamashtu is a former god whom the AI has subjugated. With no worshippers left, her level has been halved, and she is now a parade mount in a showgirl headdress. Samantha recognises her as a friend.
