beats.headline: A scroll with her name on it
beats.text: For the record: this name first appears on a prize list. Among the scroll choices for the three- and five-hand prizes at this evening's game is one called the Milk of Lamashtu. Crawler Carl reads it out to Mordecai alongside a scroll of mapping and one called Paw Patrol, and admits he does not know what any of these do. Mordecai calls the potions a waste and recommends the boost to Crawler Donut's lowest base stat and a random spell book instead. The name is logged.

beats.headline: A donkey with a closed eye
beats.text: Chaco rides into the parade on a donkey bigger than Sweety, dressed in yellow-and-blue regalia, rhinestoned tack and a showgirl headdress. She has crow's talons where hooves should be, and over her head a small symbol: the red curve of a closed eye. Lamashtu the Donkey, level 125, a mortal, subjugated god. The subjugator field reads Error, and then the AI owns up: it did this, and the donkey is its property now. It wanted a mount for its grand master, and a message for any watching gods that they are next.

beats.headline: Halved, and tied to her captor
beats.text: The terms of her condition, as the notice sets them out. She has no worshippers left, so under the Ascendency rules her level has been cut in half and she has lost most of her powers. As a subjugated deity she stays alive only as long as her subjugator does. If that subjugator is itself subjugated rather than killed, her power halves again and she passes to the new master. From the procession, Samantha recognises her as a friend: Lammy is grumpy about being ridden, she says, so she must like Chaco.

beats.headline: The fleshmancer on her back
beats.text: Chaco loses his wings on her back and collapses. The AI takes over Grigori, who lands on the donkey and takes the microphone, and the pair pull off the road to wait by the stands while every float passes. When the court's float goes by, the fleshmancer is standing upon her with Chaco at his feet, still in the red, and Crawler Carl heals Chaco while holding the AI's gaze.

beats.headline: Left standing in the road
beats.text: Afterwards, the broadcast shows the AI releasing Grigori, and Chaco, just as bewildered, blinking away and leaving the donkey behind. The chicken truck, driven by the slug who finished off Vinata, putters to a stop beside her. They exchange words. Lamashtu turns and walks alongside the other animals streaming toward the crawlers' garage. That is the last position logged for her on this floor.

tagline.text: Crawler Forkith left a comment in the twentieth edition of the Cookbook, confirming that a smoke curtain soaked in healing potion clears a room of undead.
Forkith wrote the twentieth edition of the Cookbook and reached at least the eleventh floor. One of his notes mourns his little sister, Barkith, who was all he had left.
Forkith is a small demon in Sheol who has separated himself from the code. He is friends with Pontiff, and sort of with Carl, and he has put a leech on Louis so that he can survive down here.

beats.headline: A comment in the margin
beats.text: For the record: the first trace of this crawler is a comment under someone else's note. Crawler Sinjin, fifteenth edition, advises soaking a hobgoblin smoke curtain in a healing potion and letting it dry, to mass-kill undead. Crawler Forkith, twentieth edition, confirms it: works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad. He used them to clear rooms of invisible Swamp Wights. Crawler Carl slams the Cookbook shut, knowing that if he keeps reading, he never stops.

beats.headline: Rest well, little sister
beats.text: Under a note on keeping explosives stable in an equipped backpack, Forkith adds that backpacks now only slow destabilisation, and that he found this out the hard way. Rest well, little sister, he writes. Her name was Barkith, and she was all he had left; he asks those who read it to kill an enemy in her honour today. Crawler Carl pieces together the rest. Forkith wrote the twentieth edition and reached at least the eleventh floor. He was an Urgyle, a small, winged, demon-like race, kept it at selection, and was a Sapper.

beats.headline: For Barkith, on the twelfth
beats.text: In the Cookbook's few notes on deities, Crawler Coolie advises staying away from gods entirely. Forkith's addition: they may be invulnerable, but they still feel pain, they still bleed, and the drivers of those bodies suffer. In honour of his sister, he prays he reaches the twelfth floor just so he may slay one. He knows it is a dream. He has the line ready anyway: he means to look in the god's eyes and say, this is for Barkith. This is for my sister.

beats.headline: The map stays; the monsters change
beats.text: On the Hunting Grounds, Forkith has set earlier editions against what he saw himself. Herot wrote of tall creatures bellowing into the sky each night, Azin of kite birds overhead, Ikicha of ice and cold. None of those were there in his iteration. The jungle is constant; the monsters change, so earlier advice on this floor needs care. The map, though, is the same every time, and so is the political landscape: a round world with a single named metropolis and dozens of unnamed cities.

beats.headline: Named among the Big Six
beats.text: The AI, listing what it calls the Big Six groups in the dungeon trying to take over or escape, puts the crawlers first and says the group includes former crawlers: that Herot guy, that Forkith dude, and so forth. It says so in passing, between a shadow mimic named Mitch and the NPCs, in a notice mostly about something else. It is the first word of Forkith since his notes on the Hunting Grounds, and it places him inside the dungeon now, not only in its margins.

beats.headline: The demon with the leech
beats.text: Louis wakes in Sheol, the fifteenth floor, not the Pineapple Cabaret, where he was supposed to go. A small demon has put a leech on him: kept on his skin, it filters his blood so he can live here, gills and all. The demon laughs that they separated out from the code just in time. He introduces himself as Forkith: friends, sort of, with Louis's friend Carl, friends with Pontiff, hoping to be friends with Louis. The Pineapple Cabaret has hands enough, he says. Soldiers were needed on a different front. A lot of them have been waiting a very long time to move.

tagline.text: Mukta is Zev's substitute for the day. Zev had booked the crawlers on Dungeon Crawl Tactics, and Mukta has overridden her and picked a programme that pays a higher fee.
Administrator Mukta put two crawlers on the Maestro's show and told them to take their seats or be accelerated.
Mukta, the substitute who booked the Maestro's show, is a member of the Bloom, the party that runs Borant, and party members are treated much better.
Mukta, the kua-tin who booked the Maestro's show, is dead. One of Lucia Mar's dogs ate Mukta, and Zev can still hear the screaming.

beats.headline: Zev is in a time out
beats.text: For the record: Mukta (Admin) opens a chat in a safe room in the kobold quadrant. Crawlers Carl and Princess Donut are to be transported to their interview in ten minutes. Their outreach associate has been put in a time out and returns tomorrow; Mukta is the substitute until then. Zev had them booked on Dungeon Crawl Tactics. Mukta has overridden her and picked a better program, one paying a higher fee. Still round-table style. Close enough. Crawler Carl says they were promised the right to refuse. "You seem to be under the impression that you have a say in this, crawler." The chat closes. It cannot be answered.

beats.headline: Sit, or be accelerated
beats.text: On the Maestro's set the crawlers refuse to take part, and a first voice threatens to drop them in the ocean. Crawler Carl calls bullshit. Then: "Crawler Carl, this is Administrator Mukta." They are required to take their seats. Refusal means acceleration; there are plenty of other crawlers to show; this is not a bluff. Asked whether that other guy can hear, a pause, then no. Asked whether anything he says carries consequences, provided he participates, a longer pause: "They have paid for your appearance. Nothing else."

beats.headline: Should never have booked it
beats.text: Mukta warned there would be a discussion after the show. The program ends, the crawlers are transported back, and there is no sign of the admin. Afterwards a warning arrives, no weapons in the presence of Admins, and Crawler Carl says "Mukta is coming." It is Zev who appears, her censure lifted on appeal. Her verdict on the Maestro's show: Mukta should never have booked it. Her own booking would have been a discussion of dungeon tactics, done in a creative, silly way. Borant, she adds, is not allowed to discriminate against Syndicate-member production companies.

beats.headline: A party member
beats.text: Zev warns that Loita has a claim on the crawlers' account. She is Bloom, and Zev is not. By Crawler Carl's understanding, Bloom is the kua-tin political party that runs Borant, and its members receive much better treatment. For the record, he files a precedent: the last substitute they had, "the Mukta guy" who put them on the Maestro's show, was a party member.

beats.headline: One of the two dogs
beats.text: Administrator Mukta, kua-tin, party member, is dead. Reported by Zev, over chat, after saying Lucia Mar no longer answers messages and was never her client, thank goodness: one of Lucia's dogs ate Mukta, back when she still had two. It was horrible. Mukta was an ass, and a party member, but nobody deserved that. Zev can still hear the screaming. Crawler Carl laughs out loud. File note: the second kua-tin the crawlers ever spoke with, and the one responsible for putting them on the Maestro's show in the first place.

tagline.text: Manasa is a cobra-headed pop singer. The real Manasa died long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going after her death.
Manasa traded trailers with the crawlers so that they could use her cleaning machine, and she died in theirs, hit by a pulse meant for them. Her final performance was a sad soprano, sung a cappella.
A Skull Empire pulse aimed at two crawlers killed Manasa instead, and the Valtay answered by killing the Maestro.

beats.headline: A worm in a famous head
beats.text: For the record: Manasa, a silver and black cobra-headed creature whose hood is a meter wide, towers over the Danger Zone table as a hologram. The director Evo's briefing: a famed singer. A Naga, but not of the Blood Sultanate, so Crawler Donut need not kill her on the ninth floor. Not really a Naga either. The real Manasa perished long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going once she died. A worm in her brain, driving the body? Correct. Her career is hotter than ever. Latest single: eighth in the entire universe.

beats.headline: On the side of the Valtay
beats.text: She laughs at Crawler Donut's put-downs of Tucker, the comedian who is not funny, forked tongue flipping in and out. On the panel's main topic, the Valtay Corporation's attempt to collect its debt from the Borant system, she is, for obvious reasons, on the side of the Valtay. Ripper and Princess D'nadia think both sides are dicks and also side with the Valtay; Tucker mostly backs the kua-tin. The three crawlers are careful to say nothing stupid about either.

beats.headline: The pulse hit her trailer
beats.text: Manasa has been removed from the broadcast. Mid-sentence from the host, her hologram blinks in and out and is gone, and the studio bucks. The report: an attack on her trailer. She was vacationing on Earth and had ascended for the interview, and the trailer was hit with a pulse. Ripper announces that it appears she has perished. Then Prince Stalwart's statement plays, announcing the crawlers Carl and Donut executed by a pulse from his personal yacht. Tucker, no longer snooty: "It was meant for you."

beats.headline: She offered to trade
beats.text: Princess D'nadia explains. The crawlers needed cleaning facilities, and Manasa offered to trade trailers. D'nadia weeps black oil: Manasa was her friend for countless years, worm head or not, and the Prism Kingdom is filing a grievance. Tucker supposes the Valtay must see it as an accident. Ripper: does anyone know how much money she brings the Valtay each year? Their entertainment assets outearn their technology, and they just murdered her. Then word arrives: a Valtay dreadnaught claims Stalwart's yacht; the rumor puts Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince Maestro aboard.

beats.headline: Her final performance
beats.text: Ripper closes the show on a video of Manasa singing, her final performance: a cappella, in an opulent dining room, a hauntingly sad soprano. The studio watches in dead silence. Afterwards Crawler Donut says she was really nice. Over chat, Crawler Carl works it through: the crawlers were the bait, and so was Manasa, and the switch was either arranged or seized upon; it humiliates the orcs and damages their alliance with the Valtay, and his guess is that Borant benefits. Crawler Donut: MANASA HAD THE VOICE OF AN ANGEL. To Mordecai she adds that Manasa thought Mongo was adorable.

beats.headline: The worm and the retaliation
beats.text: Crawler Donut's first sponsor is Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, and Crawler Carl's is the Valtay Corporation. He notes that two parties present at the Danger Zone incident have sponsored them: D'nadia was very upset when the Skull Empire killed Manasa, who had really been controlled by a brain parasite from the Valtay. Further on, sorting out the Skull Empire's succession, he records the rest: the Maestro, once second in line, was disowned, then slain by the Valtay in retaliation for the botched assassination that killed Manasa instead of Carl.

beats.headline: The only nice one
beats.text: Crawler Donut's assessment, delivered to Princess Chandra, Esquire, who has come with legal papers: every Naga the crawlers have met has been a raging psycho. For about five seconds Donut thought Chandra might be a nice one, and she was incorrect, which is sad. The only nice one was Manasa, and she was a worm head. The Nagas, Donut concludes, are doing a terrible job as ambassadors for their species.

tagline.text: Gordo is the Bopca protector at the Belly-Rubbed Pug. He has just met the crawlers' manager, and he cannot believe that is really their manager.
Gordo fetches walnuts the moment Princess Donut asks. Mordecai dosed him with a potion so that he could search his kitchen for the newsletter.

beats.headline: A family establishment
beats.text: For the record: Gordo, Bopca protector at the Belly-Rubbed Pug, a renaissance-fair pub of a saferoom where rooms now cost ten gold a night. Twenty minutes after the crawlers left their manager, he teleports in beside the bar with his pants at his knees, asking for Grannie first. Gordo, from behind the counter: "My good sir, I must ask you sheath your sword immediately!" This is a family establishment. Mordecai vomits on the floor, sits in it and passes out. Gordo leans over: this is their manager? Yep. A sad shake of the head. "You two are so dead."

beats.headline: Right away, your majesty
beats.text: Crawler Carl's Earth Hobby Potion has given him a skill called Cesta Punta, and nobody knows what it is. Crawler Donut's theory: likely the art of cracking nuts with your toes. "Gordo, darling. Get me some walnuts. We need to experiment." Of course, right away, your majesty, and he scurries into the back kitchen. Crawler Carl's observation: Bopcas are subservient as a rule, and this one is even more so than usual. Crawler Donut's Charisma has rocketed up to 70.

beats.headline: A draft for his dignity
beats.text: Morning. Gordo is passed out at a table beside the crawlers' manager, snoring like a chainsaw. Crawler Donut demands breakfast and a brushing. "Hold yer horses, ye blowhard." She can brush herself, princess. Asked whether Mordecai taught him the finger-breaking trick: no, Mordecai made him a potion from a few things behind his own bar, because he has not felt himself since the two crawlers arrived, and it would let him regain his dignity. It is not right, taking advantage of his kind nature like that. He disappears into the back.

beats.headline: The newsletter in his kitchen
beats.text: Mordecai, over chat: the potion was meant to knock Gordo out so he could get into the kitchens and find the newsletter. Bopcas and shopkeepers have no access to the feed, so a physical brief is delivered after each recap episode. Mordecai read it and stole a few herbs for potions while he was there. This one is regional, and it warns of a potential major battle event in the area today or tonight. Eat, go, and never come back this way. Gordo returns with two bowls of what looks like lumpy oatmeal.

tagline.text: Heather was once a black bear. She lies asleep in the road under a spell, with a pink clown hat grown into her head, and Signet has captured her many times but never yet used her blood.

Heather the Bear was a level-19 neighbourhood boss who had performed at Grimaldi's circus since she was a cub, caught in its loop for two centuries. Carl beat her alone, and her blood raised Signet's paper army.

beats.headline: Asleep in the road
beats.text: For the record: Tsarina Signet has captured Heather multiple times, always to kill the sacrifice, and has never yet used her blood to summon her team. Tonight Crawler Carl is to kill Heather. Her blood is not as powerful as his, Signet says, but it is some of the most potent she has used. She lies asleep in the road under the same Water Lily spell as Crawler Donut. Once a black bear. Pink clown hat and ruff grown into her body, no skin on her face, red eyes, front paws turned to white worms, roller skates, a pink tutu.

beats.headline: Performing since she was a cub
beats.text: Heather the Bear. Level 19 Neighborhood Boss. Performing since she was a cub, Heather the Roller-Skating Bear was one of the longest-running attractions at Grimaldi's Traveling Circus, with retirement weeks away when the cataclysm hit. Now she hunts for the circus, running down mobs and crawlers and dragging them back so the clowns may feed. A spark of the old Heather survives deep down, and she has moments of lucidity. In them she thinks: "I've always hated all you assholes, anyway."

beats.headline: Worms that talk
beats.text: On her skates she stands about eight feet tall. From fifteen feet away she whips the worms at Crawler Carl and wraps him three times; they burrow into his bare legs and talk inside his head about primal flesh and hungry clowns. Protective Shell severs them and blows her fifty feet back. A thrown jug of moonshine and a torch set her alight. She trips on a dumbbell, sheds half her skin and fur, and comes on as a skeleton wrapped in worms, with half her health left.

beats.headline: Custard, not fireball
beats.text: Crawler Carl scratches a lottery ticket saved for a dire moment: a level-15 fireball or strawberry custard, fifty-fifty. Custard. It heals her, and the healing kills the worms. Her skin and fur re-form; the roller skates and the hat fall off and turn to dust. What sits down on all fours is an elderly black bear with a silver sheen on her muzzle, free of the parasites. Without them her body is breaking down fast. Her eyes, by his reading, say: end it. I should never have lived this long.

beats.headline: Two punches and a heel
beats.text: Heather the Bear, Level 19 Neighborhood Boss, is dead. Crawler Carl kept an eye on her claws, found no trick, and finished it: two quick punches to the head, then his foot pressed down on her skull until it caved. Winner. It is his first solo boss battle, and he reaches level 15. A line of red rises from the corpse and flies to Tsarina Signet. Looted from the remains: a neighborhood map upgrade.

beats.headline: She was family
beats.text: Signet's retinue rises on Heather's blood, strength bought with shorter lives: dozens of paper elementals in red outline. Signet thanks Crawler Carl. He actually freed Heather tonight, she says. For two centuries the bear had been caught in that loop. A grumpy old bear; Signet told Grimaldi more than once she would snap and try to eat a spectator if they did not retire her. But she was family. At the big top, the blood is not enough: Signet had hoped it would break the tent's protection, and it does not.

beats.headline: What her boss box held
beats.text: Loot note. Sorting his rewards, Crawler Carl opens what came out of the bronze boss box from his fight with Heather: a whole box of hobgoblin dynamite and three globs of Hobgoblin Pus, the remote-controlled explosive detonators. He has never seen hobgoblin dynamite before. The sticks are white instead of red, with a larger yield, and much more stable. Mordecai's advice on the trap supplies he has also been collecting: leave them alone until there is a sapper's table.

beats.headline: Like the bear
beats.text: Asked what became of the circus, Tsarina Signet uses Heather as the measure. Grimaldi killed the parasites and set their family free. It was like when Carl freed Heather the bear: all the clowns and lemurs and other performers simply crumbled away, finally free. All but Grimaldi himself, whom Signet took with her.

entities.name: GumGum
entities.role: Orc · regular at the One-Eyed Narwhal

tagline.text: GumGum is a level-5 orc who drinks alone at the One-Eyed Narwhal, her shirt stained red like a butcher's. She asked the crawlers for help, and wept when she was turned down.
GumGum asked the crawlers to find out who was killing the town's women. Now she lies dead in an alley with her chest torn open.
GumGum carried the dead women out of town and asked why they were dying. The elves of the 201st tortured her for the crawlers' name, and she died in an alley.

beats.headline: I really need your help
beats.text: For the record: a woman orc drinking alone in the corner of the One-Eyed Narwhal. Older, swaying, her medieval shirt stained red, like a butcher who forgot her apron. Crawler Carl is reminded of an orcish, well-muscled Agatha. Tooltip: Level-5 Orc NPC. Name: GumGum. "I see you're adventurers. I really need your help." Mordecai: no; fuck off; not tonight. She settles back into her chair, puts her face in her hands and weeps. When Carl slips back out to ask what she needed, she is gone.

beats.headline: A pile outside the gates
beats.text: The next evening, outside the gates, she tosses a body onto a pile of about fifteen: humans, orcs, elves and dwarves, every one of them a woman. The system groups them as Pile of Dead Hookers. She was hoping to catch the crawlers. New ones are found in the alleys every morning, strangers to the town, most of their blood gone. The skyfowl do not care as long as the bodies go; the guards do not work at night. "These were people." Quest issued: The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens. "We'll see what we can do," says Carl.

beats.headline: In the alley
beats.text: GumGum, orc, level 5, is dead. Found when Crawler Donut's torch lights an alley that Mongo ran down: her chest rent open. Three disembodied female heads, organs dangling beneath them, shriek at the light and corkscrew into the dark, and a tall figure with a smoking, burning hand stands over the scene. The crawlers had seen her only a few hours before.

beats.headline: Four gold and two papers
beats.text: Crawler Carl had told her they would help, and he had not meant it. Lootable Corpse. GumGum. Orc. Level 5. It does not say what killed her. A ripped-open chest and no blood suggest the flying heads. Her inventory: four gold coins, a Gate Pass, and a Mysterious Letter, blood-soaked and in an odd language nobody present can read. Crawler Donut: she was a nice lady, for an orc, and she was doing the right thing. They have to finish the quest now.

beats.headline: Fitz's best customer
beats.text: Back at the inn Crawler Donut tells Mordecai that GumGum died because of them, and they are going to make it right. Fitz the barkeep hears it: GumGum dead. His best customer. Pressed by Donut, he tells the rest. GumGum went into the alleys at night when she heard one of the fallen women, and had nightmares of one dying with nobody to hold her hand. Her own mother was a lady of the night, stabbed, who crawled home to die on the stoop, leaving a red streak half a kilometer long. Nobody helped. The nicest orc you'd ever meet.

beats.headline: Tortured for a name
beats.text: Outside the elves' temple, Salvatore of the 201st Security Group explains. They had to torture her to tease the crawlers' name from her lips. GumGum was serving an important purpose, removing the unworthy filth from the streets. Then she started asking questions, and the questions attracted the Oak Fell, just as the Master predicted. "You tortured GumGum?" asks Crawler Donut. Yes, says Salvatore, just as they shall torture the crawlers.

beats.headline: The letter was listening
beats.text: That morning the crawlers stand over a dead woman with "No you won't" carved into her, dropped on their inn the night before moments after Crawler Carl promised revenge for GumGum with her letter in his hand. Mordecai works it out. The Mysterious Letter was likely planted in her inventory for whoever investigated the deaths: a spent necroscript scroll, Suppurating Eye, soaked in the caster's blood. Out of inventory, the caster can see and hear anything near it. Crawler Donut's idea: use it as bait.

beats.headline: Somebody did notice
beats.text: Remex explains why the women were brought in from out of town: the raw materials came from elsewhere, so nobody would notice his wife collecting them. Crawler Donut corrects him. "Somebody did notice. Gumgum noticed." For the record, the one who noticed asked two crawlers for help at a pub table, and was told to fuck off.

tagline.text: Ricky Joe is a level-2 juvenile fathom dwarf whose pet salamander, Benjamin, went into Mongo twice. So did his right arm, below the elbow.
Ricky Joe has one arm and a twice-eaten salamander, and he has seen a skyfowl lady leave with a group of other women. Now his mother is in labour next door, and he is in charge of her left leg.

beats.headline: Benjamin, on a stick
beats.text: For the record: about fifteen dwarven kids in patched clothes play in the street beside the elves' temple. One of the older ones chases the rest with a small salamander tied to a stick and jabs it at a robed elf; the lizard spits a single spark. Left in the street, it tries to drag itself away, and Mongo swallows it whole with half the stick. It comes back up, dead, in the middle of a standoff. "Benjamin?" asks the young dwarf. Ricky Joe. Level 2. Juvenile Fathom Dwarf.

beats.headline: He punches the raptor
beats.text: His mother, Eunice, level-30 fathom dwarf and enormously pregnant, has been frozen solid by an Icer, and the swordsmen guards raise their blades over her. Crawler Carl punches a guard. At the same moment Ricky Joe punches Mongo in the face: "You killed my best friend!" On the second swing his arm is no longer there. Mongo has bitten it off below the elbow and swallowed it, along with Benjamin, for the second time. Crawler Donut's "Mongo, hold!" saves his life. Carl tucks the bleeding boy under his arm like a football.

beats.headline: Give me my arm back
beats.text: Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes the crawlers and the boy to a rooftop across the street as the boom jug lands below and crisps the remaining eight elves. Crawler Carl shoves a health potion into the squealing boy's mouth. The blood stops, and his health returns to green. His arm does not grow back. He moves to hit the dinosaur again with his left, and Carl holds him back. "Give it back! Give me my arm back!"

beats.headline: Benjamin was in training
beats.text: He sits cross-legged on the roof, clutching his severed limb and Benjamin's twice-eaten corpse. He screamed bloody murder on learning the arm could not be reattached, and Crawler Donut talked him down. Told that tying a lizard to a stick is not cool: at least he did not eat him, and Benjamin liked it. Fathom dwarves strap them to their hats when they go into mines. He was in training. The boy's own home, attached to the temple, has burned to the ground.

beats.headline: The skyfowl lady
beats.text: Asked about the temple: the elves were always weird. One cried for his mama every morning, through the walls. His brother Bubba Lane saw something fly from the roof a couple of nights ago, probably just that skyfowl lady. She visits a lot, just before dark, and leaves with a bunch of other ladies, elves and dwarves and humans, dressed like they are going to the Desperado. Where she takes them he does not know. They are not allowed past the street.

beats.headline: In charge of the left leg
beats.text: Crawler Carl carries the protesting boy down the rope under his arm and drops him the last ten feet. He belly-flops, loses his grip on the arm and the salamander, and wails. His health has barely blipped. "Walk it off, kid." A scream from the building next door: "That's me mom." She is in labor again, and she is going to be really mad if he misses it. He is in charge of holding her left leg. "Bye, Princess Donut! Bye Mongo!"

beats.headline: Whether the baby came
beats.text: On the stairs down, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met on this floor. Among them, little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf, whose word that a female skyfowl was visiting the city elves had first made Carl suspect Miss Quill. He wonders whether the boy's mom ever had her baby.

tagline.text: Burgundy is a young, dark-haired human carrying papers up the magistrate's stairs, with one pale blue eye and one brown. She wishes the crawlers luck.
Burgundy came to town for work at the Desperado Club. By day she was an assistant and by night a flying head, and she begged to be killed while she was still mortal.

beats.headline: On the magistrate's stairs
beats.text: For the record: in the skyfowl mall below the magistrate's quarters, a human carrying a blue folder of papers rushes up the stairs, then back down, almost into the crawlers. "Pardon me." The name over her head: Burgundy. Young, dark-haired, pretty, with one pale blue eye and one brown, like a Siberian husky. Are they lost? They do not see many of their kind up here. They are going to see the magistrate. She snorts. "Good luck." Her blue folder is on Miss Quill's desk.

beats.headline: Healing would undo her
beats.text: The magistrate's building is coming apart when one of the burnt, headless corpses flickers from X to red to white. Her head has magically returned to her body, and the system calls her human. The lower half of her is char. The eyes identify her: Burgundy, from the stairs. Crawler Carl pulls a healing potion. No: healing her would heal her body, and she would turn into one of those things again. She is cursed. The kindest thing is to kill her while she is still mortal. "Hurry. Please. It hurts."

beats.headline: The job at the club
beats.text: A person by day and one of those things at night, she confirms. The elves brought her from another settlement with a promise of work at the Desperado Club. Everyone knows a job there is a chance to descend: to the Hunting Grounds, then maybe deeper, where it is safe. It was all a lie. Asked whether she was a prostitute: yes, and if they do not like it, fuck off. She has stabbed men for less. Crawler Donut's torch keeps the curse back, and she can feel it fading.

beats.headline: Her husband, across the street
beats.text: Featherfall did not do this. He hangs on that thing, dead before she arrived, turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill is the real magistrate. Quill took Burgundy from the temple to her husband, Remex, across the street above where the guards sleep: not alive, not dead, casting a big spell to bring himself fully back. By day the women work in the building and the shops below, plucking a feather from every skyfowl or chickadee customer for Quill. At night they are his army.

beats.headline: The ones who do not turn
beats.text: The women in the alleys, she says, are those whose sins are not enough. They came to work at the Desperado Club, and when Remex twists them they do not always turn. Sometimes they simply die. Then the survivors are allowed to feed on them, and one of his avatars drops them in the alleys, within a few blocks of his lair. The avatars are his limbs, but they cannot go far. Not yet.

beats.headline: Before the floor goes
beats.text: Final entry for Burgundy, magistrate's assistant, whom the system filed as human. The room slumps forward and her body begins to slide away as the roof above her caves in. "Kill me, please!" Crawler Princess Donut hits her with a Magic Missile in the moments before the body disappears into the collapse. She had asked for exactly that twice, while the torch still held her curse back and she was mortal.

tagline.text: Levi the Seventh is a level-7 Troll Flesher and Hobgoblin Skellie Symbiote, and the engineer of the Dismemberment Limited. He begs crawlers not to get on.
Levi the Seventh is still the seventh. One party held the fleshers off him for a whole trip and took the war mage's head, and he waved as the train pulled away.

beats.headline: Please do not get on
beats.text: For the record: the Dismemberment Limited is a sleek white train of three cars, one pair of doors, and a lone operator on a bouncy seat behind a glass nose. Subject notices crawlers on the platform the moment they notice him. Please, he says as the doors open. Find another way. We're not open to crawlers. The car around him is caked floor to ceiling in dried gore. Subject wears only his engineer's hat and green-tinted skin that hangs off him like a fitted sheet.

beats.headline: Two creatures, one name
beats.text: The file: two creatures, intelligent only together. The bones belonged to a hobgoblin. The skin is a Flesher, peeled from a Basher Troll by a war mage's You're Not Done Yet spell; it melted its victim and cast Boned, and the thing that stood up was new to the world, confused, afraid and easy to kill. Other Fleshers come for such things, and each resleeving comes back smarter. A footnote: this is Levi the 7th. The quest has triggered six times since the floor opened.

beats.headline: Levi is On the Menu
beats.text: The doors close. The back doors only open when crawlers are aboard, subject explains, and it hurts so bad when they get to him. Quest: do not allow Levi the 7th to be devoured; failure turns every crawler on the train into a Flesher. Subject spends the siege at the front predicting the end while Crawler Carl and Crawler Katia hold an eight-hundred-pound plate against the door. The war mage behind it is Dismember. Stay away from me, subject shouts. You don't control me anymore.

beats.headline: Waving from the window
beats.text: Dismember's head is off, pulled through a hole in the plate. The Fleshers, now Bereft Minions, swarm the barrier, and one of them takes the war mage's body. Subject screams for most of the remaining trip: You did it! By the gods, you killed him! and a dozen more shapes wait in the third car. At the stop the door to car two slides closed on its own; the crawlers take the head and their plates and get off. Subject waves as the train leaves the station.

tagline.text: Limp Richard is a level-36 Mole Man who runs Limp Richard's Sundries at transfer station 83. He reads in his doorway, as his kind do day and night.
Limp Richard has fifteen books, all read to pieces, and a Battery Fabricator in a dusty corner at seventy-five thousand gold, not negotiable.
Limp Richard let the Battery Fabricator go for a stack of westerns and a jug of moonshine, and practically begged Carl to take it.

beats.headline: Supplies for the weary
beats.text: For the record: at the top of the stairs at transfer station 83 stand a saferoom, a mace and bashing weapons guild, and Limp Richard's Sundries. Subject is a Mole Man, level thirty-six, non-combatant, short and squat, glasses, reading a book in his open doorway. The system's note on his kind: they call themselves Men and Women, which is exhausting, and spend their days and nights reading. Welcome to station 83, says subject. Supplies for the weary travellers. Crawler Carl says they are weary, and they'll be by after they sleep. Suit yourself.

beats.headline: Price not negotiable
beats.text: Subject's stock is wide and mostly useless. Crawler Donut talks a padded mallet down from 250 gold to 150 and then negotiates all the patience out of him on a pile of junk. In a dusty corner sits a Battery Fabricator, 75,000 gold, lifted from a dwarven automaton factory: pour in mana potions, insert a metal block, a charged battery comes out. Box of fifty. Price not negotiable. How much charge? Ask a dwarf, says subject. Better than elven soul gems, which run on actual souls.

beats.headline: Fifteen books, read to pieces
beats.text: Subject is reading an Andre Norton, and says a lot of his books are about cats. Crawler Carl says Norton was a woman. Shopkeepers get no entertainment feeds, subject explains, only physical media, and he has fifteen books, sixteen counting the one with the last chapters torn out. He has read this one dozens of times. Carl trades five westerns he has already read for five of his; subject has never read a western and notes they are short. Don't give the rest to the other mole men. Book hogs.

beats.headline: Westerns for a fabricator
beats.text: A trade entered after the fact, as Crawler Carl files it: he traded the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine for the dwarven Battery Fabricator, and the moleman shopkeeper practically begged him to, having finished the first five. Carl suspected the machine's odd placement in the first store he came across was no coincidence. It came with fifty batteries, five fully charged and five at half, and they are the same dwarven batteries the trainyard's repair carts run on.

tagline.text: Silfa is a level-25 Wisteria Fairy and Holistic Healer who rides with Brynhild's Daughters. She is plump, looks about fifty, is half the size of the cat, and heals only when she is told to.
Silfa held back her heals on Eva's orders, and Carl reckons she was left in the car as bait. She owns a bakery, and the two mages waiting outside are her own daughters.
Silfa formed a new party with Eva and took her two daughters with her, and according to Katia, Eva got all three of them killed.

beats.headline: The healer rides up front
beats.text: For the record: on the Vermillion engine's run to station 101, one more daughter rides in the cab. Silfa, Wisteria Fairy, level twenty-five, Holistic Healer. Plump, about fifty in appearance, half the size of Crawler Donut. She hangs back quietly. Crawler Carl hopes her healing works better in here than holistic snake oil did at home, eyes her nervously because he has never fought beside her, and keeps eight scrolls of healing ready anyway. Crawler Donut has six more.

beats.headline: Supposed to wait for 25
beats.text: Crawler Katia is the train's scoop and her health keeps falling, and subject has not healed her once. When a blister ghoul torso reaches for her, subject buzzes to the ceiling screaming for Hekla. Pressed, she says she is supposed to wait until Katia is at 25 percent. She looks at Hekla. Hekla nods. Then she heals. Before the next horde Crawler Carl gives her exact orders, and again she looks to Hekla first. When the horde hits, subject runs into the engineer's apartment.

beats.headline: She heals Hekla
beats.text: Crawler Donut puts a full-strength Magic Missile into Hekla's face for the invisible bolts, and the cab fills with the Daughters: Eva with her swords, two mages with glowing hands, and subject out of the apartment with her eyes wide. Hekla is back on her feet shouting hold, fully healed by subject. Then Hekla sends the mages out, and subject with them. They wait right outside the door.

beats.headline: Bait, and a bakery
beats.text: After Hekla's death Donut spots a blue dot hiding in the apartment. Subject bolts for the exit and is pinned under the gore; one weak ice spell at Crawler Carl. Traitor, she tells Katia. Carl explains she was bait. She insists Hekla would never. Then: Eva told her to stop healing, not Hekla. The two mages outside are her real daughters, told to kill Carl first if anything went wrong. I own a bakery, subject says. I just want my girls to be safe.

beats.headline: The Daughters are no more
beats.text: Subject's account of what is left. With Hekla dead, Eva is automatically party leader, and nobody likes her; they are leaving. Brynhild's Daughters is no more. Hardly any equipment, no personal space. Most share Hekla's sponsor, the crab ranch, which has never sent them anything. What are we going to do? Crawler Carl does not know, only that it cannot be with them. He opens the door enough for her to slip out, and on the other side three women start to sob.

beats.headline: Back with Eva
beats.text: Crawler Silfa is dead. So are her two daughters. The report is Crawler Katia's, given on the fifth floor: despite everything, the three formed a new party with Eva, Katia tried to talk them out of it, and in Katia's words Eva got them killed. Crawler Carl remembers subject as the older woman who turned herself into a healer, and who was used as bait. It seems so long ago. Eva has increased her player killer marks.

tagline.text: Widget is a level-19 grease gremlin and steam engine technician, working a trainyard overrun with ghouls. His wife makes a nice stew, and he likes a lass with meat on her bones, which the cat hears as being called fat.
Widget told the crawlers about the Escape Velocity line and set them on their route. Then a ghoul that was not as dead as it looked ripped his head off.

beats.headline: A wrench three times his length
beats.text: For the record: the subject arrives at the broken port-side window of an engine that has just rolled into Station and Repair Hub E. Goblin-shaped, covered in black bristly hair, about Zev's height, wearing a railroad cap and a toolbelt that drags a wrench three times his length. Level nineteen Iron Tangle Steam Engine Train Technician. His file notes that grease gremlins could go either way, and that the only thing keeping this one from attacking is a Sensitivity Training class human resources made him take. He opens by complaining that the station is closed.

beats.headline: Nobody ever asks Widget
beats.text: He asks after CrackJack, and Crawler Carl tells him the engineer is dead. He hopes for their sake they did not hurt Brandy. Told they want a stairwell, he laughs: this train stops at 83 Tangerine and Plum, the Tangerine runs to 89, and the Escape Velocity goes to all the stairwells. Then the ghouls. Someone cheaped out combining systems. The ghouls were meant to be caged and carried back on a conveyor, then wheeled onto the Terminus direct lines. Too many came at once. Nobody ever asks Widget what he thinks.

beats.headline: A stew at station sixty
beats.text: He waves his wrench at a climbing ghoul like a halberd, and Crawler Donut blasts it onto its back with a Magic Missile; it goes unconscious, then to an X. Oi, nice shot, lassie. He likes a lass with meat on her bones and fight in her, which Crawler Donut hears as being called fat. He gets off shift in a couple of hours, has a place up at station sixty, and his wife cooks a nice stew. There is fresh fish in their food boxes. Crawler Donut wants to know what kind of fish. Crawler Carl wants to know how they get out.

beats.headline: Plan change at the yard
beats.text: His system involves climbing his chain into the tower. He has Crawler Carl turn a red spigot, and the steam sends the ghouls below scrambling. Then a section of the yard's wall collapses and the ghouls pour out through it. Plan change. He lays out the route: onto the turntable, onto the employee line, a loop at sixty, a service entrance at every station. Then he drops a ghoul at the cab door with a bonk from the wrench and unhooks the cargo cars. He means to come down and ride out with them. He winks at Crawler Donut about the fish.

beats.headline: The ghoul that got back up
beats.text: Widget, grease gremlin, is dead. He turns and runs to the edge of the engine, and pauses to wave. The spider ghoul Crawler Donut had put down turns from an X back to a red dot, grabs him, rips his head off in one smooth motion and starts to eat the rest. Less than a second. Crawler Donut goes up his chain to the tower in his place and tries his controls. Her review of his quarters: very messy, and a great many lotion containers for one gremlin.

beats.headline: The line he mentioned
beats.text: The party is studying a large paper map of the lines spread on a counter. Crawler Katia points out the Vermillion line, which is coloured like the others but behaves differently, running the whole route in about a day. She thinks it is one of the lines Widget the gremlin was talking about when he mentioned the Terminus Direct. Hekla's plan is built on it: a Vermillion train down to 101 to pick everybody up. The subject is not present to confirm.

tagline.text: Crawler Coolie wrote the nineteenth edition of the Cookbook, and his advice on deities is to avoid every kind of summoning. In his short experience, they all ended with the summoner dead.
Coolie hid bugbear paste in his boots and blew up a ship in orbit to kill two admins, and the two admins were only holograms. His last note was written looking down at his home planet, Qurux.
Coolie died after a failed attempt on two admins, and his last view was of his own planet from a ship in orbit. Now Carl is looking down on Earth the same way, and he thinks of him.

beats.headline: Three kinds of summoning
beats.text: For the record: the subject's first note on file sits in the middle of the Cookbook's miscellaneous chapter. Avoid all three types of deity summoning. The big gods, Apito and Eris and so forth, are sponsored by some rich prick who paid extra to play the Celestial Ascendency, and they are invulnerable below the twelfth floor. Celestial boons, indentured summonings, involuntary summonings. In his short experience, all three lead to the summoner's death. Even the first. His advice: just stay the fuck away.

beats.headline: Gods as a revenue stream
beats.text: Below Crawler Forkith's reply, a second note by the subject covers involuntary summonings, which is what Crawler Carl's gauntlet did. They are common. God-summoning equipment is sprinkled through the dungeon as a way to collect more sponsorship money, allowing for special guest appearances, and the deity spots are often bought by celebrities. It is a safe way into the game for anyone not part of the dynastic families who control the armies of the ninth floor. Crawler Carl already knew most of it. He asks Mordecai anyway, so there is a record of the question.

beats.headline: A window with no glass
beats.text: Nineteenth edition, entry one of three. The subject went on a program tonight. They transported him to a ship floating in low orbit over his planet, with an open window that has no glass and is protected only by a forcefield. He calls it amazing. He can look down on his beautiful, lost planet. If he is to die here, he wants this to be his last view. Crawler Carl is at that moment about to be transferred to a sponsor's trailer, with the admin Loita, for a toy commercial.

beats.headline: Bugbear paste in his boots
beats.text: Entry two. Another program tonight. He has secreted bugbear paste into his boots and means to detonate them while in orbit. There are to be two admins on board. His Blast Shield skill should protect him from the explosion, if the skill works at all in that place; he does not know. If he blows the ship, it does not matter. Think of me, brothers, he writes. It is little, but it is all he has. Crawler Carl leaves robot Donut on the couch next to Loita and goes to do the commercial.

beats.headline: The admins were holos
beats.text: Entry three, and the last on file. He has blown the ship. His skill protected him, but the forcefield kept the ship from breaking apart, and the two admins who appeared to be with him were holograms. He was fooled, and he is ashamed. The gravity has failed, the temperature is dropping, and it is getting difficult to breathe. He does not think they can remove him while the forcefield holds. He can see his beloved Qurux. It shines and warms him in the cold. He prays someone avenges her, because he cannot.

beats.headline: Not god. Coolie.
beats.text: Robot Donut explodes in the green room. A massive crack runs across the picture window, and the blue forcefield is the only thing keeping the water out. It holds. Crawler Carl's first thought is to thank god, and his second corrects it: not god, Coolie. The admin Loita dies on the floor of that room, unable to teleport while the shield is up. Crawler Carl adds a note of his own to the Cookbook, addressed to the subject: he used this passage to plan the first step, and he did it for Coolie and for a little girl named Bonnie.

beats.headline: The source he protects
beats.text: Pressed to name his outside source, and offered a Legendary box for it, Crawler Carl does not give it up. If he names the Cookbook, it disappears. The version put to him, with polymers and technicolor residue reacting to space plastic, is more complicated than what happened. What he actually knew was simpler: the forcefield, thanks to the subject's passage, and that a disco ball covers everything in dust, from the same book. The rest was a toy panel he already knew was a piece of shit.

beats.headline: What Coolie would do
beats.text: In the saferoom, with the children watching The Last Unicorn and tens of thousands of NPC deaths planned for phase four, Crawler Carl thinks of the subject: the Cookbook author who sacrificed everything just in an attempt to kill two admins. He thinks of Priestly, too, and wonders what either would do in his position. His own answer: Coolie would do exactly what he is doing. Priestly would not.

beats.headline: His last view
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut are pulled onto a ship without warning, and the side wall is clear. Earth fills it: the Indian Ocean, the edge of Madagascar, mostly clear skies. Crawler Carl feels tears come, and thinks at once of the subject, who wrote the nineteenth edition. This was his last view, though of his own home planet. The file is now explicit: he died after a failed assassination attempt on a pair of admins. Crawler Donut vomits her tuna lunch.

tagline.text: Priestly wrote the fourteenth edition of the Cookbook and is its single best source on the ninth floor. When Carl weighs his own plan, he knows that Coolie would do the same, and Priestly would not.
Priestly loved Larracos, a living, breathing poem of a city, and he broke when he saw it destroyed. His last entry is an incoherent jumble.
Priestly was conscripted into the bugbears' army in the final days of Faction Wars. According to another author's note, he never reached the battle.

beats.headline: The best source on the ninth
beats.text: For the record: the subject enters the file as a thought. Crawler Carl sits in the saferoom while the children watch The Last Unicorn, with tens of thousands of NPC deaths planned for phase four, and thinks of two Cookbook authors. One is Coolie. The other is Priestly, who wrote the fourteenth edition and is the single best source of information on the ninth floor. He wonders what either would do in his position. Coolie would do exactly what he is doing. Priestly would not.

beats.headline: A living, breathing poem
beats.text: Fourteenth edition. Larracos is like a dream, the subject writes, a living, breathing poem. An inverted funnel of museums, galleries, colleges and colour, layered like a cone going deeper. The NPCs live there, with purpose and life, and for the first time since he was dragged into this he feels awe instead of rage. It is too beautiful to be used this way, and too real not to be a copy of somewhere that existed. Tonight, before the crawlers are expelled, he plans to sit down and watch a play.

beats.headline: He fears for his mind
beats.text: The same note turns. The aliens who buy their weapons in the pleasure districts are expelled with the crawlers, less than thirty hours before the fighting begins, and return once only three armies remain. By the time it is over, they say, none of the NPCs are left alive and none of the buildings stand, all for an imaginary prize. It makes his heart hurt. He offers to draw a map; the one Milk drew is still good but lacks detail. He fears what happens to his mind when he sees the city destroyed.

beats.headline: So much. So little.
beats.text: The crawler counter falls under a hundred thousand, and Crawler Carl thinks of the subject. The system broke him. Seeing that city destroyed as he marched with the bugbear army over the bodies of the NPCs, among them actors he had watched in a play, finally snapped what sanity he had left. His last entry came shortly after, an incoherent jumble. So much. So little. Stab, stab, stab. If I fall, if I stand. It matters not when the song is done.

beats.headline: The trap he fell into
beats.text: Crawler Carl has just killed a great many innocent NPCs, and weighs it against the subject. Priestly fell into the trap of caring so much it paralysed him into inaction, and it broke him. Crawler Carl decides he is not going to make the same mistake: this is war, and the NPCs he killed were spared a bloody conflict that ended in their deaths anyway. A distant part of him is alarmed at this attitude. The file records both parts.

beats.headline: Stab, stab, stab
beats.text: Fourteenth edition, second-to-last entry. It is the final days of Faction Wars, the orcs are going to win, and the army the subject was conscripted into is going to fall; he writes that he dies tomorrow. The bugbears march in the morning and laugh at everything. Conscripts in his squad plan to flee into the forest. His people number three hundred, down from millions, and the real gods have not intervened. He hopes there is music. Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, adds: do not read the last one. He does not make it to the battle once he sees what happened to Larracos.

beats.headline: What the Conscript spell hid
beats.text: Crawler Carl leads a party into a tower lobby while the sluggalos who came with him run back into the city. During the real Faction Wars, he could open his warlord menu and force them back into line. That, the file notes, is something Priestly and several other Cookbook authors before him did not know about the Conscript spell.

beats.headline: The city he meant
beats.text: Entering the Larracos College of Magic. Crawler Carl steps outside and, for the first time, sees the city whole: towers growing out of the ring like crystals, an alabaster saferoom tower wrapped in flowering vines, an observatory, the scent of drained ocean under the flowers. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who loved this city so much it drove him mad to see it destroyed. Now he can see what Priestly meant. It is like something out of a Tolkien novel.

beats.headline: His greatest desires
beats.text: Fourteenth edition. In the absolute, scorching heat of battle, the subject writes, one learns who one really is and what one really wants. One faces one's greatest fears and, much worse, one's greatest desires laid bare. For him they are the same, and it is his devastation. Stab, stab, stab. The note sits in the Cookbook while Crawler Carl's people hold the entrance of a castle under pulse rifle fire.

beats.headline: Slam, slam, slam
beats.text: At the bottom of Larracos, Crawler Carl walks through ruin: walls scarred as if by electrical strikes, the roof long gone, wet slime and ash, a smell of burned fish, rotten milk and sulfur. Red ash rains on everything. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who went insane at the sight of this city after it had fallen. Stab, stab, stab, he thinks. Slam, slam, slam. A statue that once stood at the entrance lies shattered, glittering in the ash.

tagline.text: Edict is a level-50 mantis merchant of the Dark Hive. Every choice left to him would ruin either him or his hive, so he found a fourth: he threw a punch at Carl and was teleported away naked, leaving a metric ton of gold behind.

beats.headline: Frozen twice for punching Bomo
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl sent Bomo into Zockau with a note for the last mantis on the floor, the one who trades the looted gear, offering protection in exchange for that gear: no gear, no deal. The mantis comes. In the saferoom he attacks Bomo twice with his fists, and is frozen for a minute and then an hour. He is small and shivering, without the sword-arms the females carry, and looks like a child. Edict. Mantis. Level fifty. Merchant. The Dark Hive. He is not a hunter or a fighter, he says. He is just the accountant.

beats.headline: Already paid for
beats.text: He learns from Crawler Donut's joke that the elf Akland is dead, and deflates further. Vrah is almost here, and has told him he must mate with her. His loot is contracted to the Burrowers, the mantis government, paid in advance and due to them when this floor collapses; he goes straight to the ninth. Giving it to Crawler Carl would ruin his family and his hive. He is of Deep Mind. So he has already handed it to another entity for a small fee, and does not say who.

beats.headline: A split in the tunnel
beats.text: The disease Crawler Carl gave Vrah has put his hive's fate at a split in the tunnel. Hand over the gear, and his family is ruined and he must kill himself in shame. Refuse Vrah, and her family takes revenge on his. Mate with her, and it is a forbidden coupling between his hive and hers; they would be deemed traitors. He explains to Crawler Donut that the female eats the male's head, and a secondary brain in his abdomen keeps him going. The more he talks, the straighter he stands. He needs to die in battle.

beats.headline: Finding the stars
beats.text: He hates this place, he says, and everything about it. Finding the stars was the worst thing that ever happened to his people: a slow, horrific death, expansion to the point of oblivion. The primals finally understood, too late. Some of the kua-tin know it too. They call it the Great Consensus, but it is not; there is no agreement, and their young do not understand. Then he asks, quickly, to be let into Crawler Carl's space.

beats.headline: Super Naughty, an inch short
beats.text: Vrah limps into the hallway, smoke rising from her crotch. Crawler Carl gives the subject a one-time pass through his door. With a strangled battle cry, Edict lunges at Crawler Carl and punches, and freezes with his small fist an inch short. Super Naughty. He blinks twice and disappears, teleported naked to the closest mob nest. Despite his report that he gave all his loot away, a metric ton of gold coins drops at Crawler Carl's feet, burying him to the ankles. Crawler Carl suspects this was the best possible outcome for him, or if not him, his family.

beats.headline: What he said stays
beats.text: At the end of a long day, approaching an ursine village, Crawler Donut says she kind of feels bad for that guy, Edict: he did not want to be here, and they forced him to play the game. Crawler Carl is not sympathetic. He has been thinking about what the subject said all day and cannot get it out of his head. He believes Edict did not want to be there and hated how the universe works, and he still thinks he was wrong. That is what bothers him most.

tagline.text: Sierra was Viscount Fog's flying mount, a level-65 northropi vampire turned by the very thing they hunted. Carl fell out of the sky onto her and drove a jagged branch through her heart.

beats.headline: Out of the storm
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl is levitating above the forest in a freezing downpour, and has just spotted Miriam Dom's sparks when something slams into him from the side. The spell snaps off and he falls, then freezes in midair as the boss music starts. Special Forest Encounter. Two talons hang fifteen feet away. The shape is the same kind of mob as Quetzalcoatlus from the last floor, but flesh and undead: a pelican crossed with a vulture, the size of a flying giraffe, a beak as long as Crawler Carl. Sierra. Northropi Vampire. Level sixty-five Neighborhood Boss.

beats.headline: A bereft minion
beats.text: Her description files her as a Bereft Minion of Viscount Fog, the now-deceased hunter of vampires, who trained his trusty mount never to leave his side. Together they hunted evil. When Fog set out to exterminate a newcomer, a vampire by the name of Miriam Dom, it went bad. Sierra swept down to save her master, was injured by Miriam, and stumbled away. In less than a day the bloodlust ravaged her. Now on the hunt for her first kill, she has become what she and her master hated most. Free her from her misery.

beats.headline: Holy water and a new sun
beats.text: Her talons close on Crawler Carl's legs and chest and pull, and his health flashes red. Crawler Donut's Magic Missile hits her wing. Crawler Carl heals and smashes a Holy Gooper against the talon on his chest; the foot sizzles, and she only crushes harder. Then Crawler Donut rises out of the canopy with her light turned up like a new sun. The boss rears back, her head bursts into flames, and she flings Crawler Carl straight up into the sky before landing on her back atop the trees.

beats.headline: A branch through the heart
beats.text: Sierra, northropi vampire, is dead. Crawler Carl falls out of the sky onto her, fist first, and tears through her chest. She hangs impaled between two trees with her head burning and her guts falling on him, her health in the red and refusing to drop further. Her heart lies on the ground, still beating in time to the music. Crawler Carl picks up a jagged broken branch and stabs it into the organ, and she explodes. Winner! Crawler Donut announces that he punched her in the lady garden.

beats.headline: His flying mount
beats.text: In the clearing, Crawler Carl tells Miriam Dom that they have just killed Viscount Fog's flying mount, Sierra. Miriam's answer: good. She was dangerous. Fog, she explains, was the star of one of the programs this place runs, and started hunting her the moment she landed on this floor. The viewer counter has been jacked all the way to the right since the boss battle.

tagline.text: Prudence is a level-28 ursine barmaid, hiding behind her counter with her two cubs while Big Tina roams outside. Tina has already eaten her husband, and Prudence knows why Tina hunts.
Prudence, widowed by Big Tina, is sheltering with her cubs, Randy and Todd, in Carl's guildhall.
Prudence, the barmaid who told Carl the story of Tina's recital, died protecting two children when the mantises came.

beats.headline: Behind the counter
beats.text: For the record: the pub is dark and stinks of death when a voice behind the counter hisses at Crawler Donut to turn off her light. She is out there. She came in once already and ate the subject's husband right out of the doorway. The subject is a large bear in an apron with two small cubs clutched in her arms, and a Terrified debuff blinking over her head. Prudence. Level twenty-eight Ursine Barmaid. Yes, she says, that is Big Tina outside. She came back for her revenge, for what the clerics did.

beats.headline: The secret recital
beats.text: Her account. Dancing is forbidden, but a community of mothers taught the children ballet in secret and planned a small recital. The best dancer was eight years old, the daughter of the town's head cleric, and was to dance last. Her name was Tina. Her father found out and stormed the school with his clerics. Tina's mother slapped him in front of the congregation. He whipped her to the edge of death on the stage, pushed Tina aside, and she fell. The wand that was meant to shoot sparkles broke. Sinners get what they deserve, says her cub Randy. That's right, honey.

beats.headline: Her grandmother's faith
beats.text: Before the cleric could punish the others, the nine-tier attack came. Most died. Only females were transformed; a small handful survived unchanged, including the subject's grandmother, the most pious, whose faith saved her. Tina was the only child who turned, and her mind is gone. Her mother and several other mothers survive as dinosaurs, and her mother still tries to hold her back. Her name, the subject tells Crawler Carl, is Kiwi. Quest Update: The Recital.

beats.headline: Now you can
beats.text: Crawler Carl tells the subject to take her children through the door they came out of. She tried it before, she says, and it would not let her. You can now, he says, and gives her and her cubs access. Once Big Tina has moved down the street, Prudence and her two cubs are inside the guildhall, and Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut go out into the rain.

beats.headline: Dinosaur movies on the couch
beats.text: The subject sits on the couch with her cubs crawling all over her, acting like nothing happened. A Land Before Time sequel is on, which Crawler Carl finds a little fucked-up, since the cubs have just watched their dad get eaten by a dinosaur. They seem to like it. Little Todd complains to Mordecai about the accuracy of the dinosaurs.

beats.headline: Samantha in her lap
beats.text: Back in the saferoom, the subject sits on the couch with a cub on either side while a nineties horror movie with an animatronic tyrannosaurus plays. Samantha is in her lap, having her hair stroked by the bear. Crawler Carl does not ask. Bomo and the Sledge watch the screen with the rest of them.

beats.headline: Asleep through the bickering
beats.text: Her cubs spend the evening feuding with the changeling children. Randy tells Bonnie the gnome she is going to hell and that all heathens burn in the fires of judgement; When Skarn tells him not to be mean, Todd stands behind his brother. The subject, the mother of the two bears, is passed out on the couch, snoring.

beats.headline: Never part of the plan
beats.text: The mantises take the airship, and the Sledge has to jump. His report: he is okay, Bonnie is okay, the bear cubs are okay, Prudence is okay. Crawler Carl notes that they never agreed to save Prudence and the cubs; they were meant to stay in the saferoom until the collapse and simply disappear. He tells the Sledge to protect Bonnie and the bears if he can, but not to sacrifice himself for any of them.

beats.headline: Died protecting two babies
beats.text: Prudence, ursine barmaid, is dead. The notice comes from the Sledge, in his clipped way, while a mushroom crawler takes the stage in the ballroom: Prudence dead. Died protecting two babies. They're crying. Hugging Bonnie. Too many mantises. Still fighting. Crawler Carl's assessment at that moment is that the plan is done. The Sledge reports a while after that the cubs are safe, for now.

beats.headline: According to Prudence
beats.text: Tina finally dances. Two cretins hold up a ship's mainsail painted with waves, and she twirls across the stage, casting sparkles. According to Prudence, poor dead Prudence, the dance Tina was supposed to perform was called the Water Ballad, and it was about a mer-bear. The recital the subject described goes on, long after, without her.

beats.headline: The orphaned cubs
beats.text: Randy and Todd, the orphaned ursine cubs, come running out of a guild in metal skull caps, dragging training spears, with little Clint, a flesh golem now in a kindergartner's body. They want to fight. Miss Nadine has told them to stay away from Tina because she killed their dad, Clint reports, but Tina is different now and her mother says she has apologized. Randy says they have been practising. Todd means to bathe in apostate blood.

tagline.text: Gideon is a crawler with some sort of human tank class who is active in the chats. Princess Donut likes him because he once said he was allergic to dogs.
Gideon is not in the top thousand, and he likes it that way. His team is waiting in the woods outside the castle, ready to assault the front if needed.
Gideon and almost thirty crawlers stayed in the woods outside the castle to sow chaos, because Carl asked them to. They died there.

beats.headline: Allergic to dogs
beats.text: For the record: the subject messages Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut just as a message from Zev ends. He is active in the chats. Crawler Carl has met him once, and cannot remember his details or where he is from: some sort of human tank class. His team popped their bubble early, so he never needed saving, and he was there for the last fight on the previous floor. Crawler Donut likes him because he once said he was allergic to dogs. Crawler Carl tells him to go down the stairs.

beats.headline: A warning about a whip
beats.text: He is about to go down, he says, but first a warning. Two god things just rolled past his world, beating the shit out of each other: a giant hairless gorilla, and a snake with the head of a bald guy who looked like Woody Harrelson. The snake killed the gorilla, but first threw it against a bubble with a monster inside. The bubble popped. The monster got out, it may be headed their way, and it is carrying a very large whip.

beats.headline: Not in the top thousand
beats.text: With vampirism spreading through the forest, the subject reports in: he just fought a half-genie, half-owl vampire that tried to rip his neck out, and his team's cleric killed it before it could get him. It was damn close. Crawler Carl asks who is in the top fifty, since that is who gets invited to the party. The subject is not even in the top thousand, and likes it that way.

beats.headline: The Gideon distraction
beats.text: Crawler Carl's plan for the party runs through him. From the planning notes: go with the Gideon distraction to empty the castle of as many guards as possible, then make the move. Britney, given the choice between assisting Crawler Donut on stage or joining the subject's assault team, took the stage. While the Sledge and the changelings head for the castle's secret entrance, Gideon and his team set up in the woods outside, to observe and to assault the front of the castle if needed.

beats.headline: Two hundred mounted elves
beats.text: Hidden near the castle with a few dozen crawlers, the subject reports: about two hundred mounted elves just rode out. The airship crept in, a spotlight caught it, and its bomb missed. The mantises are mostly further north. Then: holy shit, gotta go. Next message: mantises and elves everywhere, fighting each other. His team is still hidden. The airship is covered with bugs like moths on a lightbulb, and the towers are shooting magic missiles. Crawler Carl tells him to stay down and not attack until told.

beats.headline: Two words: Gideon. Run.
beats.text: Gideon, crawler, is dead. Queen Imogen holds Crawler Carl in the air and asks whether those were not his friends hiding in the trees just outside. Crawler Carl sends two words: Gideon. Run. Warning: This crawler is deceased. They have been removed from your address book. There is blood running down the queen's dress. Almost thirty crawlers were in that team. They stayed back to sow chaos because Crawler Carl asked them to, and Crawler Carl's own assessment is that they died because he asked. Imani does not know yet.

beats.headline: Why it doesn't hurt
beats.text: After the fight, Crawler Donut lists her dead friends to Crawler Carl: Firas, Gwen, the Popov brothers, Gideon, even Signet and the dinosaurs who did not know how to dance. She should be crying, she says, and she is not. Florin cried, and Chris, and Elle. She asks why it does not hurt as much as it should, and whether she is doing something wrong.

beats.headline: He talked Gideon into it
beats.text: Crawler Donut's account of the floor, set down for her fans. It was not all good; lots of sad things happened. Her friend Firas died. Another guy named Gideon died. She did not know him very well except in the chat, but Crawler Carl was sad, because he had talked Gideon into helping them.

tagline.text: Horton is a mushroom crawler at the queen's party who is afraid of Elle. When she shouts that Ferdinand's hat is his merch, he gives her the finger from across the room.
Horton was the talent show's second-to-last act. He played 'Wonderwall' on a guitar missing a string, and the building shook.
Horton, the mushroom crawler who played 'Wonderwall' at the queen's party, died in the fight that followed.

beats.headline: You have merch
beats.text: For the record: the subject was in the first group led into the main ballroom, a mushroom guy Crawler Carl had only seen in passing, afraid of Elle for some unknown reason. When Ferdinand turns up in a tall hat, Elle says it looks like a hat designed to look like Horton the mushroom guy over there. Hey, Horton, come here, she shouts. You have merch. From across the room, the mushroom guy lifts a middle finger at her. Elle keeps laughing. I love that guy, she says.

beats.headline: The second-to-last act
beats.text: The second-to-last act appears on stage: the mushroom guy, Horton, with an acoustic guitar missing a string. It is the same guitar Britney is meant to play for the final act. He tunes it for a long while, and Queen Imogen grows impatient. This is 'Wonderwall,' he says, and starts to play. Crawler Donut's reaction is OMG. Crawler Carl laughs at the absurdity of it all: a mushroom dude playing a poorly-tuned guitar and singing his cat's favourite song, with the whole universe watching.

beats.headline: I guess I'm done
beats.text: Ka-Blam. The building shakes, tables fall, the buffet collapses and scatters the hunters. The subject pauses his song. The floor tiles have shattered like windshield glass, and near the exits they are simply gone, leaving burning, jagged holes. Crawlers standing over the gaps do not fall through. Samantha, somewhere in the castle, reports by chat that she has chomped down on the soul crystals. On stage, the subject speaks: Uh, I guess I'm done. He goes offstage.

beats.headline: The Wonderwall guy
beats.text: Horton, crawler, is dead. The notice comes from Crawler Donut, reeling off the dead to Crawler Carl after the fight: Firas, Gwen, and Horton, the Wonderwall guy, and the Popovs. Poor Horton, too, she says; it is always sad to lose a fellow musician. Elle is really upset about it. Crawler Donut thinks Elle feels bad about making fun of him all the time.

beats.headline: A really good singer
beats.text: Crawler Donut's account of the floor, set down for her fans, lists what went wrong. Firas died. Gideon died. Gwendolyn Duet died. This mushroom guy who was a really good singer died. She does not give his name. The Popov brothers died too, and then turned into babies and were kicked out of the game, which made everyone happy.

entities.name: Everly
entities.role: Author of the fifth edition of the Cookbook

tagline.text: Crawler Everly wrote the fifth edition of the Cookbook, and her verdict on hiring mercenaries is that it is a disaster: 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die.
Everly's last entries tell of a sponsor who kept her alive and a gift she dared to hope for. Then: I take it all back.

Everly was a Sward Mantis and an Explosives Engineer. Her sponsor's compass led her to the top of a tower on the eighth floor that was only an advertisement, and she was crushed to death on the way down.

beats.headline: Five mercenaries, one disaster
beats.text: For the record: a note in the Cookbook, signed Crawler Everly, fifth edition. Her party hired five mercenaries: four from the Merc guild in the Desperado Club, a healer from Club Vanquisher who charges per spell. It was, and continues to be, a disaster. 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die. Lose one through a personal space and he turns up three saferooms away. One wandered off and cannot be fired. Her level-50 dwarf died when a chair hit him. The whole thing is a scam.

beats.headline: Carl cannot stop thinking of her
beats.text: Crawler Carl turns over the items just given to Donut and suspects the reason: they expect everyone else to be dead. He finds a seven worn into the end of a metal rod, then another in a hammer's handle. Seven, as in the seventh floor? And he cannot stop thinking of the subject's final, heartbreaking entry in the Cookbook: My sponsor was deliberately steering me not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered. He thinks of Orren the liaison, and of the warning Orren tried to give.

beats.headline: Hasten Poison, and a hope
beats.text: Two entries, fifth edition. First: her sponsor sent a box meant for someone else in her party, and not a crawler but a mercenary. A spellbook of Hasten Poison. She was upset. Not five hours afterwards, he used it to kill the boss holding the lockbox key and saved them all. She does not trust her sponsors, but she trusts they want her alive, so their advertisements stay on display. Second: on floor eight, a great box, a tool for shortcuts through the maze. A spark in her chitin. A longing for warmth and stars.

beats.headline: I take it all back
beats.text: Her last entry, fifth edition. I take it back. I take it all back. Her sponsor was deliberately steering her not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered and heartrending and painful. She was a fool. She curses Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited, whatever that means, and wishes pain on its children. Beneath it, Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition: this is Everly's last entry. She did not say how she was set up, which is unfortunate. Future authors, be as detailed as you can.

beats.headline: An outcast of the sward
beats.text: For the record, the subject's file. A mantis who left her colony a few days before the demons came to her world, because she could not abide the rules or the lack of individualism, and wandered the sward alone. In the dungeon she found thousands of her fellow mantises, confused and afraid, who wanted to work with her. She struck out on her own anyway, with hired NPCs and the invisible words on her prayer mat. Two or three dozen mercenaries over the floors: some fired in a rage, some vanished onto her payroll, the rest dead.

beats.headline: Gordon's Compass, forty-nine uses
beats.text: The eighth floor: a flat grassland pocked with thousands of holes leading down, and in its middle a tower fifty levels high, with a note on the door saying that whoever enters must reach the top before coming back down. Then a benefactor box from her generous sponsor, Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited: Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management, forty-nine uses, for the quickest and safest path through a maze, but not a subterranean one. She and ten mercenaries go up. Each time, the safe door. On the forty-ninth use, it shatters.

beats.headline: This dead end was sponsored
beats.text: At the top, she has been getting viewership awards, and allows herself a glimmer of hope for a fan box. On a pedestal sits a folded note, which the system reads aloud: Never trust your life to Gordon Waystation Outfitters. This dead end was sponsored by Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited. Don't get caught with nowhere to go. The whole tower was an advertisement, built by her own sponsor, and the compass led her to it. Humiliation, then anger. She scrawls an angry note in the Cookbook as the roof begins to come down.
