beats.headline: The Inevitable Ruin
beats.text: Ten flights down, three are left, under a lowering ceiling. The dwarf digs for a keyhole they have no key for; the subject pities him, a first. Her queen called this moment the Inevitable Ruin. She decides it arrived earlier, when she abandoned the others. The ogre, silent since she hired him, says maybe it is not inevitable, like she says. She reaches out and touches him. Class: Explosives Engineer. Race: Primal. Birth Race: Sward Mantis. Top Level: 62. Dungeon Exit: crushed to death on the eighth floor. Current status: Dead.

entities.name: Toyotomi
entities.role: Sai mercenary · Sergeant in the Princess Posse

tagline.text: Toyotomi is a level-70 Sai mercenary leader, a rhinoceros inherited along with the Prism's castle. His squad died at the Desperado Club and he refuses to lead men now, and Rend has just eaten his boot.
Toyotomi is a sergeant in the Princess Posse, leading Li Na's builder squad, and his next job is the tall synergy tower they are calling the Nest.
Toyotomi died defending the Nest's door against a crawler with a dog, cleaved in half by a spell. Bomo will regenerate. Toyotomi will not.

beats.headline: He ate my boot
beats.text: For the record: found duct-taped in the Prism's castle, with Crawler Carl's pet attempting to swallow his foot. A large bipedal rhinoceros, a true NPC, now under a Princess Posse banner. He frees his wrists and moves to clobber the pet. He ate my boot, he reports; one boot is gone, revealing a round foot. Carl apologizes and promises a replacement. Toyotomi. Level 70 Sai Outpost Guard Mercenary Leader. Sergeant in the Princess Posse. A hired mercenary, paid to the end of the floor or his death, inherited when the Prism fell.

beats.headline: A broken creature, per the file
beats.text: The System's file on the subject. Once an honorable, experienced leader of Sai. His entire squad died in an incident at the Desperado Club that Crawler Carl may or may not have been partially responsible for, and the few survivors went to the mercenary markets. His failure to protect his friends against the demon haunts him, and he refuses to lead men now, despite great talent. He was regaining his confidence when a man in underwear and a talking cat trounced him, tied him up and slaughtered his charge.

beats.headline: Accepting his exile
beats.text: His magic is for outposts, not palaces. Edifice Shield cannot cover a castle bigger than this one, and this one was already too big; Warlord D'Nadia insisted, so he shielded it in spurts, and was resting when the crawlers arrived. I am shamed. Leave him here, he asks, to defend this building until he dies. It is what he wants. Carl changes the plan and sends him to Shanty Town. He accepts his exile. It is not an exile, Carl says. They need his talents.

beats.headline: Leader of Li Na's builders
beats.text: Earlier, at the foot of Li Na's new clocktower in Shanty Town, the subject was seen pointing up and talking animatedly, in his element, directing the last-minute construction. Now dozens of wires dangle from the clocktower's arms, an exploit; if it works, Li Na's builder squad, led by the subject, gets straight to work on a very tall, very powerful, very specialized and very expensive synergy tower at the edge of the hole leading down into Larracos. It only works during the next phase. In the menu, its name is simple. It is called the Nest.

beats.headline: It is the color of granite
beats.text: The Nest is up, and Crawler Donut wants it purple. It is the color of granite, the subject answers, because it is made of granite; paint it now and the mages cannot coat it in protections, and if the build is master quality it glows gold. The protections: at least twenty per block by bleed and net pattern, strength to two hundred percent on completion, doubled by his Edifice Shield. Four deflector towers where one would do. Carl asks, for the third time, about tunneling. It is protected enough to float if the ground disappears.

beats.headline: Deflector towers keep the gods away
beats.text: Crawler Donut relays the subject's professional opinion to Carl over the chat: Toyotomi says the deflector towers keep the gods away. Carl advises her to think of them as an electric fence. They are far from foolproof. She should avoid unnecessary god attention, which means not shrieking over a massive PA. She does not shriek, she says.

beats.headline: A woman with a dog
beats.text: The last messages from the Nest's lower floor, where the subject stands guard over Crawler Donut with Bomo and several mages. Bomo: someone is trying to come into the tower. Toyotomi: he is securing the front entrance. Donut: she cannot leave the tower; there is a net around it. Carl asks if it is one of the zarogoth things. No, the subject answers. It is a crawler. A woman with a dog. She's coming in. System note on that message: This message is from a deceased mercenary.

beats.headline: Toyotomi was dead-dead
beats.text: Crawler Carl reaches the Nest and spares a quick, sad glance for the subject, Bomo and the defending mages, all of them cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo is supposed to regenerate on the tenth floor. Toyotomi is not. Toyotomi was dead-dead. Up the curving stairwell, Lucia Mar is shouting at her dog.

tagline.text: Kandy "Bigs" Newton is a level-29 sluggalette of the Princess Posse who burst out of Carl's slugpox and planted a hatchet between Vinata's eyes. The System credits her with the kill on the Sepsis Whore.
Bigs rides in uninvited on other people's mounts, asking who she gets to chop, and she has to be told not to kill the prisoners.
The sluggalo code is unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches. Bigs calls Carl daddy-o, and she holds him to all four.
Bigs took the chicken truck's wheel from Tipid, turned on the deep fryer, and drove it into the arena. About ten sluggalos were still inside at the end, and they had lost Hedy.

beats.headline: Credit for the kill
beats.text: For the record: System Message. The Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Kandy "Bigs" Newton of the Princess Posse. Katia asks who the hell that is. The answer: a sluggalo who burst out of Crawler Carl's back, out of his slugpox, and planted a hatchet between Vinata's eyes. Level 29. The size of a bulldog, pink-dyed hair in a monk's ring, piercings down her head, a single hatchet growing from its crown, dripping. Oh, daddy, you don't look so good.

beats.headline: Call me Bigs
beats.text: Samantha flies in, a charred husk, and the subject objects: He's mine, bitch. When Victory returns, the subject swings at her too, and the hatchet goes straight through her leg. With an ogre and a squad of mantaurs closing in, Crawler Carl asks, Okay, Kandy is it? Stay with him and kill anyone in his way. Call me Bigs, the subject says, flecking naga blood everywhere. Is this ogre dude a friend, or is he getting kneecapped? Not a friend. After the fight: Who am I killing?

beats.headline: Imma get my chop on
beats.text: Dong Quixote arrives through a teleport trap on Gonk the swamp yak, which was not the plan, and the subject arrives on the back of it, which was even less the plan. New paint: a massive teardrop on the stalk of her right eye. She leaps off with a whoop, waving the axe. Imma get my chop on today. Where the bad guys at? She heard from another slug that Justice Light says a mount through a teleport trap brings every rider. Carl orders her back on the yak.

beats.headline: Outside the witness's reach
beats.text: A witness spell has pulled almost everyone into a frozen pile. Left out of it: Carl, Dong Quixote, the pets, Jamal and the subject. Only Carl and Dong carry the invulnerable glow; Jamal and the subject simply were not affected. Carl already knows why: the system counts the sluggalos and the former tattoos as a different kind of NPC. At the Madness castle she bounces to Donut's distant battle playlist while Carl tries to clear the halls.

beats.headline: One of you is getting the chop
beats.text: The subject ties up Selvi and Tuba, the two conscripted women from Burcu's party, and asks whether she can kill one of them, since that one is already bleeding pretty good. She is a friend, Carl says. Keep them safe. I'll wait until he's gone, the subject whispers loudly to them. Then one of you is getting the chop. Carl sends her off on reconnaissance instead. Yeah, baby. She returns: Yo, daddy-o, the front door is wide open. Nothing out there but fields.

beats.headline: No, she's a bad guy
beats.text: The subject growls, strangely dog-like, when she looks up at Li Na. She's not a bad guy, Carl says; her brother died. No, she's a bad guy, says the subject. You know what she did to Sneaky Tyler C? Tied a potion to him and ordered him to run right into the god. He blew up the moment he touched it. That is what she heard. It was a bitch-ass move. She does not like her.

beats.headline: Girl talk on borrowed carpet
beats.text: Samantha's account. Samantha has promised to catch Tipid up on Faction Wars herself, and the subject slimes up: Yo, I want to hear this, too. Samantha likes her even though she gets orange goo all over the new carpet borrowed from the Larracos College of Magic. They have girl talk. The subject is now invited to Samantha's bachelorette party. Samantha tells it all, down to the thing at the bottom of the dungeon waking up. I thought you explained it perfect, says the subject.

beats.headline: You're going to drown in fire
beats.text: Mordecai's new form glitches whenever a different race comes near him for the first time, and when the subject wandered in, Rosetta feared they had lost him entirely. He told the subject she was going to drown in fire. If he were not on the don't-chop list, he would be getting the kneecap treatment. He also told Splash Zone he was going to die screaming while his family watched. Mordecai: nobody should put stock in it. This stuff is designed to be scary, not true.

beats.headline: How come I didn't get no hat
beats.text: An enchanted hat and an enchanted headband for the pets, each with a list of powers, and the subject wants to know why she did not get a hat. Because she is not a pet, Carl says. She is technically a mercenary. Mordecai suspects that if they reach the eleventh floor, Donut's class may come with mercenary accessories too.

beats.headline: The sluggalo code, and Real Gs
beats.text: Dong Quixote is dying on the couch with the subject covering his head, glaring at Carl. She lays out the sluggalo code: unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches. Carl provides none of it, is not killing the Li Na murderer, and is not letting her kneecap anyone. That makes him the bitch. You're right, Carl says. I'm sorry. Wait, I am? Carl remembers saying they need to help each other or stop being something. Real Gs? she offers. Real Gs. You're a good daddy, she says. But not the one he owes an apology.

beats.headline: The birth that saved his ass
beats.text: Crawler Carl has kept his slugpox active under the Emberus ring on purpose, arguing that the birth of the subject on the previous floor saved his ass. Everyone else thought this was a terrible idea. The cure Mordecai made sits on the crafting table. Pop: a level 30 slug bursts out of his back in a shower of blood and pus, backward cap on an eye stalk. His name is Lil' Mello Haze, a level higher than the subject and much smaller.

beats.headline: Never been so proud
beats.text: The airship's bay doors open and the sluggalos rain down onto the stands, among the masked bankers and politicians who cannot fight back, and start to slaughter them one by one. The smallest of the small, the lowest form of dungeon NPC. From the subject, in the chat: I've never been so proud. Unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches! Hell yeah!

beats.headline: Get out of our chair
beats.text: Carl needs the worst possible drivers for the last part. Yeah, get out of our chair, the subject tells Tipid. We's driving. The blood-soaked sluggalos pile into the chicken truck, and someone turns on the deep fryer: the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express is open for business. Carl orders the fryer off, since it is going to splash or catch fire and burn them all to death. The subject: You do your thing. We do our thing. Don't worry about us, Daddy. When the great door opens: You got it!

beats.headline: We lost Hedy
beats.text: The chicken truck, so smashed that Carl is surprised it runs, spins, slows and pulls up beside him. About ten sluggalos are left inside, and the whole thing stinks of fire. The subject leans out of the window. We done killing? For now, Carl says: thirty minutes to collapse, gather the survivors and get back to the safe room. Sure thing, daddy-o. Then, head lowered, she tells him: We lost Hedy. She points with her head hatchet at the wreck of the ice-cream truck.

tagline.text: Burcu is new to the top ten: a level-59 Porsuk swashbuckler with the head of a badger. She fought Osvaldo and Prepotente after Imogen's death at the close of the last floor.

Burcu is Turkish and very serious, and she was one of the three who fought over the memorial crystal. Tonight her drunk, jealous teammate punched Carl and promised that his Burcu is going to kill him.
Burcu's whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness, and nobody can reach them. That most likely means conscription.
Architect Houston cut out Burcu's tongue and voice box, and he murdered her mother in front of her. She died in his theatre when the traps fired, looking at Carl with accusation in her eyes.

beats.headline: Number ten, a newcomer
beats.text: For the record: the top ten list repopulates after the show, and number ten is a woman named Burcu, new to the list. Level 59, a badger-headed Porsuk, the same race as every bartender at the Desperado Club. Class: Swashbuckler, the same as Crawlers Tran and Bautista. Crawler Carl met her briefly at the Butcher's Masquerade and has her in his chat. She, Osvaldo and Prepotente got into a fight after Imogen's death at the end of the previous floor. Carl was knocked out during it.

beats.headline: My Burcu is going to kill you
beats.text: The Desperado Club, minutes before an assassination. Carl warns four dancing crawlers to leave. Zeynep, a level-52 mage, agrees. Emir Akbas, a level-55 Zebani, is drunk and jealous, punches Carl, and loses a boot for it; Zeynep mutes him. As he is dragged out: My Burcu is going to kill you. Carl's file on the subject is short. Around number ten, never spoken to, very serious, like Hekla. Turkish. One of three who fought over the memorial crystal. Maybe these are all one family.

beats.headline: Taken in by the Madness
beats.text: Boomer's report on missing crawlers, walking the ruined base. Most are under the Posse banner now. The goat stays unaffiliated and hidden; so does Lucia Mar. And there is a crawler named Burcu whose whole team appears, by the Find Crawler skill, to have been taken in by the Madness. People who know them say they are not answering messages. That likely means conscription.

beats.headline: Three dots and a corpse
beats.text: In the Madness castle, the Voodoo book updates with three entries, and Find Crawler puts them on the map. Two women from the dancing party stand among the guards with the blue glow of conscription. The subject has no glow and is not moving, in the operating theater with Architect Houston. Also there: the corpse of Crawler Zeynep, level 58. Carl is fairly sure the subject had her own quest involving the memorial crystal. His message is not delivered: she is unaffiliated, and planning may be illegal corroboration.

beats.headline: A map, slammed shut
beats.text: Your Book of Voodoo has been updated with an entry from Crawler Burcu. Her entry page is the last one, and she is not writing to Carl. She is swiftly drawing a map of the surgical theater: a line of Xs marked Fireball traps. She begins to write something about Houston, and before Carl can read it, the thing slams itself shut. The System's ruling: This is still cheating, you clown. Nice try, though.

beats.headline: He cut out my tongue
beats.text: The theater, white and bloody. Table one: Zeynep's corpse. Table two: the subject, alive, bound, mouthing words that do not come, dried blood down her face and throat, tears running. The floor is set with Sheol-fire traps, and she has no invulnerability. A message finally gets through. He cut out my tongue and voice box. He tortured my mother. He killed her right in front of me. Free me so I can kill him. You owe me, Carl. You killed my father. Carl has no idea what she means.

beats.headline: Accusation, on the way down
beats.text: Carl calls to her not to leave the table, then puts her to sleep with a wand of Nighty-Night as she thrashes, eyes wide, and hits the switch on her bindings. His invulnerability is gone. He leaps onto her table, and it rolls, and tips. She wakes the moment he touches her, and as she falls to the white floor he sees accusation in her eyes, as in her dead mother's. The traps fire. Carl phases out. Architect Houston is dead. Burcu is dead.

beats.headline: Tuba and Selvi take a deal
beats.text: The dead Burcu's party members, Tuba and Selvi, leave. Both say they are taking a deal. Neither ever told Carl why or how the subject considered him the one who killed her father, and he fears he may never know. His own reflection on it: that is the problem with such chaos. You lose so much around the edges.

beats.headline: A guess about her father
beats.text: Carl's new mercenary is Nester, a rare blue-skinned Zebani cartographer, and her race reminds him of something he cannot shake. The now-dead crawler Burcu accused him of killing her father. He assumes her father was a crawler named Emir, who was also a Zebani. The file does not confirm it. Carl calls it just another mystery, a reminder of how fractured they still are.

entities.name: Pater Coal
entities.role: High Cleric Supreme of Emberus · Club Vanquisher

tagline.text: Pater Coal is a level-101 Hobbledehoy, the High Cleric Supreme of Emberus at Club Vanquisher and one of the few mortals in constant contact with the god. He washes Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus, and he does not always do his own talking.
Pater Coal arranged a loan from the church for Carl's new ring: 990,000 gold, interest-free for martyrs, with an asterisk. While he owes it, Carl may not renounce his religion.
Pater Coal was the first body Carl watched the AI wear. Now it is wearing Growler Gary.

beats.headline: A cleric who was expecting him
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl reaches the Club Vanquisher door with slugpox, a boil on his stomach, and a ram named Potsy refusing him entry over paperwork. A small man in long red robes pushes the ram aside. I have been waiting for you, he says. Pater Coal, Hobbledehoy, level 101, non-combatant, High Cleric Supreme of Emberus, one of the few mortals in constant contact with the deity. He walks Carl briskly past the mantaur guards toward the healer, with one extra stop at the Emberus shrine that the guards are not to be told about.

beats.headline: Feet washed in the dying sun
beats.text: Sacrament log. In the secret Temple of the Ending Sun, on ground made of fire, Pater Coal suppresses the pox with a spell, kneels, and washes Crawler Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus. The other gods cannot eavesdrop on this sacrament. The briefing: no clue to Geyrun's killer but the dog, whose memory the Nothing has spoiled; Hellik still the top suspect; a memorial crystal made by Apito, who lives. Then his eyes go milky white, and the voice names Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet. Then a toe goes into his mouth.

beats.headline: We all have our roles
beats.text: Crawler Carl tests a suspicion aloud: Zev is worried, because he has dropped off the feed. Back soon enough, the cleric answers without missing a beat, and parts of this conversation still make the feed, so the viewers have context for the quest. Carl asks outright whether he is talking to the AI. We all have our roles, Pater Coal says, and our limitations. Afterwards his pupils fade back to colour, and Emberus grants Carl a floor boon, the Martyr's Path, plus ten percent Strength, for as long as he stays in grace.

beats.headline: The ring that burns
beats.text: Field note from a turkey barn. Crawler Carl ends a deck fight pierced in several places, wrapped in a dead ogre's bear hug and loaded with debuffs, among them one called Bonked. The ring on his finger burns. It looks like his strength ring. It is not. Pater Coal secretly helped him buy it at Club Vanquisher, it is meant to hold certain debuffs at bay, and Carl was warned that it could get overloaded. He cannot take it off.

beats.headline: What if we skip the healer
beats.text: Filed out of order, the way Crawler Carl remembers it. Out of the temple, past a wisp secretary named Yasmine at the portal desk and a mantaur guard admiring himself in a mirror, Pater Coal pulls Carl aside. They must get to the healer quickly, before the guard realises where they have been and bars Carl until tomorrow. Carl, one hand on a boil that has already gone down, asks a different question. What if they do not go to the healer at all?

beats.headline: Interest-free, with an asterisk
beats.text: Transaction record. Beside a satyr jeweler, also of Emberus, Pater Coal prices the work at a million gold. Nobody ever has that much on them; the church is happy to spot it. Ten thousand down, no interest charged to martyrs, and one long-worn piece of jewellery traded in. Carl hands over his first ring. The notice reads interest-free, with an asterisk, for 990,000 gold, and bars him from renouncing his religion while in debt. Carl asks about the asterisk. The jeweler does not understand. Sure, sure, says Pater Coal. Best get this done.

beats.headline: His limitations, remembered
beats.text: Ninth floor. Crawler Carl, turning over how every person and object down here is real, imaginary or somewhere between, comes back to Pater Coal: the high cleric of the Emberus temple at Club Vanquisher, taken over by the AI, who seemed unable to separate the dungeon's story from what was actually being done to the crawlers. We all have our limitations, the cleric had said. Carl's own assessment of that sentence is on file. Terrifying.

beats.headline: Another body, same tenant
beats.text: Growler Gary, the gnoll from the Iron Tangle, is standing in Orren's office and laughing at the liaison. Crawler Carl works it out the way the Emberus temple taught him to: this is not Gary. This is the AI using his body, just as it used Pater Coal's. Orren confirms it and makes the introduction, an avatar for the system AI, and admits he had understood it only took over mobs and NPCs from the current floor.

beats.headline: Find the cleric, says Emberus
beats.text: Outside the temple portal, flat on his back and buried in notifications, Crawler Carl receives another message from Emberus: find Pater Coal, and go talk to somebody. He pushes it away. There are more urgent entries on the same screen. The Emberus ring on his finger is burning, overloaded, and the slugpox it was holding back was never cured.

beats.headline: The same trick, one more time
beats.text: Mid-parade, Grigori takes the microphone and speaks in his own voice, far faster than usual, and it is plain that the AI has taken him over, much as it took Growler Gary and Pater Coal. Crawler Carl's reading of the choice: Grigori is dungeon-born. The man he replaced at the microphone is a former crawler, and the AI does not appear able to do the same with one of those.

relations.note: The church's loan, and the disguised ring
Both worn by the AI

tagline.text: Raul is a level-70 red Maníseros land crab and a Sun-Kissed Cloud Rank warrior, meditating on top of a crashed box truck on the eve of the Chowder War. After years of cultivation, he is on the verge of a breakthrough.
Raul the crab is a totem card in Princess Donut's deck. He fights well, chants his slow spells and grovels to everybody, and he and Geraldo come to blows on sight.
Raul has been summoned onto a beach full of corpses and told that his people are dead, that he is the last of them, and that he must fertilise the eggs right now, in front of everyone.
Raul has ascended to level 110, and his card is mythic now: ten minutes per summoning, and a much deeper voice. He still calls Carl Daddy.

beats.headline: Cultivating on a box truck
beats.text: Enemy intelligence, the eve of the Chowder War. The land crabs have massed in the south to sneak-attack the monk seals, and one of them sits on top of a crashed box truck, glowing faintly yellow and talking to himself. Raul, level 70. Years of cultivation have brought him to the verge of a breakthrough, which he prays to reach before the battle begins. Probably not, notes the description, if his meditations keep getting interrupted. Crawler Carl wants one of these crabs for the deck. He picks this one.

beats.headline: A crab trap with a roll-up door
beats.text: Raul has not sensed anyone. He is rehearsing threats for the seals. Crawler Donut casts Hole under him, drops him into the truck's empty cargo bay and mutes him; Crawler Carl phases through the floor and walls on a potion, punching, while Donut dangles from the door rope with free weights through her tail and the door stays stuck half open. Under a Fear smoke curtain and Brain Freeze the crab cowers, claws up, saying no. Carl flags him on a second potion. The card is common. Carl has doubts.

beats.headline: This worthless maggot begs
beats.text: Training record. Raul casts Bris, which snaps things from a distance, and a shell that takes ten seconds of chanting. He fights well and submits to everybody. Paying Donut a compliment, he calls anyone blind to her brilliance blind to her vastness; asked whether that means fat, he throws himself down and begs permission to kill himself in his dishonour. With Geraldo it is insults, then blows over a remark about Raul's mother. Donut says stop. Raul, who is winning, stops. Geraldo cracks his shell and kills him.

beats.headline: Greased Lightning on a ghost
beats.text: Deckmaster fight on the road to Key West. A level-65 Reef Explorer in a glowing deep-dive suit is a ghost, and only magic hurts him. Donut summons Raul, who bows, sits, chants, and sets off after the fleeing creature with a glowing claw. Lazarus calls him a pansy for taking too long; Donut throws him a Greased Lightning instead of sending in the bazooka, to build his self-confidence. The speeded crab snaps the ghost's leg off, and the suit deflates. Donut reports that Raul and Geraldo are finally tolerating each other.

beats.headline: This insignificant cur is here
beats.text: Crawler Carl is blind, pierced and caught in a bear hug by Sharp-Elbows, an ogre necromancer and deckmaster nine of ten, in a collapsing barn full of turkeys. Master Carl, comes the cry, this insignificant cur is here to rescue you. Raul snaps her necro staff in half, killing her last totem, and a Heal gives Carl his sight back. The ogre's eyes are right there, pleading. Raul snaps again and takes her head, and tumbles away in a rain of turkeys.

beats.headline: The holy discharge
beats.text: A many-headed card boss, and Crawler Carl is on fire. Raul arrives calling him Daddy Carl, promises to quench the demon fire with his holy discharge, and sprays water into Carl's face, and keeps spraying after the fire is out. Alpha Carl, fighting for the boss, announces that he is the crab's daddy now. Raul calls him a demon unworthy of respect. Alpha Carl says something about Raul's mother. Crack. Totem eliminated.

beats.headline: Ascending, under pressure
beats.text: The demon Amayon needs millions of souls to go home, and the AI has ruled that crab sperm counts. On a beach of corpses, Crawler Carl summons Raul, tells him his people are dead, that he is the last one, and that he must fertilise the eggs now. Raul objects to the pressure, asks Carl not to watch, and requests a baby seal; there is a pile of dead ones. What finally works is Alpha Carl, summoned on Carl's side this time, yelling at him. Raul announces that he is ascending past the cloud rank. No more kowtowing.

beats.headline: Special mention to Crawler Carl
beats.text: Crawler Donut has already reported that Raul timed out back into her deck and is way stronger now. Then the announcement to all crawlers in Cuba: the eviction worked. The AI singles out Crawler Carl, who, it says, literally pulled off a guy named Raul to make it happen, and spells out the metaphor for anyone who missed it. Carl informs the ceiling that this is not true. Elle asks a follow-up question about the anatomy. Carl says the crab did it himself.

beats.headline: Mythic, and furious about it
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Lucia Mar go tumbling together, caked in oil, and Crawler Donut finally summons Raul. The level-up at the end of the previous floor took him from 70 to 110, his card is now mythic, and a summoning lasts ten minutes. His voice is deeper. He tears into Lucia's shield, asks how she dares challenge Daddy Carl, and for crimes against the heavens sentences her to eternal death. Please, Lucia says. Wait, says Carl.

beats.headline: Die, demon, die
beats.text: Daddy Carl is magnanimous today, Raul informs Lucia, who should now kiss his famed alabaster feet; then Carl sends him up the ramp to help Donut. Soon after, he comes back out of the tower in a heap with Carl, three Mongos and Gustavo the rottweiler, his shell sizzling from lightning and his health almost gone. He lunges to snap off the dog's head, shouting die, demon, die. The lightning takes him in the centre of the chest, and he disappears in a puff of smoke.

beats.headline: Could he be set free
beats.text: Tenth floor. Imani's fairy card Jacobus has come back as something real, and Crawler Donut did not know cards could be turned real. She almost says something else, and holds it back; Carl is thinking of Paz, whose card was ripped at the end of the eighth floor. What she asks instead: could they set Raul free forever? Crawler Carl doubts it. This was a god thing.

relations.note: A totem card in her deck
The souls that sent the demon home

tagline.text: Jola is a mythic totem card from Iceland, one of Katia's spares, and Princess Donut was delighted to put him in her deck.

Jola the Yule Cat is a fat, dirty-brown Persian the size of a house, with a candle as big as a garbage can burning on his head that reveals anything hidden. He speaks only Icelandic, which nobody present understands.
Jola's Fashion Critic blew every stitch of clothing off Quan Ch, and the cat meant to eat the lot. When Carl took Quan's cloak, Jola hissed at him and crouched to pounce.

beats.headline: A spare card from Katia
beats.text: Filing note. Before the club, Katia gives Princess Donut one of her excess totem cards: a mythic creature from Iceland named Jola. Crawler Carl expected Donut to be annoyed. She reads its abilities, is delighted, and wants it in the active deck, which is one totem too many, so she combines two problem cards with a consumable Combo and makes it permanent with Glow-Up. Carl asks in chat whether Jola does what she says. Great, Donut replies, as long as there are no children around. You'll see.

beats.headline: Beware, little children
beats.text: Summoning record. Donut plays Jola against the Visitor, a level-70 deckmaster hiding invisible with half a dozen Quench Moths. The sky goes black; digital snow; fake Christmas lights on the trailers. A lumpy yellow candle the size of a garbage can lights on top of the totem's head and reveals everything hidden. Jola is not floating. He is just huge: a fat, hairy, dirty-brown Persian cat the size of a house, bigger than Shi Maria, with a 75-second timer. The System's introduction ends on severed toddler tongue.

beats.headline: Words nobody can read
beats.text: The moths dive into his candle. The Nightgaunt, maddened by Crawler Carl's nightgaunt cloak, never plays a card. Jola asks it something in Icelandic, twice, slams it to the ground with a paw, shakes it dead in his jaws and eats it. Then his yellow eyes settle on Carl, he says three more sentences nobody present understands, and he disappears into dust. Donut's summary: the candle sees invisible things, nakedness and children make him stronger, and Katia says the fairy tale got him wrong. The real Yule Cat is a grump. This one is a serial killer.

beats.headline: Crippled on arrival
beats.text: Against Judge Lucian's many-headed card boss, a snare card lands on Jola as he forms, and he arrives Crippled, slowed and weakened, hobbling through the smoke like a ship through fog. A kitten's magic missile bounces off him. Alpha Carl, fighting for the boss, sticks a sticky bomb to the side of his head, and half of the cat's face disintegrates. Alpha Carl lands on one of Carl's snare traps, Jola moves in, and the kitten sings them both away as the claw comes down. Jola times out with an angry hiss.

beats.headline: Fashion Critic, and a cloak
beats.text: Inside the ruined entrance of a capitol building, Donut sends Jola and Lazarus in against Quan Ch and Ren. Jola fills the left side of the room to the ceiling and ignores every instruction, including keep the worm off our back. He has eyes only for Quan, and says something to him in Icelandic, twice. Then a yellow bolt: Fashion Critic. Everything Quan is wearing blows off him, and he drops like a rock to the rubble. A shining cloak spins to a stop at Crawler Carl's feet. Carl scoops it into his inventory.

beats.headline: The clothes were his
beats.text: The cat was going to eat those clothes. Jola glares at Crawler Carl and says two sentences in Icelandic that the System does not translate; the threat does not need it. He finishes slurping up Quan's trousers, turns, hisses at Carl for taking the cloak, and crouches to pounce. Carl tells Donut to end the battle, now. It is already over. Jola disappears mid-pounce in a puff of smoke.

beats.headline: Too big for this place
beats.text: Crawler Carl has already filed Jola beside Imani's totem, which killed her whole party, and Uzi Jesus, who shot Florin: their own cards were never entirely safe, and Jola nearly ate him. In the burning building where the demon is being evicted, Donut runs through her hand for Carl. Alpha Carl, Shi Maria, a golden combo card, a Lamp snare. Not Jola. She has already discarded him. He is too big for this place.

relations.note: Her spare card, given to Donut
A totem card in her deck

tagline.text: People call him Paulie, but his real name is Goff. He is a Residual living in a homeless man's body at a shelter, and he gives the same speech over breakfast every day, in case a crawler is ever standing there to hear it.

In frozen time, Paulie told Carl the rest: when crawlers die, what is inside them is harvested to feed the centre system, and a drink of his coffee installs a menu that can blow the star. Then the Paulie part of him asked Carl to be sure.

beats.headline: Coffee, then speech
beats.text: For the record: a flyer from a benefactor box sent Crawler Carl to a homeless shelter in Homestead, Florida, on Christmas morning, and graffiti outside supplied the rest. Look for me at breakfast. Red hat with the flaps. Coffee, then speech. The man in the red trapper hat is about seventy, in layers of flannel. Carl takes his plastic tub into inventory. The man sits, sugars his coffee, and says hello, crawler. It is a memory. He is not looking at Carl, only at the most likely spot.

beats.headline: The same speech every day
beats.text: People call me Paulie, he says, but my real name is Goff. About a year ago the mudskippers began deep imaging of the surface, so several of his kind in large population centres were tasked with saying this out loud every day, in case a crawler ever stood there to hear it. The residents groan; one has it memorised. This is the backup plan. Plan A is to say it inside the dungeon once the AI goes primal. And whoever you are, friends on the outside have moved the very heavens to get you here.

beats.headline: Biologically gondii, not truly
beats.text: His own account of himself: biologically gondii, though that is not who he truly is. Not Valtay. Not human. The body is real, and belonged to a man named Paulie who smoked too much, trusted the brother-in-law who stole his business, and has four children who do not care. Goff has his memories. The mudskippers call his kind Residuals. There is a war among them now, two sides with very different goals. Let me tell you how to shut off the, he says, and the world flashes.

beats.headline: The liaison's version
beats.text: Orren yanks Crawler Carl out to his office in the Desperado Club. That creature, he says, had nothing of substance to say. The whole thing was a trap set by the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, which gambled that pulling Carl away, or letting him hear, would end the crawl. Agatha is also a Residual, a different kind. The AI is stripping its protections from the remaining Residuals, and Orren expects them all dead before the floor collapses. Carl trades the plastic tub for a wand recharge scroll, three Cracker Jack scrolls, and four cretins for the ninth floor.

beats.headline: The spoon stops in the air
beats.text: Replay of the same breakfast, uncut. Everything in the shelter freezes; a dropped spoon hangs above a table. Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips, in Syndicate standard. The crawl is unnecessary, he says. Every living thing born on a seeded world carries a primal system the size of a grain of sand; when the crawlers die, the elements are harvested and fed to the bloated centre system, which grows. Stopping the crawl would shrink it, slowly, and harm nobody inside it. It persists because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: Drink it with a finger
beats.text: His coffee cup holds a neural enhancement, and he tells Crawler Carl to drink it. It works only on a natural interface, and not at all on a Syndicate spy, a plant, or one of those Eulogist pricks. The coffee is frozen in time; use a finger, he adds, and put the cup back on its circle. The menu it installs reaches the AI containment and the fuse. Pop it, and the star goes nova, taking Carl and everyone else with it. The AI, says Paulie, wants this. It wants to go home.

beats.headline: The Paulie part of him
beats.text: That was the official pitch, he says. That was Goff speaking, his duty and his mission. Years in this body have left some of Paulie in him, what his people call cross-contamination, and now the Paulie part is talking. Killing everyone runs against every value he has; there is another faction of his kind, more extreme, and this feels like something they would do. Direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. Be sure it is your only option. Then the install notice appears.

beats.headline: He never made it in
beats.text: Closing entry. Before leaving the liaison's office on Christmas morning, Crawler Carl asked whether that Paulie guy ever made it into the dungeon. No, said Orren. He was outside, but never within. Most of them never make it in; with collective minds and swarms, the individual parts are often disposable. Carl, beside an old dog at a Florida gas station, opens the menu Paulie described, expecting a single button. It is not a single button.

relations.note: The enhancement in his coffee installs it
Orren says they set the meeting up
Also a Residual, of a different kind

entities.name: War Leader Arief
entities.role: Semeru war leader · Larracos Defense Force

tagline.text: War Leader Arief is a young, level-80 Semeru dwarf with a long thin moustache, wearing his great-great-grandfather's hat. He is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud.

War Leader Arief guides the party down the rings of Larracos, which are numbered from the bottom. He means to take revenge on Architect Houston, who caught his brother sabotaging the Madness fortifications.
War Leader Arief stands guard at Juice Box's door, relays messages to the NPC spies, and runs the dwarven diggers whenever she is away.

beats.headline: His great-great-grandfather's hat
beats.text: Intake record. At the foot of the college stairs a dwarf officer, star over his head, feeds jerky to Mongo and Rend. Squat, young, beardless, a long thin moustache; samurai-like vest flaring like a bell, feathers straight up from his helmet, a wide sickle on his back, every piece enchanted. He bows. Honored Warlords. Crawler Donut loves his hat; it was his great-great-grandfather's. War Leader Arief, level 80 Semeru dwarf, commander of the Larracos Defense Force Infantry. Status: Despondent. His goddess is dead, and he cannot worship another.

beats.headline: In the traditional manner
beats.text: Crawler Donut asks in chat whether this nice dwarf knows who flooded his city, and who killed his goddess. Crawler Carl tells her not to bring it up. Arief, meanwhile, is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud. Juice Box wants Carl privately first. And, turning to Louis with another bow, she would like to solidify the great truce in the traditional manner. Through marriage. They would like to get it over with right away.

beats.headline: Sixty-six levels, counted upward
beats.text: Guided tour. Larracos has sixty-six levels, Arief says, not all full rings, numbered from the bottom: the college is on fifty, homes on forty-nine. The water reached level 39, drained to 29 and clogged, and Juice Box had it kept that way; it now sits at level 3, just over the castle's highest tower. His uncle drained the Piccadilly theatre and found it full of jellyfish. The glowing things at the ramp corners are explosives, in case the enemy gets in. There are some on every other down ramp.

beats.headline: There was another season
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, when orcs marched down the streets and Reavers jumped in. Crawler Carl stops in the road. Arief does not remember it himself; he believes he is new, like most of them. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, is one of the Jatismara, and sits on Juice Box's war council. Most of them know about their past lives. Asked by Britney whether his uncle remembers dying: no. For most of them, Arief believes, one death is forever.

beats.headline: Revenge on Architect Houston
beats.text: Arief pulls the curved blade off his back with a shing, and everyone jumps, Mongo included. When the fighting starts, he says, he takes his revenge on Architect Houston, leader of the Madness, who caught his brother sabotaging their fortifications. His brother was tortured, they say, before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. The raids bloodied every enemy camp and got inside every inner circle but the nagas', he adds: a court of assassins, where no changeling or spy has ever got in, and where even Juice Box does not try.

beats.headline: Guarding the door
beats.text: Arief leads the party down past flooded shops and through a panel in a kitchen wall to a hidden tunnel, and stands guard at the door while Juice Box lays her papers out. When Juice Box greets Louis with a kiss that does not stop, Crawler Carl exchanges a look with the dwarf at the door, who seems as sceptical as he is. The wedding itself is small and fast, and Arief guards that door too.

beats.headline: On the relay
beats.text: Operations note. The spies sent into naga territory are a pair of changelings, and Crawler Carl cannot speak to them directly. Every message goes from Carl to Britney, and from Britney to either Juice Box or Arief of the Semeru. Britney has become the crawlers' main liaison with the NPC team, and the dwarf is one of the two hands at the other end of it.

beats.headline: The diggers answer to him
beats.text: Harpocrates, a god, is going after the crawlers' friends, and Crawler Carl wants the dwarven digger under the Dream's castle turned on him. The giant robots have done nothing yet. Britney relays: Arief controls them while Juice Box is away, and she asks him. The digger comes. Harpocrates, who had turned back toward Donut, is waylaid by one of the diggers, which Carl has still not actually seen.

relations.note: Caught his brother
Delivers Juice Box's marriage offer

entities.name: Dante
entities.role: Former crawler · Trap Master guild instructor

tagline.text: Dante was a crocodilian former crawler, a guild instructor fourteen seasons short of freedom, who wrote a single entry in the cookbook's third edition. He was reassigned to guard an ice castle, refused to follow orders, and is dead.
Dante was ordered twice to kill the ice elves he guarded, and he refused twice. There was no third warning: a beam came from the sky and erased him.

beats.headline: A newsletter read three times
beats.text: For the record: the subject, a crocodilian, reads Damien's newsletter a third time beside his skyfowl neighbour, Justice Light, whose talon is shaking. Workers are being reassigned for an entire floor, which happens when the showrunners are cheap, and the Reavers are cheap. Justice Light is worried about his shop, his shelves and his art. The subject tells him they are to be snow castle guard captains in a settlement, still white-tagged, and that it is expensive for the showrunners if they die. That is not exactly true. He considers small lies acceptable when they calm a skyfowl.

beats.headline: One entry, and a brother
beats.text: The subject recognised Justice Light for what he was once the skyfowl started making familiar choices. It is obvious when someone has the cookbook, to anyone who has owned it. He applied at once to move from the lockpicking guild to the trap master guild, to be near his brother. He has never told Justice Light who he is, though neither of them has the cookbook any more. He wrote a single entry in it, afraid of being caught, and watching those who came after pour themselves into it has only made him feel worse. Guilt, maybe.

beats.headline: Fourteen seasons from freedom
beats.text: The eighth floor this season is mountains joined by wires and gondolas, and its crawlers are a flightless mantis who do poorly in the cold. The subject is watching one named York carefully. He has 14 seasons left, and he can taste freedom. Justice Light says he cannot fight crawlers; he means to refuse. What happens to him then? Nothing good, says the subject. He envies the skyfowl his conviction. He has a lot of violence in his heart, and he wants it aimed only at those who deserve it. His last recorded thought on the matter: fuck you all.

beats.headline: Refused to follow orders
beats.text: Dante, crocodilian, is dead. Class: Thief. Top level: 89. Dungeon exit: took a deal at the beginning of the 11th floor. Worked as a Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor in the Trap Master guild. Died 14 seasons short of his exit, while temporarily reassigned as an Ice Castle guard, by administrative action, for refusing to follow orders. Author of the Third Edition of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook. The file does not say what the orders were. It lists his current status in one word: dead.

beats.headline: No third warning
beats.text: Justice Light tells the rest to Juice Box. The castle was full of ice elf servants, gentle creatures who loved puzzles and the snow, and over weeks they became the two guards' friends. At the end of the floor, off camera, the guards were ordered to kill them all. The subject looked up into the air and said he would not. They ordered a second time. He refused again. There was no third warning: a beam came from the sky and he was simply gone. Justice Light calls it execution by the AI, which is rare. He says the subject died free.

tagline.text: Volteeg's only note in the seventh edition of the cookbook says he misses her so much, and asks whether surviving this place is worth it with her gone. He does not think it is.

Volteeg was a pet songbird who became a gargoyle crawler, and then a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He filled his tank with humming energy balls, put on Mozart, and drove it into his own warlord's caravan.

beats.headline: The seventh edition's only note
beats.text: For the record: the note added by Crawler Volteeg, Seventh Edition, runs to a few lines. He misses her. He misses her so goddamn much. Is it worth it, to survive this place with her gone? No, he does not think it is. Beneath it, Crawler Drakea of the 22nd Edition adds that this is Volteeg's first, last, and only entry in the cookbook, and: fuck everything about this place. At dawn, with Prepotente watching and unable to move, Crawler Carl is thinking of that line.

beats.headline: Berries under her jacket
beats.text: Before the dungeon, the subject was a bird in a cage, and Mistress Henspar kept it clean. She let him perch on her shoulder at the market. Once he bit a shopkeeper's finger when the man tried to feed him a berry, and she forgave him that night by the fire. After that she hid him inside her jacket and slipped him stolen berries, and he tried very hard not to peep. Back outside, belly full, he would sing for her, and salty tears would run down her cheeks. His birth race is Sturnus. His file says he does not consider himself worthy of love.

beats.headline: A race that cannot sing
beats.text: The pet biscuit gave the subject speech and a little intelligence. On the third floor he chose to become a gargoyle, and only then did his mind begin to work, and the world stop being simple. A gargoyle cannot sing, not the way he used to. He counts that as a terrible mistake. He remembers standing over her, transformed and screaming, trying to protect her from the scags. Mistress Henspar died on the seventh floor. After that he was not scared any more. There was only the rage. The cookbook came to him then.

beats.headline: One entry at the ninth's end
beats.text: He did not notice the hidden words on the seemingly useless prayer cast projection until the very first days of the ninth floor. He spent most of Faction Wars in hiding, like the rest, unable to raise his head for fear of the Conscription spell, reading the words of those who came before him and feeling nothing but shame. He told himself the cookbook had come to him too late. At the very end of the ninth floor, as the orc armies roared in victory, he made his one and only entry.

beats.headline: Twenty-six seasons without a fight
beats.text: On the tenth floor he took the first deal offered: an unprotected NPC guard in a combat-based external guild for 26 seasons, low chance of survival. He survived without fighting, let alone killing, a single crawler. Nobody wants to fight a gargoyle. On exit, the magic of his adopted race stopped working. In heavy gravity he needs a brace just to stand. He took security work on the Auditor General's compliance barge, among the One-Offs: unique former crawlers with no home. His two friends there are a djinn in a wheelchair and a cave fairy who can no longer fly.

beats.headline: A pet on the form
beats.text: Now he is on the surface as Weeper Commander Volteeg for the Operatic Collective, racial abilities returned. He was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the other former-crawler mercenaries: he entered the dungeon as a pet, and someone in the Pacifist Network changed that designation so he reads as a refugee. That was Porthus's doing. Rosetta recognised his strange name and told Porthus, who asked him to his face. He said he was ashamed at his inaction. Porthus told him it is not too late to do something about it.

beats.headline: Show me Mistress Henspar
beats.text: Volteeg, gargoyle, Tank Buttress, top level 71, is dead. The Weepers have a flaw in their fire control. He removed the chamber and filled his tank with dozens of humming energy balls, put Mozart on, and sang along as he turned toward the litter carrying Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit. Told he was too close to the caravan, he answered that this was the point. He lit a blitz stick, said Show me Mistress Henspar, and pushed it into the ball on his lap. Over 10,000 of his fellow soldiers died with him, and the Operatic Collective was eliminated.

tagline.text: Rectrix is a sponsor whom Baroness Victory has reminded, along with the Maestro, that making a deity act outside its nature is against the rules.
Rectrix is the Open Intellect's agent and is driving the goddess Theia this season, which is why Samantha found a male skyfowl in her mother's temple.

beats.headline: A boy eagle in the temple
beats.text: For the record: Samantha was promised a chance to go into the temple of her mother, the goddess Theia, and went. She came back shouting. Her mother was an eagle. A boy eagle. The plan had counted on Theia's sponsor, an agent of the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, to have her clerics help at best. Nobody expected Samantha to meet the god in person. Sponsored gods may appear in their own form, and NPCs are meant to see the god regardless. Samantha did not. She calls him the imposter.

beats.headline: Reminded of the rules
beats.text: Baroness Victory returns to the room. Samantha accuses her of being in on it: Victory was there, and told the imposter he would not be allowed to help. Victory's ruling is that sponsors causing deities to act outside their nature is against faction wars rules. It gives an unfair advantage and happens anyway. She reminded both the Maestro and Rectrix of that before coming to watch Crawler Carl drop a bomb at his own feet. Crawler Carl does not think he has heard the name before. It sounds oddly familiar.

beats.headline: The Open Intellect's agent
beats.text: Crawler Carl is banned from every temple except his own and those where he has been named friend of the church. Theia is on that list. Of the gods on that list, Odette drives Nekhebit, and the Open Intellect's agent, Rectrix, drives Theia. So the male skyfowl in Theia's temple has a name, and a network behind him. All Rosetta has told Crawler Carl of the sponsor is that it is nobody he knows: a previous crawler activist who hates the dungeon as much as he does.

beats.headline: Work after the crawlers
beats.text: In a message to Justice Light, with the war mages holding the Gate, Rosetta lays out what is left. Perhaps the mages winning is not such a bad thing: it will be quick, and the remaining mercenaries and leaders will be dead. Justice Light says he is not done yet. If all the crawlers die, she answers, the Ascendency starts at once, and Rectrix gets to work. Perhaps, after all this, York and Rectrix survive. A longer crawl risks the AI growing stronger.

beats.headline: Not really your mother
beats.text: Samantha gives Tipid her account of the ninth floor. She went to kill her mother, Theia, and found some skyfowl dude instead, which has a way of messing with a girl's head. He told her, Look, I'm not really your mother. She told him no shit. He tried again: no, he meant Theia is not. She told him okay, weirdo. That is the whole of the exchange on file, and the subject is not named in it. Samantha moved on to the part where the whole club went nuts.

tagline.text: Nami is a model and influencer who outbid the Priory to drive the goddess Eris. She had surgery to look and sound just like Hekla, and now she wants out.
Someone stripped Eris's soul armour and threw Nami out of the goddess. She landed in the grass outside the ball of flesh, and the fleshers took her.

beats.headline: How do I eject
beats.text: For the record: in the distance, Meatus shouts at Eris to stay out of this. A psychotic female laugh answers, then the same voice swearing. She said she did not want to come down to other floors. How does she eject? Get her out of here. She laughs again, crazier, and insists she is not the one laughing. Crawler Katia hears Hekla in it. Mordecai says someone new is driving Eris this year and has just been sucked back into the goddess's body by the new rule.

beats.headline: A face bought to match
beats.text: Rosetta supplies the name. Eris is sponsored by Nami, a model and influencer, who outbid the Priory; the Priory usually has a different priestess pilot Eris each season. The subject sounds like that old crawler because she had surgery to look and sound just like her. It is, Rosetta says, a thing. Eris herself looks a little like Hekla too. Crawler Donut wants to know whether there is one of her. Rosetta: they usually wait until the person is dead.

beats.headline: Out of the ball of flesh
beats.text: Something bursts out of the rolling ball of flesh as if from a blowhole: a person, arms waving, rocketing straight up and slamming into the grass. A human woman, off-worlder outline, no army glow. One slender arm rises for help. Baroness Victory does not know what to make of it, and Fopsy finds nothing in the ruleset for it. She crawls toward them, screaming soundlessly, in armor Crawler Carl half recognises. He asks Crawler Donut whether she cast Laundry Day. She did not.

beats.headline: Taken by the fleshers
beats.text: Nami, influencer, is dead. Three fleshers fall off the ball and scuttle to her. The first wraps her legs and climbs her, dissolving her flesh, and her scream rises. Dong Quixote asks whether they should help. Crawler Carl says no: wait until it kills her. Baroness Victory recognises her then. Someone has stripped the goddess's soul armor, ejecting the driver. Crawler Carl works out that a war mage is inside the ball. The flesher stands up wearing her, a dromedarian skin draped over her like a ghost costume, and two more attach. Crawler Carl throws a hob-lobber. It kills her and the fleshers at once.

beats.headline: A fan at the gate
beats.text: At Squirties, Zander has a customer he did not hear dock: a tall, elf-like woman with a long neck and naga-like eyes, holding the Uzi Jesus toy. He compliments her costume, or surgery, then remembers what happened. Is she a fan of Nami? Shame what happened to her. Has she come to the gate to pay her respects? She asks whether he is asking Eris, goddess of chaos, if she is wearing a costume. She laughs, and snaps her fingers.

entities.name: Fopsy
entities.role: Adjutant for the Dream · former Prime Minister

tagline.text: Former Prime Minister Fopsy is the Dream's adjutant: a tripod, a round body covered in black dots on three long, jointed legs. He observes, and keeps his theories to himself.
Fopsy says he had no idea that his own client was a robot, and if the vote goes a certain way, he may be Prime Minister again.
Fopsy was passed over for the vacant office of Prime Minister, because nobody was certain of his relationship to the Dream. Victory has the job instead, for now.

beats.headline: A basketball on three legs
beats.text: For the record: a second adjutant appears beside Baroness Victory, a type of alien Crawler Carl has never seen. A round, basketball-like body covered in black dots that may be eyes, standing on three long, multi-jointed legs. A tripod. Tripods are supposedly completely without emotion. Former Prime Minister Fopsy. Adjutant for The Dream. Non-combatant observer. He says nothing and scuttles aside. His arrival makes Crawler Carl realise that the Dream's warlord must be inside the ball of flesh as well.

beats.headline: Five potions for a Gate
beats.text: His first words, when a woman shoots out of the ball, are that the ruleset has nothing for this, and there is nothing to do but observe and report. Then the adjutants talk past Crawler Carl. Bao has not called foul. A spell to do this would need level 19, perhaps 18, and would not work on sponsored gods, which explains the ejection. Victory says potions. The subject checks his menus, every eye twinkling like a disco ball: the war mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods at the Midnight Market for five of them.

beats.headline: A theory kept back
beats.text: The subject's reading of the war mages' warlord: the residual is not only trying to win Faction Wars and zero out the crawlers, but to end the ascendency game fast. Once it is finished with no crawlers left, a hard-coded shutdown and hibernation follows, an alternative to the failsafe. That makes sense if she believes the local AI is a threat to the Eulogist. How she convinced the war mages, he does not understand. He has additional theories, and declines to voice them in the presence of a combatant.

beats.headline: Get fucked, Prime Minister
beats.text: He teleports into the Nest Tower without Crawler Carl hearing a thing, and his presence reminds Crawler Carl that two warlords, Tagg and Fang, are still unaccounted for. Rosetta arrives out of breath with Edgar the tortoise strapped to her back and does a double take at him. Former prime minister, she says, and grins. Get fucked. But she is glad he is here to witness this.

beats.headline: Quite clever, says the tripod
beats.text: A second net is holding Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut inside the Nest Tower, and the two adjutants diagnose it while watching. Victory calls it classic Lucia Mar. The subject agrees: her first net was a personal one from a scroll, and she likely cast a second in case of a countermeasure, which sat waiting for a power source. Victory names it Power Siphon, drawing on the tower jewels in Larracos. Quite clever, says the subject. Crawler Carl, who has already ordered Lucia to turn it all off, is less impressed.

beats.headline: An outline in the power view
beats.text: At one point both adjutants are simply gone, and Crawler Carl never sees them leave. Then, at the front of the castle, the Reavers' antlered adjutant whispers to someone over his left shoulder, where nobody is standing. Crawler Donut cannot see through the invisibility, but switching to the power view gives her a rough outline: that weird alien who looks like a basketball on stilts. Fopsy. With both missing warlords' adjutants present, Crawler Carl concludes the trap is looking more likely, calls off the fooling around, and switches to plan B.

beats.headline: No inkling whatsoever
beats.text: He and Victory return with a crack from a virtual meeting of the Syndicate Council, called back because the AI was throwing a fit about them missing all this. A No Confidence vote on Glory is under way. Tagg was secretly moving toward the post-physical path, and Victory notes that, depending on the vote, the subject might be Prime Minister again, which is doubly interesting in the Dream's own adjutant. He had no idea, he says. No inkling whatsoever, though it makes sense now, considering some clues.

beats.headline: Passed over for Prime Minister
beats.text: Asked when the stairwells appear, Victory says immediately; the subject corrects her: about ten seconds. The office goes elsewhere. Victory reports that because people were not certain of former Prime Minister Fopsy's relationship to the Dream, he was passed over for the newly vacated position of Syndicate Prime Minister. She is acting Prime Minister Victory now, with a real vote in a few months. Rosetta sounds strangely irritated at the news.

tagline.text: Quemada is a level-96 fire fairy, the protection in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad. She speaks with a thick Spanish accent, and she has just tripled her price.
Since the elf mage spoke, Quemada no longer knows what is real, and her panic heats the cab by the moment. Finley has had to put her to sleep.
Quemada never woke. Finley was carrying her to a temple, so that she would not wake alone, when an APV hit him in the street, and Olga and Quemada died with him.

beats.headline: Team Helix, three for one
beats.text: For the record: Rosetta brings in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad that has raced two heats and placed first and second. A level 75 Grulke named Olga, a level 81 Porsuk named Finley, and the subject: a level 96 flaming fire fairy about Crawler Donut's size. Olga says the second place does not count. A demon with chains cheated, killing one of their two clients and their friend Helado. The subject speaks with a thick Spanish accent, worships Emberus, and has not taken her eyes off the bubbling Emberus shrine.

beats.headline: Triple the price, or walk
beats.text: She turns to Crawler Carl and changes her mind. It is not double the price. It is triple. Rosetta objects that the price has been negotiated and paid to the mercenary guild, and it cannot be raised after the fact. It is triple, the subject says, or they walk. Crawler Carl asks whether they drove in the last races. Finley and Olga can both drive; she is protection. Crawler Carl looks at her for a moment, and agrees to pay.

beats.headline: The unappeasable fire beckons
beats.text: Passing the temple to Club Vanquisher, she whispers that she had a vision. Their lord told her to help any fellow worshipper who was also a racer, and they are tasked with slaying his brother, Hellik: impossible, but they must try. She raised the price because she expects to be slain in the attempt, and the fee is to keep Olga and Finley safe for a while. She has already lost one friend. Her small hand on his shoulder sets his cape smouldering. Prepare yourself, brother. The unappeasable fire beckons.

beats.headline: She stops talking about Hellik
beats.text: In the village she rides Crawler Carl's shoulder, oblivious to what has just happened to him, giving him a pep talk about dying as a martyr. At the start line of the next heat she is hovering in the back of the truck, strangely depressed. Asked about Crawler Donut's singing, she manages a noncommittal squeak. She has stopped talking about killing Hellik. She keeps raising a finger as if to say something, then changing her mind. Crawler Carl suspects the conversation in the shop with Akuma: NPCs act differently after meeting one fully awakened.

beats.headline: Are you real
beats.text: On the start line, Crawler Carl feels heat on his shoulder. The subject is floating there, sobbing. Finley asks from the back whether Que is doing okay. She does not know what is real any more. Is this real? Is Crawler Carl real? Is she? Does any of it matter? Over the chat, meanwhile, Osvaldo is naming the god his second memorial crystal is for. Ahead, the floating traffic lights turn from red to yellow.

beats.headline: Doing this over and over
beats.text: In the truck it comes on suddenly, a full-blown panic attack, and the cab heats by the moment. Did Finley not hear what that elf mage said? Did nothing break in his small brain? It broke in hers. They have been doing this over and over. Olga explains, sheepish: a panic disorder. Their ice fairy, Helado, used to calm her. After the chain demon killed Helado, the subject killed one of their two clients, until Finley talked her down. Only one of them, Olga adds. She is better now.

beats.headline: Sleep now, friend
beats.text: Entering the forest, she babbles. She is not crazy. Or is she? What can she burn? She begs Emberus to show himself and speak to her and Crawler Carl. Finley grabs her out of the air in both hands. Stop, Fin, she says. Please stop. Let me end it all. He pokes her with one of his claws. Sleep now, friend, he says, gently, and Unconscious appears over her. He lays her carefully in the sink.

beats.headline: Carried into the street
beats.text: Quemada, fire fairy, is dead. She never woke. Finley regrets using so strong a sedative; she'll be mad he did not protect Olga. In town he carries the toad in his arms and the subject over his shoulder, on a scorched leather patch strapped to his jacket for carrying her while she is out. He is taking Que to a temple so she does not wake alone. He says they are his family. He steps into the street, and the APV of team One Fine Pig runs all three down, reverses, and runs them down again.

beats.headline: A scorch mark on the street
beats.text: Crawler Carl sits at the curb in front of what is left. Finley's legs are gone. Olga's head is caved in. The subject simply poofed out in a flare and left a scorch mark. Crawler Carl asks Crawler Donut to take the corpses, Finley and Olga at least; there is nothing of the subject to take. The crew cannot hire new mercenaries between heats. Crawler Carl sits there thinking how unfair it is: an NPC he barely knew, on his way to help his two friends, and all three snuffed out.

entities.name: Minus
entities.role: Syndicate security soldier · the tourist who was not Linus

tagline.text: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, sent into the crawl under the name of his dead brother, Linus. He has a primary target, a secondary target, and orders to act the pervert for a while.
Minus, the tourist who was not really Linus, was outed at the crawlers' farewell gathering by the fan club he had been imitating. His first target was Imani, and his second was Louis.
The AI has told the whole dungeon that Linus was replaced by his brother, a soldier sent to kill two crawlers and break what the rest have built. Princess Donut's only question: his name was Minus?

beats.headline: A brother in a trash-filled berth
beats.text: For the record: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, and the file opens on him standing over his brother Linus's corpse, in a trash-filled berth on one of the swanky habitats orbiting the star, just killed by Syndicate security. The brothers last spoke five cycles ago, a month after their father's funeral. Minus had not known Linus moved off the surface. Posters of Elle cover the walls. He feels guilt, then shame, then the thought that their mother is going to be so pissed.

beats.headline: Orders: act the pervert
beats.text: Captain Fresh hands him a datapad: some five hundred hours of the fairy crawler's footage and every post his brother made about her, to rapid-inject tonight, because the tenth floor begins in hours. He is to be half-corporeal, a non-combatant, attached to the fairy crawler, with a primary and a secondary target. So act the pervert for some time, the captain says. He calls it a suicide mission: a surgical crawler kill to destabilise the group and start the Ascendency game early. Minus salutes. Whatever it takes, sir.

beats.headline: Between Louis and the fleshmancer
beats.text: At the Lollipop, the tourist on file as Linus sits on one side of Grigori the Placid, with Louis on the other scattering cookie crumbs. He stares at Elle with puppy dog eyes. His shirt has moved on from a naked picture of her to a moving, all-over print of her screaming face mid-spell, captioned: Right in the keister! The fleshmancer sits ramrod straight between them, flicking crumbs off his robes, and looks absolutely out of place.

beats.headline: His fingers in Donut's tail
beats.text: While Donut has the fleshmancer brush her, the tourist pats her chain mail crupper and then runs his long fingers along her tail. I'm touching her, he announces. Elle threatens to have someone in the outside world break his creepy little fingers. He carries on regardless: she smells good, Elle doesn't let him sniff her. He whispers something to Donut and sucks his triple-segmented finger. Donut turns: excuse me? Elle gives up and takes him with her. Oh goody, he says. The orders said act the pervert.

beats.headline: Pestering Bautista about tea
beats.text: In the guildhall he is across the room, whispering at Bautista, who is not amused. Per Princess Donut, he keeps trying to get Daniel to make tea: Bautista tea is trending, Daniel has no outreach manager, and the members of her message board are all jealous. Of the tourist, she clarifies, not of Daniel. Elle's Snow Cones fan club raided her server the other day; now the two boards are friends and working together. The tea is noted.

beats.headline: A cup kept ready for two
beats.text: In the entrance square of Hungry Eyes Village, where crawlers bound for the Pineapple Cabaret are saying their goodbyes, Bautista has set out his teapots, and the subject pours: for a chainsaw crawler named Karac, for Prepotente, who demands the recipe blow by blow. Imani and Louis, he says, like it really hot, so he has one ready for them. Elle asks whether he has poisoned their tea out of jealousy. He gives a nervous laugh. Bautista pours for his friends himself.

beats.headline: Outed at his own farewell
beats.text: Elle's speech turns to him. The Snow Cones knew an impostor the moment he arrived, and she reads out an essay the real Linus posted before this floor: he misses his family, especially his big brother. Did he really write that, the soother asks. He never wrote me. He was brought in after his brother was already dead, he says. Donut tells him half the alien internet worked it out five minutes after he arrived. He never really watched the show, he admits. Elle: the poison he pretended to drop in the tea would not have worked anyway. Every drinker was immune.

beats.headline: Imani first, pork chop second
beats.text: Asked for his target, he laughs. Not Carl: the last person they want taken out, the best chance anyone has, because he is the one most likely to get everyone killed. Not the cat: losing her would make Carl too volatile. The target was Imani. The secondary, thumbed over his shoulder, was pork chop, meaning Louis. I was just following orders, he says. Carl's grip pops through the illusion of his neck. It does not hurt him. He is told everyone who put the crawlers here has already lost.

beats.headline: Back to a small ship
beats.text: The subject does not answer. He knows what comes next: out of the dungeon and back to his small, defenseless spaceship, currently trapped in orbit over Earth, where a few friends of the crawlers are waiting for him. The file records that he knew it, and that he said nothing. Elle, wiping her eyes, says her Barry really did love that song.

beats.headline: Named to the whole dungeon
beats.text: The AI, explaining why it changed this race at the last minute, briefs the out-of-the-loop crawlers: the tourist Linus was replaced by his brother, Minus, a soldier, sent to kill two crawlers in hopes their deaths would destabilise the rest. His targets were Imani C and Louis Santiago 2. That surprised it, the AI admits; it does not understand why not Florin, or why not Princess Donut. Donut's first question is only about the name. His name was Minus?

tagline.text: Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut. Her uncle makes her pay for his recap by fixing a sink she knows nothing about.
When Taurins came to the house on a contract and hurt her father, Tempest fired the very illegal blaster her uncle had given her, and she was the one left standing.

beats.headline: A sink for a recap
beats.text: For the record: Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on perceptions of the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut, because her teacher knows who her uncle is. Most people she interviews give their answers for free. He does not. The trade is that she fixes his plumbing, of which she knows nothing. She informs him that the only lesson she has learned today is that her uncle is a colossal prick, and tells him to start talking.

beats.headline: Terms, and a recap
beats.text: His opening recap is three sentences, the last of them The end. Terms improve when she threatens to tell her father that Quasar claimed to be her real dad: now we're talking, says her uncle. She records the eighth floor from him, cards, Quan, the dog girl with the flamethrower, the nun, and presses on what he skips: the homeless shelter, the last card, the spider in Carl's chest. The pipe comes away in her hands. Don't worry, kid, he says. The sink doesn't work anyway. It's an art piece.

beats.headline: Are you in danger?
beats.text: She turns the recorder off before she asks the serious question. Is he in danger for representing Carl? Real danger? Quasar wants to lie and decides against it; the kid deserves the truth. He thinks they all are, he tells her. It is the first time in his life he is glad they live so far out in the middle of nowhere. Filed without comment, beyond this: she asked it with the recorder off.

beats.headline: Blood at her temple
beats.text: Her uncle is heading for a tunnel booth when his tablet shows her face, panicked, blood on her temple. Taurins came looking for Quasar; her dad told them to fuck themselves, and he is hurt. A voice finds her off screen, she shrieks, and the feed goes fuzzy. Then a Taurin's head fills the screen, apologetic. He took a contract with Quasar's client's wife. Quasar can come to him, and his brother and this sweet little piece of Nullian ass need not get hurt.

beats.headline: The illegal blaster
beats.text: The Taurin's head explodes. So does the second one's. Tempest comes back on screen crying, holding the blaster her uncle gave her, very illegal, already tagged by law enforcement sniffers until Quasar flags the call as attorney business. Is that all of them? She thinks so. He tells her to check on her dad and go with the someone he is sending to the house. Her dad, she reports, is screaming, more mad than hurt. Quasar hires Kiki for one credit: legal help, and the other kind.
